law-of-contract-i-u1-t11.subtitle: Section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872; section 2(46) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019; section 10A of the Information Technology Act, 2000

en.inOneMinute: A standard form contract is a contract whose terms are printed or written in advance by one party (usually a big company, the State or a service provider) and offered to everyone on a "take it or leave it" basis. The other party cannot bargain; he can only sign, click or take the ticket. Railway and bus tickets, insurance policies, bank forms, courier consignment notes, dry-cleaning bills, builder-buyer agreements and website "I agree" terms are all standard forms. In the USA they are called "contracts of adhesion" ( LIC of India v. Consumer Education & Research Centre ). Such contracts save time, but they are often used to slip in exemption clauses that cut down the stronger party's liability. The law protects the weaker party in five ways: Notice. A printed term binds only if reasonable notice of it was given before or at the time of the contract ( Parker ; Olley ; Thornton ). A mere receipt is not a contract document ( Chapelton ). Signature. A person who signs a document is normally bound by it, read or not ( L'Estrange v. Graucob ; Bharathi Knitting v. DHL ). Strict reading. An unclear term is read against the party who drafted it ( contra proferentem ). Unfair terms. Courts will not enforce an unfair and unreasonable clause imposed by a party with superior bargaining power; such a clause can be void under Section 23 as opposed to public policy ( Brojo Nath Ganguly ; Lilly White ). A clause barring the usual legal proceedings is void under Section 28 . Consumer law. Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the State and National Commissions can declare an unfair contract term null and void (Sections 2(46), 49(2), 59(2)); Pioneer v. Govindan Raghavan applied this to a builder's one-sided agreement. Online terms accepted by clicking "I agree" are standard forms too; such contracts are valid under Section 10A of the IT Act, and the same protections apply. In the exam, define, give examples, then explain each protection with a case. In real life, this tells you when the "terms and conditions" on a bill, ticket or website really bind you.
legalProvision: There is no single section on standard form contracts . The rules come from case law and these provisions.

Section 23, Indian Contract Act, 1872. What considerations and objects are lawful, and what not. The consideration or object of an agreement is lawful, unless— it is forbidden by law; or is of such a nature that if permitted, it would defeat the provisions of any law; or is fraudulent ; or involves or implies injury to the person or property of another; or the Court regards it as immoral, or opposed to public policy. In each of these cases, the consideration or object of an agreement is said to be unlawful. Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.

Section 28, Indian Contract Act, 1872 (main part). Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings, void. Every agreement,— (a) by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract, by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals, or which limits the time within which he may thus enforce his rights; or (b) which extinguishes the rights of any party thereto, or discharges any party thereto, from any liability, under or in respect of any contract on the expiry of a specified period so as to restrict any party from enforcing his rights, is void to the extent.

Section 10A, Information Technology Act, 2000. Validity of contracts formed through electronic means. Where in a contract formation, the communication of proposals, the acceptance of proposals, the revocation of proposals and acceptances, as the case may be, are expressed in electronic form or by means of an electronic records, such contract shall not be deemed to be unenforceable solely on the ground that such electronic form or means was used for that purpose.

Section 2(46), Consumer Protection Act, 2019. "unfair contract" means a contract between a manufacturer or trader or service provider on one hand, and a consumer on the other, having such terms which cause significant change in the rights of such consumer, including the following, namely:— (i) requiring manifestly excessive security deposits to be given by a consumer for the performance of contractual obligations; or (ii) imposing any penalty on the consumer, for the breach of contract thereof which is wholly disproportionate to the loss occurred due to such breach to the other party to the contract; or (iii) refusing to accept early repayment of debts on payment of applicable penalty; or (iv) entitling a party to the contract to terminate such contract unilaterally, without reasonable cause; or (v) permitting or has the effect of permitting one party to assign the contract to the detriment of the other party who is a consumer, without his consent; or (vi) imposing on the consumer any unreasonable charge, obligation or condition which puts such consumer to disadvantage;

Section 49(2), Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Without prejudice to the provisions of sub-section (1), the State Commission may also declare any terms of contract, which is unfair to any consumer, to be null and void.

Section 59(2), Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Without prejudice to sub-section (1), the National Commission may also declare any terms of contract, which is unfair to any consumer to be null and void.
In simple words

Section 23: an agreement (or a clause) whose object is opposed to public policy is void . The Supreme Court used this to strike down an unfair clause in a standard form ( Brojo Nath Ganguly ). Section 28: a clause that stops a party from going to court at all, or cuts down the time for suing, is void to that extent . Arbitration clauses are saved by the exceptions to the section. Section 10A, IT Act: a contract is not invalid merely because the offer and acceptance were made electronically , for example by clicking "I agree". Section 2(46), CPA 2019: an unfair contract is a contract between a trader or service provider and a consumer with terms that significantly change the consumer's rights , such as excessive deposits, disproportionate penalties or one-sided termination. Sections 49(2) and 59(2), CPA 2019: the State Commission and the National Commission can declare an unfair term null and void . A complaint that an unfair contract has been adopted is a "complaint" under Section 2(6)(i); such complaints go to the State Commission (consideration up to ₹10 crore, Section 47(1)(a)(ii)) or the National Commission (above ₹10 crore, Section 58(1)(a)(ii)).
en.meaning:
What a standard form contract is

A standard form contract is a contract in which:

the terms are drafted in advance by one party , usually in print or on a screen; the same terms are offered to every customer ; the other party has no real chance to bargain ; he must accept the whole form or go without the goods or service.

The Supreme Court described the position in LIC of India v. Consumer Education & Research Centre (1995): "In dotted line contracts there would be no occasion for a weaker party to bargain or to assume to have equal bargaining power. He has either to accept or leave the services or goods in terms of the dotted line contract."

Other names

Contract of adhesion: "In USA, the standard forms of contracts are called 'Contracts of Adhesion'" ( LIC ). The weaker party merely "adheres" to terms set by the other. Dotted line contract: the customer only signs "on the dotted line" ( Brojo Nath Ganguly ; Pioneer ). E-contracts: online standard forms. In a click-wrap contract the user clicks "I agree" after the terms are shown; in a browse-wrap contract the terms are only on a link and the site says that using it means accepting them; in a shrink-wrap contract the terms come inside the package of a product such as software.

Why they are used, and the danger

Advantages Dangers Saves time when thousands of similar contracts are made (railways, insurance, banks) The customer usually does not read the small print Same terms for everyone; easy to administer The drafter can insert exemption clauses limiting his liability Lower cost of each transaction Unequal bargaining power: "take it or leave it"

Running example

Priya gives a silk saree worth ₹12,000 to Sparkle Dry Cleaners for cleaning. She pays ₹300 and gets a printed bill. On the back, in small print: "Liability for loss or damage is limited to 10 times the cleaning charge." The saree is lost. Under the clause, Sparkle would pay only ₹3,000 (10 × ₹300), and Priya would lose ₹9,000 (₹12,000 − ₹3,000). Below we test whether the clause binds her.
keyPoints: Standard form: terms drafted by one party; "take it or leave it"; "contracts of adhesion" ( LIC ). Unsigned terms bind only with reasonable notice ( Parker ). Notice must be before or at the time of contract ( Olley ; Thornton ). A mere receipt is not a contract document ( Chapelton ). Signed terms bind, read or not ( L'Estrange ; Bharathi Knitting ). Contra proferentem : unclear terms read against the drafter. Unfair clause between unequal parties is void under Section 23 ( Brojo Nath Ganguly ). Clause barring courts is void under Section 28 ; arbitration saved. CPA 2019: State and National Commissions may declare unfair terms null and void (Sections 49(2), 59(2)); Pioneer . Click-wrap contracts are valid (IT Act, Section 10A).

caseLaws.name: Parker v
caseLaws.facts: South Eastern Railway Co. (1877) Facts. Parker left a bag in a railway cloakroom, paid 2d and received a ticket whose back limited the company's liability to £10. The bag was lost. Principle. An unsigned ticket's conditions bind if the company gave reasonable notice of them, even if the customer did not read them. (1877) 2 CPD 416 (Court of Appeal). Why it matters. It is the leading case on the reasonable notice test. L'Estrange v. F. Graucob Ltd. (1934) Facts. A café owner signed an order form for a slot machine; small print excluded all warranties. The machine did not work. Principle. A person who signs a contractual document is bound by it, whether or not he has read it. [1934] 2 KB 394. Why it matters. It is the leading case on signed standard forms . Lilly White v. R. Munuswami (1964) Facts. A customer's new saree (Rs. 220) was lost by a dry cleaner whose bill limited liability to 50% of the market price. Principle. Such a term "cannot be enforced by a court, merely, because it is printed on the reverse of a bill." AIR 1966 Mad 13 (Madras High Court). Why it matters. It is the Indian authority against unreasonable printed exemption clauses . Bharathi Knitting Co. v. DHL Worldwide Express Courier (1996) Facts. The sender signed a courier consignment note limiting the courier's liability to US$100. Principle. "When there is a specific term in the contract, the parties are bound by the terms in the contract." (1996) 4 SCC 704. Why it matters. It applies the signature rule in India. Central Inland Water Transport Corporation v. Brojo Nath Ganguly (1986) Facts. A Government company's service rule let it terminate permanent employees on three months' notice or pay, without reasons. Ganguly's services were terminated under it on 26 February 1983. Principle. The Courts will "strike down an unfair and unreasonable contract, or an unfair and unreasonable clause in a contract, entered into between parties who are not equal in bargaining power"; such a clause is void under Section 23. AIR 1986 SC 1571 : (1986) 3 SCC 156. Why it matters. It is the leading Indian case on unconscionable terms in standard forms . LIC of India v. Consumer Education & Research Centre (1995) Facts. LIC's term insurance policy under Table 58 was offered only to persons in Government, quasi-Government or reputed commercial firms. The condition was challenged as discriminatory. Principle. "In dotted line contracts there would be no occasion for a weaker party to bargain"; the restricting clause was unconstitutional and severable, and LIC's terms must be reasonable, just and fair. AIR 1995 SC 1811 : (1995) 5 SCC 482. Why it matters. It explains standard form ("adhesion") contracts and the weaker party's lack of choice. Pioneer Urban Land & Infrastructure Ltd. v. Govindan Raghavan (2019) Facts. A builder's agreement charged the buyer 18% interest a year for delayed payments but gave the buyer only 9% a year for the builder's delay in possession. Principle. "A term of a contract will not be final and binding if it is shown that the flat purchasers had no option but to sign on the dotted line, on a contract framed by the builder." [2019] 5 SCR 1169. Why it matters. It applies the protection against one-sided standard forms to consumer contracts .

selfTest.q: 1. What is a "contract of adhesion"?
selfTest.a: The American name for a standard form contract, where the weaker party only adheres to terms set by the other ( LIC ).

selfTest.q: 2. Why was the hotel not protected in Olley?
selfTest.a: The notice was in the bedroom, seen after the contract was made at the reception desk.

selfTest.q: 3. Why was the sender bound in Bharathi Knitting?
selfTest.a: He signed the consignment note containing the US$100 limit.

selfTest.q: 4. Under which section did the Supreme Court strike down Rule 9(i) in Brojo Nath Ganguly?
selfTest.a: Section 23, as opposed to public policy.

selfTest.q: 5. Which Commissions can declare an unfair contract term null and void under the CPA 2019?
selfTest.a: The State Commission (Section 49(2)) and the National Commission (Section 59(2)).

selfTest.q: 6. Which section of the IT Act makes click-wrap contracts valid?
selfTest.a: Section 10A.

Question Answer for Priya
Was the clause brought to her notice before or at the time of the contract? Only if the bill was given when she left the saree and the clause was reasonably drawn to her attention (Parker; Olley)

సెక్షన్ 23: ప్రజా విధానానికి విరుద్ధమైన లక్ష్యం ఉన్న ఒప్పందం (లేదా నిబంధన) శూన్యం . standard form లోని అన్యాయమైన నిబంధనను కొట్టివేయడానికి సుప్రీంకోర్టు దీన్ని ఉపయోగించింది ( Brojo Nath Ganguly ). సెక్షన్ 28: ఒక పక్షం కోర్టుకు వెళ్లకుండా పూర్తిగా అడ్డుకునే, లేదా దావా వేసే గడువును తగ్గించే నిబంధన ఆ మేరకు శూన్యం . సెక్షన్ మినహాయింపుల కింద మధ్యవర్తిత్వ (arbitration) నిబంధనలు చెల్లుతాయి. సెక్షన్ 10A, IT చట్టం: ప్రతిపాదన, అంగీకారం ఎలక్ట్రానిక్‌గా (ఉదా: "I agree" క్లిక్ చేయడం) జరిగాయన్న కారణం ఒక్కటే కాంట్రాక్టును చెల్లనిదిగా చేయదు. సెక్షన్ 2(46), CPA 2019: unfair contract అంటే వ్యాపారి లేదా సేవలు అందించేవారికి, వినియోగదారుడికి మధ్య, వినియోగదారుడి హక్కులను గణనీయంగా మార్చే నిబంధనలు ఉన్న కాంట్రాక్టు; ఉదా: అతిగా ఉన్న డిపాజిట్లు, అసమాన జరిమానాలు, ఏకపక్ష రద్దు. సెక్షన్లు 49(2), 59(2), CPA 2019: రాష్ట్ర కమిషన్ , జాతీయ కమిషన్ అన్యాయమైన నిబంధనను శూన్యం, చెల్లనిది గా ప్రకటించవచ్చు. Unfair contract స్వీకరించారన్న ఫిర్యాదు సెక్షన్ 2(6)(i) కింద "complaint"; అలాంటి ఫిర్యాదులు రాష్ట్ర కమిషన్‌కు (ప్రతిఫలం ₹10 కోట్ల వరకు, సెక్షన్ 47(1)(a)(ii)) లేదా జాతీయ కమిషన్‌కు (₹10 కోట్లకు పైగా, సెక్షన్ 58(1)(a)(ii)) వెళ్తాయి.
te.meaning:
Standard form contract అంటే

Standard form contract అంటే:

నిబంధనలను ఒక పక్షం ముందుగానే రాస్తుంది, సాధారణంగా ముద్రణలో లేదా స్క్రీన్‌పై; ప్రతి కస్టమర్‌కూ అవే నిబంధనలు ఇస్తారు; అవతలి పక్షానికి నిజంగా బేరం ఆడే అవకాశం ఉండదు ; ఫారం మొత్తాన్ని అంగీకరించాలి, లేదా వస్తువులు, సేవలు లేకుండా ఉండాలి.

LIC of India v. Consumer Education & Research Centre (1995) లో సుప్రీంకోర్టు ఈ స్థితిని ఇలా వివరించింది: "In dotted line contracts there would be no occasion for a weaker party to bargain or to assume to have equal bargaining power. He has either to accept or leave the services or goods in terms of the dotted line contract."

ఇతర పేర్లు

Contract of adhesion: "In USA, the standard forms of contracts are called 'Contracts of Adhesion'" ( LIC ). బలహీన పక్షం అవతలి వారు నిర్ణయించిన నిబంధనలకు కేవలం "అంటుకుని" ఉంటాడు. Dotted line contract: కస్టమర్ "చుక్కల గీతపై" సంతకం మాత్రమే చేస్తాడు ( Brojo Nath Ganguly ; Pioneer ). ఈ-కాంట్రాక్టులు: ఆన్‌లైన్ standard forms. Click-wrap కాంట్రాక్టులో నిబంధనలు చూపించిన తర్వాత వినియోగదారు "I agree" క్లిక్ చేస్తాడు; browse-wrap కాంట్రాక్టులో నిబంధనలు ఒక లింక్‌లో మాత్రమే ఉంటాయి, సైట్ వాడితే వాటిని అంగీకరించినట్టే అని సైట్ చెబుతుంది; shrink-wrap కాంట్రాక్టులో సాఫ్ట్‌వేర్ వంటి ఉత్పత్తి ప్యాకేజీ లోపల నిబంధనలు ఉంటాయి.

ఎందుకు వాడతారు, ప్రమాదం ఏమిటి

ప్రయోజనాలు ప్రమాదాలు ఒకే రకమైన వేలాది కాంట్రాక్టులు చేసేటప్పుడు సమయం ఆదా (రైల్వే, బీమా, బ్యాంకులు) కస్టమర్ సాధారణంగా చిన్న అక్షరాలు చదవడు అందరికీ అవే నిబంధనలు; నిర్వహణ సులభం రాసినవారు తమ బాధ్యతను తగ్గించే exemption clauses చొప్పించవచ్చు ప్రతి లావాదేవీ ఖర్చు తక్కువ అసమాన బేరసార శక్తి: "తీసుకో లేదా వదిలేయ్"

మన ఉదాహరణ

ప్రియ ₹12,000 విలువైన పట్టు చీరను శుభ్రం చేయడానికి Sparkle Dry Cleaners కు ఇచ్చింది. ఆమె ₹300 చెల్లించి ముద్రిత బిల్లు తీసుకుంది. వెనక వైపు చిన్న అక్షరాల్లో: "Liability for loss or damage is limited to 10 times the cleaning charge." చీర పోయింది. ఆ నిబంధన ప్రకారం Sparkle ₹3,000 (10 × ₹300) మాత్రమే చెల్లిస్తుంది, ప్రియ ₹9,000 (₹12,000 − ₹3,000) నష్టపోతుంది. ఆ నిబంధన ఆమెను కట్టుబడి చేస్తుందో లేదో కింద పరీక్షిస్తాం.

selfTest.q: 1. "Contract of adhesion" అంటే ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: Standard form contract కు అమెరికన్ పేరు; అవతలి వారు నిర్ణయించిన నిబంధనలకు బలహీన పక్షం కేవలం అంటుకుని ఉంటాడు ( LIC ).

selfTest.q: 2. Olley లో హోటల్‌కు రక్షణ ఎందుకు దొరకలేదు?
selfTest.a: నోటీసు పడకగదిలో ఉంది, రిసెప్షన్ వద్ద కాంట్రాక్టు జరిగిన తర్వాత కనిపించింది.

selfTest.q: 3. Bharathi Knitting లో పంపినవారు ఎందుకు కట్టుబడ్డారు?
selfTest.a: US$100 పరిమితి ఉన్న కన్సైన్‌మెంట్ నోట్‌పై సంతకం చేశారు.

selfTest.q: 4. Brojo Nath Ganguly లో Rule 9(i) ని సుప్రీంకోర్టు ఏ సెక్షన్ కింద కొట్టివేసింది?
selfTest.a: సెక్షన్ 23, ప్రజా విధానానికి విరుద్ధంగా.

selfTest.q: 5. CPA 2019 కింద అన్యాయమైన కాంట్రాక్టు నిబంధనను ఏ కమిషన్లు శూన్యంగా ప్రకటించవచ్చు?
selfTest.a: రాష్ట్ర కమిషన్ (సెక్షన్ 49(2)), జాతీయ కమిషన్ (సెక్షన్ 59(2)).

selfTest.q: 6. IT చట్టంలోని ఏ సెక్షన్ click-wrap కాంట్రాక్టులను చెల్లేలా చేస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: సెక్షన్ 10A.

A standard form contract is best described as:

Explanation. A standard form contract (contract of adhesion) is pre-drafted by one party, usually with greater bargaining power, and offered without real room for negotiation.

In L'Estrange v. Graucob, the court held that a person who signs a contractual document:

Explanation. Signature is treated as conclusive proof of assent to a document's terms, whether or not the signatory actually read it, absent fraud or misrepresentation.

Central Inland Water Transport Corp. v. Brojo Nath Ganguly held that unconscionable standard form terms are void under:

Explanation. The Supreme Court held such terms void under Section 23 as against public policy, especially where bargaining power is grossly unequal.

en.meaning:
The doctrine of privity of contract means:

Explanation. Privity of contract means only the actual parties to an agreement have standing to sue or be sued on it — a stranger generally cannot enforce it.

In Dunlop Pneumatic Tyre Co. v. Selfridge & Co., Dunlop could not sue Selfridge because:

Explanation. Only a party can sue on a contract, and no consideration moved from Dunlop to Selfridge. All the Lords relied on the lack of consideration, and Lord Haldane also relied on privity.

Which of these is NOT a recognised exception to privity of contract in India?

Explanation. Inadequate consideration is unrelated to privity exceptions. The recognised exceptions include trusts/beneficiaries, family arrangements, agency, assignment, and acknowledgment/estoppel.

law-of-contract-i-u2-t1.subtitle: Sections 10, 11 and 12 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: Capacity means the legal power to bind yourself by a contract. Section 10 says an agreement is a contract only if it is made by "parties competent to contract". Section 11 says who is competent. A person must pass three tests : He is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject. He is of sound mind (tested under Section 12). He is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject. Capacity is about legal status , not intelligence or a fair price. A clever 17-year-old lacks it. An ordinary adult has it. If a party lacks capacity, there is no contract at all. The Privy Council held in Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose (1903) that a minor 's agreement is void , not merely voidable . In exams, the three tests, the Section 12 test of sound mind with its two rules and illustrations, and the reasons given in Mohori Bibee earn the marks. In real life, capacity decides whether a shop can sue a teenager for the price of a phone, or a buyer can keep land bought from a seriously ill seller.
legalProvision: Section 10. What agreements are contracts. All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not hereby expressly declared to be void. Nothing herein contained shall affect any law in force in India and not hereby expressly repealed by which any contract is required to be made in writing or in the presence of witnesses, or any law relating to the registration of documents.

Section 11. Who are competent to contract. Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject.

Section 12. What is a sound mind for the purposes of contracting. A person is said to be of sound mind for the purpose of making a contract, if, at the time when he makes it, he is capable of understanding it and of forming a rational judgment as to its effect upon his interests. A person who is usually of unsound mind, but occasionally of sound mind, may make a contract when he is of sound mind. A person who is usually of sound mind, but occasionally of unsound mind, may not make a contract when he is of unsound mind. Illustration (a): A patient in a lunatic asylum, who is at intervals of sound mind, may contract during those intervals. Illustration (b): A sane man, who is delirious from fever or who is so drunk that he cannot understand the terms of a contract, or form a rational judgment as to its effect on his interests, cannot contract whilst such delirium or drunkenness lasts.
Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, Section 4(a). "minor" means a person who has not completed the age of eighteen years;

Indian Majority Act, 1875, Section 3 (as the bare Act note to Section 11 points to it): every person domiciled in India attains majority on completing the age of eighteen years . Older versions of Section 3 fixed twenty-one years for a minor for whom a court had appointed a guardian, or whose property was under a Court of Wards, before he turned eighteen. Mohori Bibee (1895 facts) was decided under that 21-year rule. See the verification report on whether the 21-year rule is still in force.
In simple words

Section 10: capacity is one of the conditions of every contract . No capacity, no contract. Section 11: three tests. Old enough, sound mind, and no legal bar. Section 12: "sound mind" is tested at the time of the contract . Can the person (1) understand the contract, and (2) judge how it affects his interests? A person who is usually unsound may contract in a clear interval. A person who is usually sound may not contract while he is delirious or very drunk. Majority: the general age is 18 .
en.meaning:
Capacity to contract (also called competence) is the legal ability of a person to make a contract that binds him. A person who has it is "competent to contract".

The law asks about the person, not the bargain. A very fair price does not cure a missing capacity. And a foolish bargain made by a competent adult is still a contract.

Who is not competent. Section 11 gives three groups:

Minors – persons below the age of majority. Persons of unsound mind – at the time of contracting (Section 12). Persons disqualified by law – adults of sound mind who are barred by a particular law (for example, an alien enemy in some situations).

"According to the law to which he is subject." Section 11 does not fix an age itself. It takes the age from the law that governs the person. For persons domiciled in India, the Indian Majority Act, 1875 fixes it. The bare Act places a note under Section 11: "See the Indian Majority Act, 1875 (9 of 1875)."

Why the law has this rule.

To protect the weak. A child or a person who cannot understand a deal could easily be exploited. To give certainty. A fixed age and a clear test let the other side know where it stands before it deals. Because a contract rests on consent. Only a person who can understand and judge can truly agree.

Capacity and free consent are different. Capacity asks who the person is. Free consent asks how his agreement was obtained ( coercion , fraud and so on). A competent adult who is cheated has capacity, but his consent is not free.
keyPoints: Section 10 makes "parties competent to contract" a condition of every contract. Section 11 has three tests: age of majority, sound mind, no disqualification by law. The general age of majority in India is 18. Section 12: sound mind = ability to understand the contract and judge its effect on one's interests, at the time of making it. Usually unsound but sometimes sound: may contract in a lucid interval. Usually sound but sometimes unsound: may not contract while unsound. Capacity is a legal status; a fair price does not cure its absence. A minor's agreement is void ( Mohori Bibee ), and coming of age does not cure it ( Suraj Narain Dube ). Necessaries: the supplier is reimbursed from the incapable person's property only (Section 68). A Hindu natural guardian cannot bind the minor by a personal covenant and needs court permission to sell the minor's immovable property (HMGA Section 8).

caseLaws.name: Mohori Bibee v
caseLaws.facts: Dharmodas Ghose (1903) Facts. On 20 July 1895 Dharmodas Ghose, still an infant, mortgaged his houses to a money lender, Brahmo Dutt, to secure Rs. 20,000. The lender's attorney had received a written notice from the infant's mother, his court-appointed guardian, that he was under 21. The infant sued to have the mortgage declared void. Principle. "The Act makes it essential that all contracting parties should be 'competent to contract,'" and a person incompetent by reason of infancy "cannot make a contract within the meaning of the Act". The mortgage was void; Sections 64 and 65 did not apply. Privy Council, 4 March 1903, (1903) LR 30 IA 114 : ILR 30 Cal 539. Why it matters. It is the leading authority that capacity is an essential of a contract and that a minor's agreement is void, not voidable. Suraj Narain Dube v. Sukhu Aheer (1928) Facts. Sukhu, a minor, executed a bond for Rs. 40 on 24 June 1919. After attaining majority, on 17 June 1923, he and his mother executed a fresh bond for Rs. 76 (Rs. 40 plus Rs. 36 interest) for the old loan. Principle. Following Mohori Bibee , the majority of the Full Bench said: "it is now settled law that a contract by a minor is not only voidable, but is altogether void." The new promise had no fresh consideration and was not enforceable. Allahabad High Court (Full Bench), AIR 1928 All 440. Why it matters. It shows that capacity is tested on the date of the original agreement; coming of age later does not cure it.

selfTest.q: 2. What is the test of sound mind in Section 12?
selfTest.a: Whether, at the time of making the contract, the person can understand it and form a rational judgment as to its effect upon his interests.

selfTest.q: 3. A patient in a mental hospital signs a sale deed during a clear interval and fully understands it. Is it valid?
selfTest.a: Yes. A person usually of unsound mind may contract when of sound mind (Section 12, Illustration (a)).

selfTest.q: 4. A buyer aged 17 promises to pay ₹70,000 in instalments. Can the seller sue him for the balance?
selfTest.a: No. He is a minor, so the agreement is void ( Mohori Bibee ).

selfTest.q: 5. Is a person of unsound mind personally liable for necessaries supplied to him?
selfTest.a: No. The supplier is reimbursed from his property (Section 68).

selfTest.q: 6. Does a Hindu natural guardian need court permission to sell the minor's land?
selfTest.a: Yes, previous permission of the court is needed (HMGA Section 8(2)(a)); a sale without it is voidable at the minor's instance (Section 8(3)).

legalProvision: Section 10. What agreements are contracts. All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not hereby expressly declared to be void. Nothing herein contained shall affect any law in force in India and not hereby expressly repealed by which any contract is required to be made in writing or in the presence of witnesses, or any law relating to the registration of documents.

Section 11. Who are competent to contract. Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject.

Section 12. What is a sound mind for the purposes of contracting. A person is said to be of sound mind for the purpose of making a contract, if, at the time when he makes it, he is capable of understanding it and of forming a rational judgment as to its effect upon his interests. A person who is usually of unsound mind, but occasionally of sound mind, may make a contract when he is of sound mind. A person who is usually of sound mind, but occasionally of unsound mind, may not make a contract when he is of unsound mind. Illustration (a): A patient in a lunatic asylum, who is at intervals of sound mind, may contract during those intervals. Illustration (b): A sane man, who is delirious from fever or who is so drunk that he cannot understand the terms of a contract, or form a rational judgment as to its effect on his interests, cannot contract whilst such delirium or drunkenness lasts.
Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, Section 4(a). "minor" means a person who has not completed the age of eighteen years;

Indian Majority Act, 1875, సెక్షన్ 3 (సెక్షన్ 11 కింద బేర్ యాక్ట్ నోట్ దీన్నే సూచిస్తుంది): భారతదేశంలో నివాసం (domicile) ఉన్న ప్రతి వ్యక్తి 18 సంవత్సరాలు పూర్తి చేసినప్పుడు మేజర్ అవుతాడు. పాత సెక్షన్ 3 ప్రకారం, 18 ఏళ్లు నిండకముందే కోర్టు గార్డియన్‌ను నియమించిన మైనర్‌కు, లేదా ఆస్తి Court of Wards చేతిలో ఉన్న మైనర్‌కు మేజర్ వయస్సు 21 సంవత్సరాలు . Mohori Bibee (1895 నాటి వాస్తవాలు) ఆ 21 ఏళ్ల నియమం కిందే నిర్ణయించబడింది. ఈ 21 ఏళ్ల నియమం ఇప్పటికీ అమల్లో ఉందా అనేది verification report లో చూడండి.
సులభమైన మాటల్లో

సెక్షన్ 10: ప్రతి కాంట్రాక్టుకు capacity ఒక షరతు. Capacity లేకపోతే కాంట్రాక్టు లేదు. సెక్షన్ 11: మూడు పరీక్షలు. తగిన వయస్సు, స్థిరమైన మనస్సు, చట్టపరమైన అడ్డంకి లేకపోవడం. సెక్షన్ 12: "sound mind" ను కాంట్రాక్టు చేసే సమయంలోనే పరీక్షిస్తారు. ఆ వ్యక్తి (1) కాంట్రాక్టును అర్థం చేసుకోగలడా, (2) అది తన ప్రయోజనాలపై ఎలా ప్రభావం చూపుతుందో తీర్మానించగలడా? సాధారణంగా మనస్సు స్థిరంగా లేని వ్యక్తి స్పష్టమైన విరామంలో కాంట్రాక్టు చేయవచ్చు. సాధారణంగా స్థిరంగా ఉన్న వ్యక్తి జ్వర భ్రాంతిలో గానీ బాగా తాగిన స్థితిలో గానీ ఉన్నప్పుడు కాంట్రాక్టు చేయలేడు. మేజర్ వయస్సు: సాధారణ వయస్సు 18 .
te.meaning:
కాంట్రాక్టు సామర్థ్యం (competence అని కూడా అంటారు) అంటే తనను బంధించే కాంట్రాక్టు చేసే చట్టపరమైన శక్తి. అది ఉన్న వ్యక్తి "competent to contract ".

చట్టం వ్యక్తి గురించి అడుగుతుంది, బేరం గురించి కాదు. చాలా న్యాయమైన ధర ఉన్నా, లేని capacity రాదు. సమర్థుడైన పెద్దవాడు చేసిన తెలివి తక్కువ బేరం కూడా కాంట్రాక్టే.

ఎవరు సమర్థులు కారు. సెక్షన్ 11 మూడు వర్గాలను చూపుతుంది:

మైనర్లు – మేజర్ వయస్సు రానివారు. మనస్సు స్థిరంగా లేనివారు – కాంట్రాక్టు చేసే సమయంలో (సెక్షన్ 12). చట్టం అనర్హులుగా చేసినవారు – మనస్సు స్థిరంగా ఉన్న పెద్దవారే, కానీ ఒక ప్రత్యేక చట్టం అడ్డుకుంటుంది (ఉదా: కొన్ని పరిస్థితుల్లో శత్రు దేశ పౌరుడు).

"According to the law to which he is subject." సెక్షన్ 11 స్వయంగా వయస్సును నిర్ణయించదు. ఆ వ్యక్తికి వర్తించే చట్టం నుంచి తీసుకుంటుంది. భారతదేశంలో నివాసం ఉన్నవారికి Indian Majority Act, 1875 దాన్ని నిర్ణయిస్తుంది. బేర్ యాక్ట్ సెక్షన్ 11 కింద ఈ నోట్ ఉంది: "See the Indian Majority Act, 1875 (9 of 1875)."

చట్టం ఈ నియమం ఎందుకు పెట్టింది.

బలహీనులను రక్షించడానికి. పిల్లవాడిని గానీ, బేరాన్ని అర్థం చేసుకోలేని వ్యక్తిని గానీ సులభంగా మోసం చేయవచ్చు. నిశ్చితత కోసం. స్థిరమైన వయస్సు, స్పష్టమైన పరీక్ష ఉంటే, బేరం చేసే ముందే అవతలి పక్షానికి తన స్థానం తెలుస్తుంది. కాంట్రాక్టు సమ్మతిపై ఆధారపడుతుంది కాబట్టి. అర్థం చేసుకుని, తీర్మానించగలిగిన వ్యక్తి మాత్రమే నిజంగా అంగీకరించగలడు.

Capacity, free consent వేర్వేరు. Capacity ఆ వ్యక్తి ఎవరు అని అడుగుతుంది. Free consent అతని అంగీకారం ఎలా పొందారని అడుగుతుంది (బలవంతం, మోసం మొదలైనవి). మోసపోయిన సమర్థుడైన పెద్దవాడికి capacity ఉంటుంది, కానీ అతని సమ్మతి స్వేచ్ఛాయుతం కాదు.

selfTest.q: 2. సెక్షన్ 12 లో స్థిరమైన మనస్సుకు పరీక్ష ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: కాంట్రాక్టు చేసే సమయంలో ఆ వ్యక్తి దాన్ని అర్థం చేసుకుని, తన ప్రయోజనాలపై దాని ప్రభావం గురించి హేతుబద్ధమైన తీర్మానం చేయగలడా అనేది.

selfTest.q: 3. మానసిక ఆసుపత్రిలోని రోగి స్పష్టమైన విరామంలో, పూర్తిగా అర్థం చేసుకుని అమ్మకం దస్తావేజుపై సంతకం చేస్తాడు. అది చెల్లుతుందా?
selfTest.a: చెల్లుతుంది. సాధారణంగా మనస్సు స్థిరంగా లేని వ్యక్తి స్థిరంగా ఉన్నప్పుడు కాంట్రాక్టు చేయవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 12, దృష్టాంతం (a)).

selfTest.q: 4. 17 ఏళ్ల కొనుగోలుదారు ₹70,000 వాయిదాల్లో చెల్లిస్తానని వాగ్దానం చేస్తాడు. బకాయి కోసం అమ్మినవాడు దావా వేయగలడా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. అతను మైనర్, కాబట్టి ఒప్పందం void ( Mohori Bibee ).

selfTest.q: 5. మనస్సు స్థిరంగా లేని వ్యక్తికి సరఫరా చేసిన necessaries కోసం అతను వ్యక్తిగతంగా బాధ్యుడా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. సరఫరాదారుకు అతని ఆస్తి నుంచి చెల్లిస్తారు (సెక్షన్ 68).

selfTest.q: 6. మైనర్ భూమి అమ్మడానికి హిందూ సహజ గార్డియన్‌కు కోర్టు అనుమతి కావాలా?
selfTest.a: కావాలి, కోర్టు ముందస్తు అనుమతి అవసరం (HMGA సెక్షన్ 8(2)(a)); అది లేకుండా చేసిన అమ్మకం మైనర్ కోరితే voidable (సెక్షన్ 8(3)).

law-of-contract-i-u2-t2.subtitle: Sections 10, 11, 68 and 183 to 184 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872; section 33 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963

en.inOneMinute: A minor 's agreement is void from the very beginning ( void ab initio ). It is not merely voidable . The minor cannot be sued on it, cannot be made to pay damages for breaking it, and cannot make it valid later by ratification . The Privy Council settled this in Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose (1903). The law still softens the rule in a few places: A supplier of necessaries is paid from the minor's property (Section 68). A minor may receive a benefit , for example as a mortgagee who has paid the money. A court may ask a minor to give back a benefit he still holds (Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 33(2)(b)). A guardian may, within his powers and for the minor's benefit, make a contract that binds the minor. In exams, this is a favourite problem question. Marks come from Mohori Bibee , the "no ratification, no estoppel" points, restitution, necessaries, and the minor as beneficiary , partner and agent. In real life, it tells a lender or a shop what it can and cannot recover after dealing with someone under 18.
legalProvision: Section 2(g). An agreement not enforceable by law is said to be void;

Section 10 (first paragraph). All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not hereby expressly declared to be void.

Section 11. Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject.

Section 68. Claim for necessaries supplied to person incapable of contracting, or on his account. If a person, incapable of entering into a contract, or any one whom he is legally bound to support, is supplied by another person with necessaries suited to his condition in life, the person who has furnished such supplies is entitled to be reimbursed from the property of such incapable person.

Section 184. Who may be an agent. As between the principal and third persons, any person may become an agent, but no person who is not of the age of majority and of sound mind can become an agent, so as to be responsible to his principal according to the provisions in that behalf herein contained.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 33(2). Where a defendant successfully resists any suit on the ground— … (b) that the agreement sought to be enforced against him in the suit is void by reason of his not having been competent to contract under section 11 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (9 of 1872), the court may, if the defendant has received any benefit under the agreement from the other party, require him to restore, so far as may be, such benefit to that party, to the extent to which he or his estate has benefited thereby.

Indian Partnership Act, 1932, Section 30(1). A person who is a minor according to the law to which he is subject may not be a partner in a firm, but, with the consent of all the partners for the time being, he may be admitted to the benefits of partnership.
In simple words

Sections 2(g), 10, 11: a minor is not "competent to contract ", so his agreement is not a contract. It is an agreement not enforceable by law, that is, void. Section 68: a person who supplies necessaries to a minor is repaid out of the minor's property , not by the minor personally. Section 184: a minor can act as an agent for others, but he cannot be made answerable to his principal. Specific Relief Act, Section 33(2)(b): if a minor wins a suit because his agreement is void, the court may make him give back the benefit he received, but only to the extent he or his estate is still better off. Partnership Act, Section 30: a minor cannot be a partner, but can be admitted to the benefits of a partnership.
en.meaning:
A minor's agreement is an agreement in which one of the parties had not completed the age of majority (generally 18) on the date it was made. The Act does not say "void" in so many words. The Privy Council reached that result in Mohori Bibee by reading Sections 2, 10 and 11 together, and by looking at Sections 68, 183, 184, 64 and 65 (see Diagram 1 ). Diagram 1. The Privy Council read the Act's sections together and concluded that a minor's agreement is void, not voidable. flowchart TD A["Section 11
A minor is not competent to contract"] B["Section 10
Only agreements of parties competent
to contract are contracts"] C["Section 2(g)
An agreement not enforceable by law is void"] D["Sections 68, 183, 184
The Act treats a minor as unable to bind himself"] E["Sections 64, 65
Assume a contract between competent parties
so they do not apply"] R["RESULT: minor's agreement is VOID AB INITIO
(Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose, 1903)"] F["No estoppel where the truth is known
No order to repay the money"] A --> B B --> C C --> R D --> R E --> R R --> F Text description Section 11: a minor is not competent to contract. Section 10: only agreements by competent parties are contracts. Section 2(g): an agreement not enforceable by law is void. Sections 68, 183 and 184 show the Act treats minors as unable to bind themselves. Sections 64 and 65 assume a contract between competent parties, so they do not apply. Result: a minor's agreement is void ab initio; no estoppel where the truth is known; no order to repay. Void ab initio means void from the start. The agreement never was a contract. Nobody needs to cancel it, and nobody can make it good later. Why the law takes this strict view. To protect minors. A young person may not understand a bargain and may be easily exploited. Making every agreement void is the strongest protection. Because it follows from the Act. Section 10 requires "parties competent to contract". If one party is not competent, there is no contract to call voidable. To keep the rule simple. Lenders and sellers are told plainly: deal with a minor at your own risk. What is "the effect"? The topic asks what follows from this voidness. The answer has many parts: no suit on the agreement, no ratification, no estoppel , limited restitution , necessaries, benefits to the minor, guardian's contracts, sureties, and the minor as partner, agent and shareholder. Each is explained below.
keyPoints: A minor's agreement is void ab initio ( Mohori Bibee , 1903). It cannot be ratified on attaining majority; a fresh agreement with fresh consideration is needed ( Suraj Narain Dube ). A false statement of age does not estop the minor ( Mohori Bibee ; Ajudhia Prasad ). Sections 64 and 65 do not apply; restitution only under Specific Relief Act Section 33, and only to the extent of benefit. Necessaries: reimbursed from the minor's property, never a personal liability (Section 68). A minor can take a benefit, for example as a mortgagee who has paid in full ( Raghava Chariar ). A minor can be an agent but is not responsible to his principal (Section 184). A minor can only be admitted to the benefits of a partnership (Partnership Act Section 30). A guardian's contract binds the minor if within the guardian's competence and for the minor's benefit ( Srikakulam ). On a surety for a minor's debt, give both views ( Edavan ; Kashiba ).

caseLaws.name: Mohori Bibee v
caseLaws.facts: Dharmodas Ghose (1903) Facts. An infant mortgaged his houses on 20 July 1895 to a money lender for Rs. 20,000. The lender's attorney had received written notice of the minority from the infant's court-appointed guardian. The infant sued to cancel the mortgage; the lender asked that at least the money advanced be repaid. Principle. An infant is not competent to contract, so his agreement is void. There was no estoppel because the lender knew the truth, and Sections 64 and 65 did not apply; no repayment was ordered. (1903) LR 30 IA 114 : ILR 30 Cal 539 (Privy Council). Why it matters. It decided that a minor's agreement is void, not voidable, and is the starting point of every answer on this topic. Suraj Narain Dube v. Sukhu Aheer (1928) Facts. Sukhu borrowed Rs. 40 on a bond while a minor (1919). After majority (1923), he and his mother executed a new bond for Rs. 76, being the old Rs. 40 with interest. Principle. A minor's agreement "is altogether void", and the earlier advance in minority is not consideration for a fresh promise after majority. AIR 1928 All 440 (Full Bench, majority). Why it matters. It shows that a minor's agreement cannot be ratified on attaining majority. Ajudhia Prasad v. Chandan Lal (1937) Facts. Two persons over 18 but under 21, who had a certificated guardian, executed a mortgage in 1925. Their minority was concealed. The lower court found fraud and decreed the money. Principle. "neither Section 64 nor Section 65 deals with a case where a party is incompetent to enter into a contract at all"; no personal money decree can be passed against a minor, and estoppel cannot be pleaded against the statute. AIR 1937 All 610 (Full Bench). Why it matters. Even a minor who deceives the other side cannot be made to pay under the void agreement. Srikakulam Subrahmanyam v. Kurra Subba Rao (1948) Facts. A Hindu widow, as guardian of her minor son, agreed in writing in 1935 to sell family land for Rs. 17,200 to pay off the dead father's debts. The buyers paid off a Rs. 1,200 mortgage debt and were put in possession, but no sale deed was executed or registered. The minor later sued for possession. Principle. A contract by a guardian binds the minor if it is within the guardian's competence and for the minor's benefit; here the minor was the "transferor" and was barred by Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act. (1948) 50 Bom LR 646 (Privy Council). Why it matters. It marks the line between a minor's own void agreement and a valid contract made on his behalf by his guardian. Edavan Kavingal Kelappan Nambiar v. Moolakal Kunhi Raman (1956) Facts. A minor took money in a kuri (chit) transaction, and a surety guaranteed the instalments. The suit failed against the minor, but the trial court decreed against the surety. Principle. "the liability of the surety is only ancillary and can rest only on a valid obligation on the part of the party"; the surety was not liable. AIR 1957 Mad 164. Why it matters. It answers whether a surety for a minor's void debt can be sued, and explains Kashiba as a case of indemnity.

selfTest.q: 1. Is a minor's agreement void or voidable?
selfTest.a: Void ab initio ( Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose , 1903).

selfTest.q: 2. A minor borrows ₹50,000 and on turning 18 writes "I confirm this loan". Is he now liable?
selfTest.a: No. A void agreement cannot be ratified. A fresh agreement with fresh consideration is needed ( Suraj Narain Dube ).

selfTest.q: 3. A minor lies that he is 21 and gets a loan. Can the lender use estoppel to stop him pleading minority?
selfTest.a: No. Estoppel does not take away the protection of minority ( Mohori Bibee ; Ajudhia Prasad ).

selfTest.q: 4. What can a court order a minor to give back?
selfTest.a: Under Specific Relief Act Section 33(2)(b), the benefit he received, only to the extent he or his estate has benefited.

selfTest.q: 5. Is a minor personally liable for necessaries?
selfTest.a: No. The supplier is reimbursed from the minor's property (Section 68).

selfTest.q: 6. Can a minor enforce a mortgage in his favour after he has paid the whole mortgage money?
selfTest.a: Yes ( Raghava Chariar v. Srinivasa Raghava Chariar , 1916).

Question Answer Authority
Is a minor's agreement void or voidable? Void ab initio Mohori Bibee (1903)
Can he ratify it at 18? No; a fresh agreement with fresh consideration is needed Suraj Narain Dube (1928)
Is he estopped by a false statement of age? No Mohori Bibee; Ajudhia Prasad (1937); BSA Section 121
Must he repay under Sections 64 or 65? No Mohori Bibee; Ajudhia Prasad
Can the court order him to restore a benefit? Yes, in its discretion, to the extent he is still benefited Specific Relief Act Section 33
Necessaries? Supplier paid from his property, not by him personally Section 68
Can he take a benefit? Yes, where he has performed fully Raghava Chariar (1916)
Can he be an agent? Yes, but not responsible to his principal Section 184
Guardian's contract? Binds him if within the guardian's competence and for his benefit Srikakulam (1948); Mir Sarwarjan (1911); HMGA Section 8
Surety for his debt? Views differ; indemnity is enforceable Edavan (1956); Kashiba (1894)
Partner? Only admitted to the benefits Partnership Act Section 30

Point Minor's agreement Voidable contract (e.g. coercion, fraud)
Status Void from the start; no contract A contract that stands until the wronged party avoids it
Who acts Nobody needs to cancel it The wronged party chooses
Ratification Not possible The wronged party may affirm it
Restoring benefits Not under Sections 64 or 65; only Specific Relief Act Section 33 The party who avoids it restores benefits (Section 64)
Leading case Mohori Bibee Sections 19, 19A

సెక్షన్లు 2(g), 10, 11: మైనర్ "competent to contract " కాదు, కాబట్టి అతని ఒప్పందం కాంట్రాక్టు కాదు. అది చట్టం అమలు చేయించని ఒప్పందం, అంటే void. సెక్షన్ 68: మైనర్‌కు necessaries సరఫరా చేసినవారికి మైనర్ ఆస్తి నుంచి చెల్లిస్తారు, మైనర్ వ్యక్తిగతంగా కాదు. సెక్షన్ 184: మైనర్ ఇతరుల తరఫున ఏజెంటుగా పని చేయవచ్చు, కానీ తన ప్రిన్సిపల్‌కు అతన్ని బాధ్యుడిని చేయలేం. Specific Relief Act, సెక్షన్ 33(2)(b): ఒప్పందం void కాబట్టి మైనర్ దావాలో గెలిస్తే, తాను పొందిన ప్రయోజనాన్ని తిరిగి ఇవ్వమని కోర్టు ఆదేశించవచ్చు , కానీ అతను లేదా అతని ఆస్తి ఇంకా ఎంత లాభపడి ఉందో ఆ మేరకు మాత్రమే. Partnership Act, సెక్షన్ 30: మైనర్ భాగస్వామి కాలేడు, కానీ భాగస్వామ్యపు ప్రయోజనాలకు చేర్చుకోవచ్చు .

మైనర్ ఒప్పందం అంటే ఒప్పందం చేసిన తేదీకి ఒక పక్షం మేజర్ వయస్సు (సాధారణంగా 18) పూర్తి చేయని ఒప్పందం. చట్టం "void" అని నేరుగా చెప్పదు. సెక్షన్లు 2, 10, 11 కలిపి చదివి, సెక్షన్లు 68, 183, 184, 64, 65 ను పరిశీలించి Mohori Bibee లో ప్రివీ కౌన్సిల్ ఆ ఫలితానికి వచ్చింది ( Diagram 1 చూడండి). Diagram 1. చట్టంలోని సెక్షన్లను కలిపి చదివి, మైనర్ ఒప్పందం voidable కాదు, void అని ప్రివీ కౌన్సిల్ తేల్చింది. flowchart TD A["సెక్షన్ 11
మైనర్ కాంట్రాక్టు చేయడానికి సమర్థుడు కాదు"] B["సెక్షన్ 10
సమర్థులైన పక్షాల ఒప్పందాలే కాంట్రాక్టులు"] C["సెక్షన్ 2(g)
చట్టం అమలు చేయించని ఒప్పందం void"] D["సెక్షన్లు 68, 183, 184
మైనర్ తనను తాను బంధించుకోలేడని చట్టం చూపుతుంది"] E["సెక్షన్లు 64, 65
సమర్థుల మధ్య కాంట్రాక్టును ఊహిస్తాయి
కాబట్టి వర్తించవు"] R["ఫలితం: మైనర్ ఒప్పందం మొదటి నుంచే VOID
(Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose, 1903)"] F["నిజం తెలిసినప్పుడు estoppel లేదు
డబ్బు తిరిగి ఇవ్వమని ఆదేశం లేదు"] A --> B B --> C C --> R D --> R E --> R R --> F వచన వివరణ సెక్షన్ 11: మైనర్ సమర్థుడు కాదు. సెక్షన్ 10: సమర్థుల ఒప్పందాలే కాంట్రాక్టులు. సెక్షన్ 2(g): చట్టం అమలు చేయించని ఒప్పందం void. సెక్షన్లు 68, 183, 184 మైనర్ తనను బంధించుకోలేడని చూపుతాయి. సెక్షన్లు 64, 65 వర్తించవు. ఫలితం: మైనర్ ఒప్పందం మొదటి నుంచే void. Void ab initio అంటే మొదటి నుంచే చెల్లనిది. ఆ ఒప్పందం ఎప్పుడూ కాంట్రాక్టు కాదు. దాన్ని ఎవరూ రద్దు చేయాల్సిన అవసరం లేదు, తర్వాత ఎవరూ దాన్ని సరిచేయలేరు. చట్టం ఇంత కఠినంగా ఎందుకు ఉంది. మైనర్లను రక్షించడానికి. చిన్న వయస్సు వ్యక్తి బేరాన్ని అర్థం చేసుకోలేకపోవచ్చు, సులభంగా మోసపోవచ్చు. ప్రతి ఒప్పందాన్ని void చేయడమే బలమైన రక్షణ. చట్టం నుంచే ఇది వస్తుంది కాబట్టి. సెక్షన్ 10 "parties competent to contract" ను కోరుతుంది. ఒక పక్షం సమర్థుడు కాకపోతే, voidable అని పిలవడానికి కాంట్రాక్టే లేదు. నియమం సరళంగా ఉండటానికి. అప్పిచ్చేవారికి, అమ్మేవారికి స్పష్టంగా చెబుతుంది: మైనర్‌తో వ్యవహరిస్తే రిస్కు మీదే. "ప్రభావం" అంటే ఏమిటి? ఈ void స్వభావం నుంచి ఏం జరుగుతుందని ఈ అంశం అడుగుతుంది. సమాధానంలో చాలా భాగాలు ఉన్నాయి: ఒప్పందంపై దావా లేదు, ratification లేదు, estoppel లేదు, పరిమిత restitution , necessaries, మైనర్‌కు ప్రయోజనాలు, గార్డియన్ కాంట్రాక్టులు, జామీనుదారులు, భాగస్వామిగా, ఏజెంటుగా, షేర్‌హోల్డర్‌గా మైనర్. ప్రతి దాన్నీ కింద వివరిస్తాం.

selfTest.q: 1. మైనర్ ఒప్పందం void యా voidable యా?
selfTest.a: Void ab initio ( Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose , 1903).

selfTest.q: 2. ఒక మైనర్ ₹50,000 అప్పు తీసుకుని, 18 నిండాక "ఈ అప్పును ధృవీకరిస్తున్నాను" అని రాస్తాడు. ఇప్పుడు బాధ్యుడా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. Void ఒప్పందాన్ని ratify చేయలేం. కొత్త ప్రతిఫలంతో కొత్త ఒప్పందం కావాలి ( Suraj Narain Dube ).

selfTest.q: 3. తనకు 21 ఏళ్లని అబద్ధం చెప్పి మైనర్ అప్పు తీసుకుంటాడు. మైనారిటీ వాదించకుండా అప్పిచ్చినవాడు estoppel ఉపయోగించగలడా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. Estoppel మైనారిటీ రక్షణను తీసివేయదు ( Mohori Bibee ; Ajudhia Prasad ).

selfTest.q: 4. మైనర్‌ను కోర్టు ఏం తిరిగి ఇవ్వమని ఆదేశించగలదు?
selfTest.a: Specific Relief Act సెక్షన్ 33(2)(b) కింద, అతను పొందిన ప్రయోజనాన్ని, అతను లేదా అతని ఆస్తి లాభపడిన మేరకు మాత్రమే.

selfTest.q: 5. Necessaries కోసం మైనర్ వ్యక్తిగతంగా బాధ్యుడా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. సరఫరాదారుకు మైనర్ ఆస్తి నుంచి చెల్లిస్తారు (సెక్షన్ 68).

selfTest.q: 6. తనఖా డబ్బు మొత్తం ఇచ్చిన తర్వాత, తన పేరున ఉన్న తనఖాను మైనర్ అమలు చేయించగలడా?
selfTest.a: అవును ( Raghava Chariar v. Srinivasa Raghava Chariar , 1916).

law-of-contract-i-u2-t5.subtitle: Sections 15, 19 and 72 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: Coercion is forcing a person to agree by: committing, or threatening to commit, an act forbidden by the Indian Penal Code (now read with the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023), or unlawfully detaining, or threatening to detain, any property , "to the prejudice of any person whatever", with the intention of causing any person to enter into an agreement (Section 15). Three things make Section 15 wide: the threat alone is enough; the act need not be carried out; the coercer may be anyone , even a stranger to the contract; the person harmed may be anyone , not only the person who signs. Effect. A contract caused by coercion is voidable at the option of the party coerced (Section 19). Money paid or goods delivered under coercion must be repaid or returned (Section 72). Coercion is a regular short-answer and problem question. In real life it covers threats of violence, and a creditor or pawnbroker who keeps someone's goods until they sign something new.
legalProvision: Section 15. "Coercion" defined. "Coercion" is the committing, or threatening to commit, any act forbidden by the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) or the unlawful detaining, or threatening to detain, any property, to the prejudice of any person whatever, with the intention of causing any person to enter into an agreement. Explanation. —It is immaterial whether the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) is or is not in force in the place where the coercion is employed. Illustration A, on board an English ship on the high seas, causes B to enter into an agreement by an act amounting to criminal intimidation under the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860). A afterwards sues B for breach of contract at Calcutta. A has employed coercion, although his act is not an offence by the law of England, and although section 506 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) was not in force at the time when or place where the act was done.

Section 19 (first paragraph). When consent to an agreement is caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.

Section 72. A person to whom money has been paid, or anything delivered, by mistake or under coercion, must repay or return it. Illustration (b). A railway company refuses to deliver up certain goods to the consignee, except upon the payment of an illegal charge for carriage. The consignee pays the sum charged in order to obtain the goods. He is entitled to recover so much of the charge as was illegally excessive.
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Section 358(1). The Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) is hereby repealed.

General Clauses Act, 1897, Section 8(1). Where this Act, or any Central Act or Regulation made after the commencement of this Act, repeals and re-enacts, with or without modification, any provision of a former enactment, then references in any other enactment or in any instrument to the provision so repealed shall, unless a different intention appears, be construed as references to the provision so re-enacted.
In simple words

Section 15: coercion = a crime (done or threatened) or unlawful holding of property (done or threatened) + aimed at making someone agree. Anyone may use it, and anyone may be harmed by it. Explanation: the place does not matter. The act is judged by the Indian criminal code even if that code does not apply where it was done. Section 19: the coerced party may choose to avoid the contract . Section 72: money or goods given under coercion must be returned. BNS Section 358 and General Clauses Act Section 8(1): the Indian Penal Code has been repealed and re-enacted as the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. The words "Indian Penal Code" in Section 15 are still in the Act, but by Section 8(1) they are read as references to the matching provisions of the Sanhita, unless a different intention appears.
en.meaning:
Coercion is pressure that the criminal law or the law of property forbids, used to make a person agree.

The elements of Section 15.

Element What it means 1. Committing or threatening to commit an act forbidden by the Indian Penal Code (now the BNS) Hurt, wrongful confinement, criminal intimidation, mischief to property, and so on. A threat is enough or unlawfully detaining, or threatening to detain, any property Keeping someone's goods with no legal right to keep them 2. To the prejudice of any person whatever Someone must be harmed or threatened with harm. It may be the person who signs, a relative, a stranger, or even the coercer himself ( Chikkam Ammiraju ) 3. With the intention of causing any person to enter into an agreement The act must be aimed at getting an agreement. A threat made for some other reason is not coercion 4. Causation (Section 14) Consent must have been caused by it: it "would not have been given but for" the coercion

Why the law treats it this way. Consent obtained through fear is not a real choice. But the coerced party may still want the bargain, so the law lets him choose (voidable), instead of making the contract void.

Coercion and duress. English law uses the word duress . Duress in its classic form is narrower: it is actual or threatened violence or unlawful constraint to the person, usually by a party to the contract or someone acting for him. Section 15 is wider: it covers threats to property, threats by strangers and threats to anyone.
keyPoints: Coercion is committing or threatening an act forbidden by the IPC (now read with the BNS), or unlawfully detaining or threatening to detain property, to make any person agree. The coercer may be a stranger; the prejudice may be to any person. The place where it is used does not matter (Explanation). The contract is voidable at the coerced party's option (Section 19). Money paid or goods delivered under coercion must be returned (Section 72). Chikkam Ammiraju : threat of suicide is coercion (majority). Undue influence needs a dominating relationship; coercion does not.

caseLaws.name: Chikkam Ammiraju v
caseLaws.facts: Chikkam Seshamma (1917) Facts. A husband threatened to commit suicide unless his wife and son executed a release deed, giving up their reversionary rights in certain lands, in favour of his younger brothers. They signed and later sued to set it aside. Principle. A threat of suicide is a threat of an act "forbidden by the Indian Penal Code" (Section 15), and it does not matter who made the threat or to whose prejudice it was made; held by majority (Wallis CJ and Seshagiri Aiyar J, Oldfield J dissenting). (1917) 32 MLJ 494 : 34 IC 578 (Madras High Court). Why it matters. It shows how wide Section 15 is: the coercer may be a stranger to the contract and the prejudice may fall on anyone.

selfTest.q: 1. What are the two kinds of coercion in Section 15?
selfTest.a: Committing or threatening to commit an act forbidden by the Indian Penal Code, and unlawfully detaining or threatening to detain property.

selfTest.q: 2. Can a stranger to the contract commit coercion?
selfTest.a: Yes. Section 15 does not say who must use it, and Chikkam Ammiraju held that it does not matter who made the threat.

selfTest.q: 3. What is the effect of coercion on a contract?
selfTest.a: The contract is voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused (Section 19).

selfTest.q: 4. A creditor says "pay the ₹20,000 you owe or I will file a civil suit". Is this coercion?
selfTest.a: No. Filing a civil suit for a debt actually due is not an act forbidden by the criminal law.

selfTest.q: 5. Does it matter that the threat was made on a foreign ship?
selfTest.a: No. The Explanation makes the place immaterial.

selfTest.q: 6. Which law now contains the offence of criminal intimidation?
selfTest.a: Section 351 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (earlier Sections 503 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code).

legalProvision: Section 15. "Coercion" defined. "Coercion" is the committing, or threatening to commit, any act forbidden by the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) or the unlawful detaining, or threatening to detain, any property, to the prejudice of any person whatever, with the intention of causing any person to enter into an agreement. Explanation. —It is immaterial whether the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) is or is not in force in the place where the coercion is employed. Illustration A, on board an English ship on the high seas, causes B to enter into an agreement by an act amounting to criminal intimidation under the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860). A afterwards sues B for breach of contract at Calcutta. A has employed coercion, although his act is not an offence by the law of England, and although section 506 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) was not in force at the time when or place where the act was done.

Section 19 (first paragraph). When consent to an agreement is caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.

Section 72. A person to whom money has been paid, or anything delivered, by mistake or under coercion, must repay or return it. Illustration (b). A railway company refuses to deliver up certain goods to the consignee, except upon the payment of an illegal charge for carriage. The consignee pays the sum charged in order to obtain the goods. He is entitled to recover so much of the charge as was illegally excessive.
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Section 358(1). The Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) is hereby repealed.

General Clauses Act, 1897, Section 8(1). Where this Act, or any Central Act or Regulation made after the commencement of this Act, repeals and re-enacts, with or without modification, any provision of a former enactment, then references in any other enactment or in any instrument to the provision so repealed shall, unless a different intention appears, be construed as references to the provision so re-enacted.

సెక్షన్ 15: బలవంతం = నేరం (చేసినా, బెదిరించినా) లేదా ఆస్తిని చట్టవిరుద్ధంగా నిర్బంధించడం (చేసినా, బెదిరించినా) + ఎవరినైనా ఒప్పుకునేలా చేయాలనే లక్ష్యం. ఎవరైనా వాడవచ్చు, ఎవరైనా నష్టపోవచ్చు. Explanation: చోటు ముఖ్యం కాదు. ఆ చోట భారత నేర చట్టం వర్తించకపోయినా, చర్యను దాని ప్రకారమే చూస్తారు. సెక్షన్ 19: బలవంతానికి గురైన పక్షం కాంట్రాక్టును రద్దు చేయాలని ఎంచుకోవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 72: బలవంతంతో ఇచ్చిన డబ్బు లేదా వస్తువులు తిరిగి ఇవ్వాలి. BNS సెక్షన్ 358, General Clauses Act సెక్షన్ 8(1): భారత శిక్షా స్మృతిని రద్దు చేసి భారతీయ న్యాయ సంహిత, 2023 గా తిరిగి చట్టం చేశారు. సెక్షన్ 15 లో "Indian Penal Code" అనే మాటలు ఇంకా ఉన్నాయి, కానీ సెక్షన్ 8(1) ప్రకారం, వేరే ఉద్దేశం కనిపించకపోతే, వాటిని సంహితలోని సంబంధిత నిబంధనలకు సూచనలుగా చదువుతారు.
te.meaning:
బలవంతం అంటే ఒకరిని ఒప్పుకునేలా చేయడానికి నేర చట్టం లేదా ఆస్తి చట్టం నిషేధించిన ఒత్తిడి వాడడం.

సెక్షన్ 15 లోని అంశాలు.

అంశం అర్థం 1. భారత శిక్షా స్మృతి (ఇప్పుడు BNS) నిషేధించిన చర్యను చేయడం లేదా బెదిరించడం గాయపరచడం, అక్రమ నిర్బంధం, నేరపూరిత బెదిరింపు, ఆస్తికి నష్టం మొదలైనవి. బెదిరింపు సరిపోతుంది లేదా ఏదైనా ఆస్తిని చట్టవిరుద్ధంగా నిర్బంధించడం లేదా బెదిరించడం ఉంచుకునే చట్టపరమైన హక్కు లేకుండా ఒకరి వస్తువులను ఉంచుకోవడం 2. ఎవరికైనా నష్టం కలిగేలా (to the prejudice of any person whatever) ఎవరో ఒకరికి నష్టం కలగాలి లేదా బెదిరింపు ఉండాలి. సంతకం చేసేవాడు, బంధువు, అపరిచితుడు, బలవంతం చేసేవాడు స్వయంగా కూడా కావచ్చు ( Chikkam Ammiraju ) 3. ఎవరినైనా ఒప్పందంలోకి దించే ఉద్దేశంతో చర్య ఒప్పందం పొందడం లక్ష్యంగా ఉండాలి. వేరే కారణంతో చేసిన బెదిరింపు బలవంతం కాదు 4. కారణత్వం (సెక్షన్ 14) సమ్మతి దాని వల్లే కలిగి ఉండాలి: అది "లేకపోతే ఇచ్చేవాడు కాదు"

చట్టం ఇలా ఎందుకు చూస్తుంది. భయంతో పొందిన సమ్మతి నిజమైన ఎంపిక కాదు. కానీ బలవంతానికి గురైన పక్షం ఇంకా ఆ బేరాన్ని కోరుకోవచ్చు; కాబట్టి కాంట్రాక్టును void చేయకుండా, ఎంచుకునే అధికారం అతనికే ఇస్తుంది (voidable).

బలవంతం, duress. ఇంగ్లీష్ చట్టం duress అనే మాట వాడుతుంది. సంప్రదాయ రూపంలో duress సన్నమైనది: వ్యక్తిపై వాస్తవ లేదా బెదిరించిన హింస లేదా అక్రమ నిర్బంధం, సాధారణంగా కాంట్రాక్టు పక్షం లేదా అతని తరఫున ఎవరైనా చేసేది. సెక్షన్ 15 విస్తృతమైనది: ఆస్తిపై బెదిరింపులు, అపరిచితుల బెదిరింపులు, ఎవరికైనా బెదిరింపులు – అన్నీ కవర్ చేస్తుంది.

selfTest.q: 1. సెక్షన్ 15 లోని రెండు రకాల బలవంతం ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: భారత శిక్షా స్మృతి నిషేధించిన చర్యను చేయడం లేదా బెదిరించడం; ఆస్తిని చట్టవిరుద్ధంగా నిర్బంధించడం లేదా బెదిరించడం.

selfTest.q: 2. కాంట్రాక్టుకు సంబంధం లేని వ్యక్తి బలవంతం చేయగలడా?
selfTest.a: అవును. ఎవరు వాడాలో సెక్షన్ 15 చెప్పదు; బెదిరింపు ఎవరు చేశారన్నది ముఖ్యం కాదని Chikkam Ammiraju తీర్పు చెప్పింది.

selfTest.q: 3. బలవంతం కాంట్రాక్టుపై చూపే ప్రభావం ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: ఎవరి సమ్మతి అలా కలిగిందో ఆ పక్షం ఇష్టం మేరకు కాంట్రాక్టు voidable (సెక్షన్ 19).

selfTest.q: 4. "నువ్వు బాకీ ఉన్న ₹20,000 కట్టు, లేకపోతే సివిల్ దావా వేస్తాను" అని ఒక అప్పిచ్చినవాడు అంటాడు. ఇది బలవంతమా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. నిజంగా బాకీ ఉన్న అప్పు కోసం సివిల్ దావా వేయడం నేర చట్టం నిషేధించిన చర్య కాదు.

selfTest.q: 5. బెదిరింపు విదేశీ ఓడలో జరిగిందన్నది ముఖ్యమా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. Explanation చోటును అప్రస్తుతం చేస్తుంది.

selfTest.q: 6. నేరపూరిత బెదిరింపు నేరం ఇప్పుడు ఏ చట్టంలో ఉంది?
selfTest.a: భారతీయ న్యాయ సంహిత, 2023 సెక్షన్ 351 (ఇంతకు ముందు భారత శిక్షా స్మృతి సెక్షన్లు 503, 506).

law-of-contract-i-u2-t3.subtitle: Sections 11, 12, 68, 183 and 184 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: Section 11 says that, besides being a major, a person must be of sound mind and not disqualified by law to be competent to contract. Insane persons. The Act does not use the word "insane". It uses "sound mind" and "unsound mind". Section 12 gives a working test , not a medical label: at the time of making the contract, can the person understand it and form a rational judgment about its effect on his interests? A person who is usually of unsound mind may contract in a lucid interval . A person who is usually of sound mind may not contract while he is delirious from fever or so drunk that he cannot understand. An agreement made while of unsound mind is void . Suppliers of necessaries are paid from his property (Section 68). Persons disqualified by law. Some adults of sound mind are still limited by a particular law: an alien enemy , a foreign State, ruler or ambassador (cannot be sued without the Central Government's consent), an insolvent (cannot deal with property that has vested in the receiver ), and others. Each limit comes from its own law and has its own extent. Exams ask for the Section 12 test, the two rules on intervals, the effect of unsoundness and the list of disqualified persons. In real life these rules decide whether a buyer can enforce a deal with a very ill seller, or whether a shop can sue an embassy.
legalProvision: Section 11. Who are competent to contract. Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject.

Section 12. What is a sound mind for the purposes of contracting. A person is said to be of sound mind for the purpose of making a contract, if, at the time when he makes it, he is capable of understanding it and of forming a rational judgment as to its effect upon his interests. A person who is usually of unsound mind, but occasionally of sound mind, may make a contract when he is of sound mind. A person who is usually of sound mind, but occasionally of unsound mind, may not make a contract when he is of unsound mind. Illustrations (a) A patient in a lunatic asylum, who is at intervals of sound mind, may contract during those intervals. (b) A sane man, who is delirious from fever or who is so drunk that he cannot understand the terms of a contract, or form a rational judgment as to its effect on his interests, cannot contract whilst such delirium or drunkenness lasts.

Section 68. Claim for necessaries supplied to person incapable of contracting, or on his account. If a person, incapable of entering into a contract, or any one whom he is legally bound to support, is supplied by another person with necessaries suited to his condition in life, the person who has furnished such supplies is entitled to be reimbursed from the property of such incapable person. Illustrations (a) A supplies B, a lunatic, with necessaries suitable to his condition in life. A is entitled to be reimbursed from B's property. (b) A supplies the wife and children of B, a lunatic, with necessaries suitable to their condition in life. A is entitled to be reimbursed from B's property.
Section 183. Who may employ agent. Any person who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, may employ an agent.

Section 184. Who may be an agent. As between the principal and third persons, any person may become an agent, but no person who is not of the age of majority and of sound mind can become an agent, so as to be responsible to his principal according to the provisions in that behalf herein contained.

Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Section 83. When aliens may sue. Alien enemies residing in India with the permission of the Central Government, and alien friends, may sue in any Court otherwise competent to try the suit, as if they were citizens of India, but alien enemies residing in India without such permission, or residing in a foreign country, shall not sue in any such Court. Explanation. Every person residing in a foreign country, the Government of which is at war with India and carrying on business in that country without a licence in that behalf granted by the Central Government, shall, for the purpose of this section, be deemed to be an alien enemy residing in a foreign country.

Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Section 86(1). No foreign State may be sued in any Court otherwise competent to try the suit except with the consent of the Central Government certified in writing by a Secretary to that Government: Provided that a person may, as a tenant of immovable property, sue without such consent as aforesaid a foreign State from whom he holds or claims to hold the property.
In simple words

Section 11: sound mind and freedom from legal disqualification are two of the three tests of capacity. Section 12: the test is understanding plus rational judgment, at the time of contracting . Paragraphs 2 and 3 apply it to people whose state of mind changes. Section 68: a person who supplies necessaries to a person of unsound mind, or to his wife and children, is paid from his property . Sections 183 and 184: a person of unsound mind cannot employ an agent, and cannot be an agent who is answerable to his principal. CPC Section 83: an alien enemy living abroad, or living in India without the Central Government's permission, cannot sue in Indian courts. CPC Section 86: a foreign State (and, under Section 86(4), a foreign ruler, ambassador, envoy, High Commissioner and notified staff) cannot be sued without the Central Government's written consent, except by its tenant.
en.meaning:
Person of unsound mind. A person who, at the time of making a contract , is not capable of understanding it or not capable of forming a rational judgment about its effect on his interests (Section 12). The Act's older words "lunatic" and "lunatic asylum" appear only in the illustrations.

The test has two limbs. Both must be present:

Understanding: can he grasp what the contract is, what he gives and what he gets? Rational judgment: can he weigh whether it is good or bad for him?

A person who can read the words but cannot judge whether selling his house for a third of its value harms him fails the second limb.

Three kinds of unsoundness under Section 12.

Kind Example Rule Usually unsound, at times sound A patient with clear periods between episodes May contract during a clear (lucid) interval (paragraph 2; Illustration (a)) Usually sound, at times unsound A healthy man in high fever, or dead drunk May not contract while that state lasts (paragraph 3; Illustration (b)) Unsound all the time A person who never developed the ability to understand (the older word is "idiot") Can never pass the Section 12 test

Person disqualified by law. An adult of sound mind whom a particular law prevents from contracting, or limits in contracting, suing or being sued. The words "by any law to which he is subject" in Section 11 point to that other law. The Contract Act itself lists no disqualified persons.

Why the law does this.

Unsound mind: consent means a real choice. A person who cannot understand or judge cannot really agree. The law protects him from being exploited. Disqualification: some limits protect the State (alien enemies in war), respect other countries (foreign States and envoys), or protect creditors (insolvents).
keyPoints: Section 12 tests understanding and rational judgment at the time of contracting . A usually unsound person may contract in a lucid interval; a usually sound person may not while delirious or very drunk. An adult is presumed to be of sound mind; the person alleging unsoundness must prove it. An agreement made while of unsound mind is void; the court may order restoration of a benefit still held (Specific Relief Act Section 33(2)(b)). Necessaries are paid from the incapable person's property (Section 68), not by him personally. A person of unsound mind cannot employ an agent and is not responsible as an agent (Sections 183, 184). Disqualified persons are adults of sound mind limited by a particular law: alien enemy (CPC Section 83), foreign State and envoys (CPC Section 86), insolvent.

caseLaws.name: Mohori Bibee v
caseLaws.facts: Dharmodas Ghose (1903) Facts. A minor mortgaged his houses to a moneylender for Rs. 20,000. The lender's attorney had notice that he was a minor. The minor sued to set the mortgage aside. Principle. A person who is not competent under Section 11 cannot make a contract, so his agreement is void; the Privy Council relied on Sections 10, 11, 68, 183 and 184. (1903) LR 30 IA 114 : ILR 30 Cal 539 (Privy Council). Why it matters. Section 11 treats unsound mind in the same way as minority, so this reasoning is used to hold that an agreement made while of unsound mind is void, not voidable. Indar Singh v. Parmeshwardhari Singh (1957) Facts. In April 1944 a young man sold his properties to the plaintiffs for Rs. 7,000 by a registered sale deed. His mother said he was a congenital idiot who could not understand transactions, and that the properties were worth Rs. 25,000. The buyers sued for a declaration of title. Principle. The test is whether the person was "capable of understanding the business and of forming a rational judgment as to its effect upon his interest"; the seller was not, so the sale deed was void and gave the buyers no title. AIR 1957 Pat 491 (Patna High Court). Why it matters. It applies the Section 12 test to a real sale of land and shows that an agreement by a person of unsound mind is void.

selfTest.q: 1. What is the test of sound mind in Section 12?
selfTest.a: Whether, at the time of making the contract, the person can understand it and form a rational judgment about its effect on his interests.

selfTest.q: 2. Can a person who is usually of unsound mind ever contract?
selfTest.a: Yes, during an interval when he is of sound mind (Section 12, paragraph 2; Illustration (a)).

selfTest.q: 3. Ravi signs a contract after two drinks but understands it fully. Is he bound?
selfTest.a: Yes. Only drunkenness so deep that he cannot understand the terms or judge their effect removes capacity (Illustration (b)).

selfTest.q: 4. Who pays for medicines supplied to a person of unsound mind and his children?
selfTest.a: His property; he is not personally liable (Section 68, Illustration (b)).

selfTest.q: 5. Can a shop sue a foreign embassy for unpaid goods?
selfTest.a: Only with the Central Government's consent certified in writing by a Secretary (CPC Section 86).

selfTest.q: 6. Can an undischarged insolvent sell a house that has vested in the official receiver?
selfTest.a: No. The property is no longer his to deal with.

సెక్షన్ 11: స్థిరమైన మనస్సు, చట్టపరమైన అనర్హత లేకపోవడం – ఇవి సామర్థ్యానికి ఉన్న మూడు పరీక్షల్లో రెండు. సెక్షన్ 12: పరీక్ష ఏమిటంటే అర్థం చేసుకోవడం, హేతుబద్ధమైన తీర్మానం – కాంట్రాక్టు చేసే సమయంలో . మనస్థితి మారుతూ ఉండేవారికి 2, 3 పేరాలు దీన్ని వర్తింపజేస్తాయి. సెక్షన్ 68: మతిస్థిమితం లేని వ్యక్తికి గానీ, అతని భార్యా పిల్లలకు గానీ necessaries సరఫరా చేసినవారికి అతని ఆస్తి నుంచి చెల్లిస్తారు. సెక్షన్లు 183, 184: మతిస్థిమితం లేని వ్యక్తి ఏజెంటును నియమించలేడు; ప్రిన్సిపల్‌కు జవాబుదారీ అయ్యే ఏజెంటు కాలేడు. CPC సెక్షన్ 83: విదేశంలో నివసించే, లేదా కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వ అనుమతి లేకుండా భారతదేశంలో నివసించే శత్రు దేశీయుడు భారత కోర్టుల్లో దావా వేయలేడు. CPC సెక్షన్ 86: విదేశీ రాజ్యంపై (సెక్షన్ 86(4) ప్రకారం విదేశీ పాలకుడు, రాయబారి, దూత, హైకమిషనర్, ప్రకటించిన సిబ్బందిపై కూడా) కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వ రాతపూర్వక అనుమతి లేకుండా దావా వేయలేం; దాని కౌలుదారుకు మాత్రం మినహాయింపు.
te.meaning:
మతిస్థిమితం లేని వ్యక్తి (person of unsound mind). కాంట్రాక్టు చేసే సమయంలో దాన్ని అర్థం చేసుకోలేని , లేదా తన ప్రయోజనాలపై దాని ప్రభావం గురించి హేతుబద్ధంగా తీర్మానించలేని వ్యక్తి (సెక్షన్ 12). చట్టంలోని పాత మాటలు "lunatic", "lunatic asylum" దృష్టాంతాల్లో మాత్రమే కనిపిస్తాయి.

పరీక్షకు రెండు భాగాలు. రెండూ ఉండాలి:

అర్థం చేసుకోవడం: కాంట్రాక్టు ఏమిటో, తాను ఏం ఇస్తున్నాడో, ఏం పొందుతున్నాడో గ్రహించగలడా? హేతుబద్ధమైన తీర్మానం: అది తనకు మంచిదా చెడ్డదా అని తూకం వేయగలడా?

మాటలు చదవగలిగినా, తన ఇంటిని విలువలో మూడో వంతుకు అమ్మడం తనకు నష్టమని తీర్మానించలేని వ్యక్తి రెండో భాగంలో విఫలమవుతాడు.

సెక్షన్ 12 కింద మూడు రకాలు.

రకం ఉదాహరణ నియమం సాధారణంగా మనస్సు స్థిరంగా లేదు, అప్పుడప్పుడు స్థిరం ఎపిసోడ్‌ల మధ్య స్పష్టమైన కాలాలు ఉన్న రోగి స్పష్టమైన విరామ సమయంలో (lucid interval) కాంట్రాక్టు చేయవచ్చు (పేరా 2; దృష్టాంతం (a)) సాధారణంగా మనస్సు స్థిరం, అప్పుడప్పుడు కాదు తీవ్ర జ్వరంలో ఉన్న ఆరోగ్యవంతుడు, లేదా పూర్తిగా తాగి ఉన్నవాడు ఆ స్థితి ఉన్నంతసేపు కాంట్రాక్టు చేయలేడు (పేరా 3; దృష్టాంతం (b)) ఎప్పుడూ మనస్సు స్థిరంగా లేదు అర్థం చేసుకునే శక్తి ఎప్పుడూ ఏర్పడని వ్యక్తి (పాత మాట "idiot") సెక్షన్ 12 పరీక్షలో ఎప్పుడూ నెగ్గలేడు

చట్టం అనర్హుడిగా చేసిన వ్యక్తి. మనస్సు స్థిరంగా ఉన్న పెద్దవాడు, కానీ ఒక ప్రత్యేక చట్టం అతన్ని కాంట్రాక్టు చేయకుండా, దావా వేయకుండా లేదా దావాకు గురి కాకుండా ఆపుతుంది లేదా పరిమితం చేస్తుంది. సెక్షన్ 11 లోని "by any law to which he is subject" అనే మాటలు ఆ ఇతర చట్టాన్ని సూచిస్తాయి. కాంట్రాక్టు చట్టం స్వయంగా అనర్హుల జాబితా ఇవ్వదు.

చట్టం ఇలా ఎందుకు చేస్తుంది.

మతిస్థిమితం లేకపోవడం: సమ్మతి అంటే నిజమైన ఎంపిక. అర్థం చేసుకోలేని, తీర్మానించలేని వ్యక్తి నిజంగా ఒప్పుకోలేడు. అతను దోపిడీకి గురికాకుండా చట్టం కాపాడుతుంది. అనర్హత: కొన్ని పరిమితులు దేశాన్ని కాపాడతాయి (యుద్ధంలో శత్రు దేశీయులు), కొన్ని ఇతర దేశాలను గౌరవిస్తాయి (విదేశీ రాజ్యాలు, రాయబారులు), కొన్ని అప్పిచ్చినవారిని కాపాడతాయి (దివాలాదారులు).

selfTest.q: 1. సెక్షన్ 12 లో స్థిరమైన మనస్సుకు పరీక్ష ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: కాంట్రాక్టు చేసే సమయంలో ఆ వ్యక్తి దాన్ని అర్థం చేసుకుని, తన ప్రయోజనాలపై దాని ప్రభావం గురించి హేతుబద్ధంగా తీర్మానించగలడా అనేది.

selfTest.q: 2. సాధారణంగా మనస్సు స్థిరంగా లేని వ్యక్తి ఎప్పుడైనా కాంట్రాక్టు చేయగలడా?
selfTest.a: అవును, మనస్సు స్థిరంగా ఉన్న విరామ సమయంలో (సెక్షన్ 12, పేరా 2; దృష్టాంతం (a)).

selfTest.q: 3. రవి రెండు పెగ్గులు తాగి, కాంట్రాక్టును పూర్తిగా అర్థం చేసుకుని సంతకం చేస్తాడు. అతను బద్ధుడా?
selfTest.a: అవును. షరతులు అర్థం చేసుకోలేనంత లేదా ప్రభావం తీర్మానించలేనంత తాగుడే సామర్థ్యాన్ని తీసేస్తుంది (దృష్టాంతం (b)).

selfTest.q: 4. మతిస్థిమితం లేని వ్యక్తికి, అతని పిల్లలకు సరఫరా చేసిన మందులకు ఎవరు చెల్లిస్తారు?
selfTest.a: అతని ఆస్తి; అతను వ్యక్తిగతంగా బాధ్యుడు కాదు (సెక్షన్ 68, దృష్టాంతం (b)).

selfTest.q: 5. చెల్లించని సరుకుల కోసం ఒక షాపు విదేశీ ఎంబసీపై దావా వేయగలదా?
selfTest.a: కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వ కార్యదర్శి రాతపూర్వకంగా ధృవీకరించిన అనుమతితో మాత్రమే (CPC సెక్షన్ 86).

selfTest.q: 6. డిశ్చార్జ్ కాని దివాలాదారు, అధికారిక రిసీవర్‌కు సంక్రమించిన ఇంటిని అమ్మగలడా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. ఆ ఆస్తి ఇక అతనిది కాదు.
