law-of-contract-i-u2-t13.subtitle: Section 29 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: An uncertain agreement is one whose meaning is not certain and cannot be made certain. Section 29 makes such an agreement void . A court cannot enforce a promise when it cannot tell what was promised. The problem is vagueness, not illegality. Nothing wrong is being done; the words simply do not say enough. The key phrase is "capable of being made certain" . If the agreement itself, the nature of the trade, or an agreed method settles the meaning, the agreement stands. In exams this is a short, predictable question built on the Act's six Illustrations. In real life it decides whether a bargain with a missing price, an unclear quantity or two possible figures can be enforced at all.
legalProvision: Section 29. Agreements void for uncertainty. Agreements, the meaning of which is not certain, or capable of being made certain, are void. Illustrations (a) A agrees to sell to B "a hundred tons of oil". There is nothing whatever to show what kind of oil was intended. The agreement is void for uncertainty. (b) A agrees to sell to B one hundred tons of oil of a specified description, known as an article of commerce. There is no uncertainty here to make the agreement void. (c) A, who is a dealer in cocoanut-oil only, agrees to sell to B "one hundred tons of oil". The nature of A's trade affords an indication of the meaning of the words, and A has entered into a contract for the sale of one hundred tons of cocoanut-oil. (d) A agrees to sell to B "all the grain in my granary at Ramnagar". There is no uncertainty here to make the agreement void. (e) A agrees to sell B "one thousand maunds of rice at a price to be fixed by C". As the price is capable of being made certain, there is no uncertainty here to make the agreement void. (f) A agrees to sell to B "my white horse for rupees five hundred or rupees one thousand". There is nothing to show which of the two prices was to be given. The agreement is void.

Sale of Goods Act, 1930, Section 9. Ascertainment of price. (1) The price in a contract of sale may be fixed by the contract or may be left to be fixed in manner thereby agreed or may be determined by the course of dealing between the parties. (2) Where the price is not determined in accordance with the foregoing provisions, the buyer shall pay the seller a reasonable price. What is a reasonable price is a question of fact dependent on the circumstances of each particular case.

Sale of Goods Act, 1930, Section 10. Agreement to sell at valuation. (1) Where there is an agreement to sell goods on the terms that the price is to be fixed by the valuation of a third party and such third party cannot or does not make such valuation, the agreement is thereby avoided: Provided that, if the goods or any part thereof have been delivered to, and appropriated by, the buyer, he shall pay a reasonable price therefor. (2) Where such third party is prevented from making the valuation by the fault of the seller or buyer, the party not in fault may maintain a suit for damages against the party in fault.
In simple words

If the meaning of an agreement is not certain, and nothing can make it certain, the agreement is void. If the meaning can be made certain (by a trade description, the seller's trade, a clear identification, or an agreed method), the agreement is valid. In a sale of goods , a price left open is not fatal: it may be fixed by an agreed method or by the course of dealing, or else a reasonable price is paid.
en.meaning:
The Act does not define "uncertain". Section 29 simply says that an agreement whose meaning is "not certain, or capable of being made certain" is void. An agreement is uncertain when its terms are too vague to give a clear meaning. Section 29 covers two kinds of vagueness alike: Kind What is wrong Illustration A missing or unclear term A term (kind of goods, price, quantity) is not stated and cannot be found (a) "a hundred tons of oil" Two readings with no way to choose The agreement gives alternatives and nothing shows which applies (f) "rupees five hundred or rupees one thousand" The rule rests on a simple point: a court can enforce only what it can identify. The Latin maxim id certum est quod certum reddi potest ("that is certain which can be made certain") states the other side of the rule. A term need not be stated in exact figures, so long as there is a way to fix it. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. Start at the top. The agreement is void only if its meaning is unclear and nothing can make it certain. flowchart TD Q1{"Is the meaning of the agreement

Advance recoverable (s.65)"] Q1 -- "Yes" --> OK1 Q1 -- "No" --> Q2 Q2 -- "Yes" --> OK2 Q2 -- "No" --> V Text description Is the meaning of the agreement clear on its face? If yes, it is not void for uncertainty (Illustrations (b), (d)). If no, can a trade description, the nature of the seller's trade, a clear identification or an agreed method make it certain? If yes, it is not void (Illustrations (c), (e)). If no, the agreement is void for uncertainty (Illustrations (a), (f)); any advance can be recovered under Section 65.
keyPoints: Section 29: an agreement whose meaning is not certain, or capable of being made certain, is void. The agreement stands if a trade description, the seller's trade, a clear identification or an agreed method makes the meaning certain. Illustration (f): two prices with no way to choose make the agreement void. In a sale of goods, a price left open is fixed by the agreed method or course of dealing, or a reasonable price is paid (SoGA Section 9). If a named valuer does not value, the agreement is avoided, but goods taken must be paid for at a reasonable price (SoGA Section 10). Uncertainty is about the words of the agreement. Mistake is about the parties' beliefs. Uncertain agreements are void, not illegal.

caseLaws.name: Mayawanti v
caseLaws.facts: Kaushalya Devi (1990) Facts. By a receipt of 16 September 1971, the defendant agreed to sell a jointly owned factory property in Ludhiana for Rs. 50,000 and took Rs. 5,000 as earnest money. If the co-owner did not sign, she would sell "one of the two shares", otherwise pay back the advance. The buyer sued for specific performance. Principle. "The stipulations and terms of the contract have, therefore, to be certain and the parties must have been consensus ad idem "; with an undefined share at an unstated price, there was no enforceable contract and no specific performance. The High Court's decree for return of the Rs. 5,000 earnest money was upheld. (1990) 3 SCC 1 : [1990] 2 SCR 350. Why it matters. A court will not enforce terms that do not show what was promised; the payer gets back the advance.

selfTest.q: 1. When is an agreement void under Section 29?
selfTest.a: When its meaning is not certain and is not capable of being made certain.

selfTest.q: 2. Is an agreement to sell "one thousand maunds of rice at a price to be fixed by C" void?
selfTest.a: No. The price is capable of being made certain (Illustration (e)).

selfTest.q: 3. What is the effect of an uncertain agreement?
selfTest.a: It is void, and neither party can enforce it. Any advance paid can be recovered under Section 65.

selfTest.q: 4. A agrees to sell B "all the paddy in my barn at Tenali". Is it uncertain?
selfTest.a: No. The goods are clearly identified (compare Illustration (d)).

selfTest.q: 5. The price of goods is to be fixed by Mr. X, who refuses to value. The buyer has already received and used the goods. What must he pay?
selfTest.a: A reasonable price (SoGA Section 10(1), proviso).

selfTest.q: 6. How is uncertainty different from mistake?
selfTest.a: Uncertainty lies in the words of the agreement; mistake lies in the parties' beliefs about facts.

ఒప్పందం అర్థం నిశ్చితంగా లేకపోతే, దాన్ని ఏదీ నిశ్చితం చేయలేకపోతే, ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు. అర్థాన్ని నిశ్చితం చేయగలిగితే (వ్యాపారంలో తెలిసిన వర్ణన, అమ్మేవాడి వ్యాపారం, స్పష్టమైన గుర్తింపు, లేదా అంగీకరించిన పద్ధతి ద్వారా), ఒప్పందం చెల్లుతుంది. వస్తువుల అమ్మకంలో, ధర తెరిచి ఉంచడం ప్రాణాంతకం కాదు: అంగీకరించిన పద్ధతి ద్వారా గానీ, వ్యవహార క్రమం ద్వారా గానీ దాన్ని నిర్ణయించవచ్చు; లేకపోతే సహేతుకమైన ధర చెల్లించాలి.
te.meaning:
చట్టం "uncertain" ను నిర్వచించదు. అర్థం "not certain, or capable of being made certain" అయిన ఒప్పందం చెల్లదని మాత్రమే సెక్షన్ 29 చెబుతుంది. ఒప్పందం నిబంధనలు స్పష్టమైన అర్థం ఇవ్వలేనంత అస్పష్టంగా ఉన్నప్పుడు ఒప్పందం అనిశ్చితం . సెక్షన్ 29 రెండు రకాల అస్పష్టతలను ఒకేలా చూస్తుంది: రకం ఏం తప్పు Illustration లేని లేదా అస్పష్టమైన నిబంధన ఒక నిబంధన (వస్తువు రకం, ధర, పరిమాణం) చెప్పలేదు, కనుక్కోవడానికి వీలు లేదు (a) "a hundred tons of oil" ఎంచుకోలేని రెండు అర్థాలు ఒప్పందం ప్రత్యామ్నాయాలు ఇస్తుంది, ఏది వర్తిస్తుందో ఏదీ చూపదు (f) "rupees five hundred or rupees one thousand" నియమం ఒక సులభమైన విషయంపై ఆధారపడింది: కోర్టు తాను గుర్తించగలిగినదాన్నే అమలు చేయగలదు. id certum est quod certum reddi potest ("నిశ్చితం చేయగలిగినది నిశ్చితమే") అనే లాటిన్ సూత్రం నియమానికి మరో వైపు చెబుతుంది. నిబంధనను ఖచ్చితమైన సంఖ్యల్లో చెప్పనక్కర్లేదు; దాన్ని తేల్చే మార్గం ఉంటే చాలు. selfTest.q: 1. సెక్షన్ 29 కింద ఒప్పందం ఎప్పుడు చెల్లదు?
selfTest.a: దాని అర్థం నిశ్చితం కానప్పుడు, నిశ్చితం చేయడానికి వీలు లేనప్పుడు.

selfTest.q: 2. "one thousand maunds of rice at a price to be fixed by C" అమ్మే ఒప్పందం చెల్లదా?
selfTest.a: చెల్లుతుంది. ధరను నిశ్చితం చేయవచ్చు (Illustration (e)).

selfTest.q: 3. అనిశ్చిత ఒప్పందం ప్రభావం ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: అది చెల్లదు; ఏ పక్షమూ దాన్ని అమలు చేయించలేదు. చెల్లించిన అడ్వాన్స్ సెక్షన్ 65 కింద తిరిగి పొందవచ్చు.

selfTest.q: 4. A "తెనాలిలోని నా గాదెలో ఉన్న వడ్లన్నీ" B కి అమ్మడానికి ఒప్పుకుంటాడు. ఇది అనిశ్చితమా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. వస్తువులు స్పష్టంగా గుర్తించబడ్డాయి (Illustration (d) తో పోల్చండి).

selfTest.q: 5. వస్తువుల ధరను Mr. X నిర్ణయించాలి; అతను విలువ కట్టడానికి నిరాకరిస్తాడు. కొనేవాడు ఇప్పటికే వస్తువులు పొంది వాడుకున్నాడు. అతను ఏం చెల్లించాలి?
selfTest.a: సహేతుకమైన ధర (SoGA సెక్షన్ 10(1), proviso).

selfTest.q: 6. అనిశ్చితత్వం పొరపాటు నుంచి ఎలా వేరు?
selfTest.a: అనిశ్చితత్వం ఒప్పందంలోని మాటల్లో ఉంటుంది; పొరపాటు వాస్తవాల గురించి పక్షాల నమ్మకాల్లో ఉంటుంది.

law-of-contract-i-u2-t10.subtitle: Sections 10, 23 and 24 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: An agreement is a contract only if its consideration and its object are lawful (Section 10). Section 23 says both are lawful unless one of five grounds applies: it is forbidden by law ; if permitted, it would defeat the provisions of any law ; it is fraudulent ; it involves or implies injury to the person or property of another ; the Court regards it as immoral or opposed to public policy . If any ground applies, the consideration or object is unlawful , and the agreement is void . If even part of a single consideration or object is unlawful, the whole agreement is void (Section 24). Void is wider than unlawful. A wager is void (Section 30) but not forbidden by law ( Gherulal Parakh v. Mahadeodas Maiya ). In exams, the five grounds and the Act's illustrations earn the marks. In real life, no court will enforce a deal to break the law.
legalProvision: Section 10. What agreements are contracts. All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not hereby expressly declared to be void.

Section 23. What considerations and objects are lawful, and what not. The consideration or object of an agreement is lawful, unless— it is forbidden by law; or is of such a nature that if permitted, it would defeat the provisions of any law; or is fraudulent; or involves or implies injury to the person or property of another; or the Court regards it as immoral, or opposed to public policy. In each of these cases, the consideration or object of an agreement is said to be unlawful. Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.

Section 24. Agreements void, if considerations and objects unlawful in part. If any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or any one or any part of any one of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful, the agreement is void. Illustration. A promises to superintend, on behalf of B, a legal manufacture of indigo, and an illegal traffic in other articles. B promises to pay to A a salary of 10,000 rupees a year. The agreement is void, the object of A's promise, and the consideration for B's promise, being in part unlawful.

Related sections. Section 2(g): "An agreement not enforceable by law is said to be void." Sections 57 and 58 save the legal part of reciprocal and alternative promises (see Illegal agreements ). Section 65: a person who has received an advantage under an agreement discovered to be void must restore it or make compensation.
In simple words

Section 10: a lawful consideration and a lawful object are two of the essentials of every contract. Section 23: what you promise, and what you aim at, must not break the law, get round the law, cheat, harm someone, or offend morality or public policy . If they do, the agreement is void. Section 24: if even a part of a single bargain is unlawful, the whole bargain fails.
en.meaning:
Object is the purpose the parties set out to achieve by the agreement. Consideration is what each party gives or promises in return . Under Section 2(d) it is an act, an abstinence or a promise, done or made at the promisor's desire by the promisee or any other person. Section 23 treats both alike: if either is unlawful, the agreement is void. How Section 23 is worded. It starts from lawfulness: the consideration or object "is lawful, unless" a listed ground applies. So the party who says an agreement is unlawful must bring it within one of the grounds. The five grounds at a glance. Ground Meaning in short Act's illustration Forbidden by law Punishable or prohibited by a statute or rule made under it (h): dropping a robbery prosecution for money Defeats a law Allowed on its face, but would get round a law (i): defaulter buying back his own estate through a benamidar Fraudulent Aims at or involves a fraud (e): dividing gains made by fraud; (g): agent secretly getting a lease of his principal's land Injury to person or property of another Involves or implies harm to someone (no illustration; see example below) Immoral or opposed to public policy As regarded by the Court (f): paying for a government job; (j): mukhtar selling his influence; (k): letting a daughter for concubinage See Diagram 1 . Would permitting it leave every law intact? Is it free from fraud? Does it avoid injury to the person or property of another? Does the Court regard it as neither immoral nor opposed to public policy? A "No" to any question makes the object or consideration unlawful and the agreement void (Section 23); restore any advantage (Section 65). If all are "Yes", it is lawful; but if any part of a single consideration or object is unlawful, the whole agreement is void (Section 24), subject to Sections 57 and 58.
keyPoints: Section 23 makes the consideration or object lawful unless a listed ground applies. The grounds: forbidden by law, defeating a law, fraud, injury to another, and immorality or public policy. An agreement with an unlawful object or consideration is void. Section 24: an unlawful part of a single bargain makes the whole agreement void. "Forbidden by law" means acts punishable under the penal law or prohibited by special laws. Void is wider than unlawful: a wager is void but not unlawful. Section 65: an advantage received under an agreement discovered to be void must be restored.

caseLaws.name: Gherulal Parakh v
caseLaws.facts: Mahadeodas Maiya (1959) Facts. Two parties formed a partnership to enter into forward contracts for wheat with other firms and share profit and loss equally. The transactions made a loss; one partner paid it and sued the other for half. Principle. A wagering contract is void under Section 30 but not forbidden by law, so an agreement collateral to it (the partnership) is not unlawful under Section 23; "immoral" is confined to settled heads, and public policy is invoked only in clear cases of harm to the public. AIR 1959 SC 781 : [1959] Supp 2 SCR 406. Why it matters. It explains "forbidden by law", "immoral" and "public policy" in Section 23, and shows that void and unlawful are different.

selfTest.q: 1. When is the object or consideration of an agreement unlawful?
selfTest.a: When it is forbidden by law, would defeat a law, or is fraudulent; when it involves or implies injury to another's person or property; or when the Court regards it as immoral or opposed to public policy (Section 23).

selfTest.q: 2. What is the effect of an unlawful object?
selfTest.a: The agreement is void (Section 23).

selfTest.q: 3. What does Section 24 say about an agreement partly unlawful?
selfTest.a: If any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or any part of one of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful, the agreement is void.

selfTest.q: 4. Is a wagering agreement "forbidden by law" under Section 23?
selfTest.a: No. It is void under Section 30 but not forbidden by law ( Gherulal Parakh ).

selfTest.q: 5. A promises B ₹5,000 to withdraw a robbery prosecution that B has started against A's son. Is this lawful?
selfTest.a: No. Like Illustration (h), the object is unlawful and the agreement is void.

selfTest.q: 6. How does a "fraudulent object" differ from fraud under Section 17?
selfTest.a: Under Section 17, fraud is used to obtain consent and the contract is voidable. A fraudulent object means the agreement's purpose is to defraud, and the agreement is void.

సెక్షన్ 10: చట్టబద్ధమైన ప్రతిఫలం, చట్టబద్ధమైన లక్ష్యం ప్రతి కాంట్రాక్టుకూ అవసరమైన రెండు అంశాలు. సెక్షన్ 23: మీరు ఇచ్చే వాగ్దానం, మీరు ఆశించే లక్ష్యం చట్టాన్ని ఉల్లంఘించకూడదు, చట్టాన్ని తప్పించుకోకూడదు, మోసం చేయకూడదు, ఎవరికీ హాని చేయకూడదు, నైతికతను లేదా ప్రజా విధానాన్ని దెబ్బతీయకూడదు. అలా చేస్తే ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు. సెక్షన్ 24: ఒకే బేరంలో ఒక భాగం చట్టవిరుద్ధమైనా, మొత్తం బేరం విఫలమవుతుంది.

లక్ష్యం (object) అంటే ఒప్పందం ద్వారా పక్షాలు సాధించాలనుకునే ఉద్దేశం . ప్రతిఫలం ( consideration ) అంటే ప్రతి పక్షం బదులుగా ఇచ్చేది లేదా వాగ్దానం చేసేది . సెక్షన్ 2(d) ప్రకారం అది వాగ్దానం చేసినవాడి కోరిక మేరకు, వాగ్దానం పొందినవాడు లేదా ఇంకెవరైనా చేసిన చర్య, మానుకోవడం, లేదా వాగ్దానం. సెక్షన్ 23 రెండింటినీ ఒకేలా చూస్తుంది: ఏది చట్టవిరుద్ధమైనా, ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు. సెక్షన్ 23 పదజాలం. అది చట్టబద్ధత నుంచి మొదలవుతుంది: ప్రతిఫలం లేదా లక్ష్యం "is lawful, unless" జాబితాలోని కారణం వర్తిస్తే తప్ప. కాబట్టి ఒప్పందం చట్టవిరుద్ధమని చెప్పే పక్షమే దాన్ని ఏదో ఒక కారణం కిందకు తీసుకురావాలి. ఐదు కారణాలు ఒక్క చూపులో. కారణం క్లుప్తంగా అర్థం చట్టంలోని illustration చట్టం నిషేధించినది చట్టం లేదా దాని కింది నియమం శిక్షించేది లేదా నిషేధించేది (h): డబ్బు కోసం దోపిడీ ప్రాసిక్యూషన్ ఉపసంహరించడం చట్టాన్ని నిష్ఫలం చేసేది పైకి అనుమతించినట్టే ఉన్నా, చట్టాన్ని తప్పించుకునేది (i): బకాయిదారు బినామీ ద్వారా తన ఎస్టేట్ ను తిరిగి కొనడం మోసపూరితమైనది మోసాన్ని లక్ష్యంగా పెట్టుకున్నది లేదా అందులో మోసం ఉన్నది (e): మోసంతో వచ్చిన లాభాలు పంచుకోవడం; (g): ఏజెంట్ రహస్యంగా యజమాని భూమిని లీజుకు ఇప్పించడం ఇంకొకరి శరీరానికి లేదా ఆస్తికి హాని ఎవరికైనా హాని కలిగించేది లేదా సూచించేది (illustration లేదు; కింది ఉదాహరణ చూడండి) అనైతికం లేదా ప్రజా విధానానికి వ్యతిరేకం కోర్టు అలా భావిస్తే (f): ప్రభుత్వ ఉద్యోగం కోసం డబ్బు; (j): ముఖ్తార్ తన ప్రభావాన్ని అమ్ముకోవడం; (k): కూతురిని ఉంపుడుగత్తెగా అద్దెకు ఇవ్వడం Diagram 1 చూడండి. Diagram 1. ఐదు ప్రశ్నలను వరుసగా చూడండి. ఏ దశలో "కాదు" వచ్చినా, లక్ష్యం లేదా ప్రతిఫలం చట్టవిరుద్ధం, ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు. flowchart TD Q1{"1. చట్టం నిషేధించలేదా?"} Q2{"2. అనుమతిస్తే, ప్రతి చట్టం
నిబంధనలూ నిలుస్తాయా?"} Q3{"3. మోసం లేదా?"} Q4{"4. ఇంకొకరి శరీరానికి లేదా
ఆస్తికి హాని లేదా?"} Q5{"5. కోర్టు దాన్ని అనైతికంగా గానీ, ప్రజా
విధానానికి వ్యతిరేకంగా గానీ భావించదా?"} U["చట్టవిరుద్ధం
ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు (సె.23)
ప్రయోజనం తిరిగి ఇవ్వాలి (సె.65)"] L["లక్ష్యం, ప్రతిఫలం చట్టబద్ధం"] P{"ఒకే ప్రతిఫలం లేదా లక్ష్యంలో
ఏదైనా భాగం చట్టవిరుద్ధమా?"} V24["మొత్తం ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు (సె.24)
(వేర్వేరు వాగ్దానాలు: సె.57, 58)"] OK["చట్టబద్ధమైన లక్ష్యం షరతు నెరవేరింది (సె.10)"] Q1 -- "కాదు" --> U Q1 -- "అవును" --> Q2 Q2 -- "కాదు" --> U Q2 -- "అవును" --> Q3 Q3 -- "కాదు" --> U Q3 -- "అవును" --> Q4 Q4 -- "కాదు" --> U Q4 -- "అవును" --> Q5 Q5 -- "కాదు" --> U Q5 -- "అవును" --> L L --> P P -- "అవును" --> V24 P -- "కాదు" --> OK వచన వివరణ చట్టం నిషేధించలేదా? అనుమతిస్తే ప్రతి చట్టమూ నిలుస్తుందా? మోసం లేదా? ఇంకొకరి శరీరానికి, ఆస్తికి హాని లేదా? కోర్టు దాన్ని అనైతికంగా, ప్రజా విధానానికి వ్యతిరేకంగా భావించదా? ఏ ప్రశ్నకు "కాదు" వచ్చినా చట్టవిరుద్ధం, ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు (సె.23); ప్రయోజనం తిరిగి (సె.65). అన్నీ "అవును" అయితే చట్టబద్ధం; కానీ ఒకే బేరంలో ఒక భాగం చట్టవిరుద్ధమైతే మొత్తం చెల్లదు (సె.24), సె.57, 58 కు లోబడి.

selfTest.q: 1. ఒప్పందం లక్ష్యం లేదా ప్రతిఫలం ఎప్పుడు చట్టవిరుద్ధం?
selfTest.a: చట్టం నిషేధించినప్పుడు, చట్టాన్ని నిష్ఫలం చేసేటప్పుడు, మోసపూరితమైనప్పుడు; ఇంకొకరి శరీరానికి లేదా ఆస్తికి హాని కలిగించినప్పుడు లేదా సూచించినప్పుడు; లేదా కోర్టు దాన్ని అనైతికంగా, ప్రజా విధానానికి వ్యతిరేకంగా భావించినప్పుడు (సెక్షన్ 23).

selfTest.q: 2. చట్టవిరుద్ధమైన లక్ష్యం ప్రభావం ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు (సెక్షన్ 23).

selfTest.q: 3. పాక్షికంగా చట్టవిరుద్ధమైన ఒప్పందం గురించి సెక్షన్ 24 ఏం చెబుతుంది?
selfTest.a: ఒకటి లేదా అంతకంటే ఎక్కువ లక్ష్యాలకు ఒకే ప్రతిఫలంలో ఏ భాగమైనా, లేదా ఒకే లక్ష్యానికి అనేక ప్రతిఫలాల్లో ఏదైనా లేదా దాని భాగమైనా చట్టవిరుద్ధమైతే, ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు.

selfTest.q: 4. పందెం ఒప్పందం సెక్షన్ 23 కింద "forbidden by law" అవుతుందా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. అది సెక్షన్ 30 కింద చెల్లదు, కానీ చట్టం నిషేధించినది కాదు ( Gherulal Parakh ).

selfTest.q: 5. A కొడుకుపై B వేసిన దోపిడీ ప్రాసిక్యూషన్ ను ఉపసంహరించడానికి A, B కి ₹5,000 ఇస్తానని వాగ్దానం చేస్తాడు. ఇది చట్టబద్ధమా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. Illustration (h) లాగే, లక్ష్యం చట్టవిరుద్ధం; ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు.

selfTest.q: 6. "మోసపూరిత లక్ష్యం", సెక్షన్ 17 కింద మోసం ఎలా భిన్నం?
selfTest.a: సెక్షన్ 17 కింద సమ్మతి పొందడానికి మోసం వాడతారు; కాంట్రాక్టు రద్దు చేయదగినది. మోసపూరిత లక్ష్యం అంటే ఒప్పందం ఉద్దేశమే మోసగించడం; ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు.

visuals.html:
కారణం క్లుప్తంగా అర్థం చట్టంలోని illustration
చట్టం నిషేధించినది చట్టం లేదా దాని కింది నియమం శిక్షించేది లేదా నిషేధించేది (h): డబ్బు కోసం దోపిడీ ప్రాసిక్యూషన్ ఉపసంహరించడం
చట్టాన్ని నిష్ఫలం చేసేది పైకి అనుమతించినట్టే ఉన్నా, చట్టాన్ని తప్పించుకునేది (i): బకాయిదారు బినామీ ద్వారా తన ఎస్టేట్ ను తిరిగి కొనడం
మోసపూరితమైనది మోసాన్ని లక్ష్యంగా పెట్టుకున్నది లేదా అందులో మోసం ఉన్నది (e): మోసంతో వచ్చిన లాభాలు పంచుకోవడం; (g): ఏజెంట్ రహస్యంగా యజమాని భూమిని లీజుకు ఇప్పించడం
ఇంకొకరి శరీరానికి లేదా ఆస్తికి హాని ఎవరికైనా హాని కలిగించేది లేదా సూచించేది (illustration లేదు; కింది ఉదాహరణ చూడండి)
అనైతికం లేదా ప్రజా విధానానికి వ్యతిరేకం కోర్టు అలా భావిస్తే (f): ప్రభుత్వ ఉద్యోగం కోసం డబ్బు; (j): ముఖ్తార్ తన ప్రభావాన్ని అమ్ముకోవడం; (k): కూతురిని ఉంపుడుగత్తెగా అద్దెకు ఇవ్వడం

visuals.caption: Diagram 1. ఐదు ప్రశ్నలను వరుసగా చూడండి. ఏ దశలో "కాదు" వచ్చినా, లక్ష్యం లేదా ప్రతిఫలం చట్టవిరుద్ధం, ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు.

visuals.html:
సందర్భం ఒప్పందం కారణం
A నిషేధిత మాదకద్రవ్యాలు సరఫరా చేయడానికి దినేష్ సలీంకు ₹2,00,000 ఇస్తాడు చట్టం నిషేధించినది
B పన్ను బకాయిల కోసం దినేష్ భూమి వేలం వేస్తున్నారు; అతను వేలంలో పాల్గొనకూడదని చట్టం చెబుతుంది; అతను తన బంధువుతో దాన్ని కొనిపించి, తన కోసం ఉంచమంటాడు చట్టాన్ని నిష్ఫలం చేసేది
C నకిలీ బ్రాండెడ్ వస్తువులు అమ్మి వచ్చే లాభాలు పంచుకోవడానికి దినేష్, రవి ఒప్పుకుంటారు మోసపూరితం
D ప్రత్యర్థి గోదాములోకి చొరబడి సరుకు పాడు చేయడానికి దినేష్ కిరణ్ కు ₹50,000 వాగ్దానం చేస్తాడు ఇంకొకరి ఆస్తికి హాని
E తన కొడుకుకు ప్రభుత్వ ఉద్యోగం ఇప్పించడానికి దినేష్ మోహన్ కు ₹1,00,000 ఇస్తాడు ప్రజా విధానానికి వ్యతిరేకం

law-of-contract-i-u2-t9.subtitle: Sections 20, 21 and 22 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: A mistake is a wrong belief about a fact or about the law, held when the agreement is made. The Act does not define it; it states its effect : Kind Effect Section Both parties mistaken about a fact essential to the agreement Agreement void 20 Wrong opinion about value Not a mistake of fact; no relief 20, Explanation Mistake about Indian law Contract not voidable 21 Mistake about foreign law Treated as a mistake of fact 21 One party mistaken about a fact Contract not voidable merely for that 22 So only one kind spoils the agreement completely: a shared mistake about an essential fact . A mistake by one party alone gives relief only where the other side caused it (fraud or misrepresentation ), or where a person signed a document radically different from what he thought ( non est factum ). In exams, the three sections and their illustrations are the core. In real life the rule tells you that you carry the risk of your own error.
legalProvision: Section 20. Agreement void where both parties are under mistake as to matter of fact. Where both the parties to an agreement are under a mistake as to a matter of fact essential to the agreement, the agreement is void. Explanation. —An erroneous opinion as to the value of the thing which forms the subject-matter of the agreement, is not to be deemed a mistake as to a matter of fact. Illustrations. (a) A agrees to sell to B a specific cargo of goods supposed to be on its way from England to Bombay. It turns out that, before the day of the bargain, the ship conveying the cargo had been cast away and the goods lost. Neither party was aware of the facts. The agreement is void. (b) A agrees to buy from B a certain horse. It turns out that the horse was dead at the time of the bargain, though neither party was aware of the fact. The agreement is void. (c) A, being entitled to an estate for the life of B, agrees to sell it to C. B was dead at the time of the agreement, but both parties were ignorant of the fact. The agreement is void.

Section 21. Effect of mistakes as to law. A contract is not voidable because it was caused by a mistake as to any law in force in India; but a mistake as to a law not in force in India has the same effect as a mistake of fact. Illustration. A and B make a contract grounded on the erroneous belief that a particular debt is barred by the Indian Law of Limitation: the contract is not voidable.

Section 22. Contract caused by mistake of one party as to matter of fact. A contract is not voidable merely because it was caused by one of the parties to it being under a mistake as to a matter of fact.
Section 14 (relevant part). Consent is said to be free when it is not caused by— … (5) mistake, subject to the provisions of sections 20, 21 and 22.
In simple words

Section 20: if both sides are wrong about a basic fact that the deal rests on, there is no deal at all. Being wrong about the price or worth of the thing does not count. Section 21: you cannot escape a contract by saying you did not know Indian law. Foreign law is treated as a fact. Section 22: if only you were wrong, that alone does not let you escape the contract.
en.meaning:
Mistake means an erroneous belief, held at the time of the agreement , about a fact or about the law. The effect depends on three questions:

Whose mistake? Both parties, or only one? About what? A fact, Indian law, or foreign law? How important? Is the fact essential to the agreement, or only about value?

Section 20: three conditions.

Condition What it means 1. Both parties are mistaken A shared (mutual or common) mistake 2. About a matter of fact Not law, not opinion about value 3. The fact is essential to the agreement It goes to the root: existence of the thing, its identity, or a basic quality the deal rests on

Why the law treats mistakes differently. A shared mistake on an essential fact means there was nothing real to agree about; the agreement fails. But where only one side is wrong, the law protects the other side, who did nothing wrong and relied on the deal. Every person must look after his own interests.

Mistake and consent. Where the parties do not agree on the same thing in the same sense (Section 13), there is no consent at all. Raffles v. Wichelhaus (1864) is the standard example: two ships named Peerless .
keyPoints: A mistake of both parties on an essential fact makes the agreement void (Section 20). A wrong opinion about value is not a mistake of fact. A mistake of one party does not make the contract voidable merely for that reason (Section 22). A mistake of Indian law has no effect. A mistake of foreign law is a mistake of fact (Section 21). A mistake caused by the other side's fraud or misrepresentation gives relief under Section 19. A signature on a radically different document may be disowned by non est factum, if the signer was not careless. Money paid under a void agreement or by mistake must be returned (Sections 65, 72).

caseLaws.name: Raffles v
caseLaws.facts: Wichelhaus (1864) Facts. 125 bales of Surat cotton were sold "to arrive ex Peerless from Bombay". Two ships named Peerless sailed from Bombay, one in October and one in December; the buyer meant the October ship and the seller tendered cotton from the December ship. Principle. The buyer's plea that he meant a different ship was held a good answer on demurrer, and judgment was given for the buyer. (1864) 2 H & C 906 (Court of Exchequer). Why it matters. The standard example of parties not agreeing on the same thing, so there is no contract. Ningawwa v. Byrappa (1968) Facts. A young, illiterate woman executed a gift deed in favour of her husband, believing it covered only two plots in one village. The husband had fraudulently included two valuable plots she had inherited in another village. Principle. Fraud as to the character of a document makes the transaction void; fraud as to its contents makes it only voidable. Here it was as to contents, so the gift was voidable. AIR 1968 SC 956 : (1968) 2 SCR 797. Why it matters. It marks when a mistake about a signed document destroys consent altogether (non est factum) and when it only makes the deal voidable. Tarsem Singh v. Sukhminder Singh (1998) Facts. An agreement of 1988 to sell agricultural land in Village Panjetha, Patiala, was made at a rate per unit of area, and ₹77,000 was paid as earnest money. Both parties were mistaken about the area (kanals or bighas) and so about the price. Principle. A mutual mistake about the area, an essential fact, made the agreement void under Section 20; the seller was bound under Section 65 to refund the earnest money. "Unilateral mistake is outside the scope of this Section." (1998) 3 SCC 471 : AIR 1998 SC 1400. Why it matters. It is a Supreme Court application of Sections 20 and 65 together: void agreement, money returned.

selfTest.q: 1. What makes an agreement void for mistake under Section 20?
selfTest.a: Both parties being under a mistake as to a matter of fact essential to the agreement.

selfTest.q: 2. Does a mistake of Indian law make a contract voidable?
selfTest.a: No (Section 21). A mistake as to a law not in force in India is treated like a mistake of fact.

selfTest.q: 3. Does a wrong opinion about the value of the thing count as a mistake of fact?
selfTest.a: No. The Explanation to Section 20 says it does not.

selfTest.q: 4. A sells B a horse. Unknown to both, it died an hour earlier. B has paid ₹40,000. What can B do?
selfTest.a: The agreement is void (Section 20, Illustration (b)). B can recover ₹40,000 (Section 65).

selfTest.q: 5. When does a one-sided mistake give relief?
selfTest.a: When the other side caused it by fraud or misrepresentation (Sections 17, 18(3), 19), or when the signer was misled about the nature of the document (non est factum).

selfTest.q: 6. What is the difference between fraud as to the character and as to the contents of a document?
selfTest.a: Fraud as to character makes the transaction void; fraud as to contents makes it voidable ( Ningawwa v. Byrappa ).

సెక్షన్ 20: బేరం ఆధారపడిన ప్రాథమిక వాస్తవం గురించి ఇద్దరూ తప్పుగా అనుకుంటే, బేరమే ఉండదు. వస్తువు ధర లేదా విలువ గురించి తప్పుగా అనుకోవడం దీని కిందకు రాదు. సెక్షన్ 21: భారత చట్టం తెలియదని చెప్పి కాంట్రాక్టు నుంచి తప్పించుకోలేరు. విదేశీ చట్టాన్ని వాస్తవంగా చూస్తారు. సెక్షన్ 22: మీరు ఒక్కరే తప్పుగా అనుకుంటే, దాని వల్ల మాత్రమే కాంట్రాక్టు నుంచి బయటపడలేరు.
te.meaning:
పొరపాటు అంటే ఒప్పందం సమయంలో ఒక వాస్తవం గురించి గానీ, చట్టం గురించి గానీ ఉన్న తప్పు నమ్మకం. దాని ప్రభావం మూడు ప్రశ్నలపై ఆధారపడుతుంది:

ఎవరి పొరపాటు? ఇద్దరిదా, ఒక్కరిదా? దేని గురించి? వాస్తవమా, భారత చట్టమా, విదేశీ చట్టమా? ఎంత ముఖ్యం? ఆ వాస్తవం ఒప్పందానికి అత్యవసరమైనదా , లేక కేవలం విలువ గురించా?

సెక్షన్ 20: మూడు షరతులు.

షరతు అర్థం 1. ఇద్దరు పక్షాలూ పొరపడాలి ఉమ్మడి (mutual లేదా common) పొరపాటు 2. వాస్తవం గురించి చట్టం గురించి కాదు, విలువపై అభిప్రాయం కాదు 3. ఆ వాస్తవం ఒప్పందానికి అత్యవసరం మూలాన్ని తాకేది: వస్తువు ఉనికి, దాని గుర్తింపు, లేదా బేరం ఆధారపడిన ప్రాథమిక గుణం

చట్టం పొరపాట్లను వేర్వేరుగా ఎందుకు చూస్తుంది. అత్యవసర వాస్తవం గురించి ఉమ్మడి పొరపాటు అంటే, ఒప్పుకోవడానికి నిజంగా ఏమీ లేదు; ఒప్పందం విఫలమవుతుంది. కానీ ఒక్క పక్షమే పొరపడితే, ఏ తప్పూ చేయకుండా ఆ బేరాన్ని నమ్ముకున్న ఎదుటి పక్షాన్ని చట్టం కాపాడుతుంది. ప్రతి వ్యక్తీ తన ప్రయోజనాలను తానే చూసుకోవాలి.

పొరపాటు, సమ్మతి. పక్షాలు ఒకే విషయాన్ని ఒకే అర్థంలో ఒప్పుకోకపోతే (సెక్షన్ 13), అసలు సమ్మతే లేదు. Raffles v. Wichelhaus (1864) దీనికి ప్రామాణిక ఉదాహరణ: Peerless అనే పేరుతో రెండు ఓడలు.

selfTest.q: 1. సెక్షన్ 20 కింద ఒప్పందాన్ని పొరపాటు వల్ల చెల్లనిదిగా చేసేది ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: ఒప్పందానికి అత్యవసరమైన వాస్తవం గురించి ఇద్దరు పక్షాలూ పొరపడటం.

selfTest.q: 2. భారత చట్టం గురించిన పొరపాటు కాంట్రాక్టును రద్దు చేయదగినదిగా చేస్తుందా?
selfTest.a: లేదు (సెక్షన్ 21). భారతదేశంలో అమలులో లేని చట్టం గురించిన పొరపాటును వాస్తవ పొరపాటు లాగే చూస్తారు.

selfTest.q: 3. వస్తువు విలువ గురించిన తప్పు అభిప్రాయం వాస్తవ పొరపాటా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. సెక్షన్ 20 Explanation అలా చెబుతుంది.

selfTest.q: 4. A, B కి ఒక గుర్రాన్ని అమ్ముతాడు. ఇద్దరికీ తెలియకుండా, అది గంట ముందే చనిపోయింది. B ₹40,000 చెల్లించాడు. B ఏం చేయవచ్చు?
selfTest.a: ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు (సెక్షన్ 20, Illustration (b)). B ₹40,000 తిరిగి పొందవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 65).

selfTest.q: 5. ఒక్క పక్షం పొరపాటుకు ఉపశమనం ఎప్పుడు దొరుకుతుంది?
selfTest.a: ఎదుటి పక్షం మోసం లేదా తప్పుడు ప్రాతినిధ్యంతో దాన్ని కలిగించినప్పుడు (సెక్షన్లు 17, 18(3), 19), లేదా పత్రం స్వభావం గురించి సంతకం చేసినవాణ్ని తప్పుదారి పట్టించినప్పుడు (non est factum).

selfTest.q: 6. పత్రం స్వభావం గురించి మోసానికి, దాని విషయం గురించి మోసానికి తేడా ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: స్వభావం గురించి మోసం లావాదేవీని చెల్లనిదిగా చేస్తుంది; విషయం గురించి మోసం రద్దు చేయదగినదిగా చేస్తుంది ( Ningawwa v. Byrappa ).

law-of-contract-i-u2-t11.subtitle: Sections 23, 26, 27 and 28 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: An agreement is void if the Court regards its object or consideration as immoral or opposed to public policy (Section 23). The Act does not list the heads of public policy. Courts apply a settled set of heads worked out in decided cases, and use the doctrine cautiously . Immoral in Section 23 has a narrow meaning. The Supreme Court has said that judicial decisions confined it to sexual immorality ( Gherulal Parakh ). It does not need a crime: Illustration (k) is void "though the letting may not be punishable". The Act also declares three kinds of agreement void by their own sections: restraint of marriage of any person other than a minor (Section 26); restraint of trade , with one exception for sale of goodwill (Section 27); restraint of legal proceedings , with exceptions for arbitration and bank guarantees (Section 28). In exams, restraint of trade is the favourite problem. In real life it decides whether a non-compete clause in your job letter can be enforced.
legalProvision: Section 23 (relevant part). The consideration or object of an agreement is lawful, unless— … the Court regards it as immoral, or opposed to public policy. In each of these cases, the consideration or object of an agreement is said to be unlawful. Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void. Illustrations. (f) A promises to obtain for B an employment in the public service and B promises to pay 1,000 rupees to A. The agreement is void, as the consideration for it is unlawful. (h) A promises B to drop a prosecution which he has instituted against B for robbery, and B promises to restore the value of the things taken. The agreement is void, as its object is unlawful. (j) A, who is B's mukhtar, promises to exercise his influence, as such, with B in favour of C, and C promises to pay 1,000 rupees to A. The agreement is void, because it is immoral. (k) A agrees to let her daughter to hire to B for concubinage. The agreement is void, because it is immoral, though the letting may not be punishable under the Indian Penal Code.
Section 26. Agreement in restraint of marriage, void. Every agreement in restraint of the marriage of any person, other than a minor, is void.

Section 27. Agreement in restraint of trade, void. Every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void. Exception 1. One who sells the good-will of a business may agree with the buyer to refrain from carrying on a similar business, within specified local limits, so long as the buyer, or any person deriving title to the good-will from him, carries on a like business therein, provided that such limits appear to the Court reasonable, regard being had to the nature of the business.

Section 28. Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings, void. Every agreement,— (a) by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract, by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals, or which limits the time within which he may thus enforce his rights; or (b) which extinguishes the rights of any party thereto, or discharges any party thereto, from any liability, under or in respect of any contract on the expiry of a specified period so as to restrict any party from enforcing his rights, is void to the extent. Exception 1. A contract by which two or more persons agree that any dispute which may arise between them in respect of any subject or class of subjects shall be referred to arbitration, and that only the amount awarded in such arbitration shall be recoverable in respect of the dispute so referred. Exception 2. Any contract in writing, by which two or more persons agree to refer to arbitration any question between them which has already arisen, or any provision of any law in force for the time being as to references to arbitration. Exception 3. A contract in writing by which any bank or financial institution stipulate a term in a guarantee … for extinguishment of the rights or discharge of any party thereto from any liability … on the expiry of a specified period which is not less than one year from the date of occurring or non-occurring of a specified event.
Indian Partnership Act, 1932. Each of these provisions applies " notwithstanding anything contained in section 27 of the Indian Contract Act":

Section 11(2): partners may agree that a partner "shall not carry on any business other than that of the firm while he is a partner". Section 36(2): an outgoing partner may agree not to carry on a similar business within a specified period or local limits, valid if the restrictions are reasonable. Section 54: partners may, on or in anticipation of dissolution, agree not to carry on a similar business within a specified period or local limits, valid "if the restrictions imposed are reasonable". Section 55(3): a partner may, on sale of the firm's goodwill , agree with the buyer not to carry on a similar business within a specified period or local limits, valid if the restrictions are reasonable.
In simple words

Section 23: if the Court finds the purpose or the price of a deal immoral, or harmful to the public, the deal is void. Section 26: you cannot validly bind an adult not to marry. Section 27: you cannot validly bind a person not to carry on his work or business, even partly, except when he sells his business's goodwill (and in a few partnership cases). Section 28: you cannot validly shut someone out of the courts or shorten the time the law gives him to sue; but you can agree to go to arbitration.
en.meaning:
Immoral agreement . An agreement whose object or consideration the Court regards as immoral. In Gherulal Parakh v. Mahadeodas Maiya (1959), the Supreme Court said "immoral" is "a very comprehensive word", but Section 23 shows "the legislative intention to give it a restricted meaning". Decided cases and text-book writers "confined it, with every justification, only to sexual immorality", and the words "the court regards it as immoral" show it "should be confined to the principles recognized and settled by Courts". Public policy . The general good of the community, as the courts protect it. In Gherulal Parakh the Supreme Court summarised the doctrine: it is "an illusive concept", described as an "unruly horse"; the primary duty of a court is "to enforce a promise which the parties have made and to uphold the sanctity of contracts"; the doctrine "is only a branch of common law" and "is governed by precedents; the principles have been crystallized under different heads"; it "should only be invoked in clear and incontestable cases of harm to the public"; "though the heads are not closed … it is advisable in the interest of stability of society not to make any attempt to discover new heads in these days". Immoral, opposed to public policy, forbidden by law. All three make an agreement void under Section 23. They differ in how the Court identifies them. Ground Test Example Forbidden by law A statute prohibits or punishes it Selling banned drugs Immoral The Court regards it as immoral (sexual immorality), even if no law punishes it Illustration (k): letting a daughter for concubinage Opposed to public policy Clear harm to the public, under a head the courts recognise Illustration (h): dropping a prosecution for robbery See Diagram 1 . keyPoints: Section 23 voids agreements that the Court regards as immoral or opposed to public policy. "Immoral" is confined to settled heads (sexual immorality); no crime is needed (Illustration (k)). Courts apply public policy to settled heads and only in clear cases of harm to the public. Section 26: restraint of marriage of an adult is void. Section 27: even a partial restraint of trade is void, unless within the goodwill exception or a Partnership Act exception; no reasonableness test. Covenants operating during employment are generally valid; post-employment restraints are void. Section 28: an absolute bar on suing, or a shorter time to sue, is void; arbitration and bank guarantees of at least one year are saved.

caseLaws.name: Gherulal Parakh v
caseLaws.facts: Mahadeodas Maiya (1959) Facts. Two persons formed a partnership to enter into forward contracts for wheat with other firms, sharing profit and loss. The contracts made a loss, and one partner sued the other for half. Principle. "Immoral" is confined to settled principles (sexual immorality); public policy is governed by settled heads and invoked "only … in clear and incontestable cases of harm to the public"; wagering is not opposed to public policy. AIR 1959 SC 781 : [1959] Supp 2 SCR 406. Why it matters. It is the Supreme Court's leading statement on immorality and public policy under Section 23. Superintendence Company of India v. Krishan Murgai (1980) Facts. A branch manager's appointment letter barred him, for two years after he left, from serving a competitor or starting a similar business at his last place of posting. The company terminated him, and he started a similar business. Principle. The majority held the clause, which used the word "leave", did not apply to an employee whose service was terminated. A.P. Sen J. held a post-service restraint void under Section 27, following Madhub Chunder . [1980] 3 SCR 1278. Why it matters. Sen J.'s opinion is the main Supreme Court statement that post-service restraints are void in India. Niranjan Shankar Golikari v. Century Spinning (1967) Facts. A shift supervisor, trained in making tyre cord yarn, agreed to serve for five years and not to work elsewhere in that period. He left soon after training for a rival. Principle. " Negative covenants operative during the period of the contract of employment when the employee is bound to serve his employer exclusively are generally not regarded as restraint of trade", unless the contract is unconscionable, excessively harsh, unreasonable or one-sided. [1967] 2 SCR 378. Why it matters. It separates restraints during a contract from those after it. Gujarat Bottling v. Coca Cola (1995) Facts. A bottler licensed by Coca Cola agreed not to deal in competing beverages during the franchise. Pepsi-linked concerns acquired control of the bottler, which then ended the agreements. Principle. A franchisee's promise not to deal in competing goods while the franchise lasts facilitates distribution "and it cannot be regarded as in restraint of trade". [1995] Supp 2 SCR 513 (page from the report). Why it matters. It applies the "during the contract" rule to commercial franchises. Percept D'Mark v. Zaheer Khan (2006) Facts. A cricketer's agent had a clause that, after the agreement expired, he must give the agent a right to match any offer from another agent. After expiry he appointed another agent. Principle. The clause operating after the term was a restraint of trade void under Section 27; "neither the test of reasonableness nor the principle of restraint being partial is applicable, unless it falls within express exception engrafted in Section 27". [2006] 3 SCR 145 (page from the report). Why it matters. It confirms the strict Indian reading of Section 27 for post-term restraints. Central Inland Water Transport Corporation v. Brojo Nath Ganguly (1986) Facts. A government company's service rule allowed it to end a permanent employee's service on three months' notice or pay, without reasons. Principle. An unconscionable term imposed on a weaker party with no meaningful choice is opposed to public policy and void under Section 23. (1986) 2 SCR 278. Why it matters. Public policy can strike down unfair standard terms in unequal bargains. Vijaya Bank v. Prashant B. Narnaware (2025) Facts. A bank's appointment letter required a senior manager to serve at least three years or pay ₹2,00,000. He resigned early, paid under protest, and the High Court struck the clause down. Principle. The minimum-term clause operated during employment, was not unconscionable, and "does not amount to restraint of trade nor is it opposed to public policy". 2025 INSC 691. Why it matters. It is the latest Supreme Court word on employment bonds under Sections 23 and 27.

selfTest.q: 1. Does an immoral agreement need to be punishable by law to be void?
selfTest.a: No. Illustration (k) to Section 23 is void as immoral though the letting may not be punishable.

selfTest.q: 2. What is the only exception to Section 27 in the Contract Act itself?
selfTest.a: The sale of goodwill, with a promise not to carry on a similar business within reasonable local limits. The Partnership Act, 1932 adds exceptions for partners.

selfTest.q: 3. What did Madhub Chunder v. Rajcoomar Doss decide?
selfTest.a: That Section 27 applies to partial restrictions, including one limited to a particular place, and not only to total restraints.

selfTest.q: 4. Is a clause not to work for a competitor during employment void?
selfTest.a: Generally not. It is not a restraint of trade unless unconscionable or one-sided ( Niranjan Shankar Golikari ).

selfTest.q: 5. A contract says all claims must be filed in court within six months. Is it valid?
selfTest.a: No, to that extent. It limits the time within which rights may be enforced (Section 28(a)).

selfTest.q: 6. Is a wagering agreement opposed to public policy in India?
selfTest.a: No. It is void under Section 30 but not opposed to public policy ( Gherulal Parakh ).

legalProvision: Section 23 (relevant part). The consideration or object of an agreement is lawful, unless— … the Court regards it as immoral, or opposed to public policy. In each of these cases, the consideration or object of an agreement is said to be unlawful. Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void. Illustrations. (f) A promises to obtain for B an employment in the public service and B promises to pay 1,000 rupees to A. The agreement is void, as the consideration for it is unlawful. (h) A promises B to drop a prosecution which he has instituted against B for robbery, and B promises to restore the value of the things taken. The agreement is void, as its object is unlawful. (j) A, who is B's mukhtar, promises to exercise his influence, as such, with B in favour of C, and C promises to pay 1,000 rupees to A. The agreement is void, because it is immoral. (k) A agrees to let her daughter to hire to B for concubinage. The agreement is void, because it is immoral, though the letting may not be punishable under the Indian Penal Code.
Section 26. Agreement in restraint of marriage, void. Every agreement in restraint of the marriage of any person, other than a minor, is void.

Section 27. Agreement in restraint of trade, void. Every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void. Exception 1. One who sells the good-will of a business may agree with the buyer to refrain from carrying on a similar business, within specified local limits, so long as the buyer, or any person deriving title to the good-will from him, carries on a like business therein, provided that such limits appear to the Court reasonable, regard being had to the nature of the business.

Section 28. Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings, void. Every agreement,— (a) by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract, by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals, or which limits the time within which he may thus enforce his rights; or (b) which extinguishes the rights of any party thereto, or discharges any party thereto, from any liability, under or in respect of any contract on the expiry of a specified period so as to restrict any party from enforcing his rights, is void to the extent. Exception 1. A contract by which two or more persons agree that any dispute which may arise between them in respect of any subject or class of subjects shall be referred to arbitration, and that only the amount awarded in such arbitration shall be recoverable in respect of the dispute so referred. Exception 2. Any contract in writing, by which two or more persons agree to refer to arbitration any question between them which has already arisen, or any provision of any law in force for the time being as to references to arbitration. Exception 3. A contract in writing by which any bank or financial institution stipulate a term in a guarantee … for extinguishment of the rights or discharge of any party thereto from any liability … on the expiry of a specified period which is not less than one year from the date of occurring or non-occurring of a specified event.
భారత భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932. ఈ నిబంధనలు ప్రతిదీ " notwithstanding anything contained in section 27 of the Indian Contract Act" వర్తిస్తాయి:

సెక్షన్ 11(2): భాగస్వామి "shall not carry on any business other than that of the firm while he is a partner" అని భాగస్వాములు ఒప్పుకోవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 36(2): బయటికి వెళ్లే భాగస్వామి, నిర్దిష్ట కాలంలో లేదా నిర్దిష్ట స్థానిక పరిధిలో అలాంటి వ్యాపారం చేయనని ఒప్పుకోవచ్చు; ఆంక్షలు సహేతుకమైతే చెల్లుతుంది. సెక్షన్ 54: సంస్థ రద్దు సమయంలో లేదా రద్దును ఊహించి, నిర్దిష్ట కాలంలో లేదా స్థానిక పరిధిలో అలాంటి వ్యాపారం చేయబోమని భాగస్వాములు ఒప్పుకోవచ్చు; "if the restrictions imposed are reasonable" అయితే చెల్లుతుంది. సెక్షన్ 55(3): సంస్థ గుడ్‌విల్ అమ్మినప్పుడు, నిర్దిష్ట కాలంలో లేదా స్థానిక పరిధిలో అలాంటి వ్యాపారం చేయనని భాగస్వామి కొనేవాడితో ఒప్పుకోవచ్చు; ఆంక్షలు సహేతుకమైతే చెల్లుతుంది.
సులభంగా చెప్పాలంటే

సెక్షన్ 23: ఒక బేరం ఉద్దేశం లేదా ధర అనైతికమని, లేదా ప్రజలకు హానికరమని కోర్టు భావిస్తే, బేరం చెల్లదు. సెక్షన్ 26: పెద్దవారిని పెళ్లి చేసుకోకూడదని చెల్లుబాటయ్యేలా కట్టడి చేయలేరు. సెక్షన్ 27: ఒక వ్యక్తిని తన పని లేదా వ్యాపారం చేయకుండా, పాక్షికంగానైనా, చెల్లుబాటయ్యేలా కట్టడి చేయలేరు; అతను తన వ్యాపార గుడ్‌విల్ అమ్మినప్పుడు (కొన్ని భాగస్వామ్య సందర్భాల్లో) తప్ప. సెక్షన్ 28: ఒకరిని కోర్టులకు వెళ్లకుండా పూర్తిగా ఆపలేరు, చట్టం ఇచ్చిన దావా గడువును తగ్గించలేరు; కానీ మధ్యవర్తిత్వానికి (arbitration) వెళ్లడానికి ఒప్పుకోవచ్చు.

అనైతిక ఒప్పందం. లక్ష్యాన్ని లేదా ప్రతిఫలాన్ని కోర్టు అనైతికంగా భావించే ఒప్పందం. Gherulal Parakh v. Mahadeodas Maiya (1959) లో సుప్రీంకోర్టు, "immoral" అనేది "a very comprehensive word" అయినా, సెక్షన్ 23 "the legislative intention to give it a restricted meaning" ను చూపిస్తుందని చెప్పింది. న్యాయ నిర్ణయాలు, పాఠ్యగ్రంథ రచయితలు దాన్ని "confined it, with every justification, only to sexual immorality"; "the court regards it as immoral" అనే పదాలు అది "should be confined to the principles recognized and settled by Courts" అని చూపిస్తాయి. ప్రజా విధానం. కోర్టులు కాపాడే సమాజ సాధారణ హితం. Gherulal Parakh లో సుప్రీంకోర్టు ఈ సూత్రాన్ని ఇలా సంక్షిప్తీకరించింది: అది "an illusive concept", దాన్ని "unruly horse" అని వర్ణించారు; కోర్టు ప్రాథమిక కర్తవ్యం "to enforce a promise which the parties have made and to uphold the sanctity of contracts"; ఈ సూత్రం "is only a branch of common law", "is governed by precedents; the principles have been crystallized under different heads"; దాన్ని "should only be invoked in clear and incontestable cases of harm to the public"; "though the heads are not closed … it is advisable in the interest of stability of society not to make any attempt to discover new heads in these days". అనైతికం, ప్రజా విధానానికి వ్యతిరేకం, చట్టం నిషేధించినది. మూడూ సెక్షన్ 23 కింద ఒప్పందాన్ని చెల్లనిదిగా చేస్తాయి. కోర్టు వాటిని గుర్తించే విధానంలో తేడా ఉంది. కారణం పరీక్ష ఉదాహరణ చట్టం నిషేధించినది ఒక చట్టం దాన్ని నిషేధిస్తుంది లేదా శిక్షిస్తుంది నిషేధిత మందులు అమ్మడం అనైతికం ఏ చట్టమూ శిక్షించకపోయినా, కోర్టు దాన్ని అనైతికంగా (లైంగిక అనైతికత) భావిస్తుంది Illustration (k): కూతురిని ఉంపుడుగత్తెగా అద్దెకు ఇవ్వడం ప్రజా విధానానికి వ్యతిరేకం కోర్టులు గుర్తించిన శీర్షిక కింద, ప్రజలకు స్పష్టమైన హాని Illustration (h): దోపిడీ ప్రాసిక్యూషన్ ఉపసంహరించడం Diagram 1 చూడండి. selfTest.q: 1. అనైతిక ఒప్పందం చెల్లనిది కావడానికి అది చట్టప్రకారం శిక్షార్హం కావాలా?
selfTest.a: అవసరం లేదు. సెక్షన్ 23 Illustration (k) లో, అద్దెకు ఇవ్వడం శిక్షార్హం కాకపోయినా, అనైతికం కాబట్టి చెల్లదు.

selfTest.q: 2. కాంట్రాక్టు చట్టంలోనే సెక్షన్ 27 కు ఉన్న ఒకే మినహాయింపు ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: సహేతుకమైన స్థానిక పరిధిలో అలాంటి వ్యాపారం చేయనన్న వాగ్దానంతో గుడ్‌విల్ అమ్మకం. భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932 భాగస్వాములకు మినహాయింపులు జోడిస్తుంది.

selfTest.q: 3. Madhub Chunder v. Rajcoomar Doss ఏం నిర్ణయించింది?
selfTest.a: సెక్షన్ 27 పూర్తి నిరోధాలకే కాకుండా, ఒక నిర్దిష్ట ప్రదేశానికి పరిమితమైన వాటితో సహా పాక్షిక నిరోధాలకూ వర్తిస్తుందని.

selfTest.q: 4. ఉద్యోగంలో ఉండగా పోటీ సంస్థ కోసం పనిచేయకూడదనే క్లాజు చెల్లదా?
selfTest.a: సాధారణంగా చెల్లుతుంది. అన్యాయమైనది లేదా ఏకపక్షమైనది కాకపోతే అది వ్యాపార నిరోధం కాదు ( Niranjan Shankar Golikari ).

selfTest.q: 5. అన్ని క్లెయిములూ ఆరు నెలల్లోగా కోర్టులో దాఖలు చేయాలని ఒక కాంట్రాక్టు చెబుతుంది. అది చెల్లుతుందా?
selfTest.a: ఆ మేరకు చెల్లదు. హక్కులను అమలు చేసే కాలాన్ని అది పరిమితం చేస్తుంది (సెక్షన్ 28(a)).

selfTest.q: 6. భారతదేశంలో పందెం ఒప్పందం ప్రజా విధానానికి వ్యతిరేకమా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. అది సెక్షన్ 30 కింద చెల్లదు, కానీ ప్రజా విధానానికి వ్యతిరేకం కాదు ( Gherulal Parakh ).

law-of-contract-i-u2-t14.subtitle: Section 30 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: A wagering agreement is a bet. Two people promise that one will pay the other, depending on how an uncertain future event turns out. Neither has any interest in the event except the stake. Section 30 makes wagers void , and no suit lies to recover anything won on a wager, or anything handed to a person to hold until the result. A wager is void but not illegal . So a deal connected with a wager, such as a partnership to make wagering contracts, is not tainted ( Gherulal Parakh ). In exams, the essentials and the contrast with a contingent contract earn the marks. In real life this explains why a court will not help you collect a bet.
legalProvision: Section 30. Agreements by way of wager void. Agreements by way of wager are void; and no suit shall be brought for recovering anything alleged to be won on any wager, or entrusted to any person to abide the result of any game or other uncertain event on which any wager is made. Exception in favour of certain prizes for horse-racing. —This section shall not be deemed to render unlawful a subscription or contribution, or agreement to subscribe or contribute, made or entered into for or toward any plate, prize or sum of money, of the value or amount of five hundred rupees or upwards, to be awarded to the winner or winners of any horse-race. Section 294A of the Indian Penal Code not affected. —Nothing in this section shall be deemed to legalize any transaction connected with horse-racing, to which the provisions of section 294A of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) apply.

Indian Penal Code, 1860, Section 294A. Keeping lottery office. Whoever keeps any office or place for the purpose of drawing any lottery not being a State lottery or a lottery authorised by the State Government, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both. And whoever publishes any proposal to pay any sum, or to deliver any goods, or to do or forbear doing anything for the benefit of any person, on any event or contingency relative or applicable to the drawing of any ticket, lot, number or figure in any such lottery, shall be punished with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Section 297. Keeping lottery office. (1) Whoever keeps any office or place for the purpose of drawing any lottery not being a State lottery or a lottery authorised by the State Government, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both. (2) Whoever publishes any proposal to pay any sum, or to deliver any goods, or to do or forbear from doing anything for the benefit of any person, on any event or contingency relative or applicable to the drawing of any ticket, lot, number or figure in any such lottery, shall be punished with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees.
In simple words

A bet is void. The winner cannot sue the loser for the winnings. Nor can anyone sue the person holding the bet money (the stakeholder) for it. A contribution of ₹500 or more towards a prize for the winner of a horse-race is not made unlawful by Section 30. But Section 30 does not make lawful a horse-racing transaction caught by the lottery offence (IPC Section 294A, now BNS Section 297).
en.meaning:
The Act does not define a wager. The classic description is that of Hawkins J. in Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co. (first instance, 1892): a wagering contract is one by which two persons, "professing to hold opposite views" about a future uncertain event, agree that one shall win from the other a sum of money or other stake depending on how the event turns out, neither of them having any other interest in the contract than the stake he will win or lose. From this, a wager has four marks : Mark Meaning 1. Uncertain future event The result of a match, an election or a draw (or a past event unknown to the parties) 2. Mutual chances of gain and loss Each side promises to pay if the event goes against him 3. One must win, the other lose If only one side can lose, it is not a wager 4. No interest except the stake Neither party has any interest in the event apart from the money bet If a party has a real interest in the event, such as an owner insuring his own house against fire, it is not a wager. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. Go down the questions in order. A "No" at any step means it is not a wager. All "Yes" means a wager: void, with no suit to recover. flowchart TD Q1{"1. Does the agreement depend
on an uncertain event?"} Q2{"2. Do both sides stand to win
or lose depending on it?"} Q3{"3. Does neither side have any interest
in the event except the stake?"} N1["Not a wager"] N2["Not a wager
(only one side can lose)"] CC["Not a wager: may be a
contingent contract (s.31),
e.g. insurance"] W["WAGER: void (s.30)
No suit for winnings or
against a stakeholder"] G["Void but not illegal:
collateral deals not tainted
(Gherulal Parakh)"] Q1 -- "No" --> N1 Q1 -- "Yes" --> Q2 Q2 -- "No" --> N2 Q2 -- "Yes" --> Q3 Q3 -- "No" --> CC Q3 -- "Yes" --> W W --> G Text description Does the agreement depend on an uncertain event? If no, not a wager. Do both sides stand to win or lose depending on that event? If no, not a wager. Does neither side have any interest in the event except the stake? If no, it may be a contingent contract (Section 31), such as insurance. If all are yes, it is a wager: void, no suit to recover winnings or a stake held by a stakeholder (Section 30); but it is not illegal, so collateral deals are not tainted (Gherulal Parakh).
keyPoints: A wager depends on an uncertain event, with mutual win-or-lose promises and no interest except the stake. Section 30: wagers are void, and no suit lies to recover winnings or a stake held by a third person. A wager is void but not illegal; collateral transactions are not tainted ( Gherulal Parakh ). Horse-race prizes of 500 rupees or more are saved from Section 30, but not lottery transactions under IPC Section 294A (now BNS Section 297). A genuine interest in the event makes the agreement a contingent contract, not a wager. "Mere skill" means substantial degree or preponderance of skill ( K.R. Lakshmanan ).

caseLaws.name: Gherulal Parakh v
caseLaws.facts: Mahadeodas Maiya (1959) Facts. The managers of two joint families formed a partnership to enter into wagering contracts in wheat with two firms of Hapur, sharing profit and loss. The contracts made a loss, and one partner sued the other for half. Principle. "Though a wager is void and unenforceable, it is not forbidden by law and therefore the object of a collateral agreement is not unlawful under s. 23 of the Contract Act". The appeal was dismissed and the partner had to share the loss. AIR 1959 SC 781 : [1959] Supp 2 SCR 406. Why it matters. It is the leading case that a wager is void, not illegal. Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co. (1893) Facts. A company promised £100 to anyone who caught influenza after using its smoke ball three times daily for two weeks, and deposited £1,000 with a bank to show its sincerity. When sued, it argued among other things that the promise was a bet or an insurance policy. Principle. Lindley L.J. agreed with Hawkins J. that "nobody ever dreamt of a bet" and that the transaction "had nothing whatever in common with a bet"; the plaintiff recovered £100. [1893] 1 QB 256 (CA), affirming [1892] 2 QB 484. Why it matters. Hawkins J.'s judgment gives the classic description of a wager, and the case shows that a promise depending on an uncertain event is not a wager unless both sides stand to win or lose. K.R. Lakshmanan v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996) Facts. The Madras Race Club ran horse races with betting on its premises. Tamil Nadu treated this as gaming, and a 1974 Act abolished betting on horse races. Principle. "We, therefore, hold that the expression "mere skill" would mean substantial degree or preponderance of skill." Horse racing is a game of skill, so betting on it is not gaming under the two Madras laws. AIR 1996 SC 1153 : (1996) 2 SCC 226. Why it matters. Skill or chance decides whether betting on a game is gaming under State law.

selfTest.q: 1. What is the effect of a wagering agreement under Section 30?
selfTest.a: It is void, and no suit lies to recover anything won on the wager.

selfTest.q: 2. What separates a wager from a contingent contract?
selfTest.a: In a wager neither party has any interest in the event except the stake. In a contingent contract the event is collateral and the parties have a genuine interest.

selfTest.q: 3. Is a wager illegal?
selfTest.a: No. It is void but not forbidden by law ( Gherulal Parakh v. Mahadeodas Maiya ).

selfTest.q: 4. A and B each give ₹2,000 to C to hold until a match ends. A wins. Can A sue C for ₹4,000?
selfTest.a: No. Section 30 bars a suit for anything entrusted to a person to abide the result of a wager.

selfTest.q: 5. Club members agree to contribute towards a ₹1,00,000 prize for the winner of a horse-race. Is this unlawful under Section 30?
selfTest.a: No. It falls within the horse-race exception (500 rupees or more).

selfTest.q: 6. What did K.R. Lakshmanan decide?
selfTest.a: That horse racing is a game of skill ("mere skill" means substantial degree or preponderance of skill), so betting on it was not gaming under the Madras gaming laws.

(1) Whoever keeps any office or place for the purpose of drawing any lottery not being a State lottery or a lottery authorised by the State Government, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both. (2) Whoever publishes any proposal to pay any sum, or to deliver any goods, or to do or forbear from doing anything for the benefit of any person, on any event or contingency relative or applicable to the drawing of any ticket, lot, number or figure in any such lottery, shall be punished with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees.
సులభంగా చెప్పాలంటే

పందెం చెల్లదు. గెలిచినవాడు గెలుపు సొమ్ము కోసం ఓడినవాడిపై దావా వేయలేడు. పందెం డబ్బు దగ్గర ఉంచుకున్న వ్యక్తి (stakeholder) పైనా దాని కోసం ఎవరూ దావా వేయలేరు. గుర్రపు పందెంలో గెలిచినవారికి ₹500 లేదా అంతకంటే ఎక్కువ బహుమతి కోసం ఇచ్చే చందాను సెక్షన్ 30 చట్టవిరుద్ధం చేయదు. కానీ లాటరీ నేరం (IPC సెక్షన్ 294A, ఇప్పుడు BNS సెక్షన్ 297) కిందకు వచ్చే గుర్రపు పందెపు లావాదేవీని సెక్షన్ 30 చట్టబద్ధం చేయదు.

చట్టం పందేన్ని నిర్వచించదు. Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co. (మొదటి విచారణ, 1892) లో Hawkins J. ఇచ్చిన వర్ణనే ప్రసిద్ధమైనది: ఒక భవిష్యత్ అనిశ్చిత సంఘటన గురించి "professing to hold opposite views" ఇద్దరు వ్యక్తులు, ఆ సంఘటన ఎలా తేలుతుందనే దాన్ని బట్టి ఒకరు ఇంకొకరి నుంచి కొంత డబ్బు లేదా పందెం సొమ్ము గెలుస్తారని ఒప్పుకుంటారు; తాము గెలిచే లేదా ఓడే సొమ్ము తప్ప ఆ కాంట్రాక్టులో ఇద్దరిలో ఎవరికీ వేరే ఆసక్తి ఉండదు. దీని నుంచి పందేనికి నాలుగు లక్షణాలు : లక్షణం అర్థం 1. అనిశ్చిత భవిష్యత్ సంఘటన మ్యాచ్ ఫలితం, ఎన్నిక లేదా డ్రా (లేదా పక్షాలకు తెలియని గత సంఘటన) 2. పరస్పర లాభనష్టాల అవకాశం సంఘటన తనకు వ్యతిరేకంగా జరిగితే చెల్లిస్తానని ప్రతి పక్షమూ వాగ్దానం చేస్తుంది 3. ఒకరు గెలవాలి, ఇంకొకరు ఓడాలి ఒక్క పక్షమే ఓడే వీలుంటే అది పందెం కాదు 4. పందెం సొమ్ము తప్ప వేరే ఆసక్తి లేదు పందెం కాసిన డబ్బు తప్ప సంఘటనలో ఏ పక్షానికీ ఆసక్తి లేదు ఒక పక్షానికి సంఘటనలో నిజమైన ఆసక్తి ఉంటే, ఉదాహరణకు యజమాని తన ఇంటిని అగ్ని ప్రమాదానికి బీమా చేయిస్తే, అది పందెం కాదు. (Gherulal Parakh)"] Q1 -- "కాదు" --> N1 Q1 -- "అవును" --> Q2 Q2 -- "కాదు" --> N2 Q2 -- "అవును" --> Q3 Q3 -- "కాదు" --> CC Q3 -- "అవును" --> W W --> G వచన వివరణ ఒప్పందం అనిశ్చిత సంఘటనపై ఆధారపడుతుందా? కాదు అయితే పందెం కాదు. ఆ సంఘటనను బట్టి ఇద్దరూ గెలిచే లేదా ఓడే స్థితిలో ఉన్నారా? కాదు అయితే పందెం కాదు. పందెం సొమ్ము తప్ప సంఘటనలో ఎవరికీ ఆసక్తి లేదా? ఆసక్తి ఉంటే షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టు కావచ్చు (సె.31), ఉదాహరణకు బీమా. అన్నీ అవును అయితే పందెం: చెల్లదు, గెలుపు సొమ్ము లేదా stakeholder దగ్గరి సొమ్ము కోసం దావా లేదు (సె.30); కానీ చట్టవిరుద్ధం కాదు, అనుబంధ బేరాలు కళంకితం కావు (Gherulal Parakh).

selfTest.q: 1. సెక్షన్ 30 కింద పందెపు ఒప్పందం ప్రభావం ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: అది చెల్లదు; పందెంలో గెలిచినదాన్ని తిరిగి పొందడానికి దావా లేదు.

selfTest.q: 2. పందేన్ని షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టు నుంచి ఏది వేరు చేస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: పందెంలో పందెం సొమ్ము తప్ప సంఘటనలో ఏ పక్షానికీ ఆసక్తి లేదు. షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టులో సంఘటన అనుబంధమైనది, పక్షాలకు నిజమైన ఆసక్తి ఉంటుంది.

selfTest.q: 3. పందెం చట్టవిరుద్ధమా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. అది చెల్లదు కానీ చట్టం నిషేధించలేదు ( Gherulal Parakh v. Mahadeodas Maiya ).

selfTest.q: 4. మ్యాచ్ ముగిసేవరకు ఉంచమని A, B చెరో ₹2,000 C కి ఇస్తారు. A గెలుస్తాడు. ₹4,000 కోసం A, C పై దావా వేయగలడా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. పందెం ఫలితం వరకు ఒక వ్యక్తి దగ్గర ఉంచినదాని కోసం దావాను సెక్షన్ 30 నిషేధిస్తుంది.

selfTest.q: 5. గుర్రపు పందెంలో గెలిచినవారికి ₹1,00,000 బహుమతి కోసం క్లబ్ సభ్యులు చందా ఇవ్వడానికి ఒప్పుకుంటారు. సెక్షన్ 30 కింద ఇది చట్టవిరుద్ధమా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. ఇది గుర్రపు పందెం మినహాయింపు కిందకు వస్తుంది (500 రూపాయలు లేదా ఎక్కువ).

selfTest.q: 6. K.R. Lakshmanan ఏం నిర్ణయించింది?
selfTest.a: గుర్రపు పందెం నైపుణ్యపు ఆట అని ("mere skill" అంటే గణనీయమైన స్థాయి లేదా ప్రాధాన్య స్థాయి నైపుణ్యం); కాబట్టి దానిపై బెట్టింగ్ మద్రాస్ జూద చట్టాల కింద జూదం కాదు.

లక్షణం అర్థం
1. అనిశ్చిత భవిష్యత్ సంఘటన మ్యాచ్ ఫలితం, ఎన్నిక లేదా డ్రా (లేదా పక్షాలకు తెలియని గత సంఘటన)
2. పరస్పర లాభనష్టాల అవకాశం సంఘటన తనకు వ్యతిరేకంగా జరిగితే చెల్లిస్తానని ప్రతి పక్షమూ వాగ్దానం చేస్తుంది
3. ఒకరు గెలవాలి, ఇంకొకరు ఓడాలి ఒక్క పక్షమే ఓడే వీలుంటే అది పందెం కాదు
4. పందెం సొమ్ము తప్ప వేరే ఆసక్తి లేదు పందెం కాసిన డబ్బు తప్ప సంఘటనలో ఏ పక్షానికీ ఆసక్తి లేదు

సందర్భం ఒప్పందం ఫలితం
A రెండు జట్ల మధ్య IPL మ్యాచ్ లో ఓడినవాడు గెలిచినవాడికి ₹5,000 చెల్లించాలని రవి, సునీల్ ఒప్పుకుంటారు పందెం: చెల్లదు
B మ్యాచ్ ముగిసేవరకు ఉంచమని ఇద్దరూ చెరో ₹5,000 తమ స్నేహితుడు కిరణ్ కు ఇస్తారు కిరణ్ stakeholder; గెలుపు సొమ్ము కోసం అతనిపై దావా లేదు
C బుక్ మేకర్ల దగ్గర పందేలు కాసి లాభనష్టాలు పంచుకోవడానికి రవి, సునీల్ భాగస్వామ్యం ఏర్పాటు చేసుకుంటారు పందేలకు అనుబంధం; చట్టవిరుద్ధం కాదు (Gherulal Parakh)
D రవి ప్రీమియం చెల్లిస్తాడు; రవి దుకాణం కాలిపోతే ₹5,00,000 ఇస్తానని బీమా సంస్థ వాగ్దానం చేస్తుంది షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టు: చెల్లుతుంది

అంశం నియమం ఆధారం

law-of-contract-i-u2-t15.subtitle: Sections 31 to 36 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: A contingent contract is a contract to do or not to do something if some event, collateral to the contract, does or does not happen (Section 31). An insurance policy is the everyday example: the insurer pays only if the insured event (fire, theft, death) happens. Sections 32 to 36 say when such a contract can be enforced and when it becomes void : event must happen: enforce after it happens; void if it becomes impossible (Section 32); event must not happen: enforce when it becomes impossible (Section 33); event is a living person's conduct: impossible once he makes it so (Section 34); event within a fixed time: time limit decides (Section 35); impossible event: void from the start (Section 36). In exams, each section with its Illustration earns the marks. In real life these rules govern insurance, guarantees and conditional sales.
legalProvision: Section 31. "Contingent contract" defined. A "contingent contract" is a contract to do or not to do something, if some event, collateral to such contract, does or does not happen. Illustration. A contracts to pay B Rs. 10,000 if B's house is burnt. This is a contingent contract.

Section 32. Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event happening. Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event happens cannot be enforced by law unless and until that event has happened. If the event becomes impossible, such contracts become void. Illustrations. (a) A makes a contract with B to buy B's horse if A survives C. This contract cannot be enforced by law unless and until C dies in A's lifetime. (b) A makes a contract with B to sell a horse to B at a specified price, if C, to whom the horse has been offered, refuses to buy him. The contract cannot be enforced by law unless and until C refuses to buy the horse. (c) A contracts to pay B a sum of money when B marries C. C dies without being married to B. The contract becomes void.

Section 33. Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event not happening. Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event does not happen can be enforced when the happening of that event becomes impossible, and not before. Illustration. A agrees to pay B a sum of money if a certain ship does not return. The ship is sunk. The contract can be enforced when the ship sinks.

Section 34. When event on which contract is contingent to be deemed impossible, if it is the future conduct of a living person. If the future event on which a contract is contingent is the way in which a person will act at an unspecified time, the event shall be considered to become impossible when such person does anything which renders it impossible that he should so act within any definite time, or otherwise than under further contingencies. Illustration. A agrees to pay B a sum of money if B marries C. C marries D. The marriage of B to C must now be considered impossible, although it is possible that D may die and that C may afterwards marry B.

Section 35. When contracts become void which are contingent on happening of specified event within fixed time. Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if a specified uncertain event happens within a fixed time become void if, at the expiration of the time fixed, such event has not happened, or if, before the time fixed, such event becomes impossible. When contracts may be enforced, which are contingent on specified event not happening within fixed time. —Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything, if a specified uncertain event does not happen within a fixed time may be enforced by law when the time fixed has expired and such event has not happened or, before the time fixed has expired, if it becomes certain that such event will not happen. Illustrations. (a) A promises to pay B a sum of money if a certain ship returns within a year. The contract may be enforced if the ship returns within the year, and becomes void if the ship is burnt within the year. (b) A promises to pay B a sum of money if a certain ship does not return within a year. The contract may be enforced if the ship does not return within the year, or is burnt within the year.

Section 36. Agreement contingent on impossible events void. Contingent agreements to do or not to do anything, if an impossible event happens, are void, whether the impossibility of the event is known or not to the parties to the agreement at the time when it is made. Illustrations. (a) A agrees to pay B 1,000 rupees if two straight lines should enclose a space. The agreement is void. (b) A agrees to pay B 1,000 rupees if B will marry A's daughter C. C was dead at the time of the agreement. The agreement is void.
In simple words

A contingent contract is a real contract from the start; only the duty to perform waits for the event. "If it happens" contracts : wait for the event; void if the event becomes impossible. "If it does not happen" contracts: enforce once the event becomes impossible. A time limit sets a cut-off. An event that is impossible from the start makes the agreement void.
en.meaning:
A contingent contract has a promise whose performance depends on an event. Three things mark the event: Mark Meaning Example 1. Future It has not yet happened A fire next year 2. Uncertain It may or may not happen Fire, theft, a ship's return 3. Collateral It is separate from the promised act itself, not the consideration or the performance The fire is not part of what the insurer promises to do The contract exists from the start. What waits is the duty to perform. Collateral, not part of the bargain. If the "event" is simply one party doing his part of the exchange, it is not a contingent event. "I will pay you ₹1,000 when you deliver the books" is an ordinary contract with reciprocal promises, not a contingent contract. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. If yes, the agreement is void (Section 36). If no, does the contract depend on the event happening or not happening? If happening: with a fixed time, enforce if it happens in time, void if the time expires or it becomes impossible (Section 35); without a fixed time, enforce only after it happens, void if it becomes impossible (Section 32). If not happening: with a fixed time, enforce when the time expires without it or it becomes certain it will not happen (Section 35); without a fixed time, enforce when it becomes impossible (Section 33). If the event is a living person's conduct, it is impossible once he makes it so (Section 34).
keyPoints: A contingent contract depends on an uncertain event collateral to the contract (Section 31). If the event must happen, the contract is enforceable once it happens and void if it becomes impossible (Section 32). If the event must not happen, the contract is enforceable once the event becomes impossible (Section 33). A living person's own act can make an event impossible (Section 34). A fixed time adds a cut-off (Section 35). An impossible event makes the agreement void, whether known or not (Section 36). The contract is enforceable, and limitation runs, from the event ( Ramzan v. Hussaini ).

caseLaws.name: Ramzan v
caseLaws.facts: Hussaini (1989) Facts. By an agreement of 23 June 1965, a brother agreed to execute a sale deed of a house to his sister once she redeemed its mortgage. She redeemed it in 1970, served a notice in 1984 and sued for specific performance. The courts below held the suit within time. Principle. The agreement "is a typical illustration of a contingent contract" under Section 31; it "became enforceable as soon as the event of redemption" happened, and the date for performance was fixed by that event, so the three-year period under Article 54 ran from it. The appeal was allowed and the suit dismissed. AIR 1990 SC 529 : (1990) 1 SCC 104. Why it matters. A contingent contract becomes enforceable when the event happens, and limitation runs from then.

selfTest.q: 1. What is a contingent contract?
selfTest.a: A contract to do or not to do something if some event, collateral to the contract, does or does not happen (Section 31).

selfTest.q: 2. When can a contract contingent on an event not happening be enforced?
selfTest.a: When the happening of the event becomes impossible, and not before (Section 33).

selfTest.q: 3. What is the effect of a contingent agreement on an impossible event?
selfTest.a: It is void, whether or not the parties knew of the impossibility (Section 36).

selfTest.q: 4. A promises B ₹1,00,000 if B marries C. C marries D. What is the position?
selfTest.a: The marriage of B to C is considered impossible (Section 34), so the contract becomes void (Section 32).

selfTest.q: 5. A promises to pay B if a ship returns within a year. The ship is burnt in the sixth month. Effect?
selfTest.a: The contract becomes void (Section 35, Illustration (a)).

selfTest.q: 6. Is "I will pay you ₹1,000 when you deliver the books" a contingent contract?
selfTest.a: No. Delivery is B's own performance, not a collateral event.

షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టు మొదటి నుంచే నిజమైన కాంట్రాక్టు; అమలు చేసే బాధ్యత మాత్రమే సంఘటన కోసం ఆగుతుంది. "అది జరిగితే" కాంట్రాక్టులు: సంఘటన కోసం ఆగాలి; సంఘటన అసాధ్యమైతే చెల్లదు. "అది జరగకపోతే" కాంట్రాక్టులు: సంఘటన అసాధ్యమైన వెంటనే అమలు. కాల పరిమితి ఒక గడువు పెడుతుంది. మొదటి నుంచే అసాధ్యమైన సంఘటన ఒప్పందాన్ని చెల్లనిదిగా చేస్తుంది.
te.meaning:
షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టులో ఒక వాగ్దానం అమలు ఒక సంఘటనపై ఆధారపడి ఉంటుంది. ఆ సంఘటనకు మూడు లక్షణాలు: లక్షణం అర్థం ఉదాహరణ 1. భవిష్యత్ ఇంకా జరగలేదు వచ్చే ఏడాది అగ్ని ప్రమాదం 2. అనిశ్చితం జరగవచ్చు, జరగకపోవచ్చు అగ్ని, దొంగతనం, ఓడ తిరిగి రావడం 3. అనుబంధం ( collateral ) వాగ్దానం చేసిన పని నుంచి వేరైనది; ప్రతిఫలం గానీ, అమలు గానీ కాదు అగ్ని ప్రమాదం బీమా సంస్థ చేస్తానన్న పనిలో భాగం కాదు కాంట్రాక్టు మొదటి నుంచే ఉంటుంది. ఆగేది అమలు చేసే బాధ్యత మాత్రమే. అనుబంధం, బేరంలో భాగం కాదు. "సంఘటన" అంటే కేవలం ఒక పక్షం తన వంతు బేరాన్ని నెరవేర్చడమే అయితే, అది షరతుతో కూడిన సంఘటన కాదు. "నువ్వు పుస్తకాలు అందించినప్పుడు ₹1,000 ఇస్తాను" అనేది పరస్పర వాగ్దానాలతో కూడిన సాధారణ కాంట్రాక్టు; షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టు కాదు. Diagram 1 చూడండి.
