selfTest.q: 1. షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టు అంటే ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: కాంట్రాక్టుకు అనుబంధమైన ఏదో సంఘటన జరిగితే లేదా జరగకపోతే, ఏదైనా చేయడానికి లేదా చేయకుండా ఉండడానికి చేసే కాంట్రాక్టు (సెక్షన్ 31).

selfTest.q: 2. సంఘటన జరగకపోవడంపై ఆధారపడిన కాంట్రాక్టు ఎప్పుడు అమలవుతుంది?
selfTest.a: సంఘటన జరగడం అసాధ్యమైనప్పుడు, అంతకు ముందు కాదు (సెక్షన్ 33).

selfTest.q: 3. అసాధ్యమైన సంఘటనపై ఆధారపడిన ఒప్పందం ప్రభావం ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: పక్షాలకు ఆ అసాధ్యత తెలిసినా తెలియకపోయినా అది చెల్లదు (సెక్షన్ 36).

selfTest.q: 4. B, C ని పెళ్లి చేసుకుంటే B కి ₹1,00,000 ఇస్తానని A వాగ్దానం చేస్తాడు. C, D ని పెళ్లి చేసుకుంటుంది. స్థితి ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: B, C ల పెళ్లి అసాధ్యంగా పరిగణించబడుతుంది (సెక్షన్ 34); కాబట్టి కాంట్రాక్టు చెల్లనిది అవుతుంది (సెక్షన్ 32).

selfTest.q: 5. ఒక ఓడ ఏడాదిలోపు తిరిగి వస్తే B కి చెల్లిస్తానని A వాగ్దానం చేస్తాడు. ఆరో నెలలో ఓడ కాలిపోతుంది. ప్రభావం?
selfTest.a: కాంట్రాక్టు చెల్లనిది అవుతుంది (సెక్షన్ 35, Illustration (a)).

selfTest.q: 6. "నువ్వు పుస్తకాలు అందించినప్పుడు ₹1,000 ఇస్తాను" అనేది షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. పుస్తకాలు అందించడం B సొంత అమలు; అనుబంధ సంఘటన కాదు.

law-of-contract-i-u2-t16.subtitle: Sections 2(g), 2(i), 2(j), 19, 56, 64 and 65 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: The Act uses three similar words for three different things: A void agreement is never enforceable. It never became a contract (Section 2(g)). A voidable contract is valid until the party with the option cancels it (Section 2(i)). A void contract was valid when made, but later stops being enforceable (Section 2(j)). These labels decide who can sue, who can walk away, and what happens to money already paid (Sections 64 and 65). In exams, the three definitions, the comparison table and the sources of each earn the marks. In real life they decide whether you can walk away from a deal and get your money back.
legalProvision: Section 2. In this Act the following words and expressions are used in the following senses, unless a contrary intention appears from the context:— (e) Every promise and every set of promises, forming the consideration for each other, is an agreement; (g) An agreement not enforceable by law is said to be void; (h) An agreement enforceable by law is a contract; (i) An agreement which is enforceable by law at the option of one or more of the parties thereto, but not at the option of the other or others, is a voidable contract; (j) A contract which ceases to be enforceable by law becomes void when it ceases to be enforceable.

Section 19. Voidability of agreements without free consent. When consent to an agreement is caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused. A party to a contract whose consent was caused by fraud or misrepresentation, may, if he thinks fit, insist that the contract shall be performed, and that he shall be put in the position in which he would have been if the representations made had been true. Exception. —If such consent was caused by misrepresentation or by silence, fraudulent within the meaning of section 17, the contract, nevertheless, is not voidable, if the party whose consent was so caused had the means of discovering the truth with ordinary diligence. Explanation. —A fraud or misrepresentation which did not cause the consent to a contract of the party on whom such fraud was practised, or to whom such misrepresentation was made, does not render a contract voidable. Illustration (b). A, by a misrepresentation, leads B erroneously to believe that, five hundred maunds of indigo are made annually at A's factory. B examines the accounts of the factory, which show that only four hundred maunds of indigo have been made. After this B buys the factory. The contract is not voidable on account of A's misrepresentation. Illustration (c). A fraudulently informs B that A's estate is free from incumbrance. B thereupon buys the estate. The estate is subject to a mortgage. B may either avoid the contract, or may insist on its being carried out and the mortgage debt redeemed.

Section 19A. Power to set aside contract induced by undue influence. When consent to an agreement is caused by undue influence, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused. Any such contract may be set aside either absolutely or, if the party who was entitled to avoid it has received any benefit thereunder, upon such terms and conditions as to the Court may seem just. Illustration (b). A, a money-lender, advances Rs. 100 to B, an agriculturist, and, by undue influence, induces B to execute a bond for Rs. 200 with interest at 6 per cent. per month. The Court may set the bond aside, ordering B to repay the Rs. 100 with such interest as may seem just.

Section 53 (first part). When a contract contains reciprocal promises, and one party to the contract prevents the other from performing his promise, the contract becomes voidable at the option of the party so prevented; and he is entitled to compensation from the other party for any loss which he may sustain in consequence of the non-performance of the contract.

Section 55 (first two paragraphs). When a party to a contract promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, or certain things at or before specified times, and fails to do any such thing at or before the specified time, the contract, or so much of it as has not been performed, becomes voidable at the option of the promisee, if the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract. Effect of such failure when time is not essential. —If it was not the intention of the parties that time should be of the essence of the contract, the contract does not become voidable by the failure to do such thing at or before the specified time; but the promisee is entitled to compensation from the promisor for any loss occasioned to him by such failure.

Section 56 (first two paragraphs). An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. Contract to do an act afterwards becoming impossible or unlawful. —A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. Illustrations. (a) A agrees with B to discover treasure by magic. The agreement is void. (b) A and B contract to marry each other. Before the time fixed for the marriage, A goes mad. The contract becomes void. (d) A contracts to take in cargo for B at a foreign port. A's Government afterwards declares war against the country in which the port is situated. The contract becomes void when war is declared.

Section 64. Consequences of rescission of voidable contract. When a person at whose option a contract is voidable rescinds it, the other party thereto need not perform any promise therein contained in which he is promisor. The party rescinding a voidable contract shall, if he have received any benefit thereunder from another party to such contract, restore such benefit, so far as may be, to the person from whom it was received.

Section 65. Obligation of person who has received advantage under void agreement, or contract that becomes void. When an agreement is discovered to be void, or when a contract becomes void, any person who has received any advantage under such agreement or contract is bound to restore it, or to make compensation for it to the person from whom he received it. Illustration (d). A contracts to sing for B at a concert for 1,000 rupees, which are paid in advance. A is too ill to sing. A is not bound to make compensation to B for the loss of the profits which B would have made if A had been able to sing, but must refund to B the 1,000 rupees paid in advance.
In simple words

Agreement + enforceable by law = contract . Agreement + not enforceable = void. Voidable = binding until the wronged party chooses to cancel it. Only he has that choice. A contract that later becomes impossible or unlawful becomes void from that moment. The party who cancels a voidable contract gives back what he received (Section 64). Whoever got an advantage under a void agreement or a contract that becomes void gives it back (Section 65).
en.meaning:
The Act builds the three ideas on Section 2: Term Section Meaning Status from the start Agreement 2(e) Promises forming consideration for each other May or may not be enforceable Contract 2(h) Agreement enforceable by law Enforceable Void agreement 2(g) Agreement not enforceable by law Never enforceable Voidable contract 2(i) Enforceable at the option of one or more parties, not the other(s) Enforceable until avoided Void contract 2(j) Contract that ceases to be enforceable Enforceable at first; void later The key questions are always timing and choice : when did it fail, and who decides? See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. Start from the agreement. If it is not enforceable, it is a void agreement. If it is enforceable, it is a contract: valid, voidable at one party's option, or later void when it ceases to be enforceable. flowchart TD A["AGREEMENT (s.2(e))"] VA["VOID AGREEMENT (s.2(g))

A contract may be a valid contract (enforceable by both), a voidable contract (Section 2(i): enforceable at one party's option, e.g. coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation, prevention, time of essence; on rescission restore under Section 64), or a void contract (Section 2(j): valid when made, later ceases to be enforceable, e.g. impossible or unlawful under Section 56; restore under Section 65).
keyPoints: Void agreement: never enforceable (Section 2(g)). Voidable contract: enforceable until the option-holder avoids it (Section 2(i)). Void contract: valid when made, later ceases to be enforceable (Section 2(j)). The wronged party can avoid, or after fraud or misrepresentation insist on performance (Section 19). No avoidance for misrepresentation or fraudulent silence if the party could have found the truth with ordinary diligence (Section 19, Exception). Voidable contracts also arise under Sections 19A, 53 and 55. Section 64: the party who rescinds restores benefits. Section 65: benefits under a void agreement or contract are restored; not for a minor ( Mohori Bibee ).

caseLaws.name: Mohori Bibee v
caseLaws.facts: Dharmodas Ghose (1903) Facts. A minor mortgaged his houses to a money-lender to secure Rs. 20,000; the lender's agent knew he was a minor. The minor sued to set the mortgage aside, and the lender asked for repayment of the money advanced, relying on Sections 64 and 65. Principle. "There is not any such voidable contract as is dealt with in Section 64"; Section 65, "like Section 64, starts from the basis of there being an agreement or contract between competent parties". (1903) LR 30 IA 114 : ILR 30 Cal 539. Why it matters. It marks the limit of Sections 64 and 65: they do not reach a minor's agreement. Satyabrata Ghose v. Mugneeram Bangur & Co. (1953) Facts. A company agreed to sell a plot in a housing scheme in Greater Calcutta and to build roads. In 1941 much of the land was requisitioned for military purposes, and the company told the buyer to treat the agreement as cancelled and take back his earnest money . Principle. "Impossible" in Section 56 is not "physical or literal impossibility"; but a temporary requisition, with no time fixed for the roads, did not upset the foundation of the contract, so it was not frustrated. [1954] SCR 310. Why it matters. It explains when a contract "becomes void" under Section 56, and when it does not.

selfTest.q: 1. What is a voidable contract?
selfTest.a: An agreement enforceable by law at the option of one or more of the parties, but not at the option of the other or others (Section 2(i)).

selfTest.q: 2. How does a void contract differ from a void agreement?
selfTest.a: A void contract was valid when made and later ceases to be enforceable. A void agreement is not enforceable from the start.

selfTest.q: 3. What must a party do who rescinds a voidable contract?
selfTest.a: Restore any benefit he received under it, so far as may be (Section 64).

selfTest.q: 4. A, induced by B's fraud, buys B's land. Can B avoid the contract?
selfTest.a: No. Only the party whose consent was caused by fraud (A) has the option.

selfTest.q: 5. A contracts to marry B. Before the date, A goes mad. Effect?
selfTest.a: The contract becomes void (Section 56, Illustration (b)).

selfTest.q: 6. A is paid ₹10,000 in advance to sing at a wedding and falls too ill to sing. Must A refund it?
selfTest.a: Yes. The contract becomes void, and A must refund the advance, though not B's lost profits (Section 65, compare Illustration (d)).

legalProvision: Section 2. In this Act the following words and expressions are used in the following senses, unless a contrary intention appears from the context:— (e) Every promise and every set of promises, forming the consideration for each other, is an agreement; (g) An agreement not enforceable by law is said to be void; (h) An agreement enforceable by law is a contract; (i) An agreement which is enforceable by law at the option of one or more of the parties thereto, but not at the option of the other or others, is a voidable contract; (j) A contract which ceases to be enforceable by law becomes void when it ceases to be enforceable.

Section 19. Voidability of agreements without free consent. When consent to an agreement is caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused. A party to a contract whose consent was caused by fraud or misrepresentation, may, if he thinks fit, insist that the contract shall be performed, and that he shall be put in the position in which he would have been if the representations made had been true. Exception. —If such consent was caused by misrepresentation or by silence, fraudulent within the meaning of section 17, the contract, nevertheless, is not voidable, if the party whose consent was so caused had the means of discovering the truth with ordinary diligence. Explanation. —A fraud or misrepresentation which did not cause the consent to a contract of the party on whom such fraud was practised, or to whom such misrepresentation was made, does not render a contract voidable. Illustration (b). A, by a misrepresentation, leads B erroneously to believe that, five hundred maunds of indigo are made annually at A's factory. B examines the accounts of the factory, which show that only four hundred maunds of indigo have been made. After this B buys the factory. The contract is not voidable on account of A's misrepresentation. Illustration (c). A fraudulently informs B that A's estate is free from incumbrance. B thereupon buys the estate. The estate is subject to a mortgage. B may either avoid the contract, or may insist on its being carried out and the mortgage debt redeemed.

Section 19A. Power to set aside contract induced by undue influence. When consent to an agreement is caused by undue influence, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused. Any such contract may be set aside either absolutely or, if the party who was entitled to avoid it has received any benefit thereunder, upon such terms and conditions as to the Court may seem just. Illustration (b). A, a money-lender, advances Rs. 100 to B, an agriculturist, and, by undue influence, induces B to execute a bond for Rs. 200 with interest at 6 per cent. per month. The Court may set the bond aside, ordering B to repay the Rs. 100 with such interest as may seem just.

Section 53 (first part). When a contract contains reciprocal promises, and one party to the contract prevents the other from performing his promise, the contract becomes voidable at the option of the party so prevented; and he is entitled to compensation from the other party for any loss which he may sustain in consequence of the non-performance of the contract.

Section 55 (first two paragraphs). When a party to a contract promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, or certain things at or before specified times, and fails to do any such thing at or before the specified time, the contract, or so much of it as has not been performed, becomes voidable at the option of the promisee, if the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract. Effect of such failure when time is not essential. —If it was not the intention of the parties that time should be of the essence of the contract, the contract does not become voidable by the failure to do such thing at or before the specified time; but the promisee is entitled to compensation from the promisor for any loss occasioned to him by such failure.

Section 56 (first two paragraphs). An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. Contract to do an act afterwards becoming impossible or unlawful. —A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. Illustrations. (a) A agrees with B to discover treasure by magic. The agreement is void. (b) A and B contract to marry each other. Before the time fixed for the marriage, A goes mad. The contract becomes void. (d) A contracts to take in cargo for B at a foreign port. A's Government afterwards declares war against the country in which the port is situated. The contract becomes void when war is declared.

Section 64. Consequences of rescission of voidable contract. When a person at whose option a contract is voidable rescinds it, the other party thereto need not perform any promise therein contained in which he is promisor. The party rescinding a voidable contract shall, if he have received any benefit thereunder from another party to such contract, restore such benefit, so far as may be, to the person from whom it was received.

Section 65. Obligation of person who has received advantage under void agreement, or contract that becomes void. When an agreement is discovered to be void, or when a contract becomes void, any person who has received any advantage under such agreement or contract is bound to restore it, or to make compensation for it to the person from whom he received it. Illustration (d). A contracts to sing for B at a concert for 1,000 rupees, which are paid in advance. A is too ill to sing. A is not bound to make compensation to B for the loss of the profits which B would have made if A had been able to sing, but must refund to B the 1,000 rupees paid in advance.

ఒప్పందం + చట్టప్రకారం అమలు = కాంట్రాక్టు. ఒప్పందం + అమలు కాదు = చెల్లనిది. రద్దు చేయదగినది = అన్యాయానికి గురైన పక్షం రద్దు చేయాలని ఎంచుకునేవరకు కట్టుబడి ఉండేది. ఆ ఎంపిక అతనికి మాత్రమే. తర్వాత అసాధ్యమైన లేదా చట్టవిరుద్ధమైన కాంట్రాక్టు ఆ క్షణం నుంచి చెల్లనిది అవుతుంది. రద్దు చేయదగిన కాంట్రాక్టును రద్దు చేసే పక్షం తాను పొందినదాన్ని తిరిగి ఇవ్వాలి (సెక్షన్ 64). చెల్లని ఒప్పందం, లేదా చెల్లనిదిగా మారిన కాంట్రాక్టు కింద ప్రయోజనం పొందినవారు దాన్ని తిరిగి ఇవ్వాలి (సెక్షన్ 65).

selfTest.q: 1. రద్దు చేయదగిన కాంట్రాక్టు అంటే ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: ఒకరు లేదా అంతకంటే ఎక్కువ పక్షాల ఆప్షన్ మేరకు చట్టప్రకారం అమలయ్యే, మిగతావారి ఆప్షన్ మేరకు అమలు కాని ఒప్పందం (సెక్షన్ 2(i)).

selfTest.q: 2. చెల్లని కాంట్రాక్టు చెల్లని ఒప్పందం నుంచి ఎలా వేరు?
selfTest.a: చెల్లని కాంట్రాక్టు చేసినప్పుడు చెల్లుబాటయ్యేది, తర్వాత అమలు కాకుండా పోతుంది. చెల్లని ఒప్పందం మొదటి నుంచే అమలు కాదు.

selfTest.q: 3. రద్దు చేయదగిన కాంట్రాక్టును రద్దు చేసే పక్షం ఏం చేయాలి?
selfTest.a: దాని కింద పొందిన ప్రయోజనాన్ని వీలైనంత మేరకు తిరిగి ఇవ్వాలి (సెక్షన్ 64).

selfTest.q: 4. B మోసంతో A, B భూమిని కొంటాడు. B కాంట్రాక్టును రద్దు చేయగలడా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. మోసంతో సమ్మతి పొందిన పక్షానికి (A) మాత్రమే ఆప్షన్ ఉంది.

selfTest.q: 5. A, B ని పెళ్లి చేసుకోవడానికి కాంట్రాక్టు చేస్తాడు. తేదీకి ముందే A కి మతిస్థిమితం తప్పుతుంది. ప్రభావం?
selfTest.a: కాంట్రాక్టు చెల్లనిది అవుతుంది (సెక్షన్ 56, Illustration (b)).

selfTest.q: 6. ఒక పెళ్లిలో పాడటానికి A కి ₹10,000 ముందుగా ఇచ్చారు; A పాడలేనంత అనారోగ్యం పాలవుతాడు. A దాన్ని తిరిగి ఇవ్వాలా?
selfTest.a: అవును. కాంట్రాక్టు చెల్లనిది అవుతుంది; B కోల్పోయిన లాభాలు కాకపోయినా, A అడ్వాన్స్ తిరిగి ఇవ్వాలి (సెక్షన్ 65, Illustration (d) తో పోల్చండి).

en.meaning:
Under Section 11 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a person is competent to contract if they are of the age of majority, of sound mind, and:

Explanation. Section 11 lays down exactly three tests: age of majority, sound mind, and not being disqualified from contracting by any law to which the person is subject.

As per the Indian Majority Act, 1875, the general age of majority in India is:

Explanation. Section 3 of the Indian Majority Act, 1875 fixes the general age of majority at 18 years, raised to 21 years only where a court-appointed guardian or the Court of Wards is involved before the person turns 18.

A person of unsound mind who is usually insane but has occasional lucid intervals:

Explanation. Section 12's second paragraph allows a person who is usually of unsound mind, but occasionally of sound mind, to make a contract when they are of sound mind — that is, during a lucid interval.

en.meaning:
In Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose (1903), the Privy Council held that a minor's agreement is:

Explanation. The Privy Council held that Sections 10 and 11, read together, make a minor incompetent to contract, so a minor's agreement is void ab initio — void from the very start, not voidable.

In Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose, the lender's attorney knew the borrower was under age. A false statement of age made by the borrower to such a lender:

Explanation. The Privy Council held that a false statement of age made to a person who knows the truth does not estop the minor from pleading infancy. It did not decide whether an estoppel could arise against a minor who deceives an innocent lender.

Under Section 68, necessaries supplied to a minor are recoverable:

Explanation. Section 68 makes the minor's property, not the minor personally, liable to reimburse a supplier of genuine necessaries.

en.meaning:
In Derry v. Peek, the House of Lords held that fraud requires:

Explanation. Derry v. Peek established that fraud requires knowing a statement is false, making it without belief in its truth, or being reckless as to whether it is true — an honest but mistaken belief is not fraud.

Mere silence about a fact that might affect the other party's willingness to contract is:

Explanation. The explanation to Section 17 makes clear that mere silence is not fraud unless the person has a duty to speak (e.g., in a fiduciary relationship) or their silence is itself equivalent to speech.

In Raffles v. Wichelhaus, the contract was held void because:

Explanation. Since two ships named Peerless existed and each party meant a different one, there was no genuine consensus on the subject matter — a bilateral mistake of fact under Section 20, making the agreement void.

A contract is generally NOT voidable merely because:

en.meaning:
Under Section 2(j), a 'void contract' is:

Explanation. Section 2(j) specifically defines a void contract as one that was valid at formation but later becomes unenforceable — distinct from a void agreement (Section 2(g)), which was never enforceable at all.

A voidable contract, under Section 2(i), remains binding:

Explanation. A voidable contract is fully valid and binding unless and until the party with the option to avoid it actually chooses to do so.

Under Section 19, a party whose consent was caused by fraud or misrepresentation may:

Explanation. Section 19 gives the wronged party a real choice: rescind the contract, or affirm it and insist on being put in the position they would have been in had the representation been true.

en.meaning:
In Chikkam Ammiraju v. Chikkam Seshamma, a threat to commit suicide unless a release deed was executed was held to be:

Explanation. The Madras High Court (1917) held that a threat of suicide amounted to coercion under Section 15, since the Court treated the threatened act as one forbidden by the Indian Penal Code. The release deed was voidable.

Which of the following is a key difference between coercion and undue influence?

Explanation. Undue influence, by its nature, requires a relationship in which one party can dominate the other's will; coercion can come from anyone, including a total stranger to the contract.

On the Raghunath Prasad v. Sarju Prasad approach to Section 16, once a relationship of dominance and an unconscionable transaction are shown, the burden of proof:

Explanation. Raghunath Prasad sets a three-stage approach: dominance, then inducement by undue influence, then the burden of proof. Under Section 16(3), once dominance and an unconscionable bargain are shown, the dominant party must prove the transaction was not induced by undue influence. High interest alone, without proof of dominance, raises no presumption.

en.meaning:
A contingent contract, as defined under Section 31, depends on:

Explanation. Section 31 defines a contingent contract as one to do or not do something if an uncertain event, collateral to the contract, happens or does not happen.

Under Section 32, a contract contingent on the happening of an uncertain future event:

Explanation. Section 32 states such a contract cannot be enforced until the event actually happens; it becomes void if the event becomes impossible.

Under Section 33, a contract contingent on the non-happening of an event can be enforced:

Explanation. Section 33 permits enforcement only once the happening of the event becomes impossible.

en.meaning:
Under Section 27, an agreement in restraint of trade is:

Explanation. Section 27 voids agreements restraining a lawful trade, profession, or business, with the sole statutory exception being a reasonable restriction on the seller in a sale of goodwill.

In Madhub Chander v. Raj Coomar Doss, the Calcutta High Court held that even a PARTIAL restraint of trade (limited to one locality) is:

Explanation. Indian courts read Section 27 strictly — unlike English law's 'reasonableness' approach, even a partial restraint of trade is void unless it falls within the statutory goodwill exception.

In Superintendence Company of India v. Krishan Murgai, the majority held that a clause barring the employee from competing for two years after he 'left' the company:

Explanation. Tulzapurkar and Untwalia, JJ. read 'leave' as voluntary departure, so the clause never applied to an employee dismissed by the company. They did not decide the Section 27 question. Sen, J., concurring in the result, held that a post-service restraint is void under Section 27.

en.meaning:
X agrees to sell his car to B for ₹50,000 or ₹1,00,000, with nothing in the agreement showing which price was meant. This agreement is:

Explanation. Since the price term has no fixed, ascertainable meaning and nothing in the agreement resolves which figure applies, it is void for uncertainty under Section 29.

In Gherulal Parakh v. Mahadeodas Maiya, the Supreme Court held that a partnership formed to carry on wagering transactions is:

Explanation. The Court held that wagering agreements are void under Section 30 but are not 'immoral' or otherwise unlawful under Section 23 — so a partnership formed to conduct a wagering business is not itself illegal.

A collateral agreement connected to a main agreement that is merely VOID (but not illegal):

Explanation. A collateral deal made to further an illegal purpose is tainted. If the main agreement is merely void, such as a wager, a collateral deal is not automatically tainted (Gherulal Parakh v. Mahadeodas Maiya). This is the key practical difference between void and illegal.

law-of-contract-i-u3-t1.subtitle: Sections 37 to 67 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: A contract is discharged when the duties it created come to an end. After discharge, neither party can ask the other to perform. Most contracts end by performance. Others end by agreement, by a later event that makes performance impossible, by breach, by operation of law, or by lapse of time. The reason for the ending matters. It decides who can still sue, who must refund, and who must pay damages . A contract that ends by performance leaves nothing to claim. A contract that ends by breach leaves a claim for compensation. In exams, this is a list question: name each mode, give its section and add one example. Section 37 is the starting point, because every mode of discharge is an answer to one question: when is a party freed from the duty to perform?
legalProvision: Section 37. Obligation of parties to contracts. The parties to a contract must either perform, or offer to perform, their respective promises, unless such performance is dispensed with or excused under the provisions of this Act, or of any other law. Promises bind the representatives of the promisors in case of the death of such promisors before performance, unless a contrary intention appears from the contract. Illustrations. (a) A promises to deliver goods to B on a certain day on payment of Rs. 1,000. A dies before that day. A's representatives are bound to deliver the goods to B, and B is bound to pay the Rs. 1,000 to A's representatives. (b) A promises to paint a picture for B by a certain day, at a certain price. A dies before the day. The contract cannot be enforced either by A's representatives or by B.

Section 38. Effect of refusal to accept offer of performance. Where a promisor has made an offer of performance to the promisee, and the offer has not been accepted, the promisor is not responsible for non-performance, nor does he thereby lose his rights under the contract.

Section 39. Effect of refusal of party to perform promise wholly. When a party to a contract has refused to perform, or disabled himself from performing, his promise in its entirety, the promisee may put an end to the contract, unless he has signified, by words or conduct, his acquiescence in its continuance.

Section 56 (second paragraph). A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful.

Section 62. Effect of novation, rescission, and alteration of contract. If the parties to a contract agree to substitute a new contract for it, or to rescind or alter it, the original contract, need not be performed.

Section 63. Promisee may dispense with or remit performance of promisee. Every promisee may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part, the performance of the promisee made to him, or may extend the time for such performance, or may accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit.

Section 65. Obligation of person who has received advantage under void agreement, or contract that becomes void. When an agreement is discovered to be void, or when a contract becomes void, any person who has received any advantage under such agreement or contract is bound to restore it, or to make compensation for it to the person from whom he received it.
Section 2(j). A contract which ceases to be enforceable by law becomes void when it ceases to be enforceable.

Other sections used in this note. Sections 38 to 55 and 67 say how, when, where and by whom performance is made, and what follows if it is refused or delayed. Section 53 (a party prevented from performing may avoid the contract ) and Section 55 (failure to perform on time when time is essential) make the contract voidable. Section 64 deals with rescinding a voidable contract. These are quoted in full in the notes on By performance and Discharge by Breach .
In simple words

Section 37: promises must be kept, or at least offered. The only escape is a ground the law itself allows. Every other section in this unit names one such ground: performance, agreement, impossibility, breach. Some grounds come from outside the Contract Act: insolvency law, the Limitation Act and the Negotiable Instruments Act.
en.meaning:
The Act does not define "discharge". In practice, a contract is discharged when the rights and duties it created are ended. After discharge, neither party can ask the other to perform. The idea behind it. Section 37 starts from the rule that promises must be kept. Discharge is the list of settled situations in which the law says a party is now free: the parties have done what they promised (performance); they have agreed to let each other go (agreement); the law excuses them, because performance has become impossible (impossibility); one party's breach lets the other walk away (breach); the law itself ends the contract (operation of law); the time to sue has run out (lapse of time). Why the law has these rules. A contract cannot bind for ever. The law needs to say clearly when the duty ends, so that each party knows whether it may still sue, must refund money, or must pay compensation. See Diagram 1 for the order in which to test the modes. Diagram 1. Start at the top. If the answer is "Yes", that is the mode of discharge. If it is "No", go to the next question. flowchart TD Q1{"1. Did each party perform,
or validly offer to perform?

cancel or change it, or did the promisee

impossible or unlawful? (s.56)"} Q4{"4. Did one party refuse, fail
or disable himself? (ss.39, 53, 55)"} Q5{"5. Did the law end it, or has
the time to sue run out?"} P["Discharge by PERFORMANCE"] A["Discharge by AGREEMENT"] I["Discharge by IMPOSSIBILITY
contract void by itself; refund (s.65)"] B["Discharge by BREACH
if the innocent party elects to end it"] L["OPERATION OF LAW, or LAPSE OF TIME
(remedy barred, debt survives)"] F["Contract still in force"] Q1 -- "Yes" --> P Q1 -- "No" --> Q2 Q2 -- "Yes" --> A Q2 -- "No" --> Q3 Q3 -- "Yes" --> I Q3 -- "No" --> Q4 Q4 -- "Yes" --> B Q4 -- "No" --> Q5 Q5 -- "Yes" --> L Q5 -- "No" --> F Text description Question 1: did each party perform, or validly offer to perform (Sections 37, 38)? Yes: discharge by performance. Question 2: did the parties agree to replace, cancel or change the contract, or did the promisee remit or accept other satisfaction (Sections 62, 63)? Yes: discharge by agreement. Question 3: did an event after the contract make performance impossible or unlawful (Section 56)? Yes: discharge by impossibility; the contract is void by itself. Question 4: did one party refuse, fail or disable himself (Sections 39, 53, 55)? Yes: discharge by breach, if the other party chooses to end the contract. Question 5: did the law itself end the contract, or has the time to sue run out? Yes: operation of law, or lapse of time (remedy barred). If none applies, the contract is still in force.
keyPoints: Discharge means the end of the duties under a contract. Performance is only one route. Section 37 is the starting rule: perform, or offer to perform. Agreement: Sections 62 and 63. Impossibility: Section 56. Breach: Section 39. Impossibility makes the contract void by itself. Breach gives the innocent party a choice. Operation of law covers death in personal contracts, insolvency, merger and material alteration. Lapse of time bars the remedy but does not erase the debt (Sections 25(3), 60, 61). Money claims may survive discharge: refund under Section 65, damages under Section 73.

caseLaws.name: Taylor v
caseLaws.facts: Caldwell (1863) Facts. By an agreement of 27 May 1861, Caldwell let the Surrey Gardens and Music Hall to Taylor for four days of concerts at £100 a day. Before the first day, the Hall was destroyed by fire without the fault of either party, and Taylor sued for his wasted expenses. Principle. Where performance depends on a thing continuing to exist, the contract is "subject to an implied condition that the parties shall be excused in case, before breach, performance becomes impossible from the perishing of the thing without default of the contractor". Both parties were excused. (1863) 3 B & S 826 : 122 ER 309 (Queen's Bench, Blackburn J.). Why it matters. It is the origin of discharge by impossibility. Hochster v. De La Tour (1853) Facts. In April 1852 De La Tour engaged Hochster as a courier for a European tour from 1 June 1852. On 11 May 1852 he wrote that he had changed his mind. Hochster sued on 22 May, before the date of performance. Principle. On a clear renunciation before the day, the injured party may "sue immediately, or … wait till the time when the act was to be done, still holding it as prospectively binding". (1853) 2 E & B 678 : 118 ER 922 (Queen's Bench, Lord Campbell C.J.). Why it matters. It is the origin of anticipatory breach. Satyabrata Ghose v. Mugneeram Bangur & Co. (1953) Facts. A land company sold building plots, took Rs. 101 as earnest from the buyer and undertook to build roads and drains. In November 1941 the Government requisitioned part of the land for military purposes, and the company said the contract was cancelled. Principle. Section 56 is exhaustive on frustration in India, and "impossible" means practical, not "physical or literal", impossibility. The requisition was temporary and no time was fixed for the work, so the contract was not frustrated. [1954] SCR 310 : AIR 1954 SC 44 (Supreme Court, 16 November 1953, Mukherjea J.). Why it matters. It is the leading Indian authority on discharge by impossibility.

selfTest.q: 2. Which section says what happens when performance later becomes impossible?
selfTest.a: Section 56. The contract becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful.

selfTest.q: 3. Does a breach end a contract automatically?
selfTest.a: No. The innocent party may choose to end it. He loses that right if he accepts its continuance by words or conduct (Section 39).

selfTest.q: 4. A promises to paint a picture for B and dies before the day. Can his son paint it and claim the price?
selfTest.a: No. The contract needs A's personal skill and cannot be enforced by A's representatives or by B (Section 37, Illustration (b)).

selfTest.q: 5. Does the expiry of the limitation period cancel a debt?
selfTest.a: No. It bars the suit. A written signed promise to pay the time-barred debt is a valid contract (Section 25(3)).

When an agreement is discovered to be void, or when a contract becomes void, any person who has received any advantage under such agreement or contract is bound to restore it, or to make compensation for it to the person from whom he received it.
Section 2(j). A contract which ceases to be enforceable by law becomes void when it ceases to be enforceable.

ఈ నోట్‌లో వాడిన ఇతర సెక్షన్లు. నెరవేర్చడం ఎలా, ఎప్పుడు, ఎక్కడ, ఎవరి ద్వారా జరగాలో, దాన్ని తిరస్కరిస్తే లేదా ఆలస్యం చేస్తే ఏమవుతుందో సెక్షన్లు 38 నుంచి 55, 67 చెబుతాయి. సెక్షన్ 53 (నెరవేర్చకుండా అడ్డుకోబడిన పక్షం కాంట్రాక్టును రద్దు చేసుకోవచ్చు), సెక్షన్ 55 (సమయం ముఖ్యమైనప్పుడు సమయానికి నెరవేర్చకపోవడం) కాంట్రాక్టును రద్దు చేయదగినదిగా చేస్తాయి. రద్దు చేయదగిన కాంట్రాక్టును రద్దు చేయడం గురించి సెక్షన్ 64 చెబుతుంది. వీటి పూర్తి పాఠం By performance , Discharge by Breach నోట్లలో ఉంది.
సులభంగా చెప్పాలంటే

సెక్షన్ 37: వాగ్దానాలు నిలబెట్టుకోవాలి, లేదా కనీసం నెరవేర్చడానికి ముందుకు రావాలి. చట్టమే అనుమతించే కారణం ఉంటేనే తప్పించుకోవచ్చు. ఈ యూనిట్‌లోని మిగతా ప్రతి సెక్షన్ అలాంటి ఒక కారణాన్ని చెబుతుంది: నెరవేర్చడం, ఒప్పందం, అసాధ్యత, ఉల్లంఘన. కొన్ని కారణాలు కాంట్రాక్టు చట్టం బయటి నుంచి వస్తాయి: దివాలా చట్టం, Limitation Act, Negotiable Instruments Act.
te.meaning:
చట్టం "discharge" ను నిర్వచించలేదు. ఆచరణలో, కాంట్రాక్టు సృష్టించిన హక్కులు, బాధ్యతలు ముగిసినప్పుడు కాంట్రాక్టు ముగిసినట్టు. ముగిసిన తర్వాత ఏ పక్షమూ అవతలి పక్షాన్ని నెరవేర్చమని అడగలేదు. దీని వెనుక ఉన్న ఆలోచన. వాగ్దానాలు నిలబెట్టుకోవాలనే నియమంతో సెక్షన్ 37 మొదలవుతుంది. ఒక పక్షం ఇప్పుడు స్వేచ్ఛగా ఉందని చట్టం చెప్పే స్థిరమైన పరిస్థితుల జాబితానే ముగింపు: పక్షాలు వాగ్దానం చేసింది చేశాయి (నెరవేర్చడం); ఒకరినొకరు విడిచిపెట్టడానికి ఒప్పుకున్నాయి (ఒప్పందం); నెరవేర్చడం అసాధ్యమైంది కాబట్టి చట్టం వారిని క్షమిస్తుంది (అసాధ్యత); ఒక పక్షం ఉల్లంఘన వల్ల అవతలి పక్షం బయటపడవచ్చు (ఉల్లంఘన); చట్టమే కాంట్రాక్టును ముగిస్తుంది (చట్టం ద్వారా); దావా వేసే గడువు ముగిసింది (కాలం గడవడం). చట్టంలో ఈ నియమాలు ఎందుకు? కాంట్రాక్టు శాశ్వతంగా బంధించలేదు. బాధ్యత ఎప్పుడు ముగుస్తుందో చట్టం స్పష్టంగా చెప్పాలి. అప్పుడే ప్రతి పక్షానికి ఇంకా దావా వేయగలదా, డబ్బు తిరిగి ఇవ్వాలా, నష్టపరిహారం చెల్లించాలా అనేది తెలుస్తుంది. ఈ పద్ధతులను ఏ క్రమంలో పరీక్షించాలో చిత్రం 1 చూపిస్తుంది. Diagram 1. పై నుంచి మొదలుపెట్టండి. సమాధానం "అవును" అయితే అదే ముగింపు పద్ధతి. "కాదు" అయితే తర్వాతి ప్రశ్నకు వెళ్లండి. flowchart TD Q1{"1. ప్రతి పక్షం నెరవేర్చిందా,
లేదా సరిగ్గా ప్రతిపాదించిందా?
(సె.37, 38)"} Q2{"2. కాంట్రాక్టును మార్చడానికి, రద్దు చేయడానికి,
కొత్తది పెట్టడానికి ఒప్పుకున్నారా, లేదా
మాఫీ లేదా వేరే తీర్పు అంగీకరించారా?
(సె.62, 63)"} Q3{"3. తర్వాతి సంఘటన నెరవేర్చడాన్ని
అసాధ్యం లేదా చట్టవిరుద్ధం చేసిందా? (సె.56)"} Q4{"4. ఒక పక్షం నిరాకరించిందా, విఫలమైందా,
అశక్తం చేసుకుందా? (సె.39, 53, 55)"} Q5{"5. చట్టమే ముగించిందా, లేదా
దావా గడువు ముగిసిందా?"} P["నెరవేర్చడం ద్వారా ముగింపు"] A["ఒప్పందం ద్వారా ముగింపు"] I["అసాధ్యత ద్వారా ముగింపు
కాంట్రాక్టు దానంతట అదే చెల్లదు; వాపసు (సె.65)"] B["ఉల్లంఘన ద్వారా ముగింపు
నిర్దోష పక్షం ముగించాలని ఎంచుకుంటే"] L["చట్టం ద్వారా, లేదా కాలం గడవడం
(దావా నిషేధం, అప్పు మిగులుతుంది)"] F["కాంట్రాక్టు ఇంకా అమలులో ఉంది"] Q1 -- "అవును" --> P Q1 -- "కాదు" --> Q2 Q2 -- "అవును" --> A Q2 -- "కాదు" --> Q3 Q3 -- "అవును" --> I Q3 -- "కాదు" --> Q4 Q4 -- "అవును" --> B Q4 -- "కాదు" --> Q5 Q5 -- "అవును" --> L Q5 -- "కాదు" --> F వచన వివరణ ప్రశ్న 1: ప్రతి పక్షం నెరవేర్చిందా, లేదా సరిగ్గా నెరవేర్చడానికి ప్రతిపాదించిందా (సెక్షన్లు 37, 38)? అవును: నెరవేర్చడం ద్వారా ముగింపు. ప్రశ్న 2: కాంట్రాక్టును మార్చడానికి, రద్దు చేయడానికి, కొత్తది పెట్టడానికి పక్షాలు ఒప్పుకున్నాయా, లేదా వాగ్దానగ్రహీత మాఫీ చేశాడా, వేరే తీర్పు అంగీకరించాడా (సెక్షన్లు 62, 63)? అవును: ఒప్పందం ద్వారా ముగింపు. ప్రశ్న 3: కాంట్రాక్టు తర్వాత సంఘటన నెరవేర్చడాన్ని అసాధ్యం లేదా చట్టవిరుద్ధం చేసిందా (సెక్షన్ 56)? అవును: అసాధ్యత ద్వారా ముగింపు; కాంట్రాక్టు దానంతట అదే చెల్లదు. ప్రశ్న 4: ఒక పక్షం నిరాకరించిందా, విఫలమైందా, అశక్తం చేసుకుందా (సెక్షన్లు 39, 53, 55)? అవును: అవతలి పక్షం ముగించాలని ఎంచుకుంటే ఉల్లంఘన ద్వారా ముగింపు. ప్రశ్న 5: చట్టమే కాంట్రాక్టును ముగించిందా, లేదా దావా గడువు ముగిసిందా? అవును: చట్టం ద్వారా ముగింపు, లేదా కాలం గడవడం (దావా నిషేధం). ఏదీ వర్తించకపోతే కాంట్రాక్టు ఇంకా అమలులో ఉంది.

selfTest.q: 1. కాంట్రాక్టు ఏ పద్ధతుల్లో ముగుస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: నెరవేర్చడం, ఒప్పందం, అసాధ్యత, ఉల్లంఘన, చట్టం ద్వారా, కాలం గడవడం.

selfTest.q: 2. నెరవేర్చడం తర్వాత అసాధ్యమైతే ఏమవుతుందో ఏ సెక్షన్ చెబుతుంది?
selfTest.a: సెక్షన్ 56. ఆ పని అసాధ్యం లేదా చట్టవిరుద్ధం అయినప్పుడు కాంట్రాక్టు చెల్లనిది అవుతుంది.

selfTest.q: 3. ఉల్లంఘన దానంతట అదే కాంట్రాక్టును ముగిస్తుందా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. నిర్దోష పక్షం దాన్ని ముగించాలని ఎంచుకోవచ్చు. కాంట్రాక్టు కొనసాగడాన్ని మాటల ద్వారా గానీ ప్రవర్తన ద్వారా గానీ అంగీకరిస్తే ఆ హక్కు పోతుంది (సెక్షన్ 39).

selfTest.q: 4. B కి బొమ్మ వేస్తానని A వాగ్దానం చేసి, ఆ రోజుకు ముందే చనిపోతాడు. అతని కొడుకు బొమ్మ వేసి ధర కోరవచ్చా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. కాంట్రాక్టుకు A వ్యక్తిగత నైపుణ్యం అవసరం; దాన్ని A ప్రతినిధులు గానీ B గానీ అమలు చేయించలేరు (సెక్షన్ 37, Illustration (b)).

selfTest.q: 5. limitation గడువు ముగిస్తే అప్పు రద్దవుతుందా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. దావా మాత్రమే నిషేధించబడుతుంది. కాలదోషం పట్టిన అప్పు చెల్లిస్తానని రాతపూర్వకంగా సంతకం చేసి ఇచ్చిన వాగ్దానం చెల్లుబాటయ్యే కాంట్రాక్టు (సెక్షన్ 25(3)).

visuals.caption: Diagram 1. పై నుంచి మొదలుపెట్టండి. సమాధానం "అవును" అయితే అదే ముగింపు పద్ధతి. "కాదు" అయితే తర్వాతి ప్రశ్నకు వెళ్లండి.

కాంట్రాక్టు ఏం జరిగింది పద్ధతి
A ఒక దర్జీ ₹3,000కు 1 జూన్ లోగా ఆమెకు సూట్ కుడతాడు. సమయానికి ఇస్తాడు, ఆమె డబ్బు చెల్లిస్తుంది నెరవేర్చడం
B మీనా తన సరఫరాదారుకు ₹5,000 బాకీ. గడువు రోజున ₹2,000 చెల్లిస్తుంది, అతను దాన్ని పూర్తి తీర్పుగా అంగీకరిస్తాడు ఒప్పందం
C 15 డిసెంబర్ ఫ్యాషన్ షో కోసం ఒక హాల్ బుక్ చేస్తుంది. 1 డిసెంబర్‌న ప్రమాదవశాత్తు అగ్నిలో అది కాలిపోతుంది అసాధ్యత
D ఒక మోడల్ రెండు నెలల పాటు వారానికి రెండు షోలలో నడుస్తానని వాగ్దానం చేస్తుంది. ఆరో షోకి కావాలనే రాదు ఉల్లంఘన
E ఒక చిత్రకారుడు ఒక రోజులోగా ఆమె షాప్ బోర్డు వేస్తానని వాగ్దానం చేసి, ఆ రోజుకు ముందే చనిపోతాడు చట్టం ద్వారా
F ఒక కస్టమర్ 2021 ఆర్డర్‌కు ఆమెకు ₹40,000 బాకీ; ఆమె ఎప్పుడూ దావా వేయదు కాలం గడవడం

పద్ధతి మిగిలే డబ్బు క్లెయిమ్ సెక్షన్
అసాధ్యత పొందిన ప్రయోజనం తిరిగి ఇవ్వడం, ఉదా: అడ్వాన్స్ వాపసు 65

law-of-contract-i-u3-t2.subtitle: Sections 37 to 55 and 67 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: Performance is the normal way a contract ends. Each party does what he promised, and the duties are over. The Act also protects a promisor who tries to perform and is turned away: a proper tender that is refused counts in his favour (Section 38). The Act answers practical questions. Who may perform? When and where? Who goes first when both sides owe something? What if time was important? Sections 37 to 55 and 67 answer each in turn. In exams, tender under Section 38 and time under Section 55 earn the marks. In real life, these rules decide whether a late or refused delivery is a breach .
legalProvision: Section 37. Obligation of parties to contracts. The parties to a contract must either perform, or offer to perform, their respective promises, unless such performance is dispensed with or excused under the provisions of this Act, or of any other law. Promises bind the representatives of the promisors in case of the death of such promisors before performance, unless a contrary intention appears from the contract.

Section 38. Effect of refusal to accept offer of performance. Where a promisor has made an offer of performance to the promisee, and the offer has not been accepted, the promisor is not responsible for non-performance, nor does he thereby lose his rights under the contract. Every such offer must fulfil the following conditions:— (1) it must be unconditional; (2) it must be made at a proper time and place, and under such circumstances that the person to whom it is made may have a reasonable opportunity of ascertaining that the person by whom it is made is able and willing there and then to do the whole of what he is bound by his promise to do; (3) if the offer is an offer to deliver anything to the promisee, the promisee must have a reasonable opportunity of seeing that the thing offered is the thing which the promisor is bound by his promise to deliver. An offer to one of several joint promisees has the same legal consequences as an offer to all of them.

Section 40. Person by whom promise is to be performed. If it appears from the nature of the case that it was the intention of the parties to any contract that any promise contained in it should be performed by the promisor himself, such promise must be performed by the promisor. In other cases, the promisor or his representatives may employ a competent person to perform it.
Section 41. Effect of accepting performance from third person. When a promisee accepts performance of the promise from a third person, he cannot afterwards enforce it against the promisor.

Section 46. Where, by the contract, a promisor is to perform his promise without application by the promisee, and no time for performance is specified, the engagement must be performed within a reasonable time. Explanation. —The question "what is a reasonable time" is, in each particular case, a question of fact.

Section 47. When a promise is to be performed on a certain day, and the promisor has undertaken to perform it without application by the promisee, the promisor may perform it at any time during the usual hours of business on such day and at the place at which the promise ought to be performed.

Section 48. When a promise is to be performed on a certain day, and the promisor has not undertaken to perform it without application by the promisee, it is the duty of the promisee to apply for performance at a proper place and within the usual hours of business.

Section 49. When a promise is to be performed without application by the promisee, and no place is fixed for the performance of it, it is the duty of the promisor to apply to the promisee to appoint a reasonable place for the performance of the promise, and to perform it at such place.
Section 50. The performance of any promise may be made in any manner, or at any time which the promisee prescribes or sanctions.

Section 51. When a contract consists of reciprocal promises to be simultaneously performed, no promisor need perform his promise unless the promisee is ready and willing to perform his reciprocal promise.

Section 52. Where the order in which reciprocal promises are to be performed is expressly fixed by the contract, they shall be performed in that order; and where the order is not expressly fixed by the contract, they shall be performed in that order which the nature of the transaction requires.

Section 53. When a contract contains reciprocal promises, and one party to the contract prevents the other from performing his promise, the contract becomes voidable at the option of the party so prevented; and he is entitled to compensation from the other party for any loss which he may sustain in consequence of the non-performance of the contract.

Section 54. When a contract consists of reciprocal promises, such that one of them cannot be performed, or that its performance cannot be claimed till the other has been performed, and the promisor of the promise last mentioned fails to perform it, such promisor cannot claim the performance of the reciprocal promise, and must make compensation to the other party to the contract for any loss which such other party may sustain by the non-performance of the contract.

Section 55. Effect of failure to perform at fixed time, in contract in which time is essential. When a party to a contract promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, or certain things at or before specified times, and fails to do any such thing at or before the specified time, the contract, or so much of it as has not been performed, becomes voidable at the option of the promisee, if the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract. Effect of such failure when time is not essential. —If it was not the intention of the parties that time should be of the essence of the contract, the contract does not become voidable by the failure to do such thing at or before the specified time; but the promisee is entitled to compensation from the promisor for any loss occasioned to him by such failure. Effect of acceptance of performance at time other than that agreed upon. —If, in case of a contract voidable on account of the promisor's failure to perform his promise at the time agreed, the promisee accepts performance of such promise at any time other than that agreed, the promisee cannot claim compensation for any loss occasioned by the non-performance of the promise at the time agreed, unless, at the time of such acceptance, he gives notice to the promisor of his intention to do so. Uttar Pradesh amendment (U.P. Act 57 of 1976, s. 26). In the third paragraph, for the words "unless at the time of such acceptance he gives notice to the promiser of his intention to do so", the words "where at the time of such acceptance he has waived his right to do so" are substituted.

Section 67. Effect of neglect of promisee to afford promisor reasonable facilities for performance. If any promisee neglects or refuses to afford the promisor reasonable facilities for the performance of his promise, the promisor is excused by such neglect or refusal as to any non-performance caused thereby.
Sections 42 to 45 (joint promises) are quoted in the note on Performance by joint promisors .
In simple words

Perform, or offer to perform (Section 37). A proper offer that is refused protects you (Section 38). Personal promises must be performed personally; others may be performed through someone competent (Section 40). Time, place and manner come from the contract , or from Sections 46 to 50. In reciprocal promises , each side's duty depends on the other's readiness and on the order of performance (Sections 51 to 54). Late performance makes the contract voidable only if time was of the essence (Section 55).
en.meaning:
Discharge by performance has two forms. Form What happens Effect Actual performance The promisor does what he promised and the promisee accepts it The promise is discharged Attempted performance (tender) The promisor offers to perform, and the promisee refuses The promisor is not responsible for non-performance and keeps his rights (Section 38) Why the law values a tender. The promisor has done all he can. It would be unjust to call him a defaulter when the other side stopped performance. Why the other rules exist. The rules on who, when, where and in what order give both sides a fair way to know what each must do and when. Without them, every late or refused delivery would become a dispute about what was expected. See Diagram 1 to test whether an offer of performance is a valid tender. Diagram 1. Question 2: is it made at a proper time and place, so that the promisee can see the promisor is able and willing there and then to do the whole (Section 38(2))? Question 3: if goods are offered, can the promisee see that they are the goods promised (Section 38(3))? A "No" to any question: not a valid tender. "Yes" to all: a valid tender. If the promisee refuses it, the promisor is not responsible for non-performance and keeps his rights under the contract.
keyPoints: Performance is actual (accepted) or attempted (a tender that is refused). A valid tender is unconditional, at a proper time and place, and for the whole promise (Section 38). A refused valid tender protects the promisor and keeps his rights. Personal contracts must be performed by the promisor. Others may be performed through a competent person (Section 40). Accepting performance from a third person bars a later claim against the promisor (Section 41). In reciprocal promises, the party who must perform first and fails cannot claim the other's performance (Section 54). Time of the essence makes a late performance voidable. Otherwise only compensation is due (Section 55). A promisee who refuses reasonable facilities excuses the promisor (Section 67).

caseLaws.name: Saradamani Kandappan v
caseLaws.facts: S. Rajalakshmi (2011) Facts. On 17 January 1981 the sellers agreed to sell 24 acres 95 cents of land to the buyer for Rs. 3.75 lakh. Clause 6 said payment of the instalments on the due dates "was the essence of the contract". The buyer did not pay the later instalments on time, and the sellers cancelled. Principle. Time is normally not of the essence in a land sale, but where the contract makes the payment dates essential, time is of the essence for payment (though not for execution of the sale deed). The Court added that, given steep price rises, a buyer "can no longer take shelter under the principle that time is not of essence" to cover his delays. [2011] 8 SCR 874 (Supreme Court, 4 July 2011). Why it matters. It shows Section 55 at work: the parties' intention, read from the terms, decides whether time is essential. K.S. Vidyanadam v. Vairavan (1997) Facts. On 15 December 1978 the sellers agreed to sell a house in Madurai for Rs. 60,000, with a six-month period for the buyer to act. The buyer paid Rs. 5,000 and then did nothing for over two and a half years, until a notice on 11 July 1981. Principle. "Even where time is not the essence of the contract, the plaintiff must perform his part of the contract within a reasonable time." Specific performance was refused. (1997) 3 SCC 1 (Supreme Court, 6 February 1997). Why it matters. Delay can defeat a claim even when time is not of the essence.

selfTest.q: 1. What makes a tender valid?
selfTest.a: It must be unconditional, made at a proper time and place, and in the case of goods allow the promisee to see that they are as promised (Section 38).

selfTest.q: 2. What is the effect of a valid tender that the promisee refuses?
selfTest.a: The promisor is not responsible for non-performance and does not lose his rights under the contract.

selfTest.q: 3. When does late performance make a contract voidable?
selfTest.a: When the parties intended time to be of the essence. If not, the promisee may claim only compensation (Section 55).

selfTest.q: 4. A brings goods to B's warehouse on the due day, but after closing time. Has A performed?
selfTest.a: No (Section 47, Illustration).

selfTest.q: 5. B owes A Rs. 100 and A asks him to post a note. When is the debt discharged?
selfTest.a: As soon as B posts the letter containing the note, duly addressed to A (Section 50, Illustration (d)).

నెరవేర్చండి, లేదా నెరవేర్చడానికి ప్రతిపాదించండి (సెక్షన్ 37). తిరస్కరించబడిన సరైన ప్రతిపాదన మిమ్మల్ని రక్షిస్తుంది (సెక్షన్ 38). వ్యక్తిగత వాగ్దానాలను స్వయంగా నెరవేర్చాలి; మిగతావి సమర్థుడైన వేరొకరి ద్వారా నెరవేర్చవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 40). సమయం, స్థలం, పద్ధతి కాంట్రాక్టు నుంచి గానీ, సెక్షన్లు 46 నుంచి 50 నుంచి గానీ వస్తాయి. పరస్పర వాగ్దానాల్లో ప్రతి పక్షం బాధ్యత అవతలి పక్షం సంసిద్ధతపై, నెరవేర్చే క్రమంపై ఆధారపడుతుంది (సెక్షన్లు 51 నుంచి 54). సమయమే ప్రధానమైతేనే ఆలస్యంగా నెరవేర్చడం కాంట్రాక్టును రద్దు చేయదగినదిగా చేస్తుంది (సెక్షన్ 55).

నెరవేర్చడం ద్వారా ముగింపుకు రెండు రూపాలు ఉన్నాయి. రూపం ఏం జరుగుతుంది ప్రభావం వాస్తవంగా నెరవేర్చడం (actual performance) వాగ్దానకర్త వాగ్దానం చేసింది చేస్తాడు, వాగ్దానగ్రహీత అంగీకరిస్తాడు వాగ్దానం తీరిపోతుంది నెరవేర్చే ప్రయత్నం (టెండర్) వాగ్దానకర్త నెరవేర్చడానికి ప్రతిపాదిస్తాడు, వాగ్దానగ్రహీత తిరస్కరిస్తాడు నెరవేర్చకపోవడానికి వాగ్దానకర్త బాధ్యుడు కాదు, తన హక్కులు కోల్పోడు (సెక్షన్ 38) టెండర్‌కు చట్టం ఎందుకు విలువ ఇస్తుంది? వాగ్దానకర్త చేయగలిగిందంతా చేశాడు. అవతలి పక్షమే నెరవేర్చడాన్ని ఆపినప్పుడు అతన్ని ఎగవేతదారు అనడం అన్యాయం. మిగతా నియమాలు ఎందుకు? ఎవరు, ఎప్పుడు, ఎక్కడ, ఏ క్రమంలో అనే నియమాలు ప్రతి పక్షం ఏం చేయాలో, ఎప్పుడు చేయాలో తెలుసుకోవడానికి న్యాయమైన మార్గం ఇస్తాయి. అవి లేకపోతే ప్రతి ఆలస్యమైన లేదా తిరస్కరించబడిన డెలివరీ ఏం ఆశించారనే వివాదంగా మారుతుంది. నెరవేర్చే ప్రతిపాదన సరైన టెండర్ అవుతుందా అని పరీక్షించడానికి చిత్రం 1 చూడండి. Diagram 1. ప్రశ్నలను క్రమంగా చూడండి. ఏ ఒక్కదానికి "కాదు" అయినా అది సరైన టెండర్ కాదు. flowchart TD S["వాగ్దానకర్త నెరవేర్చడానికి ప్రతిపాదిస్తాడు"] Q1{"1. ప్రతిపాదన షరతులు లేనిదా?
(సె.38(1))"} Q2{"2. సరైన సమయం, స్థలంలో, అప్పటికప్పుడే
మొత్తం చేయగలడని, సిద్ధంగా ఉన్నాడని
వాగ్దానగ్రహీత చూసుకోగలడా? (సె.38(2))"} Q3{"3. సరుకులైతే: అవి వాగ్దానం చేసినవేనని
వాగ్దానగ్రహీత చూసుకోగలడా? (సె.38(3))"} N["సరైన టెండర్ కాదు"] V["సరైన టెండర్
తిరస్కరిస్తే: నెరవేర్చకపోవడానికి
వాగ్దానకర్త బాధ్యుడు కాదు; హక్కులు ఉంటాయి"] S --> Q1 Q1 -- "కాదు" --> N Q1 -- "అవును" --> Q2 Q2 -- "కాదు" --> N Q2 -- "అవును" --> Q3 Q3 -- "కాదు" --> N Q3 -- "అవును, లేదా సరుకులు కావు" --> V వచన వివరణ ప్రశ్న 1: ప్రతిపాదన షరతులు లేనిదా (సెక్షన్ 38(1))? ప్రశ్న 2: వాగ్దానకర్త అప్పటికప్పుడే మొత్తం చేయగలడని, సిద్ధంగా ఉన్నాడని వాగ్దానగ్రహీత చూసుకునేలా సరైన సమయం, స్థలంలో చేశారా (సెక్షన్ 38(2))? ప్రశ్న 3: సరుకులు ఇస్తుంటే, అవి వాగ్దానం చేసినవేనని వాగ్దానగ్రహీత చూసుకోగలడా (సెక్షన్ 38(3))? ఏ ప్రశ్నకైనా "కాదు": సరైన టెండర్ కాదు. అన్నింటికీ "అవును": సరైన టెండర్. వాగ్దానగ్రహీత దాన్ని తిరస్కరిస్తే, నెరవేర్చకపోవడానికి వాగ్దానకర్త బాధ్యుడు కాదు, కాంట్రాక్టు కింద హక్కులు ఉంటాయి.

selfTest.q: 1. టెండర్ సరైనది కావాలంటే ఏం కావాలి?
selfTest.a: అది షరతులు లేనిదై, సరైన సమయం, స్థలంలో చేయబడి, సరుకుల విషయంలో అవి వాగ్దానం చేసినవేనని వాగ్దానగ్రహీత చూసుకునే అవకాశం ఇవ్వాలి (సెక్షన్ 38).

selfTest.q: 2. వాగ్దానగ్రహీత తిరస్కరించిన సరైన టెండర్ ప్రభావం ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: నెరవేర్చకపోవడానికి వాగ్దానకర్త బాధ్యుడు కాదు, కాంట్రాక్టు కింద తన హక్కులు కోల్పోడు.

selfTest.q: 3. ఆలస్యమైన నెరవేర్పు కాంట్రాక్టును ఎప్పుడు రద్దు చేయదగినదిగా చేస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: సమయమే ప్రధానమని పక్షాలు ఉద్దేశించినప్పుడు. లేకపోతే వాగ్దానగ్రహీత పరిహారం మాత్రమే కోరవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 55).

selfTest.q: 4. గడువు రోజున, కానీ మూసే సమయం తర్వాత, A సరుకులను B గిడ్డంగికి తెస్తాడు. A నెరవేర్చాడా?
selfTest.a: లేదు (సెక్షన్ 47, Illustration).

selfTest.q: 5. B, A కి Rs. 100 బాకీ; నోటు పోస్టులో పంపమని A అడుగుతాడు. అప్పు ఎప్పుడు తీరుతుంది?
selfTest.a: A కి సరైన చిరునామాతో, నోటు ఉన్న లేఖను B పోస్టులో వేసిన వెంటనే (సెక్షన్ 50, Illustration (d)).

visuals.html:
రూపం ఏం జరుగుతుంది ప్రభావం
వాస్తవంగా నెరవేర్చడం (actual performance) వాగ్దానకర్త వాగ్దానం చేసింది చేస్తాడు, వాగ్దానగ్రహీత అంగీకరిస్తాడు వాగ్దానం తీరిపోతుంది
నెరవేర్చే ప్రయత్నం (టెండర్) వాగ్దానకర్త నెరవేర్చడానికి ప్రతిపాదిస్తాడు, వాగ్దానగ్రహీత తిరస్కరిస్తాడు నెరవేర్చకపోవడానికి వాగ్దానకర్త బాధ్యుడు కాదు, తన హక్కులు కోల్పోడు (సెక్షన్ 38)

visuals.caption: Diagram 1. ప్రశ్నలను క్రమంగా చూడండి. ఏ ఒక్కదానికి "కాదు" అయినా అది సరైన టెండర్ కాదు.

visuals.html:
పరిస్థితి సెక్షన్
ఆశ 1 మార్చిన భరత్ గిడ్డంగికి 100 బేళ్ల పత్తిని ₹6,00,000కు ఇవ్వాలి; డెలివరీపై చెల్లింపు 38, 47, 51
భరత్ ఆర్డర్ చేసిన 20 అదనపు బేళ్లను ఆశ తమ్ముడు ఇస్తాడు, భరత్ అంగీకరిస్తాడు 41
రెండో లాట్ పంపే ముందు భరత్ లెటర్ ఆఫ్ క్రెడిట్ తెరవాలి 52, 54
మూడో లాట్ కోసం ఆశ లారీని మిల్ గేటు లోపలికి రానివ్వడానికి భరత్ నిరాకరిస్తాడు 53, 67

పరిస్థితి నియమం సెక్షన్
సమయం నిర్ణయించలేదు, అడగాల్సిన అవసరం లేదు సహేతుక సమయంలో నెరవేర్చాలి; ఏది సహేతుకమో అది వాస్తవ ప్రశ్న 46
రోజు నిర్ణయించారు, అడగాల్సిన అవసరం లేదు ఆ రోజు సాధారణ పని వేళల్లో ఎప్పుడైనా, సరైన చోట నెరవేర్చవచ్చు 47
రోజు నిర్ణయించారు, అడగాల్సిన అవసరం ఉంది వాగ్దానగ్రహీత సరైన చోట, సాధారణ పని వేళల్లో నెరవేర్చమని అడగాలి 48
స్థలం నిర్ణయించలేదు, అడగాల్సిన అవసరం లేదు సహేతుక స్థలాన్ని నిర్ణయించమని వాగ్దానకర్త వాగ్దానగ్రహీతను అడిగి, అక్కడ నెరవేర్చాలి 49
వాగ్దానగ్రహీత పద్ధతి లేదా సమయం నిర్ణయిస్తాడు అతను నిర్ణయించిన లేదా ఆమోదించిన పద్ధతిలో, సమయంలో నెరవేర్చడం సరైనదే 50

సెక్షన్ పరిస్థితి నియమం
37 నెరవేర్చే బాధ్యత నెరవేర్చాలి లేదా ప్రతిపాదించాలి; వ్యక్తిగత కాంట్రాక్టులు తప్ప ప్రతినిధులను బంధిస్తుంది
38 టెండర్ తిరస్కరణ టెండర్ షరతులు లేనిదై, సరైన సమయం, స్థలంలో జరిగి, సరుకులు పరిశీలించగలిగితే, వాగ్దానకర్త బాధ్యుడు కాదు, హక్కులు ఉంటాయి
40, 41 ఎవరు నెరవేర్చాలి కాంట్రాక్టు కోరితే స్వయంగా; లేకపోతే సమర్థుడైన వ్యక్తి. మూడో వ్యక్తి నెరవేర్పును అంగీకరిస్తే వాగ్దానకర్తపై క్లెయిమ్ ఉండదు
46 సమయం నిర్ణయించలేదు, అడగనవసరం లేదు సహేతుక సమయంలో నెరవేర్చాలి
47 రోజు నిర్ణయించారు, అడగనవసరం లేదు ఆ రోజు సాధారణ పని వేళల్లో, సరైన చోట
48 రోజు నిర్ణయించారు, అడగాల్సిన అవసరం ఉంది వాగ్దానగ్రహీత సరైన చోట, సమయంలో అడగాలి
49 స్థలం నిర్ణయించలేదు, అడగనవసరం లేదు సహేతుక స్థలాన్ని చెప్పమని వాగ్దానకర్త అడగాలి
50 వాగ్దానగ్రహీత పద్ధతి లేదా సమయం నిర్ణయిస్తాడు ఆ పద్ధతిలో, ఆ సమయంలో నెరవేర్చడం సరైనదే
51 నుంచి 54 పరస్పర వాగ్దానాలు అవతలి పక్షం సంసిద్ధత; నెరవేర్చే క్రమం; అడ్డుకోవడం; మొదటి వాగ్దానంలో వైఫల్యం

law-of-contract-i-u3-t3.subtitle: Sections 59 to 61 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: A debtor may owe a creditor several distinct debts and pay less than the total. Appropriation decides which debt that payment clears. The order is fixed by law: The debtor chooses first (Section 59). If he does not, the creditor chooses (Section 60). If neither chooses, the law decides : the earliest debt is cleared first (Section 61). In exams, this three-step order earns the marks. In real life, it settles which loan or invoice a part payment has cleared.
legalProvision: Section 59. Application of payment where debt to be discharged is indicated. Where a debtor, owing several distinct debts to one person, makes a payment to him, either with express intimation, or under circumstances implying, that the payment is to be applied to the discharge of some particular debt, the payment, if accepted, must be applied accordingly. Illustration (a): A owes B, among other debts, 1,000 rupees upon a promissory note which falls due on the first June. He owes B no other debt of that amount. On the first June, A pays to B 1,000 rupees. The payment is to be applied to the discharge of the promissory note. Illustration (b): A owes to B, among other debts, the sum of 567 rupees. B writes to A and demands payment of this sum. A sends to B 567 rupees. This payment is to be applied to the discharge of the debt of which B had demanded payment.

Section 60. Application of payment where debt to be discharged is not indicated. Where the debtor has omitted to intimate and there are no other circumstances indicating to which debt the payment is to be applied, the creditor may apply it at his discretion to any lawful debt actually due and payable to him from the debtor, whether its recovery is or is not barred by the law in force for the time being as to the limitation of suits.

Section 61. Application of payment where neither party appropriates. Where neither party makes any appropriation, the payment shall be applied in discharge of the debts in order of time, whether they are or are not barred by the law in force for the time being as to the limitation of suits. If the debts are of equal standing, the payment shall be applied in discharge of each proportionably.
In simple words

Section 59: the debtor says, or the facts show, which debt the money is for. If the creditor accepts the money, he must apply it to that debt. Section 60: the debtor says nothing and the facts show nothing. The creditor may apply it to any lawful debt that is actually due and payable , even a time-barred debt . Section 61: nobody chooses. The payment clears the debts in order of time , earliest first, even time-barred ones. Debts of equal standing share it in proportion .
en.meaning:
Appropriation of payments means applying a payment to a particular debt out of several debts.

The question arises only when all of these are present:

One debtor. One creditor. Several distinct debts owed by that debtor to that creditor. A payment that is not enough to clear all of them.

If there is only one debt, there is nothing to choose, so Sections 59 to 61 do not apply.

Why the choice matters. Debts are not all the same. One may carry high interest. One may be secured by a mortgage or a surety . One may be close to becoming time-barred. So which debt is cleared changes the rights of both parties.

Why this order. The money belongs to the debtor, so he gets the first say. If he is silent, the creditor gets the next say. If both are silent, the law applies a fixed rule so that no dispute is left open.
keyPoints: Appropriation arises only with one debtor, one creditor, several distinct debts and an insufficient payment. Order: debtor (Section 59) → creditor (Section 60) → law (Section 61). Section 59: direction may be express or implied; the creditor must follow it if he accepts the payment. Section 60: creditor may choose any lawful debt actually due and payable, even a time-barred one. Section 61: earliest debt first, even if time-barred; equal debts proportionately. An exact match of amount is only a clue to intention. Appropriation to a time-barred debt does not revive it (Limitation Act, Section 19). One debt with interest: interest and costs first, then principal ( Smithaben H. Patel ; Meghraj ).

caseLaws.name: Industrial Credit and Development Syndicate v
caseLaws.facts: Smithaben H. Patel (1999) Facts. A mortgage decree for about ₹5.25 lakh carried 18% interest and allowed monthly instalments . The debtors paid part amounts and said they were towards principal. Principle. Sections 59 to 61 apply only where a debtor owes several distinct debts. They do not deal with principal and interest due on a single debt. Payments on a decree go first as the decree directs; otherwise to interest and costs, then principal, unless the parties agreed otherwise. (1999) 3 SCC 80 : AIR 1999 SC 1036. Why it matters. It is the Supreme Court authority that marks the limit of Sections 59 to 61. Meghraj v. Bayabai (1969) Facts. Mortgagors deposited money in court under a mortgage decree. Some deposit applications said the money was towards principal. Principle. For a debt with interest, payment goes first to interest and costs, then to principal. A debtor's recital does not bind the creditor unless the creditor accepted the money on that condition, which the debtor must prove. (1969) 2 SCC 274 : AIR 1970 SC 161. Why it matters. A debtor cannot change the interest-first rule on a single debt by a one-sided direction. Clayton's Case (Devaynes v. Noble) (1816) Facts. Clayton had a current account with a banking partnership. One partner died. The surviving partners later paid Clayton more than the balance due at the death, and then the bank failed. Principle. In a running account, the first sum paid in is presumed to be the first drawn out ("first in, first out"), unless a contrary intention appears. (1816) 1 Mer 572 : 35 ER 781. Why it matters. It is the English source of the "earliest debt first" rule for running accounts, which Section 61 reflects.

selfTest.q: 1. Who has the first right to appropriate?
selfTest.a: The debtor (Section 59).

selfTest.q: 2. A owes ₹2,000, ₹3,000 and ₹5,000 (earliest to latest). He pays ₹4,000 and nobody chooses. What is left?
selfTest.a: Debt 1: ₹0. Debt 2: ₹1,000. Debt 3: ₹5,000 (Section 61).

selfTest.q: 3. Can a creditor apply a payment to a debt not yet due?
selfTest.a: No. It must be lawful and actually due and payable (Section 60).

selfTest.q: 4. Does applying a payment to a time-barred debt revive it?
selfTest.a: No. Section 19 of the Limitation Act needs payment before the period expires.

selfTest.q: 5. Do Sections 59 to 61 apply to principal and interest of one loan?
selfTest.a: No ( Smithaben H. Patel , 1999).

సెక్షన్ 59: డబ్బు ఏ అప్పు కోసమో అప్పుదారు చెబుతాడు, లేదా పరిస్థితులే చూపిస్తాయి. అప్పిచ్చినవాడు ఆ డబ్బును తీసుకుంటే , దాన్ని ఆ అప్పుకే జమ చేయాలి. సెక్షన్ 60: అప్పుదారు ఏమీ చెప్పలేదు, పరిస్థితులూ ఏమీ చూపించవు. అప్పిచ్చినవాడు దాన్ని చట్టబద్ధమైన, ఇప్పటికే చెల్లించాల్సిన గడువు వచ్చిన ఏ అప్పుకైనా జమ చేయవచ్చు, కాలదోషం పట్టిన అప్పుకైనా సరే. సెక్షన్ 61: ఎవరూ ఎంచుకోలేదు. చెల్లింపు అప్పులను కాల క్రమంలో , ముందు పుట్టినది ముందుగా తీరుస్తుంది, కాలదోషం పట్టినవి కూడా. సమాన స్థాయి అప్పులు దాన్ని దామాషా ప్రకారం పంచుకుంటాయి.
te.meaning:
చెల్లింపుల కేటాయింపు అంటే, చాలా అప్పుల్లో ఒక చెల్లింపును ఒక ప్రత్యేక అప్పుకు జమ చేయడం.

ఈ ప్రశ్న ఇవన్నీ కలిసి ఉన్నప్పుడే వస్తుంది:

ఒకే అప్పుదారు. ఒకే అప్పిచ్చినవాడు. ఆ అప్పుదారు ఆ అప్పిచ్చినవాడికి బాకీ ఉన్న వేర్వేరు అప్పులు . అన్నీ తీర్చడానికి సరిపోని చెల్లింపు .

ఒకే అప్పు ఉంటే ఎంచుకోవడానికి ఏమీ లేదు. కాబట్టి సెక్షన్లు 59 నుంచి 61 వర్తించవు.

ఎంపిక ఎందుకు ముఖ్యం. అన్ని అప్పులూ ఒకేలా ఉండవు. ఒకదానికి వడ్డీ ఎక్కువ ఉండవచ్చు. ఒకదానికి తనఖా గానీ జామీను (surety) గానీ ఉండవచ్చు. ఒకటి త్వరలో కాలదోషం పట్టేదై ఉండవచ్చు. కాబట్టి ఏ అప్పు తీరుతుందనేది ఇరువురి హక్కులనూ మారుస్తుంది.

ఈ వరుస ఎందుకు. డబ్బు అప్పుదారుది, కాబట్టి మొదటి మాట అతనిది. అతను మౌనంగా ఉంటే, తర్వాతి మాట అప్పిచ్చినవాడిది. ఇద్దరూ మౌనంగా ఉంటే, ఏ వివాదమూ మిగలకుండా చట్టం ఒక స్థిర నియమాన్ని వర్తింపజేస్తుంది.

selfTest.q: 1. కేటాయించే మొదటి హక్కు ఎవరిది?
selfTest.a: అప్పుదారుది (సెక్షన్ 59).

selfTest.q: 3. గడువు రాని అప్పుకు అప్పిచ్చినవాడు చెల్లింపును జమ చేయగలడా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. అది చట్టబద్ధమై, గడువు వచ్చినదై ఉండాలి (సెక్షన్ 60).

selfTest.q: 4. కాలదోషం పట్టిన అప్పుకు చెల్లింపు జమ చేస్తే అది బతుకుతుందా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. Limitation Act సెక్షన్ 19 కు గడువు ముగియకముందే చెల్లింపు జరగాలి.

selfTest.q: 5. ఒకే లోన్ అసలు, వడ్డీకి సెక్షన్లు 59 నుంచి 61 వర్తిస్తాయా?
selfTest.a: లేదు ( Smithaben H. Patel , 1999).
