Part II, Specific Relief, has six kinds of relief: recovery of possession (Sections 5 to 8), specific performance (Sections 9 to 25), rectification (Section 26), rescission (Sections 27 to 30), cancellation (Sections 31 to 33) and declaratory decrees (Sections 34 and 35). Part III, Preventive Relief, is injunctions (Sections 36 to 42; Sections 43 and 44 repealed). The Schedule, added in 2018, lists infrastructure projects.
keyPoints: Specific relief gives the thing itself. Damages give its money value. Act 47 of 1963, in force from 1 March 1964. It replaced the 1877 Act. It has three Parts, eight Chapters and a Schedule. Sections 43 and 44 are repealed. Seven kinds of relief: possession, specific performance, rectification, rescission, cancellation, declaration and injunction (Sections 5 to 42). Section 2(e) borrows Contract Act meanings. Section 3 saves other remedies. Section 4 limits the Act to individual civil rights. The 2018 Amendment came into force on 1 October 2018. Section 10 now says "shall be enforced", subject to Sections 11(2), 14 and 16. The old discretion in Section 20 was replaced by substituted performance. Katta Sujatha Reddy (2022) held the amendment prospective. The 2024 review recalled that judgment without deciding the point again.

caseLaws.name: Katta Sujatha Reddy v
caseLaws.facts: Siddamsetty Infra Projects Pvt. Ltd. (2022) Facts. A purchaser under two agreements of 26 and 27 March 1997 for about 40 acres in Budvel Village, Ranga Reddy District, paid ₹34,80,850 of ₹40,20,000. The balance was due within three months. The purchaser sued in 2002. The High Court held the amended Section 10 retrospective and decreed the suit in part. Principle. The 2018 Amendment is prospective and "cannot apply to those transactions that took place prior to its coming into force". The Court also held the suit barred by limitation and the purchaser not ready and willing. Civil Appeal No. 5822 of 2022, decided 25 August 2022 (Ramana CJI, Krishna Murari and Hima Kohli JJ). On 8 November 2024 the Court recalled this judgment in review and restored the High Court's decree, without deciding the prospective point again (2024 INSC 861). Why it matters. It is the leading authority on whether the amended Section 10 applies to older contracts. K.S. Vidyanadam v. Vairavan (1997) Facts. An agreement of 15 December 1978 to sell a house in Madurai for ₹60,000 required the sale within six months. The buyer paid ₹5,000 and did nothing for about two and a half years. He sent notice on 11 July 1981 and sued on 23 August 1981, after prices had risen sharply. Principle. Not every suit for specific performance must be decreed merely because it is filed within limitation. Total inaction for 2½ years together with a steep rise in prices made the relief inequitable . (1997) 3 SCC 1 : AIR 1997 SC 1751. Why it matters. It shows how the old discretion under Sections 10 and 20 worked before 2018, and why delay and readiness still matter. Lallu Yeshwant Singh v. Rao Jagdish Singh (1967) Facts. Tenant-cultivators of agricultural land in Gwalior district said the landlord forcibly stopped them from cultivating and had the land cultivated by others. They sued for restoration of possession under a Gwalior law similar to Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. Principle. The Court approved the Privy Council's words: "In India persons are not permitted to take forcible possession". In such a suit the question of title is irrelevant. AIR 1968 SC 620 : (1968) 2 SCR 203, decided 29 November 1967. Why it matters. It supports the rule now in Section 6 of the 1963 Act. Anathula Sudhakar v. P. Buchi Reddy (2008) Facts. Two house sites in Matwada, Warangal were sold to the plaintiffs by Rukminibai in 1968 and the same land was sold to the defendant by her brother in 1977. The plaintiffs sued only for a permanent injunction. Principle. A suit for injunction alone lies where the plaintiff is in lawful possession and his title is not under a cloud. Where the title is in dispute, he must sue for declaration and consequential injunction. (2008) 4 SCC 594 : AIR 2008 SC 2033. Why it matters. It shows how declaration and injunction under the Act work together.

selfTest.q: 1. What does Section 4 of the Act say?
selfTest.a: Specific relief can be granted only to enforce individual civil rights. It cannot be granted for the mere purpose of enforcing a penal law.

selfTest.q: 2. On what date did the 2018 Amendment come into force?
selfTest.a: On 1 October 2018.

selfTest.q: 3. What does the amended Section 10 say?
selfTest.a: The specific performance of a contract "shall be enforced" by the court, subject to Section 11(2), Section 14 and Section 16.

selfTest.q: 4. What did the old Section 20 say, and what does the new Section 20 deal with?
selfTest.a: The old Section 20 made the jurisdiction to decree specific performance discretionary. The new Section 20 deals with substituted performance after at least 30 days' written notice.

selfTest.q: 5. Does the Act take away the right to claim damages under the Contract Act?
selfTest.a: No. Section 3 saves every right to relief under a contract other than specific performance.

సెక్షన్ 1: చట్టం భారతదేశం అంతటికీ వర్తిస్తుంది. ఇది 1 మార్చి 1964 నుంచి అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది. సెక్షన్ 2: obligation, settlement, trust, trustee అనే పదాలను నిర్వచిస్తుంది. ఈ చట్టం నిర్వచించని, కానీ కాంట్రాక్టు చట్టం నిర్వచించిన పదాలకు కాంట్రాక్టు చట్టం అర్థమే వర్తిస్తుంది. సెక్షన్ 3: కాంట్రాక్టు కింద ఒక వ్యక్తికి ఉన్న, నిర్దిష్ట అమలు తప్ప, మరే ఉపశమన హక్కునూ ఈ చట్టం తీసివేయదు. Indian Registration Act, 1908 ను ఇది ప్రభావితం చేయదు. సెక్షన్ 4: నిర్దిష్ట ఉపశమనం ఒక వ్యక్తి సొంత పౌర హక్కులను అమలు చేయడానికి మాత్రమే. కేవలం శిక్షా (క్రిమినల్) చట్టాన్ని అమలు చేయడానికి దీన్ని ఎప్పుడూ ఇవ్వరు. సెక్షన్ 10 (కొత్తది): కోర్టు కాంట్రాక్టు నిర్దిష్ట అమలును తప్పనిసరిగా అమలు చేయాలి. మినహాయింపులు సెక్షన్ 11(2), సెక్షన్ 14, సెక్షన్ 16 లోనివి మాత్రమే.

నిర్దిష్ట ఉపశమనం అంటే వ్యక్తికి హక్కు ఉన్న అదే రూపంలో ఇచ్చే ఉపశమనం. కోర్టు అసలు వస్తువునే ఆదేశిస్తుంది: భూమిని అప్పగించడం, కాంట్రాక్టును నెరవేర్చడం, పత్రాన్ని సరిదిద్దడం, హక్కును ప్రకటించడం, తప్పును ఆపడం. నష్టపరిహారం నష్టానికి డబ్బు విలువ మాత్రమే. చట్టం "specific relief" ను నిర్వచించదు, కానీ దాని పేరు, సెక్షన్ 4 దాని పరిధిని చూపుతాయి. చట్టం తన గురించి చెప్పేది. ప్రవేశిక (preamble) దీన్ని "An Act to define and amend the law relating to certain kinds of specific relief." అంటుంది. ఈ విషయంపై ఇది రెండో చట్టం. ఇది Specific Relief Act, 1877 స్థానంలో వచ్చింది, లా కమిషన్ తొమ్మిదో నివేదిక తర్వాత రూపొందింది. చట్టంలో ఇది ఎందుకు ఉంది. ఇంగ్లండ్‌లో కామన్ లా కోర్టులు మొదట నష్టపరిహారం మాత్రమే ఇచ్చేవి. నష్టపరిహారం సరిపోని చోట Courts of Equity నిర్దిష్ట అమలును ఆదేశించడం మొదలుపెట్టాయి. అందుకే ఈ పరిష్కారాలు equity (కఠిన నియమాలకు బదులు న్యాయబద్ధతపై ఆధారపడిన చట్ట శాఖ) నుంచి వచ్చాయి. అందుకే 2018 కి ముందు వాటిని ఇవ్వాలా వద్దా అనే దానిపై కోర్టుకు విస్తృత విచక్షణ (నిర్ణయించే స్వేచ్ఛ) ఉండేది. 2018 సవరణ నిర్దిష్ట అమలును నియమంగా మార్చింది. చట్టంలోని ఇతర అనేక ఉపశమనాలు, ఉదాహరణకు injunctions (సెక్షన్ 36), declarations (సెక్షన్ 34), ఇప్పటికీ కోర్టు విచక్షణపైనే ఆధారపడతాయి. నిర్మాణం. చట్టంలో మూడు భాగాలు (Parts), ఎనిమిది అధ్యాయాలు (Chapters) ఉన్నాయి. Part I, Preliminary: సెక్షన్లు 1 నుంచి 4. Part II, Specific Relief: అధ్యాయాలు I నుంచి VI, సెక్షన్లు 5 నుంచి 35. Part III, Preventive Relief : అధ్యాయాలు VII, VIII, సెక్షన్లు 36 నుంచి 44 (సెక్షన్లు 43, 44 రద్దయ్యాయి). The Schedule: మౌలిక సదుపాయ (infrastructure) ప్రాజెక్టుల జాబితా, 2018 లో చేర్చబడింది. చట్టం నిర్మాణం కోసం Diagram 1 చూడండి. Diagram 1. పై పెట్టె నుంచి మొదలుపెట్టి గీతల వెంట కిందికి చదవండి. కింది పెట్టెలు ఏడు రకాల ఉపశమనాలు, వాటి సెక్షన్లతో. flowchart TD A["నిర్దిష్ట ఉపశమన చట్టం, 1963"] A --> P1["Part I: Preliminary

(సె. 43-44 రద్దు)"] వచన వివరణ నిర్దిష్ట ఉపశమన చట్టం, 1963 లో మూడు Parts, ఒక Schedule ఉన్నాయి. Part I, Preliminary, సెక్షన్లు 1 నుంచి 4. Part II, Specific Relief, లో ఆరు రకాల ఉపశమనాలు: స్వాధీనం తిరిగి పొందడం (సెక్షన్లు 5 నుంచి 8), నిర్దిష్ట అమలు (సెక్షన్లు 9 నుంచి 25), పత్రం సవరణ (సెక్షన్ 26), కాంట్రాక్టు రద్దు (సెక్షన్లు 27 నుంచి 30), పత్రం రద్దు (సెక్షన్లు 31 నుంచి 33), ప్రకటన డిక్రీలు (సెక్షన్లు 34, 35). Part III, Preventive Relief, injunctions (సెక్షన్లు 36 నుంచి 42; సెక్షన్లు 43, 44 రద్దు). 2018 లో చేర్చిన Schedule infrastructure ప్రాజెక్టుల జాబితా ఇస్తుంది.

selfTest.q: 1. చట్టంలోని సెక్షన్ 4 ఏమి చెబుతుంది?
selfTest.a: నిర్దిష్ట ఉపశమనాన్ని వ్యక్తిగత పౌర హక్కులను అమలు చేయడానికి మాత్రమే ఇవ్వవచ్చు. కేవలం శిక్షా చట్టాన్ని అమలు చేసే ఉద్దేశంతో ఇవ్వలేం.

selfTest.q: 2. 2018 సవరణ ఏ తేదీన అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది?
selfTest.a: 1 అక్టోబర్ 2018 న.

selfTest.q: 3. సవరించిన సెక్షన్ 10 ఏమి చెబుతుంది?
selfTest.a: కాంట్రాక్టు నిర్దిష్ట అమలును కోర్టు "shall be enforced", సెక్షన్ 11(2), సెక్షన్ 14, సెక్షన్ 16 కు లోబడి.

selfTest.q: 4. పాత సెక్షన్ 20 ఏమి చెప్పింది, కొత్త సెక్షన్ 20 దేని గురించి?
selfTest.a: పాత సెక్షన్ 20 నిర్దిష్ట అమలు డిక్రీ ఇచ్చే అధికారాన్ని విచక్షణాధికారంగా చేసింది. కొత్త సెక్షన్ 20 కనీసం 30 రోజుల లిఖిత నోటీసు తర్వాత ప్రత్యామ్నాయ నెరవేర్పు గురించి.

selfTest.q: 5. కాంట్రాక్టు చట్టం కింద నష్టపరిహారం కోరే హక్కును ఈ చట్టం తీసివేస్తుందా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. నిర్దిష్ట అమలు తప్ప, కాంట్రాక్టు కింద ఉన్న ప్రతి ఉపశమన హక్కును సెక్షన్ 3 కాపాడుతుంది.

law-of-contract-i-u5-t14.subtitle: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996: sections 7, 8, 9, 11, 16, 34 and 36, with section 25 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963

en.inOneMinute: An arbitration clause is a promise in a contract to send disputes to a private tribunal and not to the courts. The tribunal gives an arbitral award that is final and binding, subject to a narrow challenge. Most large construction, supply and infrastructure contracts have such a clause. The law is in the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The Specific Relief Act, 1963 fits in because it deals with injunctions and specific performance, and Section 25 mentions awards. In exams, you must know Section 7, the court's duty to refer under Section 8, and the limited challenge under Section 34.
legalProvision: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, Section 7. Arbitration agreement. (1) In this Part, “arbitration agreement” means an agreement by the parties to submit to arbitration all or certain disputes which have arisen or which may arise between them in respect of a defined legal relationship, whether contractual or not. (2) An arbitration agreement may be in the form of an arbitration clause in a contract or in the form of a separate agreement. (3) An arbitration agreement shall be in writing. (4) An arbitration agreement is in writing if it is contained in— (a) a document signed by the parties; (b) an exchange of letters, telex, telegrams or other means of telecommunication including communication through electronic means which provide a record of the agreement; or (c) an exchange of statements of claim and defence in which the existence of the agreement is alleged by one party and not denied by the other. (5) The reference in a contract to a document containing an arbitration clause constitutes an arbitration agreement if the contract is in writing and the reference is such as to make that arbitration clause part of the contract.

Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, Section 5. Extent of judicial intervention. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, in matters governed by this Part, no judicial authority shall intervene except where so provided in this Part.

Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, Section 8. Power to refer parties to arbitration where there is an arbitration agreement. (1) A judicial authority, before which an action is brought in a matter which is the subject of an arbitration agreement shall, if a party to the arbitration agreement or any person claiming through or under him, so applies not later than the date of submitting his first statement on the substance of the dispute, then, notwithstanding any judgment, decree or order of the Supreme Court or any Court, refer the parties to arbitration unless it finds that prima facie no valid arbitration agreement exists. (2) The application referred to in sub-section (1) shall not be entertained unless it is accompanied by the original arbitration agreement or a duly certified copy thereof: Provided that where the original arbitration agreement or a certified copy thereof is not available with the party applying for reference to arbitration under sub-section (1), and the said agreement or certified copy is retained by the other party to that agreement, then, the party so applying shall file such application along with a copy of the arbitration agreement and a petition praying the Court to call upon the other party to produce the original arbitration agreement or its duly certified copy before that Court. (3) Notwithstanding that an application has been made under sub-section (1) and that the issue is pending before the judicial authority, an arbitration may be commenced or continued and an arbitral award made.

Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, Section 9. Interim measures, etc., by Court. (1) A party may, before or during arbitral proceedings or at any time after the making of the arbitral award but before it is enforced in accordance with section 36, apply to a court— (i) for the appointment of a guardian for a minor or person of unsound mind for the purposes of arbitral proceedings; or (ii) for an interim measure of protection in respect of any of the following matters, namely:— (a) the preservation, interim custody or sale of any goods which are the subject-matter of the arbitration agreement; (b) securing the amount in dispute in the arbitration; (c) the detention, preservation or inspection of any property or thing which is the subject-matter of the dispute in arbitration, or as to which any question may arise therein and authorising for any of the aforesaid purposes any person to enter upon any land or building in the possession of any party, or authorising any samples to be taken or any observation to be made, or experiment to be tried, which may be necessary or expedient for the purpose of obtaining full information or evidence; (d) interim injunction or the appointment of a receiver; (e) such other interim measure of protection as may appear to the Court to be just and convenient, and the Court shall have the same power for making orders as it has for the purpose of, and in relation to, any proceedings before it. (2) Where, before the commencement of the arbitral proceedings, a Court passes an order for any interim measure of protection under sub-section (1), the arbitral proceedings shall be commenced within a period of ninety days from the date of such order or within such further time as the Court may determine. (3) Once the arbitral tribunal has been constituted, the Court shall not entertain an application under sub-section (1), unless the Court finds that circumstances exist which may not render the remedy provided under section 17 efficacious.

Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, Section 11. Appointment of arbitrators. . . . (6A) The Supreme Court or, as the case may be, the High Court, while considering any application under sub-section (4) or sub-section (5) or sub-section (6), shall, notwithstanding any judgment, decree or order of any Court, confine to the examination of the existence of an arbitration agreement.

Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, Section 16. Competence of arbitral tribunal to rule on its jurisdiction. (1) The arbitral tribunal may rule on its own jurisdiction, including ruling on any objections with respect to the existence or validity of the arbitration agreement, and for that purpose,— (a) an arbitration clause which forms part of a contract shall be treated as an agreement independent of the other terms of the contract; and (b) a decision by the arbitral tribunal that the contract is null and void shall not entail ipso jure the invalidity of the arbitration clause.

Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, Section 34. Application for setting aside arbitral award. (1) Recourse to a Court against an arbitral award may be made only by an application for setting aside such award in accordance with sub-section (2) and sub-section (3). (2) An arbitral award may be set aside by the Court only if— (a) the party making the application establishes on the basis of the record of the arbitral tribunal that— (i) a party was under some incapacity, or (ii) the arbitration agreement is not valid under the law to which the parties have subjected it or, failing any indication thereon, under the law for the time being in force; or (iii) the party making the application was not given proper notice of the appointment of an arbitrator or of the arbitral proceedings or was otherwise unable to present his case; or (iv) the arbitral award deals with a dispute not contemplated by or not falling within the terms of the submission to arbitration, or it contains decisions on matters beyond the scope of the submission to arbitration: Provided that, if the decisions on matters submitted to arbitration can be separated from those not so submitted, only that part of the arbitral award which contains decisions on matters not submitted to arbitration may be set aside; or (v) the composition of the arbitral tribunal or the arbitral procedure was not in accordance with the agreement of the parties, unless such agreement was in conflict with a provision of this Part from which the parties cannot derogate, or, failing such agreement, was not in accordance with this Part; or (b) the Court finds that— (i) the subject-matter of the dispute is not capable of settlement by arbitration under the law for the time being in force, or (ii) the arbitral award is in conflict with the public policy of India. Explanation 1.—For the avoidance of any doubt, it is clarified that an award is in conflict with the public policy of India, only if,— (i) the making of the award was induced or affected by fraud or corruption or was in violation of section 75 or section 81; or (ii) it is in contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian law; or (iii) it is in conflict with the most basic notions of morality or justice. Explanation 2.—For the avoidance of doubt, the test as to whether there is a contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian law shall not entail a review on the merits of the dispute. (2A) An arbitral award arising out of arbitrations other than international commercial arbitrations, may also be set aside by the Court, if the Court finds that the award is vitiated by patent illegality appearing on the face of the award: Provided that an award shall not be set aside merely on the ground of an erroneous application of the law or by reappreciation of evidence. (3) An application for setting aside may not be made after three months have elapsed from the date on which the party making that application had received the arbitral award or, if a request had been made under section 33, from the date on which that request had been disposed of by the arbitral tribunal: Provided that if the Court is satisfied that the applicant was prevented by sufficient cause from making the application within the said period of three months it may entertain the application within a further period of thirty days, but not thereafter. (4) On receipt of an application under sub-section (1), the Court may, where it is appropriate and it is so requested by a party, adjourn the proceedings for a period of time determined by it in order to give the arbitral tribunal an opportunity to resume the arbitral proceedings or to take such other action as in the opinion of arbitral tribunal will eliminate the grounds for setting aside the arbitral award. (5) An application under this section shall be filed by a party only after issuing a prior notice to the other party and such application shall be accompanied by an affidavit by the applicant endorsing compliance with the said requirement. (6) An application under this section shall be disposed of expeditiously, and in any event, within a period of one year from the date on which the notice referred to in sub-section (5) is served upon the other party.

Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, Section 35. Finality of arbitral awards. Subject to this Part an arbitral award shall be final and binding on the parties and persons claiming under them respectively.

Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, Section 36. Enforcement. (1) Where the time for making an application to set aside the arbitral award under section 34 has expired, then, subject to the provisions of sub-section (2), such award shall be enforced in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908), in the same manner as if it were a decree of the court. (2) Where an application to set aside the arbitral award has been filed in the Court under section 34, the filing of such an application shall not by itself render that award unenforceable, unless the Court grants an order of stay of the operation of the said arbitral award in accordance with the provisions of sub-section (3), on a separate application made for that purpose.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 25. Application of preceding sections to certain awards and testamentary directions to execute settlements. The provisions of this Chapter as to contracts shall apply to awards to which the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (26 of 1996), does not apply and to directions in a will or codicil to execute a particular settlement.
In simple words

Section 7: an arbitration agreement is an agreement to submit to arbitration all or certain disputes which have arisen or may arise in respect of a defined legal relationship, contractual or not. It may be a clause in a contract or a separate agreement. It must be in writing. Writing includes a signed document, an exchange of letters or electronic communications that record the agreement, or an exchange of claim and defence in which one side alleges the agreement and the other does not deny it. A written contract can also bring in a clause from another document by referring to it. Section 5: in matters governed by Part I, no judicial authority shall intervene (step in) except where the Act provides. Section 8: a judicial authority hearing an action on a matter covered by an arbitration agreement shall refer the parties to arbitration, if a party applies not later than his first statement on the substance of the dispute. It need not refer if it finds that prima facie (at first sight) no valid arbitration agreement exists. The application needs the original agreement or a certified copy. Arbitration may start or continue while the application is pending. Section 9: a party may apply to a court for interim measures before or during the arbitration, or after the award but before it is enforced. If the court passes an order before the arbitration starts, the arbitration must begin within 90 days or such further time as the court fixes. Once the tribunal is constituted, the court will not entertain the application unless the remedy under Section 17 may not be efficacious (effective). Section 11(6A): when appointing arbitrators , the court confines (limits) itself to the examination of the existence of an arbitration agreement. Section 16(1): the tribunal may rule on its own jurisdiction . The arbitration clause is treated as an agreement independent of the other terms of the contract, so a finding that the contract is void does not by itself make the clause invalid. Section 34: an award may be set aside only on the grounds listed, within three months of receiving it, with 30 more days for sufficient cause, and not after that. Section 35: subject to Part I, an award is final and binding on the parties and those claiming under them. Section 36: once the time to challenge ends, the award is enforced as if it were a decree . A challenge under Section 34 does not by itself stop enforcement; a stay needs a separate application and order. Section 25, Specific Relief Act: Chapter II (on specific performance) applies to awards to which the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 does not apply, and to directions in a will or codicil to execute a settlement.
en.meaning:
An arbitration agreement is the agreement under Section 7. When it sits inside the main contract it is called an arbitration clause. The parties agree that an arbitrator or tribunal will decide, and that the arbitral award will bind them (Section 35). The question this topic answers. When a contract has an arbitration clause, who decides a dispute, how far can the courts step in, and how is the award enforced? Why the law has this rule. Parties to large contracts want a quick, private decision by people they choose, often experts. Section 5 keeps the courts out except where the Act allows them in. If no, the dispute goes to the ordinary courts (Section 7). Step 2: if one party sues in court, does the other apply before his first statement on the substance of the dispute? If no, he may lose the right to have the matter referred (Section 8). Step 3: does the court find that prima facie no valid arbitration agreement exists? If yes, the court does not refer the parties and the suit goes on. Step 4: the parties are referred, and an arbitrator is appointed by agreement or by the court under Section 11. After appointment the court's role is over, and the tribunal decides its own jurisdiction (Section 16). Step 5: the tribunal makes an award. It may be challenged only within three months, plus 30 days for sufficient cause, on the limited grounds in Section 34. If no challenge succeeds or none is made, the award is final (Section 35). Step 6: the award is enforced as a decree (Section 36). An application to set aside does not by itself stay the award; a stay needs a separate order.
keyPoints: Section 7: a written agreement to arbitrate; it may be a clause in a contract. Section 8: the court must refer the parties if a party applies before his first statement on substance. Section 16: the tribunal decides its own jurisdiction; the clause is independent of the contract. Section 34: three months plus 30 days; limited grounds; patent illegality only on the face of a domestic award. Section 36: enforced as a decree; a challenge does not stop enforcement without a stay. Section 25, Specific Relief Act: only for awards outside the 1996 Act.

caseLaws.name: Kamal Gupta v
caseLaws.facts: L.R. Builders (2025) Facts. After a sole arbitrator was appointed under Section 11(6) in a family settlement dispute, non-signatories obtained a later court order letting them be present in the arbitration. Principle. The Supreme Court set the order aside with costs of ₹3,00,000. A non-signatory has no right to be present, as the award binds only the parties and those claiming under them. After appointing the arbitrator, the court "had become functus officio" (para 19). 2025 INSC 975 (13 August 2025, P.S. Narasimha and Atul S. Chandurkar JJ.). Why it matters. It shows the limits of court intervention and the confidentiality rule in Section 42A. Food Corporation of India v. Indian Council of Arbitration (2003) Facts. Storage-cum-milling contracts between FCI and millers had "an uniform and standardized arbitration clause" under the rules of the Indian Council of Arbitration. The Council refused to proceed unless both sides agreed "in writing afresh". Principle. Whether the clause was valid or conflicted with the rules were "matters which go to the jurisdiction of the Arbitral Tribunal ". The Council had to nominate the arbitrator "not later than sixty days". AIR 2003 SC 3011 : (2003) 6 SCC 564 (17 July 2003). Why it matters. It supports the tribunal's power to rule on its own jurisdiction under Section 16. ONGC v. Saw Pipes (2003) Facts. ONGC deducted liquidated damages of US $3,04,970.20 and ₹15,75,559 from a supplier's bills for late supply of casing pipes. The tribunal ordered a refund. Principle. An award that is patently illegal is against the public policy of India and may be set aside. The refund direction was set aside and the appeal allowed. (2003) 5 SCC 705 : AIR 2003 SC 2629 (17 April 2003). Why it matters. It is the older, wide test. Compare it with Section 34(2A) and Ssangyong . Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Co. Ltd. v. NHAI (2019) Facts. A contractor and the National Highways Authority of India disputed price adjustment under clause 70.3 of a contract for a four-lane bypass on National Highway 26, after NHAI applied a policy circular of 15 February 2013. Principle. After the 2015 Amendment, the expanded public policy test no longer applies. Patent illegality is limited, and a tribunal's construction of the contract stands unless "no fair-minded or reasonable person would" adopt it (para 29). (2019) 15 SCC 131 : AIR 2019 SC 5041 (8 May 2019). Why it matters. It states the present law of challenge for domestic awards.

selfTest.q: 1. Must an arbitration agreement be in writing?
selfTest.a: Yes. Section 7(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 says so.

selfTest.q: 2. By when must a party apply under Section 8?
selfTest.a: Not later than the date of submitting his first statement on the substance of the dispute.

selfTest.q: 3. How long does a party have to apply under Section 34?
selfTest.a: Three months from receipt of the award, with a further 30 days if sufficient cause is shown, but not after that.

selfTest.q: 4. Does filing a Section 34 application stop enforcement of the award?
selfTest.a: No. Under Section 36(2), the award stays enforceable unless the court grants a stay on a separate application.

selfTest.q: 5. What happens to the arbitration clause if the tribunal finds the contract void?
selfTest.a: The clause is not invalid by that fact alone, because it is treated as an agreement independent of the other terms (Section 16(1)).

The provisions of this Chapter as to contracts shall apply to awards to which the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (26 of 1996), does not apply and to directions in a will or codicil to execute a particular settlement.

సెక్షన్ 7: Arbitration agreement అంటే, ఒక నిర్దిష్ట చట్టపరమైన సంబంధం (కాంట్రాక్టు అయినా కాకపోయినా) విషయంలో వచ్చిన లేదా రాబోయే అన్ని లేదా కొన్ని వివాదాలను arbitration కు అప్పగిస్తామన్న ఒప్పందం. అది కాంట్రాక్టులో ఒక క్లాజుగా గానీ, విడి ఒప్పందంగా గానీ ఉండవచ్చు. అది లిఖితంగా ఉండాలి. సంతకం చేసిన పత్రం, ఒప్పందాన్ని నమోదు చేసే లేఖలు లేదా ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ సమాచార మార్పిడి, లేదా ఒక పక్షం ఒప్పందం ఉందని చెప్పి మరో పక్షం కాదనని claim, defence మార్పిడి లిఖితమే. ఒక లిఖిత కాంట్రాక్టు మరో పత్రాన్ని ప్రస్తావించి, అందులోని క్లాజును తనలో భాగం చేసుకోవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 5: Part I పరిధిలోని విషయాల్లో, చట్టం అనుమతించిన చోట తప్ప, ఏ న్యాయ అధికారీ జోక్యం చేసుకోకూడదు. సెక్షన్ 8: Arbitration agreement పరిధిలోని విషయంపై దావాను విచారిస్తున్న న్యాయ అధికారి, ఒక పక్షం వివాద సారాంశంపై తన మొదటి స్టేట్‌మెంట్ కంటే ముందే దరఖాస్తు చేస్తే, పక్షాలను arbitration కు పంపాలి. ప్రథమ దృష్ట్యా ( prima facie ) చెల్లుబాటయ్యే arbitration agreement లేదని తేలితే పంపాల్సిన అవసరం లేదు. దరఖాస్తుతో అసలు ఒప్పందం లేదా ధృవీకరించిన ప్రతి ఉండాలి. దరఖాస్తు పెండింగ్‌లో ఉన్నా arbitration మొదలుపెట్టవచ్చు, కొనసాగించవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 9: Arbitration కు ముందు, సమయంలో, లేదా అవార్డు తర్వాత అది అమలు కాకముందు, ఒక పక్షం మధ్యంతర చర్యల కోసం కోర్టుకు దరఖాస్తు చేయవచ్చు. Arbitration మొదలు కాకముందే కోర్టు ఉత్తర్వు ఇస్తే, 90 రోజుల్లో లేదా కోర్టు నిర్ణయించే అదనపు సమయంలో arbitration మొదలవ్వాలి. ట్రైబ్యునల్ ఏర్పడిన తర్వాత, సెక్షన్ 17 కింది పరిహారం ప్రభావవంతం కాకపోవచ్చని తేలితే తప్ప, కోర్టు దరఖాస్తును స్వీకరించదు. సెక్షన్ 11(6A): మధ్యవర్తులను నియమించేటప్పుడు, కోర్టు arbitration agreement ఉనికిని పరిశీలించడానికే పరిమితం అవుతుంది. సెక్షన్ 16(1): ట్రైబ్యునల్ తన సొంత అధికార పరిధిపై నిర్ణయించవచ్చు. Arbitration clause ను కాంట్రాక్టులోని ఇతర నిబంధనల నుంచి స్వతంత్ర ఒప్పందంగా చూస్తారు. కాబట్టి కాంట్రాక్టు చెల్లదని తేలినంత మాత్రాన క్లాజు చెల్లకుండా పోదు. సెక్షన్ 34: చెప్పిన కారణాలపై మాత్రమే, అవార్డు అందిన మూడు నెలల్లో, తగిన కారణం ఉంటే మరో 30 రోజుల్లో, ఆ తర్వాత కాదు, అవార్డును రద్దు చేయవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 35: Part I కి లోబడి, అవార్డు పక్షాలపై, వారి కింద హక్కు కోరేవారిపై అంతిమమైనది, కట్టుబడి ఉండాల్సినది. సెక్షన్ 36: సవాలు గడువు ముగిశాక, అవార్డును డిక్రీ లాగే అమలు చేస్తారు. సెక్షన్ 34 కింది సవాలు దానంతట అదే అమలును ఆపదు; స్టే కోసం విడి దరఖాస్తు, ఉత్తర్వు కావాలి. సెక్షన్ 25, నిర్దిష్ట ఉపశమన చట్టం: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 వర్తించని అవార్డులకు, ఒక settlement ను అమలు చేయమని వీలునామా లేదా codicil లో ఇచ్చిన ఆదేశాలకు Chapter II (నిర్దిష్ట అమలు) వర్తిస్తుంది.

Arbitration agreement అంటే సెక్షన్ 7 కింది ఒప్పందం. అది ప్రధాన కాంట్రాక్టు లోపల ఉంటే దాన్ని arbitration clause అంటారు. ఒక మధ్యవర్తి లేదా ట్రైబ్యునల్ నిర్ణయిస్తుందని, మధ్యవర్తిత్వ అవార్డు తమను కట్టుబడి ఉంచుతుందని పక్షాలు అంగీకరిస్తారు (సెక్షన్ 35). ఈ అంశం జవాబిచ్చే ప్రశ్న. కాంట్రాక్టులో arbitration clause ఉంటే, వివాదాన్ని ఎవరు నిర్ణయిస్తారు, కోర్టులు ఎంత వరకు జోక్యం చేసుకోవచ్చు, అవార్డు ఎలా అమలవుతుంది? చట్టం ఈ నియమం ఎందుకు పెట్టింది. పెద్ద కాంట్రాక్టుల పక్షాలు, తాము ఎంచుకున్న, తరచుగా నిపుణులైన వ్యక్తుల నుంచి త్వరితమైన, గోప్యమైన నిర్ణయం కోరుకుంటారు. చట్టం అనుమతించిన చోట తప్ప సెక్షన్ 5 కోర్టులను దూరంగా ఉంచుతుంది. ఫ్లోచార్టు ఒక వివాదాన్ని క్లాజు నుంచి అవార్డు వరకు అనుసరిస్తుంది. Diagram 1 చూడండి. విడి ఉత్తర్వుతోనే స్టే"] style S6 fill:#d9f2d9,stroke:#2e7d32 వచన వివరణ దశ 1: వివాదానికి లిఖిత arbitration agreement ఉందా? లేకపోతే వివాదం సాధారణ కోర్టులకు వెళ్తుంది (సెక్షన్ 7). దశ 2: ఒక పక్షం కోర్టులో దావా వేస్తే, మరో పక్షం వివాద సారాంశంపై తన మొదటి స్టేట్‌మెంట్‌కు ముందే దరఖాస్తు చేస్తుందా? లేకపోతే విషయాన్ని పంపించుకునే హక్కు కోల్పోవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 8). దశ 3: ప్రథమ దృష్ట్యా చెల్లే arbitration agreement లేదని కోర్టు తేలుస్తుందా? అవును అయితే, కోర్టు పక్షాలను పంపదు, దావా కొనసాగుతుంది. దశ 4: పక్షాలను పంపుతారు; ఒప్పందం ద్వారా లేదా సెక్షన్ 11 కింద కోర్టు మధ్యవర్తిని నియమిస్తుంది. నియామకం తర్వాత కోర్టు పాత్ర ముగుస్తుంది, ట్రైబ్యునల్ తన పరిధిపై తానే నిర్ణయిస్తుంది (సెక్షన్ 16). దశ 5: ట్రైబ్యునల్ అవార్డు ఇస్తుంది. మూడు నెలల్లో, తగిన కారణం ఉంటే మరో 30 రోజుల్లో, సెక్షన్ 34 లోని పరిమిత కారణాలపై మాత్రమే దాన్ని సవాలు చేయవచ్చు. ఏ సవాలూ నెగ్గకపోతే లేదా సవాలు లేకపోతే, అవార్డు అంతిమం (సెక్షన్ 35). దశ 6: అవార్డును డిక్రీలా అమలు చేస్తారు (సెక్షన్ 36). రద్దు దరఖాస్తు దానంతట అదే అవార్డును నిలిపివేయదు; స్టే కు విడి ఉత్తర్వు కావాలి.

selfTest.q: 1. Arbitration agreement లిఖితంగా ఉండాలా?
selfTest.a: అవును. Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 సెక్షన్ 7(3) అలా చెబుతుంది.

selfTest.q: 2. సెక్షన్ 8 కింద ఒక పక్షం ఎప్పటిలోగా దరఖాస్తు చేయాలి?
selfTest.a: వివాద సారాంశంపై తన మొదటి స్టేట్‌మెంట్ సమర్పించిన తేదీ కంటే ఆలస్యం కాకుండా.

selfTest.q: 3. సెక్షన్ 34 కింద దరఖాస్తు చేయడానికి ఎంత సమయం ఉంటుంది?
selfTest.a: అవార్డు అందినప్పటి నుంచి మూడు నెలలు, తగిన కారణం చూపితే మరో 30 రోజులు, ఆ తర్వాత కాదు.

selfTest.q: 4. సెక్షన్ 34 దరఖాస్తు వేస్తే అవార్డు అమలు ఆగుతుందా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. సెక్షన్ 36(2) కింద, విడి దరఖాస్తుపై కోర్టు స్టే ఇస్తే తప్ప అవార్డు అమలు చేయదగినదిగానే ఉంటుంది.

selfTest.q: 5. కాంట్రాక్టు శూన్యమని ట్రైబ్యునల్ తేలిస్తే arbitration clause కు ఏమవుతుంది?
selfTest.a: ఆ కారణం మాత్రాన క్లాజు చెల్లకుండా పోదు, ఎందుకంటే దాన్ని ఇతర నిబంధనల నుంచి స్వతంత్ర ఒప్పందంగా చూస్తారు (సెక్షన్ 16(1)).

law-of-contract-i-u5-t15.subtitle: The Mediation Act, 2023: sections 4, 5, 6, 27 and 28, with section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015

en.inOneMinute: Court cases about contracts take years and often end the business relationship. Arbitration is faster, but an outsider still decides who wins. A mediation agreement lets the parties promise to try a third route first: settling the dispute themselves with the help of a neutral mediator. The Mediation Act, 2023 governs it. In exams, you must define a mediation agreement, say what the mediator does, explain the legal force of a mediated settlement agreement , and compare mediation with arbitration.
legalProvision: Mediation Act, 2023, Section 4. Mediation agreement. (1) A mediation agreement shall be in writing, by or between parties and anyone claiming through them, to submit to mediation all or certain disputes which have arisen or which may arise between the parties. (2) A mediation agreement may be in the form of a mediation clause in a contract or in the form of a separate agreement. (3) A mediation agreement is in writing, if it is contained in or recorded as— (a) any document signed by the parties; (b) an exchange of communications or letters including through electronic form as provided under the Information Technology Act, 2000 (21 of 2000); (c) any pleadings in a suit or any other proceedings in which existence of mediation agreement is alleged by one party and not denied by the other. (4) A reference in any agreement containing a mediation clause shall constitute a mediation agreement if the agreement is in writing and the reference is such as to make the mediation clause as part of the agreement. (5) The parties may agree to submit to mediation any dispute arising between them under an agreement, whether entered prior to arising of the dispute or subsequent thereto. (6) A mediation agreement in case of international mediation shall refer to an agreement for resolution in matters of commercial disputes referred to in clause (a) of section 3.

Mediation Act, 2023, Section 5. Pre-litigation mediation. (1) Subject to other provisions of this Act, whether any mediation agreement exists or not, the parties before filing any suit or proceedings of civil or commercial nature in any court, may voluntarily and with mutual consent take steps to settle the disputes by pre-litigation mediation in accordance with the provisions of this Act: Provided that pre-litigation mediation in matters of commercial disputes of Specified Value shall be undertaken in accordance with the provisions of section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 (4 of 2016), and the rules made thereunder.

Mediation Act, 2023, Section 6. Disputes or matters not fit for mediation. (1) A mediation under this Act shall not be conducted for resolution of any dispute or matter contained in the indicative list under the First Schedule: Provided that nothing contained herein shall prevent any court, if deemed appropriate, from referring any dispute relating to compoundable offences including the matrimonial offences which are compoundable and pending between the parties, to mediation: Provided further that the outcome of such mediation shall not be deemed to be a judgment or decree of court referred to in sub-section (2) of section 27, and shall be further considered by the court in accordance with the law for the time being in force. (2) If the Central Government is satisfied that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, by notification, amend the First Schedule.

Mediation Act, 2023, Section 19. Mediated settlement agreement. (1) A mediated settlement agreement includes an agreement in writing between some or all of the parties resulting from mediation, settling some or all of the disputes between such parties, and authenticated by the mediator: Provided that the terms of the mediated settlement agreement may extend beyond the disputes referred to mediation. Explanation.— A mediated settlement agreement which is void under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (9 of 1872), shall not be deemed to be lawful settlement agreement within the meaning of mediated settlement agreement. (2) Where a mediated settlement agreement is reached between the parties with regard to all or some of the disputes, the same shall be reduced in to writing and signed by the parties.

Mediation Act, 2023, Section 27. Enforcement of mediated settlement agreement. (1) A mediated settlement agreement resulting from a mediation signed by the parties and authenticated by the mediator shall be final and binding on the parties and persons claiming under them respectively and enforceable as per the provisions of sub-section (2). (2) Subject to the provisions of section 28, the mediated settlement agreement shall be enforced in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908), in the same manner as if it were a judgment or decree passed by a court, and may, accordingly, be relied on by any of the parties or persons claiming through them, by way of defence, set off or otherwise in any legal proceeding.

Mediation Act, 2023, Section 28. Challenge to mediated settlement agreement. (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, in any case in which the mediated settlement agreement is arrived at between the parties and is sought to be challenged by either of the parties, such party may file an application before the court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction. (2) A mediated settlement agreement may be challenged only on all or any of the following grounds, namely:— (i) fraud; (ii) corruption; (iii) impersonation; (iv) where the mediation was conducted in disputes or matters not fit for mediation under section 6. (3) An application for challenging the mediated settlement agreement shall not be made after ninety days have elapsed from the date on which the party making that application has received the copy of mediated settlement agreement under sub-section (3) of section 19: Provided that if the court or tribunal, as the case may be, is satisfied that the applicant was prevented by sufficient cause from making the application within the said period of ninety days, it may entertain the application within a further period of ninety days.

Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Section 89. Settlement of disputes outside the Court. (1) Where it appears to the Court that there exist elements of a settlement which may be acceptable to the parties, the Court shall formulate the terms of settlement and give them to the parties for their observations and after receiving the observations of the parties, the Court may reformulate the terms of a possible settlement and refer the same for:— (a) arbitration; (b) conciliation; (c) judicial settlement including settlement through Lok Adalat; or (d) mediation. . . . (2) Were a dispute has been referred— . . . (d) for mediation, the Court shall effect a compromise between the parties and shall follow such procedure as may be prescribed.

Commercial Courts Act, 2015, Section 12A (as quoted by the Supreme Court in Patil Automation , para 24; stated closely, with the quoted words in inverted commas). (1) "A suit, which does not contemplate any urgent interim relief under this Act, shall not be instituted" "unless the plaintiff exhausts the remedy of pre- institution mediation" "in accordance with such manner and procedure as may be prescribed by rules made by the Central Government." (3) The authorised Authority "shall complete the process of mediation within a period of three months" "from the date of application made by the plaintiff under sub-section (1)"; "the period of mediation may be extended for a further period of two months with the consent of the parties"; and "the period during which the parties remained occupied with the pre-institution mediation," "such period shall not be computed for the purpose of limitation under the Limitation Act, 1963". (4) "If the parties to the commercial dispute arrive at a settlement, the same shall be" "reduced into writing and shall be signed by the parties to the dispute and the mediator." (5) "The settlement arrived at under this section shall have the same status and effect" "as if it is an arbitral award on agreed terms under sub-section (4) of section 30" "of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996".
In simple words

Section 4, Mediation Act: a mediation agreement shall be in writing. It is an agreement by or between parties, and anyone claiming through them, to submit to mediation all or certain disputes that have arisen or may arise. It may be a clause in a contract or a separate agreement. Writing includes a signed document, an exchange of letters or electronic communications, or pleadings in which one party alleges the agreement and the other does not deny it. The parties may agree to mediate before or after the dispute arises. Section 5: whether or not a mediation agreement exists, parties may voluntarily and with mutual consent try pre-litigation mediation before filing a civil or commercial suit or proceeding. For commercial disputes of Specified Value, pre-litigation mediation is to be undertaken in accordance with Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015. Section 6: disputes on the indicative list in the First Schedule are not fit for mediation. Items include disputes involving prosecution for criminal offences, claims against minors, and disputes that affect the rights of third parties. A court may still refer compoundable offences, including compoundable matrimonial offences, to mediation, but the outcome is not a decree under Section 27(2). The Central Government may amend the First Schedule. Section 19: a mediated settlement agreement is a written agreement between some or all of the parties, resulting from mediation, settling some or all of the disputes, and authenticated (confirmed as genuine) by the mediator. Its terms may go beyond the disputes referred. A settlement that is void under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 is not a lawful mediated settlement agreement. Section 27: a mediated settlement agreement, signed by the parties and authenticated by the mediator, is final and binding on the parties and those claiming under them. It is enforced under the Code of Civil Procedure as if it were a judgment or decree of a court, and may be relied on as a defence or set-off . Section 28: it may be challenged only on grounds of fraud, corruption, impersonation (pretending to be another person), or because the dispute was not fit for mediation under Section 6. The application must be made within 90 days of receiving the copy, extendable by 90 more days for sufficient cause. Section 12A, Commercial Courts Act: a commercial suit that does not contemplate urgent interim relief shall not be instituted until the plaintiff has tried pre-institution mediation. The mediation is to be completed in three months, extendable by two months with consent, and that time is not counted for limitation. A settlement is put in writing and signed by the parties and the mediator, and has the status of an arbitral award on agreed terms. Section 89, CPC: where there are elements of a settlement acceptable to the parties, the court may refer the dispute to arbitration, conciliation, judicial settlement (including Lok Adalat) or mediation. In a mediation, the court effects a compromise between the parties by the prescribed procedure.
en.meaning:
A mediation agreement is a contract in which parties agree to try to settle disputes with the help of a mediator. The mediator is a neutral (not taking either side) person who helps the parties reach their own settlement. He does not decide. The result, if the parties agree, is a mediated settlement agreement. As a contract, a mediation agreement must meet the usual conditions of the Indian Contract Act, 1872: free consent , a lawful object, and consideration , which here is the parties' mutual promises to mediate. Section 19 adds the same check at the other end: a settlement that is void under the Contract Act is not a lawful mediated settlement agreement. The question this topic answers. If parties promise to try mediation, what must the promise look like, which disputes can go to mediation, and what is the force of the settlement they reach? Why the law has this rule. Parties who settle their own dispute are more likely to keep the settlement and the business relationship. The law gives the settlement the force of a decree so that the effort is not wasted. The mediator, a neutral person, helps them talk and reach their own terms. If they agree, they sign a mediated settlement agreement, which the mediator authenticates (Section 19). It is final and binding and enforceable as a decree (Section 27), and can be challenged only on the grounds in Section 28. The mediator does not decide the dispute and cannot impose a settlement.
keyPoints: A mediation agreement is a written contract to mediate present or future disputes (Section 4). The mediator helps. The parties decide. Pre-litigation mediation is voluntary under Section 5. It is mandatory for commercial suits under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act ( Patil Automation ). A mediated settlement agreement is binding and enforceable as a decree (Section 27). Challenge only on fraud, corruption, impersonation or unfit subject matter, within 90 days, plus 90 for sufficient cause (Section 28). Sections 4, 5, 6, 19, 27 and 28 await commencement; only some sections came into force on 9 October 2023.

caseLaws.name: Patil Automation Pvt
caseLaws.facts: Ltd. v. Rakheja Engineers Pvt. Ltd. (2022) Facts. The Supreme Court considered whether pre-institution mediation under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 is mandatory, in commercial suits that did not contemplate urgent interim relief. Principle. It is mandatory: "the language used in Section 12A is plainly imperative in nature" (para 53). A commercial suit filed in breach, where no urgent interim relief is sought, must be rejected, and the court may do so on its own (para 68). Supreme Court, 17 August 2022, K.M. Joseph and Hrishikesh Roy JJ. Why it matters. It is the rule that makes mediation compulsory for commercial suits. Afcons Infrastructure Ltd. v. Cherian Varkey Construction Co. (P) Ltd. (2010) Facts. Afcons sub-contracted part of a Cochin Port Trust bridge and road contract to Cherian Varkey, under a sub-contract with no arbitration clause. The sub-contractor sued for ₹2,10,70,881 with interest, and the trial court referred the suit to arbitration under Section 89. Principle. A court must consider ADR after the pleadings, but it cannot refer a suit to arbitration under Section 89 "unless all the parties to the suit agree" (para 35). A mediation settlement is placed before the court for recording (para 28). The appeal was allowed and the reference set aside. (2010) 8 SCC 24 (26 July 2010, R.V. Raveendran and J.M. Panchal JJ.). Why it matters. It explains court-annexed mediation.

selfTest.q: 1. Must a mediation agreement be in writing?
selfTest.a: Yes. Section 4 of the Mediation Act, 2023 says so.

selfTest.q: 2. How is a mediated settlement agreement enforced?
selfTest.a: As if it were a judgment or decree of a court (Section 27).

selfTest.q: 3. On what grounds can it be challenged?
selfTest.a: Fraud, corruption, impersonation, or because the dispute was not fit for mediation (Section 28).

selfTest.q: 4. Is pre-litigation mediation compulsory under the Mediation Act?
selfTest.a: No. It is voluntary under Section 5. It is compulsory only for commercial suits of Specified Value under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, unless urgent interim relief is contemplated.

selfTest.q: 5. Can a void settlement be a mediated settlement agreement?
selfTest.a: No. The Explanation to Section 19(1) says a settlement void under the Indian Contract Act is not a lawful mediated settlement agreement.

సెక్షన్ 4, Mediation Act: మీడియేషన్ ఒప్పందం లిఖితంగా ఉండాలి. వచ్చిన లేదా రాబోయే అన్ని లేదా కొన్ని వివాదాలను మీడియేషన్‌కు అప్పగిస్తామని పక్షాల మధ్య, వారి ద్వారా హక్కు కోరేవారితో సహా, చేసుకునే ఒప్పందం అది. అది కాంట్రాక్టులో ఒక క్లాజుగా గానీ, విడి ఒప్పందంగా గానీ ఉండవచ్చు. సంతకం చేసిన పత్రం, లేఖలు లేదా ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ సమాచార మార్పిడి, లేదా ఒక పక్షం ఒప్పందం ఉందని చెప్పి మరో పక్షం కాదనని pleadings లిఖితమే. వివాదం రాకముందు గానీ, వచ్చిన తర్వాత గానీ మీడియేషన్‌కు అంగీకరించవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 5: మీడియేషన్ ఒప్పందం ఉన్నా లేకపోయినా, సివిల్ లేదా వాణిజ్య దావా వేసే ముందు, పక్షాలు స్వచ్ఛందంగా, పరస్పర అంగీకారంతో pre-litigation మీడియేషన్ ప్రయత్నించవచ్చు. Specified Value ఉన్న వాణిజ్య వివాదాల్లో, pre-litigation మీడియేషన్ Commercial Courts Act, 2015 సెక్షన్ 12A ప్రకారం జరగాలి. సెక్షన్ 6: First Schedule లోని సూచనాత్మక జాబితాలోని వివాదాలు మీడియేషన్‌కు తగినవి కావు. వాటిలో నేర విచారణతో కూడిన వివాదాలు, మైనర్లపై క్లెయిములు, మూడో పక్షాల హక్కులను ప్రభావితం చేసే వివాదాలు ఉన్నాయి. రాజీ చేయదగిన నేరాలను, రాజీ చేయదగిన వైవాహిక నేరాలతో సహా, కోర్టు ఇంకా మీడియేషన్‌కు పంపవచ్చు, కానీ ఫలితం సెక్షన్ 27(2) కింది డిక్రీ కాదు. కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వం First Schedule ను సవరించవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 19: మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందం అంటే, మీడియేషన్ ఫలితంగా, కొన్ని లేదా అన్ని వివాదాలను పరిష్కరిస్తూ, కొందరు లేదా అందరు పక్షాల మధ్య, మీడియేటర్ ధృవీకరించిన (authenticated) లిఖిత ఒప్పందం. దాని నిబంధనలు అప్పగించిన వివాదాలను మించి వెళ్లవచ్చు. Indian Contract Act, 1872 కింద శూన్యమైన సెటిల్‌మెంట్ చట్టబద్ధమైన మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందం కాదు. సెక్షన్ 27: పక్షాలు సంతకం చేసి, మీడియేటర్ ధృవీకరించిన మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందం పక్షాలపై, వారి కింద హక్కు కోరేవారిపై అంతిమమైనది, కట్టుబడి ఉండాల్సినది. కోర్టు తీర్పు లేదా డిక్రీ లాగే Code of Civil Procedure కింద దాన్ని అమలు చేస్తారు; defence లేదా set-off గా కూడా వాడుకోవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 28: మోసం, అవినీతి, ఇతరుడిగా నటించడం (impersonation), లేదా సెక్షన్ 6 కింద వివాదం మీడియేషన్‌కు తగినది కాకపోవడం అనే కారణాలపై మాత్రమే దాన్ని సవాలు చేయవచ్చు. ప్రతి అందిన 90 రోజుల్లో దరఖాస్తు చేయాలి; తగిన కారణం ఉంటే మరో 90 రోజులు పొడిగించవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 12A, Commercial Courts Act: అత్యవసర మధ్యంతర ఉపశమనం కోరని వాణిజ్య దావాను, వాది pre-institution మీడియేషన్ ప్రయత్నించే వరకు వేయకూడదు. మీడియేషన్ మూడు నెలల్లో పూర్తి కావాలి, అంగీకారంతో రెండు నెలలు పొడిగించవచ్చు, ఆ సమయాన్ని limitation కు లెక్కించరు. సెటిల్‌మెంట్‌ను లిఖితంగా రాసి పక్షాలు, మీడియేటర్ సంతకం చేస్తారు; దానికి అంగీకరించిన నిబంధనలపై arbitral award హోదా ఉంటుంది. సెక్షన్ 89, CPC: పక్షాలకు ఆమోదయోగ్యమైన సెటిల్‌మెంట్ అంశాలు ఉన్నచోట, కోర్టు వివాదాన్ని arbitration, conciliation, judicial settlement (Lok Adalat తో సహా) లేదా మీడియేషన్‌కు పంపవచ్చు. మీడియేషన్‌లో, నిర్దేశిత విధానం ప్రకారం కోర్టు పక్షాల మధ్య రాజీ కుదురుస్తుంది.
te.meaning:
మీడియేషన్ ఒప్పందం అంటే, ఒక మీడియేటర్ సహాయంతో వివాదాలను పరిష్కరించుకోవడానికి ప్రయత్నిస్తామని పక్షాలు అంగీకరించే కాంట్రాక్టు. మీడియేటర్ తటస్థ (ఏ వైపూ మొగ్గని) వ్యక్తి; పక్షాలు తమ సొంత సెటిల్‌మెంట్‌కు చేరడానికి సహాయం చేస్తారు. ఆయన నిర్ణయించరు. పక్షాలు అంగీకరిస్తే ఫలితం మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందం. కాంట్రాక్టు కాబట్టి, మీడియేషన్ ఒప్పందం Indian Contract Act, 1872 లోని సాధారణ షరతులను నెరవేర్చాలి: స్వేచ్ఛాయుత సమ్మతి , చట్టబద్ధమైన లక్ష్యం, ప్రతిఫలం ; ఇక్కడ ప్రతిఫలం మీడియేషన్ చేస్తామని పక్షాలు ఒకరికొకరు ఇచ్చుకునే వాగ్దానాలు. సెక్షన్ 19 మరో చివర కూడా ఇదే పరీక్ష పెడుతుంది: Contract Act కింద శూన్యమైన సెటిల్‌మెంట్ చట్టబద్ధమైన మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందం కాదు. ఈ అంశం జవాబిచ్చే ప్రశ్న. మీడియేషన్ ప్రయత్నిస్తామని పక్షాలు వాగ్దానం చేస్తే, ఆ వాగ్దానం ఎలా ఉండాలి, ఏ వివాదాలు మీడియేషన్‌కు వెళ్లవచ్చు, వారు చేరిన సెటిల్‌మెంట్‌కు ఎంత బలం ఉంటుంది? చట్టం ఈ నియమం ఎందుకు పెట్టింది. తమ వివాదాన్ని తామే పరిష్కరించుకున్న పక్షాలు ఆ సెటిల్‌మెంట్‌ను, వ్యాపార సంబంధాన్ని నిలుపుకునే అవకాశం ఎక్కువ. ఆ శ్రమ వృథా కాకుండా చట్టం సెటిల్‌మెంట్‌కు డిక్రీ బలాన్ని ఇస్తుంది. పక్షాల చిత్రం ఎవరు ఏం చేస్తారో చూపిస్తుంది. selfTest.q: 1. మీడియేషన్ ఒప్పందం లిఖితంగా ఉండాలా?
selfTest.a: అవును. Mediation Act, 2023 సెక్షన్ 4 అలా చెబుతుంది.

selfTest.q: 2. మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందాన్ని ఎలా అమలు చేస్తారు?
selfTest.a: కోర్టు తీర్పు లేదా డిక్రీ లాగా (సెక్షన్ 27).

selfTest.q: 3. దాన్ని ఏ కారణాలపై సవాలు చేయవచ్చు?
selfTest.a: మోసం, అవినీతి, impersonation, లేదా వివాదం మీడియేషన్‌కు తగినది కాకపోవడం (సెక్షన్ 28).

selfTest.q: 4. Mediation Act కింద pre-litigation మీడియేషన్ తప్పనిసరా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. సెక్షన్ 5 కింద అది స్వచ్ఛందం. అత్యవసర మధ్యంతర ఉపశమనం కోరితే తప్ప, Commercial Courts Act సెక్షన్ 12A కింద Specified Value వాణిజ్య దావాలకు మాత్రమే తప్పనిసరి.

selfTest.q: 5. శూన్యమైన సెటిల్‌మెంట్ మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందం కాగలదా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. Indian Contract Act కింద శూన్యమైన సెటిల్‌మెంట్ చట్టబద్ధమైన మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందం కాదని సెక్షన్ 19(1) Explanation చెబుతుంది.

Explanation. Specific relief means relief in specie — the actual thing a party was entitled to, not a substitute money value.

The Specific Relief Act, 1963 replaced which earlier statute?

Explanation. The Specific Relief Act, 1963 (Act 47 of 1963) replaced the Specific Relief Act, 1877, and came into force on 1 March 1964.

How many Parts does the Specific Relief Act, 1963 have?

Explanation. The Act has three Parts: Part I (Preliminary), Part II (Specific Relief), and Part III (Preventive Relief), across eight chapters.

law-of-contract-i-u5-t16.subtitle: Works contracts under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 and the Specific Relief Act, 1963

en.inOneMinute: Building a house, a road or a bridge takes months or years and depends on weather, materials, labour and approvals. Delay, cost overruns and defective work are common, and each leads to a dispute about who pays. Construction contracts therefore carry many detailed clauses. The general rules of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 and the Specific Relief Act, 1963 apply to them. In exams, you must know the kinds of construction contract, the key clauses, how delay is compensated under Sections 73 and 74, and what the 2018 amendments changed for specific relief.
legalProvision: Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 55. Effect of failure to perform at fixed time, in contract in which time is essential. When a party to a contract promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, or certain things at or before specified times, and fails to do any such thing at or before the specified time, the contract, or so much of it as has not been performed, becomes voidable at the option of the promisee, if the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract. Effect of such failure when time is not essential.—If it was not the intention of the parties that time should be of the essence of the contract, the contract does not become voidable by the failure to do such thing at or before the specified time; but the promisee is entitled to compensation from the promisor for any loss occasioned to him by such failure. Effect of acceptance of performance at time other than that agreed upon.—If, in case of a contract voidable on account of the promisor’s failure to perform his promise at the time agreed, the promisee accepts performance of such promise at any time other than that agreed, the promisee cannot claim compensation for any loss occasioned by the non-performance of the promise at the time agreed, unless, at the time of such acceptance, he gives notice to the promisor of his intention to do so.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 56. Agreement to do impossible act. An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. Contract to do an act afterwards becoming impossible or unlawful.—A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. Compensation for loss through non-performance of act known to be impossible or unlawful.— Where one person has promised to do something which he knew, or, with reasonable diligence, might have known, and which the promisee did not know, to be impossible or unlawful, such promisor must make compensation to such promisee for any loss which such promisee sustains through the non- performance of the promise.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 73. Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract. When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby, which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, to be likely to result from the breach of it. Such compensation is not to be given for any remote and indirect loss or damage sustained by reason of the breach. Compensation for failure to discharge obligation resembling those created by contract.—When an obligation resembling those created by contract has been incurred and has not been discharged, any person injured by the failure to discharge it is entitled to receive the same compensation from the party in default, as if such person had contracted to discharge it and had broken his contract. Explanation.—In estimating the loss or damage arising from a breach of contract, the means which existed of remedying the inconvenience caused by the non-performance of the contract must be taken into account. Illustration (l). A, a builder, contracts to erect and finish a house by the first of January, in order that B may give possession of it at that time to C, to whom B has contracted to let it. A is informed of the contract between B and C. A builds the house so badly that, before the first of January, it falls down and has to be re-built by B, who, in consequence, loses the rent which he was to have received from C, and is obliged to make compensation to C for the breach of his contract. A must make compensation to B for the cost of rebuilding the house, for the rent lost, and for the compensation made to C.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 74. Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for. When a contract has been broken, if a sum is named in the contract as the amount to be paid in case of such breach, or if the contract contains any other stipulation by way of penalty, the party complaining of the breach is entitled, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved to have been caused thereby, to receive from the party who has broken the contract reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or, as the case may be, the penalty stipulated for. Explanation.—A stipulation for increased interest from the date of default may be a stipulation by way of penalty.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 10. Specific performance in respect of contracts. The specific performance of a contract shall be enforced by the court subject to the provisions contained in sub-section (2) of section 11, section 14 and section 16.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 14. Contracts not specifically enforceable. The following contracts cannot be specifically enforced, namely:— (a) where a party to the contract has obtained substituted performance of contract in accordance with the provisions of section 20; (b) a contract, the performance of which involves the performance of a continuous duty which the court cannot supervise; (c) a contract which is so dependent on the personal qualifications of the parties that the court cannot enforce specific performance of its material terms; and (d) a contract which is in its nature determinable.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 20. Substituted performance of contract. (1) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions contained in the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (9 of 1872), and, except as otherwise agreed upon by the parties, where the contract is broken due to non-performance of promise by any party, the party who suffers by such breach shall have the option of substituted performance through a third party or by his own agency, and, recover the expenses and other costs actually incurred, spent or suffered by him, from the party committing such breach. (2) No substituted performance of contract under sub-section (1) shall be undertaken unless the party who suffers such breach has given a notice in writing, of not less than thirty days, to the party in breach calling upon him to perform the contract within such time as specified in the notice, and on his refusal or failure to do so, he may get the same performed by a third party or by his own agency: Provided that the party who suffers such breach shall not be entitled to recover the expenses and costs under sub-section (1) unless he has got the contract performed through a third party or by his own agency. (3) Where the party suffering breach of contract has got the contract performed through a third party or by his own agency after giving notice under sub-section (1), he shall not be entitled to claim relief of specific performance against the party in breach. (4) Nothing in this section shall prevent the party who has suffered breach of contract from claiming compensation from the party in breach.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 20A. Special provisions for contract relating to infrastructure project. (1) No injunction shall be granted by a court in a suit under this Act involving a contract relating to an infrastructure project specified in the Schedule, where granting injunction would cause impediment or delay in the progress or completion of such infrastructure project.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 41. Injunction when refused. An injunction cannot be granted— . . . (ha) if it would impede or delay the progress or completion of any infrastructure project or interfere with the continued provision of relevant facility related thereto or services being the subject matter of such project.
In simple words

Section 55, Contract Act: if a party fails to perform by the agreed time, the contract (or the part not performed) is voidable at the promisee's option when the parties intended time to be of the essence. If time was not of the essence, the contract is not voidable, but the promisee gets compensation for the loss. If the promisee accepts late performance of a voidable contract, he cannot claim compensation for the delay unless he gives notice of his intention to do so when accepting. Section 56: an agreement to do an impossible act is void. A contract to do an act that later becomes impossible, or unlawful because of an event the promisor could not prevent, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. Section 73: the party who suffers by a breach gets compensation for loss which naturally arose in the usual course of things, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, was likely to result. Remote and indirect loss is not compensated. The means that existed of remedying the inconvenience must be taken into account. Illustration (l) is a builder's case. Section 74: where the contract names a sum to be paid on breach, or contains any other stipulation by way of penalty , the injured party gets reasonable compensation not exceeding the sum named, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved. Section 10, Specific Relief Act (after 2018): specific performance shall be enforced, subject to Sections 11(2), 14 and 16. Section 14: four kinds of contract cannot be specifically enforced. Clause (b) covers a contract that involves a continuous duty which the court cannot supervise (watch over and direct). Section 20: unless the parties agreed otherwise, the injured party may have the work done through a third party or his own agency, and recover the expenses and costs actually incurred, after at least 30 days' written notice. He then cannot claim specific performance, but he can still claim compensation. Sections 20A and 41(ha): no injunction that would impede or delay a Schedule infrastructure project.
en.meaning:
A construction contract is an agreement in which a contractor builds, repairs or alters a structure for an owner for a price. In law, it is usually a works contract , which is a contract to carry out work as against a contract to sell goods. The tree shows the common types. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. Start at the top box and follow the lines down. for a period, then hands it over"] style L fill:#d9f2d9,stroke:#2e7d32 style I fill:#d9f2d9,stroke:#2e7d32 style K fill:#d9f2d9,stroke:#2e7d32 style T fill:#d9f2d9,stroke:#2e7d32 style B fill:#d9f2d9,stroke:#2e7d32 Text description A construction contract can be classified in two ways. By how the price is fixed: a lump-sum contract, with a fixed total price for the whole work; an item-rate or unit-price contract, with payment by measured quantities at agreed rates; and a cost-plus contract, with actual cost plus an agreed fee or percentage. By how much the contractor does: a turnkey or EPC contract, in which one contractor designs, procures and builds, then hands over a ready project; and a build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract, in which the contractor builds and runs the project for a period and then hands it over. By how the price is fixed: a lump-sum contract (a fixed total price for the whole work); an item-rate or unit-price contract (payment by measured quantities at agreed rates); a cost-plus contract (actual cost plus an agreed fee or percentage). By how much the contractor does: a turnkey or EPC (engineering, procurement and construction) contract, in which one contractor designs, procures and builds, then hands over a ready project; a build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract, in which the contractor builds and runs the project for a period and then hands it over. The question this topic answers. How do the general rules of contract and specific relief apply when a building job is late, abandoned or defective? Why the law has this rule. A construction contract runs for a long time and many things can go wrong. The law lets the owner get compensation, get the work finished by someone else, or in some cases have the contract specifically enforced, while protecting public projects from being stopped by injunction.
keyPoints: An entire building contract is a works contract, not a sale of goods ( Gannon Dunkerley ). Time is of the essence only if the parties intended it (Section 55). Delay: compensation under Sections 73 and 74. Reasonable compensation up to the named sum. After 2018: specific performance is the rule (Section 10), but a continuous duty is a bar (Section 14(b)). Substituted performance after 30 days' notice (Section 20). Infrastructure projects are shielded from delaying injunctions (Sections 20A, 41(ha)).

caseLaws.name: State of Madras v
caseLaws.facts: Gannon Dunkerley (1958) Facts. The State sought to levy sales tax under the Madras General Sales Tax Act, 1939 on the value of materials used by a contractor in building contracts. Principle. In an entire, indivisible building contract "there is no sale as such of materials used in a building contract". It is a works contract. The State's appeal "fails, and is dismissed with costs". AIR 1958 SC 560 : 1959 SCR 379 (1 April 1958). Why it matters. It places construction contracts in the law of contract and not in the law of sale. Fateh Chand v. Balkishan Dass (1963) Facts. A buyer paid ₹1,000 as earnest money and ₹24,000 towards the price of land and a building in Delhi, and the sale was not completed. The seller claimed to forfeit the whole ₹25,000 under the contract. Principle. Section 74 covers every stipulation by way of penalty, including forfeiture of money paid. The seller keeps only reasonable compensation; here, only the ₹1,000. [1964] 1 SCR 515 : AIR 1963 SC 1405 (Constitution Bench, 15 January 1963). Why it matters. It governs liquidated damages for delay. Kailash Nath Associates v. DDA (2015) Facts. A bidder paid ₹78 lakh, 25 per cent of a ₹3.12 crore bid, as earnest money for a DDA plot. DDA forfeited it "without putting the appellant on notice" and without any loss being shown. Principle. "Damage or loss caused is a sine qua non" for Section 74 (para 43). The Single Judge's order refunding the money with 9 per cent interest was restored. (2015) 4 SCC 136 (9 January 2015, R.F. Nariman and Ranjan Gogoi JJ.). In K.R. Suresh v. R. Poornima (2025), another two-judge Bench noted that "A different view was taken by this Court in Kailash Nath" and held that a clause forfeiting earnest money "is not penal in the ordinary sense", so Section 74 is "inapplicable" to it (paras 48, 51). Why it matters. It limits sums fixed in advance. ONGC v. Saw Pipes (2003) Facts. ONGC deducted liquidated damages from a supplier's bills for late supply of casing pipes. The tribunal ordered a refund. Principle. The Supreme Court set aside the refund direction as patently illegal. Where the sum is a genuine pre-estimate, actual loss need not be proved. (2003) 5 SCC 705 : AIR 2003 SC 2629. Later changes to Section 34 narrowed the " patent illegality " ground. Why it matters. It shows how an award on liquidated damages can be tested. State of Rajasthan v. Ferro Concrete Construction (2009) Facts. A contract for a 37.41 km water pipeline in Ajmer district was treated as abandoned on 22 August 1990. The award of 21 September 1994 was challenged. Principle. The Court set aside two awards and cut pre-reference interest from 18 to 9 per cent, holding that "Courts can not sit in judgment over the award of the arbitrator , nor re-appreciate the evidence" (para 37). The appeals were allowed in part. (2009) 12 SCC 1 (22 April 2009, R.V. Raveendran and Lokeshwar Singh Panta JJ.). Why it matters. It shows the limits of court review of a construction award. Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta (1994) Facts. Allottees of flats under a development authority's housing schemes paid deposits, but the flats were not delivered on time; in one appeal ₹6,132 and ₹1,09,975 were deposited in July 1988 and the flat was not delivered "as the construction work was not complete". Principle. "Housing activity is a service", and delay in delivering possession "is denial of service" under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 (para 6). The authority's appeals were dismissed with costs. AIR 1994 SC 787 : (1994) 1 SCC 243 (5 November 1993). Why it matters. It protects home buyers.

selfTest.q: 1. Is an entire building contract a sale of the materials used?
selfTest.a: No. It is a works contract ( State of Madras v. Gannon Dunkerley , 1958).

selfTest.q: 2. What does Section 74 allow for delay under a liquidated damages clause?
selfTest.a: Reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount named ( Fateh Chand ).

selfTest.q: 3. What notice does Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act require?
selfTest.a: Written notice of at least 30 days.

selfTest.q: 4. Can an owner who has got the work finished under Section 20 also sue for specific performance?
selfTest.a: No. Section 20(3) bars it, but Section 20(4) keeps his claim for compensation.

selfTest.q: 5. Does a sharp rise in the cost of materials frustrate a construction contract?
selfTest.a: No. It is commercial hardship, not impossibility under Section 56.
