en.meaning:
Under the fault theory of divorce, the petitioner must prove:

Explanation. The fault theory requires proof of a specific matrimonial offence committed by the respondent.

Which of the following is NOT currently a ground for divorce under Section 13(1)?

Explanation. Section 13(1) now lists adultery, cruelty, desertion for two years, conversion, mental disorder, communicable venereal disease, renunciation of the world and presumed death. Clause (iv) of section 13(1) was omitted by Act 6 of 2019.

How many special grounds does section 13(2) give to a wife?

Explanation. Section 13(2) gives a wife four more grounds: pre-1955 polygamy of the husband, rape, sodomy or bestiality by him, non-cohabitation for a year after a maintenance decree, and repudiation of a marriage solemnized before she was fifteen.

Which of the following is a special ground of divorce available only to the wife under Section 13(2)?

en.meaning:
Which section of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 deals with restitution of conjugal rights?

Explanation. Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides the remedy of restitution of conjugal rights.

What must the petitioner prove to succeed under Section 9?

Explanation. The core requirement under Section 9 is withdrawal from society without reasonable excuse.

Once withdrawal from society is proved, on whom does the burden shift to prove a reasonable excuse?

Explanation. The burden shifts to the respondent once withdrawal from society is established.

In T. Sareetha v. T. Venkata Subbaiah (1983), which court declared Section 9 unconstitutional?

family-law-i-u4-t2.subtitle: From custom and personal law to the 1956 Act and the Juvenile Justice Act, as recorded in the Act and in Supriyo

en.inOneMinute: Classical law. Hindu adoption came from the texts, two special works (the Dattaka Mimamsa and the Dattaka Chandrika), and custom and usage . Its objects were religious (a son to offer funeral cakes and water) and secular (an heir) (Mulla, Section 447). Only a boy could be adopted, and a woman could not adopt to herself. The 1956 Act. The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 (HAMA) put Hindu adoption into a statute. It ends any old text, rule, interpretation, custom or usage on a matter it covers (Section 4), allows a son or a daughter to be adopted, and saves adoptions made before it (Section 30). Other children. Court guidelines on inter-country adoption ( Laxmi Kant Pandey ) came first, then executive instructions, then the Juvenile Justice Act, which enables adoption among members of all faiths and communities ( Supriyo , Bhat J., para 25). Today. The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, as amended in 2021, with the Adoption Regulations, 2022, governs adoption outside HAMA; the District Magistrate issues the adoption order.
legalProvision: Section 4, Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956. Overriding effect of Act. Save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act,— (a) any text, rule or interpretation of Hindu law or any custom or usage as part of that law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect with respect to any matter for which provision is made in this Act; (b) any other law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to apply to Hindus in so far as it is inconsistent with any of the provisions contained in this Act.

Section 30. Savings. Nothing contained in this Act shall affect any adoption made before the commencement of this Act, and the validity and effect of any such adoption shall be determined as if this Act had not been passed.
Other provisions used in this note:

HAMA, Chapter II (Sections 5 to 17): the statutory law of Hindu adoption . HAMA Section 3(a): "custom" and "usage" mean a rule continuously and uniformly observed for a long time, which has obtained the force of law among Hindus in a local area, tribe, community, group or family. Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (JJ Act): Sections 2(2), 56, 63, 68(c), 101(6), (7) and 111(1). Supriyo records Section 63 (Chandrachud CJI, para 337). Bhat J. refers to Section 41 of the Juvenile Justice Act (Section 41 of the 2000 Act), which enables adoption among members of all faiths and communities (para 25). Guardians and Wards Act, 1890: Section 7.
en.meaning:
The historical perspective traces how the law of adoption moved from old texts, custom and usage to a statute for Hindus, and then to a law open to members of all faiths. The classical rules are those described in Mulla's Principles of Hindu Law (14th edition); the modern rules are in HAMA and the JJ Act. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. Hindu adoption moved from texts and custom to the 1956 Act; adoption for all faiths moved from court guidelines to the Juvenile Justice Act. flowchart TD A["Before 1956
texts, Dattaka Mimamsa, Dattaka Chandrika
custom and usage
dattaka and kritrima"] --> H["Hindus: HAMA, 1956
ss. 4 and 30"] H --> H2["Amended 1962 and 2010"] A --> G["All faiths: Laxmi Kant Pandey guidelines
executive instructions"] G --> J1["JJ Act, 2000
Guidelines 2011 and 2015"] J1 --> J2["JJ Act, 2015
Regulations 2017"] J2 --> J3["2021 amendment
Regulations 2022
District Magistrate orders"] Text description Before 1956: texts, the Dattaka Mimamsa and Dattaka Chandrika, custom and usage; dattaka and kritrima forms. Branch one, for Hindus: the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 (Sections 4 and 30), amended in 1962 and 2010. Branch two, for all faiths: Laxmi Kant Pandey guidelines and executive instructions; the Juvenile Justice Act, 2000 with the 2011 and 2015 Guidelines; the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 with the 2017 Regulations; the 2021 amendment and the 2022 Regulations, with the District Magistrate issuing orders. Stage Source of law What it allowed Before 1956 Texts, the Dattaka Mimamsa and Dattaka Chandrika, custom and usage Adoption of a boy, mainly in the dattaka form; kritrima in Mithila 1956 HAMA, Chapter II Adoption of a son or a daughter by a Hindu man or woman From 1984 Laxmi Kant Pandey guidelines, then executive instructions Inter-country adoption under court supervision 2000 to now JJ Act 2000, then JJ Act 2015 (amended 2021); CARA Guidelines and Regulations Adoption among members of all faiths and communities
keyPoints: Classical objects: religious (funeral offerings) and secular (an heir) (Mulla, Section 447). Dattaka prevailed all over India; kritrima in Mithila. Classical law: only a boy, of the same caste; a woman could not adopt to herself in dattaka form. Section 4: old texts, rules, interpretations, custom and usage cease on matters the Act covers. HAMA: statutory adoption of sons and daughters; Section 12 gives full status. Section 30 saves adoptions made before the Act. Laxmi Kant Pandey guidelines on inter-country adoption (noted in Supriyo , para 25). Juvenile Justice Act: adoption among members of all faiths and communities (Bhat J., para 25). Shabnam Hashmi : the right to adopt was not raised to a fundamental right (quoted in Supriyo , para 307). Since 2021 the District Magistrate issues JJ Act adoption orders; the Adoption Regulations, 2022 are current.

caseLaws.name: Supriyo v
caseLaws.facts: Union of India (2023) Facts. Queer couples challenged Regulation 5(3) of the Adoption Regulations, which bars unmarried couples from adopting jointly. Principle. Bhat J. traced the law: court guidelines on inter-country adoption, then executive instructions, then the Juvenile Justice Act for all faiths (para 25). The Court also quoted Shabnam Hashmi (Chandrachud CJI, paras 307–308). 2023 INSC 920. Why it matters. It records the route open to all faiths in the Supreme Court's own words. Sitabai v. Ramchandra (1969) Facts. A widow whose husband had died in 1930 adopted a son in March 1958, after HAMA. Principle. Under Sections 11, 12 and 14, the adopted child is absorbed in the adoptive family and becomes her deceased husband's son too. AIR 1970 SC 343. Why it matters. It shows the full status HAMA gives to an adopted child, even through a widow, which classical law in Mithila would have denied.

selfTest.q: 1. What does Section 4 of HAMA do to old texts and custom?
selfTest.a: They cease to have effect on any matter for which the Act makes provision.

selfTest.q: 2. Which Act made Hindu adoption statutory?
selfTest.a: The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956.

selfTest.q: 3. Which case pioneered the guidelines for inter-country adoption?
selfTest.a: Laxmi Kant Pandey v. Union of India , as noted in Supriyo v. Union of India (para 25, Bhat J.).

selfTest.q: 4. Could a widow in Mithila adopt under classical law?
selfTest.a: No, not even with her husband's express authority (Mulla, Section 452(1)).

selfTest.q: 5. Which form of adoption let a woman adopt a son to herself?
selfTest.a: The kritrima form (Mulla, Section 515).

selfTest.q: 6. Who now issues an adoption order under the JJ Act, and where does an appeal lie?
selfTest.a: The District Magistrate; an appeal lies to the Divisional Commissioner within thirty days (Section 101(6)).

selfTest.q: 1. పాత గ్రంథాలు, ఆచారంపై HAMA సెక్షన్ 4 ఏమి చేస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: చట్టం నిబంధన చేసిన ఏ విషయంపైనా వాటికి ప్రభావం ఉండదు.

selfTest.q: 2. హిందూ దత్తతను శాసనంగా మార్చిన చట్టం ఏది?
selfTest.a: హిందూ దత్తత, భరణ చట్టం, 1956.

selfTest.q: 3. అంతర్ దేశ దత్తతకు మార్గదర్శకాలను మొదట రూపొందించిన కేసు ఏది?
selfTest.a: Laxmi Kant Pandey v. Union of India , Supriyo v. Union of India (పేరా 25, Bhat J.) లో పేర్కొన్నట్లు.

selfTest.q: 4. సాంప్రదాయ చట్టం కింద మిథిలలో వితంతువు దత్తత తీసుకోగలదా?
selfTest.a: లేదు, భర్త స్పష్టమైన అధికారం ఉన్నా కాదు (ముల్లా, సెక్షన్ 452(1)).

selfTest.q: 5. ఏ రూపం స్త్రీ తనకు తానే కొడుకును దత్తత తీసుకోవడానికి అనుమతించింది?
selfTest.a: కృత్రిమ రూపం (ముల్లా, సెక్షన్ 515).

selfTest.q: 6. ఇప్పుడు JJ Act కింద దత్తత ఉత్తర్వు ఎవరు ఇస్తారు, అప్పీలు ఎక్కడికి?
selfTest.a: జిల్లా మేజిస్ట్రేట్; ముప్పై రోజుల్లో డివిజనల్ కమిషనర్‌కు అప్పీలు (సెక్షన్ 101(6)).

family-law-i-u4-t1.subtitle: Meaning, requisites of a valid adoption, who may give and take, and the effects under the 1956 Act

en.inOneMinute: What it is. Adoption moves a child for good from the family of birth to the adoptive family. From the date of adoption the child is the child of the adoptive parents for all purposes (Section 12, Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 (HAMA)). Four requisites. The taker has the capacity and right to take, the giver has the capacity to give, the child can be adopted, and the other conditions of Chapter II are met (Section 6). Void if the Act is broken. An adoption made in breach of Chapter II is void; it creates no new rights in the adoptive family and takes away none in the family of birth (Section 5). Final. A valid adoption cannot be cancelled, and the child cannot go back to the birth family (Section 15). No payment. Giving or taking payment for an adoption is punishable with up to six months' imprisonment, or fine, or both (Section 17).
legalProvision: Section 6, Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956. Requisites of a valid adoption. No adoption shall be valid unless— (i) the person adopting has the capacity, and also the right, to take in adoption; (ii) the person giving in adoption has the capacity to do so; (iii) the person adopted is capable of being taken in adoption; and (iv) the adoption is made in compliance with the other conditions mentioned in this Chapter.

Section 12. Effects of adoption. An adopted child shall be deemed to be the child of his or her adoptive father or mother for all purposes with effect from the date of the adoption and from such date all the ties of the child in the family of his or her birth shall be deemed to be severed and replaced by those created by the adoption in the adoptive family: Provided that— (a) the child cannot marry any person whom he or she could not have married if he or she had continued in the family of his or her birth; (b) any property which vested in the adopted child before the adoption shall continue to vest in such person subject to the obligations, if any, attaching to the ownership of such property, including the obligation to maintain relatives in the family of his or her birth; (c) the adopted child shall not divest any person of any estate which vested in him or her before the adoption.
Chapter II of HAMA ( Adoption ) at a glance:

Section 5: adoption only as Chapter II provides; an adoption in breach is void. Section 6: the four requisites. Sections 7 and 8: capacity of a male and a female Hindu to take in adoption, with the spouse's consent. Section 9: who may give a child in adoption. Section 10: who may be adopted. Section 11: other conditions, including actual giving and taking. Sections 12 to 17: effects, power to dispose of property, adoptive mother, no cancellation, presumption from registered documents, and prohibition of payments.
Other provisions used in this note:

HAMA Sections 2, 3 and 4: who is covered, definitions, overriding effect. Section 30: adoptions before the Act are saved. Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (JJ Act): Sections 2(2), 56, 61 and 63. Guardians and Wards Act, 1890: Sections 24 and 41 (for the contrast with guardianship).
en.meaning:
HAMA does not define adoption. Read together, Sections 6 to 12 show it: adoption is the legal act by which a child is given and taken, with the intent to transfer the child from the family of birth to the adoptive family, so that the child becomes the child of the adoptive parents for all purposes. The JJ Act, which has its own adoption system, defines it in Section 2(2) as "the process through which the adopted child is permanently separated from his biological parents and becomes the lawful child of his adoptive parents with all the rights, privileges and responsibilities that are attached to a biological child". A valid adoption must pass all four requisites of Section 6, one after the other. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. keyPoints: Section 5: an adoption in breach of Chapter II is void. Section 6: four requisites. Spouse's consent is needed (Sections 7 and 8), with exceptions. The child must be a Hindu, unmarried, under fifteen and not already adopted, unless custom permits. Giving and taking is essential; datta homam is not. Section 12: an adopted child is the child of the adopters for all purposes. Section 16 only presumes a registered adoption to be valid; registration is not compulsory under the Act. A widow may adopt in her own right (Section 8); the child becomes her late husband's son too ( Sitabai ). The Act does not apply to Scheduled Tribes unless notified (Section 2(2)).

caseLaws.name: Sitabai v
caseLaws.facts: Ramchandra (1969) Facts. Sitabai's husband died in 1930. In March 1958, after the Act, she adopted Suresh Chandra. The question was whether he became a coparcener with her late husband's brother in the joint family property. Principle. Under Sections 11, 12 and 14, a child adopted by a widow is absorbed in the adoptive family to which she belonged and becomes the son of her deceased husband as well. AIR 1970 SC 343. Why it matters. It explains the effect of Section 12 on adoption by a widow; the boy took the joint family property as sole surviving coparcener. Addagada Raghavamma v. Addagada Chenchamma (1963) Facts. A widow claimed that her husband had adopted his elder brother's only son in 1905. No document, invitation or expense entry supported it. Principle. A person who alleges adoption to displace natural succession must prove the fact of adoption and its validity. 1964 AIR 136; [1964] 2 SCR 933. Why it matters. It shows why proof of giving and taking matters; Section 16 now presumes in favour of registered documents. Supriyo v. Union of India (2023) Facts. Queer couples challenged Regulation 5(3) of the Adoption Regulations, which bars unmarried couples from adopting jointly. Principle. The Chief Justice noted that Section 12 of HAMA and Section 63 of the JJ Act deem an adopted child to be the adopters' child for all purposes (paras 337–338, his opinion). The majority did not strike down Regulation 5(3). 2023 INSC 920. Why it matters. It restates the effect of adoption in Section 12.

selfTest.q: 1. What is the result of an adoption that breaks Chapter II?
selfTest.a: It is void (Section 5).

selfTest.q: 2. Is datta homam essential for a valid adoption?
selfTest.a: No. See the proviso to Section 11.

selfTest.q: 3. Can a valid adoption be cancelled?
selfTest.a: No (Section 15).

selfTest.q: 4. A woman aged 30 wants to adopt a boy aged 10. Is the age-gap rule met?
selfTest.a: No. The gap is 20 years; Section 11(iv) requires at least twenty-one.

selfTest.q: 5. Who gives a child of unknown parentage in adoption?
selfTest.a: The guardian, with the previous permission of the court (Section 9(4)).

selfTest.q: 6. Does the JJ Act, 2015 apply to an adoption made under HAMA?
selfTest.a: No (JJ Act, Section 56(3)).

legalProvision: Section 6, Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956. Requisites of a valid adoption. No adoption shall be valid unless— (i) the person adopting has the capacity, and also the right, to take in adoption; (ii) the person giving in adoption has the capacity to do so; (iii) the person adopted is capable of being taken in adoption; and (iv) the adoption is made in compliance with the other conditions mentioned in this Chapter.

Section 12. Effects of adoption. An adopted child shall be deemed to be the child of his or her adoptive father or mother for all purposes with effect from the date of the adoption and from such date all the ties of the child in the family of his or her birth shall be deemed to be severed and replaced by those created by the adoption in the adoptive family: Provided that— (a) the child cannot marry any person whom he or she could not have married if he or she had continued in the family of his or her birth; (b) any property which vested in the adopted child before the adoption shall continue to vest in such person subject to the obligations, if any, attaching to the ownership of such property, including the obligation to maintain relatives in the family of his or her birth; (c) the adopted child shall not divest any person of any estate which vested in him or her before the adoption.

selfTest.a: అది శూన్యం (సెక్షన్ 5).

selfTest.q: 2. చెల్లుబాటయ్యే దత్తతకు దత్త హోమం తప్పనిసరా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. సెక్షన్ 11 నిబంధన చూడండి.

4. 30 ఏళ్ల స్త్రీ 10 ఏళ్ల అబ్బాయిని దత్తత తీసుకోవాలనుకుంటుంది. వయసు తేడా నియమం నెరవేరిందా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. తేడా 20 సంవత్సరాలు; సెక్షన్ 11(iv) కనీసం ఇరవై ఒక్కటి కోరుతుంది.

family-law-i-u4-t4.subtitle: Who can claim maintenance under the 1956 Act and other laws, and how the amount is fixed

en.inOneMinute: What it is. Maintenance is the support that the law makes one person pay to another. Under Chapter III (Sections 18 to 28) of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 (HAMA), a Hindu wife, a widowed daughter-in-law, children, aged or infirm parents and certain dependants of a dead person can claim it. How much. The court fixes the amount by the status of the parties, the claimant's reasonable wants and means, and the other factors in Section 23. A claimant who ceases to be a Hindu by conversion loses the claim under this Act (Section 24). Other laws. Maintenance is also given by Sections 24 and 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (in matrimonial cases), by Section 144 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), which takes the place of Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, and by the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. Nature. In V. Tulasamma v. Sesha Reddy the Supreme Court held that a Hindu woman's right to maintenance is a pre-existing right , not a mere gift.
legalProvision: Section 3(b), Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956. "maintenance" includes― (i) in all cases, provision for food, clothing, residence, education and medical attendance and treatment; (ii) in the case of an unmarried daughter, also the reasonable expenses of and incident to her marriage;

Section 18(1). Subject to the provisions of this section, a Hindu wife, whether married before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be entitled to be maintained by her husband during her life time.
Section 22(1). Subject to the provisions of sub-section (2), the heirs of a deceased Hindu are bound to maintain the dependants of the deceased out of the estate inherited by them from the deceased.
Other provisions used in this note:

Section 18(2) and (3): the wife's right to live separately without losing maintenance, and when she loses it. Section 19: widowed daughter-in-law, from her father-in-law. Section 20: children and aged or infirm parents. Sections 21 and 22: the nine classes of dependants, and the heirs' duty. Sections 23 to 28: amount; claimant must be a Hindu; alteration; debts first; charge only if created; transfer of the estate. Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, Sections 24 and 25: maintenance pendente lite and permanent alimony . BNSS, Sections 144 to 147: maintenance of wives, children and parents by order of a Magistrate; Section 531 repeals the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Domestic Violence Act, 2005, Sections 2(a), 2(b), 2(f), 12, 17, 20 to 23, 26 and 36.
en.meaning:
Maintenance is the provision of the basic needs of a person who cannot meet them, by a person whom the law binds to provide them. Section 3(b) says it includes food, clothing, residence, education, and medical attendance and treatment, and for an unmarried daughter also the reasonable expenses of her marriage. Under the Act it is a personal obligation of a living person (wife, widowed daughter-in-law, children, parents), and for dependants an obligation of the heirs, payable out of the estate they inherit. A dependant's claim is a charge on the estate only if one is created (Section 27). Who can claim under the 1956 Act. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. Chapter III of the 1956 Act groups claimants by who must pay: a living person, or the heirs out of a dead person's estate. flowchart TD A["Maintenance under Chapter III
HAMA, 1956"] --> L["From a living person"] A --> D["From the estate of a dead person"] L --> L1["Wife, from husband
s. 18"] L --> L2["Widowed daughter-in-law,
from father-in-law, s. 19"] L --> L3["Children and aged or
infirm parents, s. 20"] D --> D1["Nine classes of dependants
from the heirs, ss. 21 and 22"] L1 --> C["Common rules, ss. 23 to 28
amount, Hindu claimant, alteration,
debts, charge, transfer"] L2 --> C L3 --> C D1 --> C Text description Top: maintenance under Chapter III of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956. Branch one, from a living person: wife from husband (Section 18); widowed daughter-in-law from father-in-law (Section 19); children and aged or infirm parents (Section 20). Branch two, from the estate of a dead person: the nine classes of dependants, from the heirs (Sections 21 and 22). Common rules for both: Sections 23 to 28. Who pays Who can claim Section A living husband His wife 18 A living father-in-law His widowed daughter-in-law 19 A living Hindu His or her children and aged or infirm parents 20 The heirs of a dead Hindu, out of the estate The dead person's dependants 21 and 22
keyPoints: Section 3(b): food, clothing, residence, education, medical care; for an unmarried daughter, marriage expenses. Section 18: wife; may live apart for justified reasons; loses it if unchaste or she converts. Section 19: widowed daughter-in-law, from the father-in-law; ends on remarriage. Section 20: children (while minors) and aged or infirm parents; includes a childless step-mother. Sections 21 and 22: nine classes of dependants; heirs pay out of the estate, in proportion to their shares. Section 23: factors for the amount. Section 24: claimant must be a Hindu. Section 27: a dependant's claim is a charge only if created. Section 28: enforceable against a transferee with notice or a donee. Section 144 BNSS speaks of "any person having sufficient means"; a Magistrate of the first class orders a monthly allowance and may order interim maintenance. Hindu Marriage Act Sections 24 and 25: interim and permanent maintenance between spouses. Tulasamma : maintenance is a pre-existing right.

caseLaws.name: Yamunabai Anantrao Adhav v
caseLaws.facts: Anantrao Shivram Adhav (1988) Facts. In June 1974 a woman went through Hindu rites with a man whose first wife was alive. She left after a week and claimed maintenance as his wife under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Principle. The marriage was void under Sections 5(i) and 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, a complete nullity, so she was not a "wife" under Section 125. AIR 1988 SC 644 : (1988) 1 SCC 530. Why it matters. The claim to maintenance as a wife depends on a valid marriage. Chanmuniya v. Virendra Kumar Singh Kushwaha (2010) Facts. A widow said she was married by Katha and Sindur to her late husband's younger brother; the High Court held that the essentials of marriage were not performed. Principle. The two-Judge Bench favoured a broad meaning of "wife" in Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, but could not depart from earlier two-Judge decisions, and referred three questions to a larger Bench. (2011) 1 SCC 141. Why it matters. It is a reference order, not a final ruling, and shows the debate on who is a wife for maintenance. D. Velusamy v. D. Patchaiammal (2010) Facts. A woman claimed maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as the appellant 's wife; he said he was already married to Lakshmi in 1980. Principle. A relationship in the nature of marriage under the Domestic Violence Act is akin to a common law marriage and needs four conditions and a shared household; the case went back to the Family Court. (2010) 10 SCC 469. Why it matters. It extends relief to women in relationships in the nature of marriage, but not to every live-in relationship. Indra Sarma v. V.K.V. Sarma (2013) Facts. From 1992 an unmarried woman lived with a married man who had two children; she knew of his marriage and later claimed relief, including maintenance, under the Domestic Violence Act. Principle. The Court gave eight guidelines and held that her relationship was not in the nature of marriage, so she was not in a "domestic relationship"; the appeal was dismissed, and the Court asked Parliament to legislate. Decided 26 November 2013. Why it matters. It sets limits on maintenance claims by live-in partners. V. Tulasamma v. Sesha Reddy (1977) Facts. A widow, whose husband died in 1931 in a joint family, got a decree for maintenance; in execution, a compromise gave her properties for her life in lieu of maintenance. Principle. Her right to maintenance is a pre-existing right in property; property given in lieu of it falls under Section 14(1), not 14(2), of the Hindu Succession Act, so she became full owner. AIR 1977 SC 1944 : (1977) 3 SCC 99. Why it matters. It shows maintenance as a real right in Hindu law that can ripen into ownership.

selfTest.q: 1. Which section gives a Hindu wife maintenance from her husband?
selfTest.a: Section 18.

selfTest.q: 2. Is a dependant's claim a charge on the estate?
selfTest.a: Not unless one is created by will, decree, agreement or otherwise (Section 27).

selfTest.q: 3. Can a person who converts claim under the 1956 Act?
selfTest.a: No (Section 24).

selfTest.q: 4. Two heirs take ₹12,00,000 and ₹4,00,000 of an estate. Maintenance of a dependant is fixed at ₹8,000 a month. How much does each pay?
selfTest.a: In proportion to their shares (Section 22(3)): the heir with ₹12,00,000 holds three-quarters of ₹16,00,000 and pays ₹6,000; the heir with ₹4,00,000 holds one-quarter and pays ₹2,000.

selfTest.q: 5. Within what time must an application to levy unpaid maintenance under Section 144 of the BNSS be made?
selfTest.a: Within one year from the date the amount became due (proviso to Section 144(3)).

selfTest.q: 6. In Tulasamma , why did the widow become full owner of property given in lieu of maintenance?
selfTest.a: Because her right to maintenance was a pre-existing right, so Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act applied, not Section 14(2).

భరణం అంటే తమ ప్రాథమిక అవసరాలు తీర్చుకోలేని వ్యక్తికి, వాటిని అందించాలని చట్టం బాధ్యత పెట్టిన వ్యక్తి అందించడం. ఆహారం, దుస్తులు, నివాసం, విద్య, వైద్య సంరక్షణ, చికిత్స, పెళ్లికాని కూతురికి ఆమె పెళ్లి సహేతుక ఖర్చులు కూడా ఇందులో ఉంటాయని సెక్షన్ 3(b) చెబుతుంది. చట్టం కింద ఇది జీవించి ఉన్న వ్యక్తి వ్యక్తిగత బాధ్యత (భార్య, వితంతువైన కోడలు, పిల్లలు, తల్లిదండ్రులు), ఆశ్రితుల విషయంలో వారసులు పొందిన ఆస్తి నుంచి చెల్లించాల్సిన బాధ్యత. ఆశ్రితుడి దావా సృష్టిస్తేనే ఆస్తిపై భారం అవుతుంది (సెక్షన్ 27). 1956 చట్టం కింద ఎవరు దావా వేయవచ్చు. family-law-i-u4-t3.subtitle: Eligibility under section 57 and Regulation 5, the effect of an adoption order and the guidelines noted in Supriyo

en.inOneMinute: Two routes. The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 (HAMA) covers adoption by Hindus. The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (JJ Act) is a separate system for orphan, abandoned and surrendered children, open to people of every religion, with eligibility rules in Section 57 and in Regulation 5 of the Adoption Regulations, 2022. In-country and inter-country. In-country adoption places a child with parents resident in India. Inter-country adoption sends a child from India to parents living abroad; Indian, non-resident Indian and overseas citizen of India parents get priority (Section 59). Who decides. Since the 2021 amendment, the District Magistrate, not a court, issues the adoption order (Section 61). The Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA) frames the Regulations and acts as India's Central Authority under the Hague Convention, 1993 (Section 68). History. Bhat J. notes that guidelines pioneered in Laxmi Kant Pandey v. UOI helped inter-country adoptions, and executive instructions filled the vacuum to some extent ( Supriyo , para 25).
legalProvision: Section 57, Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015. Eligibility of prospective adoptive parents. (1) The prospective adoptive parents shall be physically fit, financially sound, mentally alert and highly motivated to adopt a child for providing a good upbringing to him. (2) In case of a couple, the consent of both the spouses for the adoption shall be required. (3) A single or divorced person can also adopt, subject to fulfilment of the criteria and in accordance with the provisions of adoption regulations framed by the Authority. (4) A single male is not eligible to adopt a girl child. (5) Any other criteria that may be specified in the adoption regulations framed by the Authority.

Section 59(1). If an orphan or abandoned or surrendered child could not be placed with an Indian or non-resident Indian prospective adoptive parent despite the joint effort of the Specialised Adoption Agency and State Agency within sixty days from the date the child has been declared legally free for adoption, such child shall be free for inter-country adoption: Provided that children with physical and mental disability, siblings and children above five years of age may be given preference over other children for such inter-country adoption, in accordance with the adoption regulations, as may be framed by the Authority.
Other provisions used in this note:

JJ Act Section 2(49): " prospective adoptive parents" means the person or persons eligible to adopt under Section 57. Section 63: an adoption order makes the child the child of the adoptive parents ( Supriyo , Chandrachud CJI, para 337). Sections 2(3) and 68(c): the Authority is CARA, which frames the Adoption Regulations. Sections 35, 38, 56 to 62, 65 to 68, 80 and 101(6): surrender, legal freedom, the adoption scheme, the roles of the Specialised Adoption Agency and the District Magistrate (since the 2021 amendment), CARA, the offence of unlawful adoption and the appeal. Adoption Regulations, 2022 (G.S.R. 726(E), 23 September 2022): principles, eligible children, eligibility, availability, registration, referral, timelines, inter-country steps, relative and step-parent adoption, grievances, and HAMA adoptions that go abroad. Hague Convention on Intercountry Adoption, 1993: Articles 1, 2, 4 to 7, 15 to 17, 19, 21, 23, 24 and 32, summarised below.
en.meaning:
Inter-country adoption is the adoption of a child from one country by parents living in another. In-country adoption is the adoption of a child within India by parents resident in India. Under the JJ Act, "adoption" is the process through which the child is permanently separated from the biological parents and becomes the lawful child of the adoptive parents, with all the rights, privileges and responsibilities of a biological child (Section 2(2)). Eligibility to adopt under the JJ Act is checked in layers: the Act first, then the Regulations. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. If met, check Regulation 5: health and no conviction; two years' stable marital relationship for a couple; age limits and a 25-year age gap. If not met, not eligible. If met, the District Magistrate's adoption order; under section 63 the child becomes the adopters' child for all purposes. keyPoints: Two routes: HAMA, 1956 and the JJ Act, 2015. Section 57: eligibility; both spouses consent; a single male cannot adopt a girl. Regulation 5(3): two years of stable marital relationship for couples; Supriyo (3:2) did not read it down. Regulation 5(4): age limits by the child's age; at least twenty-five years' gap. Indians first: sixty days for a child below five, thirty for older children and siblings (Regulation 8; Section 59(1)). The District Magistrate issues the adoption order; appeal to the Divisional Commissioner within thirty days. An adoption order makes the child the adopters' child (Section 63). Bhat J. notes the Laxmi Kant Pandey guidelines on inter-country adoption (para 25). The Authority under Section 2(3) is CARA, India's Central Authority under the Hague Convention (Section 68(d)).

caseLaws.name: Supriyo v
caseLaws.facts: Union of India (2023) Facts. Queer couples challenged Regulation 5(3) of the Adoption Regulations, which allows a couple to adopt only after two years of stable marital relationship. Principle. By 3:2, the Court did not read down Regulation 5(3). Bhat J. held that Section 57(2) of the Act contemplates joint adoption only by married couples (paras 120–123); the Chief Justice would have read down "marital" (paras 299–317). 2023 INSC 920. Why it matters. It is the Supreme Court's latest word on who may adopt jointly under the Act.

selfTest.q: 1. Which section bars a single male from adopting a girl child?
selfTest.a: Section 57(4).

selfTest.q: 2. What does Section 63 do to an adopted child's status?
selfTest.a: It makes the child the child of the adoptive parents for all purposes, including intestacy ( Supriyo , para 337).

selfTest.q: 3. Which 2023 case decided on joint adoption by unmarried couples?
selfTest.a: Supriyo v. Union of India : by 3:2 the Court did not read down Regulation 5(3).

selfTest.q: 4. A couple's composite age is 98. Can they adopt a child of three?
selfTest.a: No. For a child above two and up to four the limit is 90; they can adopt a child above four and up to eight (limit 100) (Regulation 5(4)).

selfTest.q: 5. When does a normal child below five become available to foreign parents?
selfTest.a: Only after sixty days for Indian, NRI and OCI parents and seven more days for them regardless of seniority (Regulation 8; Section 59(1)).

selfTest.q: 6. Which certificate does CARA issue under Article 23 of the Hague Convention?
selfTest.a: The Conformity Certificate (Regulation 19(1)).

legalProvision: Section 57, Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015. Eligibility of prospective adoptive parents. (1) The prospective adoptive parents shall be physically fit, financially sound, mentally alert and highly motivated to adopt a child for providing a good upbringing to him. (2) In case of a couple, the consent of both the spouses for the adoption shall be required. (3) A single or divorced person can also adopt, subject to fulfilment of the criteria and in accordance with the provisions of adoption regulations framed by the Authority. (4) A single male is not eligible to adopt a girl child. (5) Any other criteria that may be specified in the adoption regulations framed by the Authority.

Section 59(1). If an orphan or abandoned or surrendered child could not be placed with an Indian or non-resident Indian prospective adoptive parent despite the joint effort of the Specialised Adoption Agency and State Agency within sixty days from the date the child has been declared legally free for adoption, such child shall be free for inter-country adoption: Provided that children with physical and mental disability, siblings and children above five years of age may be given preference over other children for such inter-country adoption, in accordance with the adoption regulations, as may be framed by the Authority.
ఈ నోట్‌లో వాడిన ఇతర నిబంధనలు:

JJ Act సెక్షన్ 2(49): "కాబోయే దత్తత తల్లిదండ్రులు" అంటే సెక్షన్ 57 కింద దత్తతకు అర్హులైన వ్యక్తి లేదా వ్యక్తులు. సెక్షన్ 63: దత్తత ఉత్తర్వు బిడ్డను దత్తత తల్లిదండ్రుల బిడ్డగా చేస్తుంది ( Supriyo , Chandrachud CJI, పేరా 337). సెక్షన్లు 2(3), 68(c): అధికార సంస్థ CARA, అది Adoption Regulations రూపొందిస్తుంది. సెక్షన్లు 35, 38, 56 నుంచి 62, 65 నుంచి 68, 80, 101(6): అప్పగింత, చట్టపరమైన స్వేచ్ఛ, దత్తత పథకం, ప్రత్యేక దత్తత సంస్థ, జిల్లా మేజిస్ట్రేట్ (2021 సవరణ నుంచి) పాత్రలు, CARA, అక్రమ దత్తత నేరం, అప్పీలు. Adoption Regulations, 2022 (G.S.R. 726(E), 23 సెప్టెంబర్ 2022): సూత్రాలు, అర్హులైన పిల్లలు, అర్హత, లభ్యత, రిజిస్ట్రేషన్, రిఫరల్, కాల పరిమితులు, అంతర్ దేశ దశలు, బంధువులు, సవతి తల్లిదండ్రుల దత్తత, ఫిర్యాదులు, విదేశాలకు వెళ్లే HAMA దత్తతలు. అంతర్ దేశ దత్తతపై హేగ్ కన్వెన్షన్, 1993: అధికరణలు 1, 2, 4 నుంచి 7, 15 నుంచి 17, 19, 21, 23, 24, 32, కింద సంక్షిప్తంగా.

అంతర్ దేశ దత్తత అంటే ఒక దేశంలోని బిడ్డను మరో దేశంలో నివసించే తల్లిదండ్రులు దత్తత తీసుకోవడం. దేశంలో దత్తత అంటే భారతదేశంలో నివసించే తల్లిదండ్రులు భారతదేశంలోనే బిడ్డను దత్తత తీసుకోవడం. JJ Act కింద, "దత్తత" అంటే బిడ్డ జీవసంబంధమైన తల్లిదండ్రుల నుంచి శాశ్వతంగా వేరై, జీవసంబంధమైన బిడ్డకు ఉండే అన్ని హక్కులు, ప్రయోజనాలు, బాధ్యతలతో దత్తత తల్లిదండ్రుల చట్టబద్ధమైన బిడ్డ అయ్యే ప్రక్రియ (సెక్షన్ 2(2)). JJ Act కింద దత్తత అర్హతను పొరలుగా చూస్తారు: మొదట చట్టం, తర్వాత Regulations. Diagram 1 చూడండి. Diagram 1. అర్హతను పొరలుగా చూస్తారు: మొదట చట్టం (సెక్షన్ 57), తర్వాత Regulations (Regulation 5); తర్వాత దత్తత ఉత్తర్వు బిడ్డను దత్తత తీసుకున్నవారి బిడ్డగా చేస్తుంది (సెక్షన్ 63). flowchart TD A["వ్యక్తి లేదా జంట

దత్తత తల్లిదండ్రుల బిడ్డ"] వచన వివరణ ప్రారంభం: వ్యక్తి లేదా జంట JJ Act కింద దత్తత తీసుకోవాలనుకుంటున్నారు (సెక్షన్లు 56, 58, 59). సెక్షన్ 57 చూడండి: దృఢత్వం, ఆర్థిక స్థిరత్వం, చురుకుదనం, కోరిక; భార్యాభర్తలు ఇద్దరి సమ్మతి; ఒంటరి పురుషుడు అమ్మాయిని దత్తత తీసుకోలేడు. నెరవేరకపోతే అర్హులు కారు. నెరవేరితే Regulation 5 చూడండి: ఆరోగ్యం, శిక్ష లేకపోవడం; జంటకు రెండేళ్ల స్థిరమైన వైవాహిక సంబంధం; వయసు పరిమితులు, 25 సంవత్సరాల తేడా. నెరవేరకపోతే అర్హులు కారు. నెరవేరితే జిల్లా మేజిస్ట్రేట్ దత్తత ఉత్తర్వు; సెక్షన్ 63 కింద బిడ్డ అన్ని ప్రయోజనాలకూ దత్తత తీసుకున్నవారి బిడ్డ. దశ ప్రశ్న నిబంధన 1 వ్యక్తి లేదా జంట JJ Act కింద దత్తత తీసుకోవాలనుకుంటున్నారా? సెక్షన్లు 56, 58, 59 2 సెక్షన్ 57 లోని లక్షణాలు, భార్యాభర్తలు ఇద్దరి సమ్మతి ఉన్నాయా? సెక్షన్ 57 3 Regulation 5 (ఆరోగ్యం, రికార్డు, వైవాహిక స్థితి, లింగం, వయసు) నెరవేరుతుందా? Regulation 5 ఫలితం దత్తత ఉత్తర్వు బిడ్డను దత్తత తీసుకున్నవారి బిడ్డగా చేస్తుంది సెక్షన్ 63

selfTest.q: 1. ఒంటరి పురుషుడు అమ్మాయిని దత్తత తీసుకోవడాన్ని ఏ సెక్షన్ నిషేధిస్తుంది?
2. దత్తత బిడ్డ హోదాపై సెక్షన్ 63 ఏమి చేస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: వారసత్వం సహా అన్ని ప్రయోజనాలకూ బిడ్డను దత్తత తల్లిదండ్రుల బిడ్డగా చేస్తుంది ( Supriyo , పేరా 337).

selfTest.q: 3. పెళ్లికాని జంటల ఉమ్మడి దత్తతపై ఏ 2023 కేసు నిర్ణయించింది?
selfTest.a: Supriyo v. Union of India : 3:2 తో కోర్టు Regulation 5(3) ను పరిమితం చేసి చదవలేదు.

selfTest.q: 4. ఒక జంట ఉమ్మడి వయసు 98. వారు మూడేళ్ల బిడ్డను దత్తత తీసుకోవచ్చా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. 2 పైన 4 వరకు బిడ్డకు పరిమితి 90; వారు 4 పైన 8 వరకు బిడ్డను దత్తత తీసుకోవచ్చు (పరిమితి 100) (Regulation 5(4)).

selfTest.q: 5. ఐదేళ్ల లోపు సాధారణ బిడ్డ విదేశీ తల్లిదండ్రులకు ఎప్పుడు అందుబాటులోకి వస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: భారతీయ, NRI, OCI తల్లిదండ్రులకు అరవై రోజులు, సీనియారిటీతో సంబంధం లేకుండా వారికే మరో ఏడు రోజుల తర్వాత మాత్రమే (Regulation 8; సెక్షన్ 59(1)).

selfTest.q: 6. హేగ్ కన్వెన్షన్ అధికరణ 23 కింద CARA ఏ సర్టిఫికెట్ జారీ చేస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: అనుగుణత సర్టిఫికెట్ (Conformity Certificate) (Regulation 19(1)).

Guideline 5: శారీరకంగా, మానసికంగా, భావోద్వేగపరంగా స్థిరంగా, ఆర్థికంగా సమర్థులుగా, ప్రేరణతో, ప్రాణాంతక వైద్య పరిస్థితి లేకుండా. ఒంటరి స్త్రీ ఏ లింగం బిడ్డనైనా; ఒంటరి పురుషుడు అమ్మాయిని కాదు. భార్యాభర్తలు ఇద్దరి సమ్మతి. రెండేళ్ల స్థిరమైన వైవాహిక సంబంధం. నలుగురు కంటే ఎక్కువ పిల్లలున్న జంటలను పరిగణించరు. Regulation 5: సామర్థ్యం, సమ్మతి, ఒంటరి స్త్రీ, ఒంటరి పురుషుడు, రెండేళ్ల స్థిరమైన వైవాహిక సంబంధంపై అవే ముఖ్య నియమాలు. బంధువులు లేదా సవతి తల్లిదండ్రులు కాకపోతే, ఇద్దరు లేదా ఎక్కువ పిల్లలున్న జంటను ప్రత్యేక అవసరాల, కష్టంగా ఉంచగల పిల్లలకు మాత్రమే పరిగణిస్తారు (Regulation 5(7)).
వయసు నియమాలు జంట ఉమ్మడి వయసు: 0 నుంచి 3 సంవత్సరాల బిడ్డకు 90, 3 పైన 105 (Guideline 6(3), (4)). ఒంటరి తల్లి లేదా తండ్రి 30 నుంచి 50, 0 నుంచి 3 బిడ్డకు గరిష్ఠం 45 (Guideline 6(5)). బిడ్డ వయసును బట్టి పట్టిక వయసు పరిమితులు నిర్ణయిస్తుంది (Guideline 5); వాడిన ప్రతిలో దాని అంకెలు స్పష్టంగా లేవు. కనీస వయసు తేడా ఇరవై ఐదు సంవత్సరాలు. Regulation 5(4): 2 వరకు, 2 పైన 4 వరకు, 4 పైన 8 వరకు, 8 పైన 18 వరకు బిడ్డ వయసు వర్గాలను బట్టి ఉమ్మడి 85, 90, 100, లేదా 110, ఒంటరి 40, 45, 50, లేదా 55. తేడా కనీసం ఇరవై ఐదు సంవత్సరాలు.
ప్రాధాన్యం దేశంలో దత్తతకు ప్రాధాన్యం (Guideline 3(b)). ప్రత్యేక అవసరాల పిల్లలు మినహా, గుర్తింపు పొందిన భారతీయ ప్లేస్‌మెంట్ సంస్థ ఏటా ప్రాసెస్ చేసే మొత్తంలో దేశంలో, అంతర్ దేశ నిష్పత్తి 80:20 (Guideline 8(5)). అంతర్ దేశ క్రమం: NRI, OCI, PIO, విదేశీయులు (Guideline 8(6)). బిడ్డ సామాజిక, సాంస్కృతిక వాతావరణాన్ని దృష్టిలో ఉంచుకుని భారత పౌరులకు ప్రాధాన్యం (Guideline 3(b)). భారతదేశంలో నివసించే భారతీయులతో NRI లు సమానం (Guideline 15). భారత పౌరులకు ప్రాధాన్యం (Regulation 3(b)). కాల వ్యవధులు బిడ్డను మొదట భారతదేశంలో నివసించే, NRI, OCI కార్డు తల్లిదండ్రులకు కేటాయిస్తాయి (Regulation 8). family-law-i-u4-t6.subtitle: Scheme of the Act: application, definitions, overriding effect, adoption, maintenance and savings

en.inOneMinute: What it is. The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 (HAMA) is one of the four Hindu Acts of 1955–56. It codifies two subjects: adoption (Chapter II, Sections 5 to 17) and maintenance (Chapter III, Sections 18 to 28). Who it covers. It applies to Hindus in the sense of Section 2 (Hindus, Buddhists, Jainas, Sikhs and the residuary group), but not to Scheduled Tribes unless notified. Overriding effect. It prevails over older Hindu law and custom on the matters it covers (Section 4). Extent and savings. It extends to the whole of India. Adoptions made before the Act are not affected (Section 30). The Act codified adoption and let women adopt in their own right. Scope of this note. The scheme of the Act as a whole. Adoption and maintenance are explained in detail in their own notes.
legalProvision: Long title. An Act to amend and codify the law relating to adoptions and maintenance among Hindus.

Section 4. Overriding effect of Act. ―Save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act,― (a) any text, rule or interpretation of Hindu law or any custom or usage as part of that law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect with respect to any matter for which provision is made in this Act; (b) any other law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to apply to Hindus in so far as it is inconsistent with any of the provisions contained in this Act.

Section 30. Savings. ―Nothing contained in this Act shall affect any adoption made before the commencement of this Act, and the validity and effect of any such adoption shall be determined as if this Act had not been passed.
Other provisions used in this note:

Section 1: short title, and extent to the whole of India. Section 2: application to Hindus by religion in any form, Buddhists, Jainas, Sikhs and the residuary group, with the Explanation on children (including an abandoned child or a child of unknown parentage brought up as a Hindu, Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh) and converts. Section 2(2) excludes Scheduled Tribes unless notified. Section 3: definitions of "custom" and "usage", "maintenance" and "minor". Sections 5 to 17: Chapter II, adoptions . Sections 18 to 28: Chapter III, maintenance. Section 29: repeals (itself repealed in 1960).
en.meaning:
The Act is a codifying statute : a law passed by Parliament that sets out in one place the Hindu law on adoption and maintenance and replaces the old rules on those matters. Section 3 defines "maintenance" as food, clothing, residence, education and medical attendance and treatment, with the marriage expenses of an unmarried daughter. A "minor" is a person who has not completed eighteen years. Scheme of the Act. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. keyPoints: Two subjects: adoption (Sections 5 to 17) and maintenance (Sections 18 to 28). Applies to Hindus, Buddhists, Jainas, Sikhs and the residuary group (Section 2); not to Scheduled Tribes unless notified. Section 4: overrides old texts, custom and inconsistent laws. Section 30: earlier adoptions are saved. Maintenance includes food, clothing, residence, education, medical care, and marriage expenses of an unmarried daughter. Section 3(a): custom must be continuous, uniform, certain and not unreasonable or against public policy. Amended in 1962, 2010 and 2019; Section 29 repealed in 1960. Separate from the Juvenile Justice Act regime (Section 56(3) of that Act).

caseLaws.name: Sitabai v
caseLaws.facts: Ramchandra (1969) Facts. Sitabai's husband died in 1930. In March 1958, after the Act, she adopted Suresh Chandra. The question was whether he became a coparcener with her late husband's brother in the joint family property. Principle. Under Sections 11, 12 and 14, a child adopted by a widow is absorbed in the adoptive family to which she belonged and becomes the son of her deceased husband as well. AIR 1970 SC 343. Why it matters. It explains the effect of Chapter II on adoption by a widow. Yamunabai Anantrao Adhav v. Anantrao Shivram Adhav (1988) Facts. In June 1974 a woman went through Hindu rites with a man whose first wife was alive. She left after a week and claimed maintenance as his wife. Principle. The marriage was void, and she could not claim a wife's status for maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. AIR 1988 SC 644 : (1988) 1 SCC 530. Why it matters. Maintenance claims as a wife depend on a valid marriage. V. Tulasamma v. Sesha Reddy (1977) Facts. A widow got properties for her life in lieu of maintenance under a compromise in execution of her maintenance decree. Principle. Her right to maintenance is a pre-existing right, so property given for it falls under Section 14(1), not 14(2), of the Hindu Succession Act, and she became full owner. AIR 1977 SC 1944 : (1977) 3 SCC 99. Why it matters. It links the right of maintenance to the widow's full ownership.

selfTest.q: 1. Which sections form Chapter II?
selfTest.a: Sections 5 to 17, on adoptions.

selfTest.q: 2. What does Section 30 save?
selfTest.a: Adoptions made before the Act.

selfTest.q: 3. Does the Act apply to Sikhs?
selfTest.a: Yes, under Section 2(1)(b).

selfTest.q: 4. A woman aged 40 wants to adopt a boy aged 21. Can she?
selfTest.a: No. The child must be under fifteen unless custom permits (Section 10(iv)); the age gap of 19 years is also below twenty-one (Section 11(iv)).

selfTest.q: 5. Which amending Act let a married woman adopt in her own right with her husband's consent?
selfTest.a: Act 30 of 2010, which substituted Section 8 with effect from 31 August 2010.

selfTest.q: 6. Does an adoption under HAMA need a District Magistrate's order?
selfTest.a: No. Section 56(3) of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 says nothing in that Act applies to adoptions made under HAMA.

legalProvision: Long title. An Act to amend and codify the law relating to adoptions and maintenance among Hindus.

Section 4. Overriding effect of Act. ―Save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act,― (a) any text, rule or interpretation of Hindu law or any custom or usage as part of that law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect with respect to any matter for which provision is made in this Act; (b) any other law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to apply to Hindus in so far as it is inconsistent with any of the provisions contained in this Act.

Section 30. Savings. ―Nothing contained in this Act shall affect any adoption made before the commencement of this Act, and the validity and effect of any such adoption shall be determined as if this Act had not been passed.

family-law-i-u4-t7.subtitle: Scheme of the Act: extent, link to the Guardians and Wards Act, application, definitions, overriding effect and sections 6 to 13

en.inOneMinute: What it is. The Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 (HMGA) is one of the four Hindu Acts of 1955–56. It deals with the guardianship of Hindu minors in only 13 sections. Supplemental Act. It is in addition to the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, and does not replace it (Section 2). Both Acts work together for a Hindu minor. Who is a minor. A person who has not completed eighteen years (Section 4(a)). Extent. It extends to the whole of India and also to Hindus domiciled in India who are outside it (Section 1(2)). Core rules. Sections 6 to 13 name the natural guardians , limit their powers over the minor's property, allow testamentary guardians , end the powers of a de facto guardian , and make the welfare of the minor the paramount consideration. Scope of this note. The scheme of the Act as a whole. Sections 6 to 13 are explained in detail in the note on the Law of Guardianship.
legalProvision: Long title. An Act to amend and codify certain parts of the law relating to minority and guardianship among Hindus.

Section 2. Act to be supplemental to Act 8 of 1890. ―The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to, and not, save as hereinafter expressly provided, in derogation of, the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 (8 of 1890).

Section 5. Over-riding effect of Act. ―Save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act,― (a) any text, rule or interpretation of Hindu Law or any custom or usage as part of that law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect with respect to any matter for which provision is made in this Act; (b) any other law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect in so far as it is inconsistent with any of the provisions contained in this Act.
Other provisions used in this note:

Section 1: short title, and extent to the whole of India, including Hindus domiciled in India who are outside it. Section 3: application to Hindus by religion in any form, Buddhists, Jains, Sikhs and the residuary group, with the Explanation on children and converts. Section 3(2) excludes Scheduled Tribes unless notified. Section 3(2A) excludes the Renoncants of Pondicherry. Section 4: definitions of "minor", "guardian" and "natural guardian". Sections 6 to 13: the working rules on guardians.
en.meaning:
The Act is a codifying statute , but only in part: its long title says it codifies "certain parts" of the law on minority and guardianship among Hindus. Mulla notes that it does not codify the whole law of guardianship, and that rules on matters for which the Act makes no provision are not overridden by it. Section 4 gives three definitions. "Minor" (Section 4(a)): a person who has not completed the age of eighteen years. "Guardian" (Section 4(b)): a person having the care of the person of a minor, or of his property, or of both. It includes four kinds: (i) a natural guardian; (ii) a guardian appointed by the will of the minor's father or mother; (iii) a guardian appointed or declared by a court; (iv) a person empowered to act as such by or under any enactment relating to any Court of Wards. "Natural guardian" (Section 4(c)): any of the guardians mentioned in Section 6. Kinds of guardian under Section 4(b). See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. keyPoints: The Act is in addition to the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 (Section 2). A minor is a person who has not completed eighteen years (Section 4(a)). Guardian includes natural, testamentary, court-appointed and Court of Wards guardians (Section 4(b)). Section 5: overrides old texts, custom and inconsistent laws. Section 6: father then mother; mother then father for an illegitimate child; husband for a married girl; custody under five ordinarily with the mother. Section 8: no sale or mortgage of the minor's immovable property without court permission; breach is voidable. Section 11: a de facto guardian cannot deal with the minor's property. Section 13: the welfare of the minor is paramount.

caseLaws.name: Githa Hariharan v
caseLaws.facts: Reserve Bank of India (1999) Facts. The Reserve Bank refused a mother's application for Relief Bonds in her minor son's name without the father's signature; in a second petition, a father claimed to be the only natural guardian in a custody dispute. Principle. The 1956 Act and the 1890 Act are supplemental to each other (para 13); "after" in Section 6(a) does not necessarily mean after the father's death but means in the absence of the father, and the section survives (para 25). AIR 1999 SC 1149 : (1999) 2 SCC 228. Why it matters. It reads the Act's natural guardian provision in line with gender equality, so the mother can act when the father is absent, apathetic or unable.

selfTest.q: 1. How does the Act relate to the 1890 Act?
selfTest.a: It is in addition to it and does not replace it (Section 2).

selfTest.q: 2. At what age does a person stop being a minor?
selfTest.a: On completing eighteen years (Section 4(a)).

selfTest.q: 3. Which section names the natural guardians?
selfTest.a: Section 6.

selfTest.q: 4. Does the Act apply to a Renoncant of Pondicherry?
selfTest.a: No. Section 3(2A) excludes the Renoncants.

selfTest.q: 5. A natural guardian leases a 15-year-old minor's land for 5 years. Is permission needed?
selfTest.a: Yes. The minor attains majority in 3 years, so the lease ends 2 years after majority, which is more than one year beyond it (Section 8(2)(b)).

selfTest.q: 6. Can a de facto guardian sell a Hindu minor's house?
selfTest.a: No. Section 11 bars a person from dealing with a Hindu minor's property merely as de facto guardian.

legalProvision: దీర్ఘ శీర్షిక (Long title). An Act to amend and codify certain parts of the law relating to minority and guardianship among Hindus.

Section 2. Act to be supplemental to Act 8 of 1890. ―The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to, and not, save as hereinafter expressly provided, in derogation of, the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 (8 of 1890).

Section 5. Over-riding effect of Act. ―Save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act,― (a) any text, rule or interpretation of Hindu Law or any custom or usage as part of that law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect with respect to any matter for which provision is made in this Act; (b) any other law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect in so far as it is inconsistent with any of the provisions contained in this Act.
ఈ నోట్‌లో వాడిన ఇతర నిబంధనలు:

సెక్షన్ 1: సంక్షిప్త పేరు; భారతదేశం మొత్తానికి విస్తృతి, భారతదేశంలో నివాసస్థానం ఉండి బయట ఉన్న హిందువులతో సహా. సెక్షన్ 3: ఏ రూపంలోనైనా మతపరంగా హిందువులు, బౌద్ధులు, జైనులు, సిక్కులు, మిగిలిన వర్గానికి వర్తింపు; పిల్లలు, మతం మారినవారిపై వివరణ (Explanation). సెక్షన్ 3(2) నోటిఫై చేస్తే తప్ప షెడ్యూల్డ్ తెగలను మినహాయిస్తుంది. సెక్షన్ 3(2A) పాండిచ్చేరి రెనోన్సాంట్‌లను (Renoncants) మినహాయిస్తుంది. సెక్షన్ 4: "మైనర్", "సంరక్షకుడు", "సహజ సంరక్షకుడు" నిర్వచనాలు. సెక్షన్లు 6 నుంచి 13: సంరక్షకులపై పని నియమాలు.

ఈ చట్టం ఒక క్రోడీకరణ చట్టం (codifying statute) , కానీ పాక్షికంగా మాత్రమే: హిందువులలో మైనారిటీ, సంరక్షకత్వ చట్టంలోని "కొన్ని భాగాలను" (certain parts) క్రోడీకరిస్తుందని దాని దీర్ఘ శీర్షిక చెబుతుంది. ఇది సంరక్షకత్వ చట్టం మొత్తాన్ని క్రోడీకరించదని, చట్టం నిబంధన చేయని విషయాలపై నియమాలను ఇది అధిగమించదని Mulla పేర్కొన్నారు. సెక్షన్ 4 మూడు నిర్వచనాలు ఇస్తుంది. "మైనర్" (సెక్షన్ 4(a)): పద్దెనిమిది సంవత్సరాల వయస్సు పూర్తి చేయని వ్యక్తి. "సంరక్షకుడు" (సెక్షన్ 4(b)): మైనర్ వ్యక్తి (person), లేదా అతని ఆస్తి, లేదా రెండింటి సంరక్షణ ఉన్న వ్యక్తి. ఇందులో నాలుగు రకాలు ఉంటాయి: (i) సహజ సంరక్షకుడు; (ii) మైనర్ తండ్రి లేదా తల్లి వీలునామా ద్వారా నియమించిన సంరక్షకుడు; (iii) కోర్టు నియమించిన లేదా ప్రకటించిన సంరక్షకుడు; (iv) కోర్ట్ ఆఫ్ వార్డ్స్ (Court of Wards) కు సంబంధించిన ఏదైనా చట్టం ద్వారా లేదా దాని కింద అలా వ్యవహరించే అధికారం పొందిన వ్యక్తి. "సహజ సంరక్షకుడు" (సెక్షన్ 4(c)): సెక్షన్ 6 లో పేర్కొన్న సంరక్షకుల్లో ఎవరైనా. సెక్షన్ 4(b) కింద సంరక్షకుల రకాలు. Diagram 1 చూడండి. selfTest.q: 1. ఈ చట్టానికి 1890 చట్టంతో సంబంధం ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: దానికి అదనం, దాని స్థానాన్ని తీసుకోదు (సెక్షన్ 2).

selfTest.q: 2. ఏ వయస్సులో ఒక వ్యక్తి మైనర్‌గా ఉండటం ఆగిపోతుంది?
selfTest.a: పద్దెనిమిది సంవత్సరాలు పూర్తి చేసినప్పుడు (సెక్షన్ 4(a)).

selfTest.q: 3. సహజ సంరక్షకులను ఏ సెక్షన్ పేర్కొంటుంది?
selfTest.a: సెక్షన్ 6.

selfTest.q: 4. పాండిచ్చేరి రెనోన్సాంట్‌కు చట్టం వర్తిస్తుందా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. సెక్షన్ 3(2A) రెనోన్సాంట్‌లను మినహాయిస్తుంది.

selfTest.q: 5. ఒక సహజ సంరక్షకుడు 15 సంవత్సరాల మైనర్ భూమిని 5 సంవత్సరాలకు లీజుకు ఇస్తాడు. అనుమతి అవసరమా?
selfTest.a: అవును. మైనర్ 3 సంవత్సరాల్లో మేజర్ అవుతాడు, కాబట్టి లీజు మేజర్ అయిన 2 సంవత్సరాల తర్వాత ముగుస్తుంది; అది ఒక సంవత్సరానికి మించుతుంది (సెక్షన్ 8(2)(b)).

selfTest.q: 6. వాస్తవ సంరక్షకుడు హిందూ మైనర్ ఇంటిని అమ్మగలరా?

family-law-i-u4-t5.subtitle: Kinds of guardian, powers over the minor's person and property, custody and the welfare principle

en.inOneMinute: Who is a guardian. A guardian is a person who has the care of a minor's person, property or both. A Hindu minor may have a natural guardian , a guardian appointed by will, or a guardian appointed or declared by a court. Natural guardian. For a boy or an unmarried girl, the father is the natural guardian, and after him the mother. In Githa Hariharan v. Reserve Bank of India the Supreme Court read "after him" to mean "in the absence of" the father, not only after his death. Limits. The natural guardian cannot sell or mortgage the minor's immovable property without the court's permission; a sale without it is voidable. The welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration. Two laws. The Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 (HMGA) is in addition to the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 (GWA). Guardianship is different from custody.
legalProvision: Section 6, Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956. Natural guardians of a Hindu minor. —The natural guardians of a Hindu minor, in respect of the minor's person as well as in respect of the minor's property (excluding his or her undivided interest in joint family property), are— (a) in the case of a boy or an unmarried girl—the father, and after him, the mother: provided that the custody of a minor who has not completed the age of five years shall ordinarily be with the mother; (b) in the case of an illegitimate boy or an illegitimate unmarried girl—the mother, and after her, the father; (c) in the case of a married girl—the husband: Provided that no person shall be entitled to act as the natural guardian of a minor under the provisions of this section— (a) if he has ceased to be a Hindu, or (b) if he has completely and finally renounced the world by becoming a hermit (vanaprastha) or an ascetic (yati or sanyasi). Explanation.—In this section, the expressions "father" and "mother" do not include a step-father and a step-mother.
Section 13(1). In the appointment or declaration of any person as guardian of a Hindu minor by a court, the welfare of the minor shall be the paramount consideration.
Other provisions used in this note:

HMGA Section 2: the Act is in addition to, and not in derogation of, the GWA, except where it expressly says so. Section 4: a minor is a person under eighteen; a guardian is a person having the care of the minor's person or property or both, and includes a natural guardian, a guardian appointed by the will of the father or mother, a guardian appointed or declared by a court, and a person empowered under a Court of Wards law. Section 5: the Act overrides earlier Hindu law and inconsistent laws on matters it covers. Section 7: guardianship of an adopted minor son passes to the adoptive father and after him the adoptive mother. Section 8: powers of the natural guardian. Section 9: testamentary guardians . Sections 10 to 12: a minor cannot be guardian of property; a de facto guardian cannot deal with the minor's property; no guardian for the minor's undivided interest in joint family property. GWA: appointment, welfare test, duties, removal and end of a guardian's powers. HMA Section 26: custody, maintenance and education of children in matrimonial cases.
en.meaning:
A guardian is a person in charge of a minor's care and protection. Guardianship covers the minor's person (upbringing, education, health) and the minor's property. A minor is a person who has not completed eighteen years (Section 4(a)). The 1956 Act applies in addition to the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 (Section 2). Kinds of guardian of a Hindu minor. keyPoints: Minor means under eighteen (Section 4(a)). Natural guardian of a boy or unmarried girl: the father, and after him the mother; "after" means "in the absence of" ( Githa Hariharan ). Custody of a child under five ordinarily with the mother. Section 8: no sale, mortgage or long lease of the minor's immovable property without court permission; breach is voidable. De facto guardian cannot deal with the minor's property (Section 11). Welfare of the minor is paramount (Section 13). Testamentary guardian: appointment fails if the father dies before the mother but revives if she appoints none; right of a guardian of a girl ends on her marriage (Section 9). Natural guardianship of an adopted minor son passes to the adoptive father, then the adoptive mother (Section 7). GWA: welfare test (Section 17); fiduciary duty (Section 20); removal (Section 39); end of powers (Section 41).

caseLaws.name: Githa Hariharan v
caseLaws.facts: Reserve Bank of India (1999) Facts. The Reserve Bank refused a mother's application for Relief Bonds in her minor son's name without the father's signature; in a second petition, a father claimed to be the only natural guardian in a custody dispute. Principle. "After" in Section 6(a) does not necessarily mean after the father's death; it means in the absence of the father, be it temporary, by total apathy or by inability, and the section survives (para 25). AIR 1999 SC 1149 : (1999) 2 SCC 228. Why it matters. It lets the mother act as natural guardian when the father is absent, apathetic or unable.

selfTest.q: 1. Who is the natural guardian of an unmarried girl?
selfTest.a: The father, and after him the mother (Section 6(a)).

selfTest.q: 2. Is a sale by the natural guardian without permission void?
selfTest.a: No. It is voidable at the instance of the minor (Section 8(3)).

selfTest.q: 3. What did Githa Hariharan decide about "after him"?
selfTest.a: It means in the absence of the father, not only after his death.

selfTest.q: 4. A minor is exactly 16. What is the longest lease of her land a natural guardian can grant without permission?
selfTest.a: Majority comes in 2 years; a lease may not run more than 1 year beyond it, so 2 + 1 = 3 years (Section 8(2)(b)).

selfTest.q: 5. Can a court under the GWA appoint a guardian of the person of a child whose father is alive and fit?
selfTest.a: No (GWA Section 19).

selfTest.q: 6. When does a testamentary guardian's right over a girl end?
selfTest.a: On her marriage (Section 9(6)).

ఆస్తితో వ్యవహరించలేరు"] వచన వివరణ పైన: హిందూ మైనర్ సంరక్షకుడు. కింద నాలుగు పెట్టెలు. సహజ సంరక్షకుడు, సెక్షన్లు 6, 7: తండ్రి తర్వాత తల్లి; అక్రమ సంతానానికి తల్లి తర్వాత తండ్రి; పెళ్లైన బాలికకు భర్త; దత్తత తండ్రి తర్వాత దత్తత తల్లి. వీలునామా సంరక్షకుడు, సెక్షన్ 9: తండ్రి లేదా తల్లి వీలునామా ద్వారా నియమించినవారు. కోర్టు సంరక్షకుడు, సెక్షన్ 4(b)(iii), సంరక్షకులు, వార్డుల చట్టం, 1890: కోర్టు నియమించినవారు లేదా ప్రకటించినవారు. వాస్తవ సంరక్షకుడు, సెక్షన్ 11: అధికారం లేకుండా మైనర్‌ను చూసుకుంటారు; మైనర్ ఆస్తితో వ్యవహరించలేరు. రకం ఎవరు మూలం సహజ సంరక్షకుడు తండ్రి, తర్వాత తల్లి (బాలుడు లేదా పెళ్లికాని బాలిక); తల్లి, తర్వాత తండ్రి (అక్రమ సంతానం); భర్త (పెళ్లైన బాలిక); దత్తత తండ్రి, తర్వాత దత్తత తల్లి (దత్తత కొడుకు) సెక్షన్లు 6, 7 వీలునామా సంరక్షకుడు తండ్రి లేదా తల్లి వీలునామా ద్వారా నియమించినవారు సెక్షన్ 9 కోర్టు సంరక్షకుడు GWA కింద కోర్టు నియమించినవారు లేదా ప్రకటించినవారు సెక్షన్ 4(b)(iii); GWA సెక్షన్ 7 కోర్ట్ ఆఫ్ వార్డ్స్ సంరక్షకుడు కోర్ట్ ఆఫ్ వార్డ్స్ చట్టం కింద అధికారం పొందిన వ్యక్తి సెక్షన్ 4(b)(iv) వాస్తవ సంరక్షకుడు చట్టపరమైన అధికారం లేకుండా మైనర్‌ను చూసుకునేవారు; మైనర్ ఆస్తితో వ్యవహరించలేరు సెక్షన్ 11

selfTest.q: 1. పెళ్లికాని బాలిక సహజ సంరక్షకుడు ఎవరు?
selfTest.a: తండ్రి, అతని తర్వాత తల్లి (సెక్షన్ 6(a)).

selfTest.q: 2. అనుమతి లేకుండా సహజ సంరక్షకుడు చేసిన అమ్మకం శూన్యమా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. మైనర్ కోరితే రద్దు చేయదగినది (సెక్షన్ 8(3)).

selfTest.q: 3. "after him" గురించి Githa Hariharan ఏమి నిర్ణయించింది?
selfTest.a: తండ్రి మరణం తర్వాత మాత్రమే కాదు, తండ్రి లేనప్పుడు అని అర్థం.

selfTest.q: 4. మైనర్‌కు సరిగ్గా 16 ఏళ్లు. అనుమతి లేకుండా సహజ సంరక్షకుడు ఆమె భూమిని గరిష్ఠంగా ఎంత కాలానికి లీజుకు ఇవ్వవచ్చు?
selfTest.a: 2 సంవత్సరాల్లో మేజర్ అవుతుంది; లీజు దాని తర్వాత 1 సంవత్సరానికి మించకూడదు, కాబట్టి 2 + 1 = 3 సంవత్సరాలు (సెక్షన్ 8(2)(b)).

selfTest.q: 5. తండ్రి జీవించి ఉండి అర్హుడైన బిడ్డ వ్యక్తిత్వానికి GWA కింద కోర్టు సంరక్షకుడిని నియమించవచ్చా?
selfTest.a: లేదు (GWA సెక్షన్ 19).

selfTest.q: 6. బాలికపై వీలునామా సంరక్షకుడి హక్కు ఎప్పుడు ముగుస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: ఆమె పెళ్లితో (సెక్షన్ 9(6)).

వేరుగా ఉండవచ్చా అవును అవును: తల్లికి కస్టడీ ఉండగా తండ్రి సంరక్షకుడిగా ఉండవచ్చు

family-law-i-u5-t1.subtitle: Passing of a dead person's property: by will or without a will, and how the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 deals with both

en.inOneMinute: What it is. Succession is the passing of a dead person's property to other persons. Two ways. The owner may leave a will ; that is testamentary succession . If there is no valid will for a property, it passes by intestate succession . The Act. The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 (HSA) is a code of intestate succession among Hindus. It also keeps the right of every Hindu to make a will (Section 30). Extent. The Act extends to the whole of India (Section 1(2)). Scope of this note. The idea of succession and the basic scheme of the Act. The rules for intestate succession, heirs and wills are in their own notes.
legalProvision: Section 30. Testamentary succession. ―Any Hindu may dispose of by will or other testamentary disposition any property, which is capable of being so disposed of by him or by her, in accordance with the provisions of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 (39 of 1925), or any other law for the time being in force and applicable to Hindus. Explanation.―The interest of a male Hindu in a Mitakshara coparcenary property or the interest of a member of a tarwad, tavazhi, illom, kutumba or kavaru in the property of the tarwad, tavazhi, illom, kutumba or kavaru shall, notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force, be deemed to be property capable of being disposed of by him or by her within the meaning of this section.

Section 4(1). Overriding effect of Act. ―Save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act,― (a) any text, rule or interpretation of Hindu law or any custom or usage as part of that law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect with respect to any matter for which provision is made in this Act; (b) any other law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to apply to Hindus in so far as it is inconsistent with any of the provisions contained in this Act.
Other provisions used in this note:

Section 1: short title, and extent to the whole of India. Section 2: application to Hindus by religion in any form, Buddhists, Jainas, Sikhs and the residuary group. Section 2(2) excludes Scheduled Tribes unless notified. Section 3: definitions, including "heir", "intestate" and "related". Section 3(2) says that, unless the context otherwise requires, words in the masculine gender do not include females. Section 5: properties to which the Act does not apply. Sections 6 and 7: devolution of a Mitakshara coparcener 's interest and of an interest in a tarwad, tavazhi, illom, kutumba or kavaru.
en.meaning:
Section 3(1) defines the key words. "Heir" (clause (f)): any person, male or female, who is entitled to succeed to the property of an intestate under this Act. "Intestate" (clause (g)): a person is deemed to die intestate in respect of property of which he or she has not made a testamentary disposition capable of taking effect. "Related" (clause (j)): related by legitimate kinship. Illegitimate children are deemed to be related to their mother and to one another, and their legitimate descendants are deemed to be related to them and to one another. Two ways property passes. Way Basis Section Testamentary succession A valid will Section 30 Intestate succession The rules of the Act, where there is no valid will Sections 8 to 29 Outside the Act Properties listed in Section 5 Section 5 Worked example. A Hindu owner has two properties: a house worth ₹60 lakh and a deposit of ₹15 lakh. Her valid will gives the house to her niece and says nothing about the deposit. The house passes by testamentary succession (Section 30). For the deposit she is "intestate" (Section 3(1)(g)), so the ₹15 lakh passes to her heirs under the Act.
keyPoints: Succession is the passing of a dead person's property: by will or without a will. The Act extends to the whole of India (Section 1) and applies to Hindus in the wide sense of Section 2. Section 4: the Act overrides old texts, custom and inconsistent laws. Section 5: three kinds of property are outside the Act. Section 30: a Hindu may dispose of property by will, "by him or by her" since the 2005 Amendment. Section 3: agnate, cognate, full blood, half blood, uterine blood, heir, intestate and related are defined for the whole Act. Section 6(3): after 2005 a coparcener's interest passes by will or succession, not by survivorship.

caseLaws.name: Commissioner of Wealth Tax, Kanpur v
caseLaws.facts: Chander Sen (1986) Facts. Rangi Lal died on 17 July 1965, leaving his only son Chander Sen and grandsons. A sum of ₹1,85,043 stood to his credit in the firm's books, and the Wealth-tax Officer treated it as property of the joint family of Chander Sen and his sons. Principle. Under Section 8, a son takes his father's property in his individual capacity, and his own sons get no right by birth in it. AIR 1986 SC 1753 : (1986) 3 SCC 567. Why it matters. It shows Sections 4 and 8 replacing the old Mitakshara rule that made inherited property joint family property.

selfTest.q: 1. What are the two ways property passes on death?
selfTest.a: By a will (testamentary) or without a will (intestate).

selfTest.q: 2. Which section protects the right to make a will?
selfTest.a: Section 30.

selfTest.q: 3. Does the Act apply to every property?
selfTest.a: No. Section 5 excludes three kinds of property.

selfTest.q: 4. Two brothers have the same mother but different fathers. How are they related?
selfTest.a: By uterine blood (Section 3(1)(e)(ii)).

selfTest.q: 5. A will disposes of half of a man's property. What happens to the other half?
selfTest.a: He is intestate for that half (Section 3(1)(g)), so it passes under the Act's rules of intestate succession.

selfTest.q: 6. Which Act repealed Section 31 of the 1956 Act?
selfTest.a: The Repealing and Amending Act, 1960, with effect from 26 December 1960.

ఈ నోట్‌లో వాడిన ఇతర నిబంధనలు:

సెక్షన్ 1: సంక్షిప్త పేరు; భారతదేశం మొత్తానికి విస్తృతి. సెక్షన్ 2: ఏ రూపంలోనైనా మతపరంగా హిందువులు, బౌద్ధులు, జైనులు, సిక్కులు, మిగిలిన వర్గానికి వర్తింపు. సెక్షన్ 2(2) నోటిఫై చేస్తే తప్ప షెడ్యూల్డ్ తెగలను మినహాయిస్తుంది. సెక్షన్ 3: "వారసుడు" (heir), " వీలునామా లేకుండా మరణించినవారు" (intestate), "సంబంధం ఉన్న" (related) సహా నిర్వచనాలు. సందర్భం వేరేగా కోరితే తప్ప, పురుష లింగ పదాల్లో స్త్రీలు ఉండరని సెక్షన్ 3(2) చెబుతుంది. సెక్షన్ 5: చట్టం వర్తించని ఆస్తులు. సెక్షన్లు 6, 7: మితాక్షర కోపార్సినర్ (coparcener) వాటా, తరవాడ్, తవళి, ఇల్లం, కుటుంబ, కావరు ఆస్తిలో వాటా ఎలా చేరుతాయి.
te.meaning:
సెక్షన్ 3(1) ముఖ్య పదాలను నిర్వచిస్తుంది. "వారసుడు" (heir, క్లాజ్ (f)): ఈ చట్టం కింద వీలునామా లేకుండా మరణించిన వ్యక్తి ఆస్తికి వారసత్వం పొందే హక్కు ఉన్న ఏ వ్యక్తి అయినా, పురుషుడు లేదా స్త్రీ. "వీలునామా లేకుండా" (intestate, క్లాజ్ (g)): ఒక ఆస్తి విషయంలో అమలయ్యే వీలునామా పరాధీనం (testamentary disposition) చేయకపోతే, ఆ ఆస్తి విషయంలో ఆ వ్యక్తి వీలునామా లేకుండా మరణించినట్లు భావిస్తారు. "సంబంధం ఉన్న" (related, క్లాజ్ (j)): చట్టబద్ధమైన బంధుత్వం ద్వారా సంబంధం. చట్టవిరుద్ధ సంతానం తమ తల్లితో, ఒకరితో ఒకరు సంబంధం ఉన్నట్లు భావిస్తారు; వారి చట్టబద్ధ సంతతి వారితో, ఒకరితో ఒకరు సంబంధం ఉన్నట్లు భావిస్తారు. ఆస్తి చేరే రెండు మార్గాలు. selfTest.q: 1. మరణంపై ఆస్తి చేరే రెండు మార్గాలు ఏవి?
selfTest.a: వీలునామా ద్వారా (వీలునామా వారసత్వం) లేదా వీలునామా లేకుండా (వీలునామా లేని వారసత్వం).

selfTest.q: 2. వీలునామా రాసే హక్కును ఏ సెక్షన్ కాపాడుతుంది?
selfTest.a: సెక్షన్ 30.

selfTest.q: 3. చట్టం ప్రతి ఆస్తికీ వర్తిస్తుందా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. సెక్షన్ 5 మూడు రకాల ఆస్తిని మినహాయిస్తుంది.

selfTest.q: 4. ఇద్దరు సోదరులకు ఒకే తల్లి, వేర్వేరు తండ్రులు. వారి సంబంధం ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: గర్భ రక్త సంబంధం (సెక్షన్ 3(1)(e)(ii)).

selfTest.q: 5. ఒక వీలునామా ఒక వ్యక్తి ఆస్తిలో సగాన్ని ఇస్తుంది. మిగతా సగానికి ఏమవుతుంది?
selfTest.a: ఆ సగానికి అతను వీలునామా లేకుండా మరణించినట్లు (సెక్షన్ 3(1)(g)), కాబట్టి అది చట్టంలోని వీలునామా లేని వారసత్వ నియమాల ప్రకారం చేరుతుంది.

selfTest.q: 6. 1956 చట్టం సెక్షన్ 31 ను ఏ చట్టం రద్దు చేసింది?
selfTest.a: Repealing and Amending Act, 1960; 26 డిసెంబర్ 1960 నుంచి.

family-law-i-u5-t4.subtitle: Former section 23 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956: the dwelling house rule for female heirs and its omission in 2005

en.inOneMinute: The old rule. Section 23 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 once gave a special rule for a dwelling house wholly occupied by members of the intestate's family. A female class I heir could not ask for partition of it until the male class I heirs chose to divide their shares. Right of residence. Old Section 23 also gave the female heir a right of residence in that house. A daughter had that right only if she was unmarried, deserted by or separated from her husband, or a widow. Omitted. The Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 omitted Section 23 with effect from 9 September 2005. The restriction and the right of residence are no longer in the Act. Why. Parliament omitted it "so as to remove the disability on female heirs contained in that section" (Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma, para 47).
legalProvision: Section 23 as originally enacted. Special provision respecting dwelling-houses. ―Where a Hindu intestate has left surviving him or her both male and female heirs specified in class I of the Schedule and his or her property includes a dwelling-house wholly occupied by members of his or her family, then, notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, the right of any such female heir to claim partition of the dwelling-house shall not arise until the male heirs choose to divide their respective shares therein; but the female heir shall be entitled to a right of residence therein: Provided that where such female heir is a daughter, she shall be entitled to a right of residence in the dwelling-house only if she is unmarried or has been deserted by or has separated from her husband or is a widow.
Section 23 now. [Special provision respecting dwelling-houses.]―Omitted by the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 (39 of 2005), s. 4 (w.e.f. 9-9-2005).
Other provisions used in this note:

Section 17(iv): for persons who would have been governed by marumakkattayam or aliyasantana law, Section 23 was to be treated as omitted even before 2005. Section 22: preferential right of class I heirs to buy a co-heir's interest; a female heir could transfer her interest in the house subject to it. Section 24 (omitted): removed by Section 5 of the same Amendment. As originally enacted, the widow of a pre-deceased son, of a pre-deceased son of a pre-deceased son, or of a brother did not inherit as such widow if she had remarried when the succession opened (Mulla, 14th ed., Section 24).
en.meaning:
The Act's own text now keeps only the note that Section 23 was omitted. The original words are reproduced in Mulla, Principles of Hindu Law (14th ed.), Section 23. The Statement of Objects and Reasons of the 2005 Bill, as recorded by the Supreme Court in Vineeta Sharma (2020, para 47), describes the old section in one line: it " disentitles a female heir to ask for partition in respect of a dwelling house wholly occupied by a joint family until the male heirs choose to divide their respective shares therein ". Dwelling-house (Mulla). The house in which the intestate and the members of the family lived as their permanent residence, and which the family continued to occupy on the death. Occupation does not mean actual or continuous residence, nor that all members must reside there. Wholly occupied. The whole house must be occupied by members of the family. A house only partly occupied, or partly or substantially let to tenants, is not covered (Mulla). Section 23 before and after 2005. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1.
