law-of-torts-u5-t19.subtitle: Settling consumer disputes by agreement: mediation under the 2019 Act and the place of other alternative dispute resolution

en.inOneMinute: Alternative dispute resolution (ADR) means settling a dispute without a full trial. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 builds one ADR method into the Commissions: mediation. A Commission can send the parties to mediation if a settlement looks possible, and the parties must agree in writing. In exams, this topic is asked as a short note on ADR and consumer disputes, or on mediation under the Act. The usual trap is to think that mediation is compulsory. It needs the written consent of both parties.
legalProvision: Section 37: at the first hearing or later, if elements of a settlement acceptable to the parties appear, the District Commission may ask the parties to give written consent within five days to mediation under Chapter V. On consent, it refers the matter within five days. prescribed cases are excluded. Section 74: a consumer mediation cell is set up with each District and State Commission by the State Government, and with the National Commission and its regional Benches by the Central Government. Section 75: each Commission prepares a panel of mediators on the recommendation of a selection committee of its President and a member. The panel is valid for five years. Section 79: mediation is held in the cell, and the mediator is guided by the principles of natural justice. Section 80: a settlement is written down and signed by the parties, and the mediator sends it with a report to the Commission. Section 81: the Commission passes an order recording the settlement within seven days. Section 100: the Act is in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other law in force. Section 2(25): mediation means the process by which a mediator mediates the consumer disputes. Section 41 (third proviso ):
en.meaning: ADR covers methods such as negotiation, mediation, conciliation, arbitration and Lok Adalats. In these methods, the parties, with the help of a neutral person or body, reach a result outside the ordinary court process. In the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the method given a place inside the Act is mediation. A mediator helps the parties reach their own agreement and does not decide the dispute.
keyPoints: Mediation needs written consent of the parties within five days (section 37). A consumer mediation cell is attached to each Commission (section 74). The panel of mediators is valid for five years (section 75). The Commission records a settlement within seven days (section 81). If mediation fails, the Commission hears all issues. Mediation ends in three months from the first appearance unless extended (Regulation 11(2)).

selfTest.q: 1. Is mediation compulsory under the 2019 Act?
selfTest.a: No. The parties must consent in writing. 2. Within how many days must the Commission record a settlement? Seven days from receiving the settlement report (section 81). 3. What happens if mediation fails? The Commission continues to hear all the issues.

law-of-torts-u5-t18.subtitle: How the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 gives civil remedies for consumers and creates criminal offences for serious wrongs

en.inOneMinute: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 works on two tracks. The civil track gives the consumer relief such as replacement, refund and compensation. The criminal track punishes the wrongdoer with imprisonment or fine for serious wrongs, such as ignoring a Commission's order, a false advertisement, or selling adulterated or spurious goods. In exams, this topic is asked as a short note or an essay comparing civil and criminal liability under the Act. The usual trap is to say that a consumer complaint can send a trader to jail. It cannot, except through section 72 for disobeying an order.
legalProvision: Section 39: the District Commission, after finding a defect, deficiency or unfair trade practice proved, orders removal of the defect, replacement, refund, compensation, or other relief. Sections 82 to 87: product liability. A manufacturer , product service provider or product seller is liable for harm caused by a defective product. Section 72: failure to comply with a Commission's order is punishable with imprisonment of one month to three years, or fine of Rs 25,000 to Rs 1 lakh, or both. Section 88: failure to comply with a direction of the Central Authority under section 20 or 21 is punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs 20 lakh, or both. Section 89: a false or misleading advertisement is punishable with imprisonment up to two years and fine up to Rs 10 lakh, and for each later offence imprisonment up to five years and fine up to Rs 50 lakh. Section 90: selling products containing an adulterant is punishable, with heavier punishment as the injury grows. Section 91: the same for spurious goods. Section 92: a court may take cognizance offences under sections 88 and 89 only on a complaint by the Central Authority or an officer it authorises. Section 93: an officer who makes a vexatious search or seizure is punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to Rs 10,000, or both.
en.meaning: Civil liability is a duty to repair the consumer's loss by giving relief or money. Criminal liability is a duty to answer to the State for an offence and to suffer the punishment the law lays down. One act, such as selling unsafe food, can lead to both.
keyPoints: Civil track: section 39 relief and product liability (sections 82 to 87). Section 72: one month to three years, fine Rs 25,000 to Rs 1 lakh. Section 89: up to two years and Rs 10 lakh; later offence up to five years and Rs 50 lakh. Sections 90 and 91: punishment grows with the injury; death carries at least seven years. Section 92: cognizance of sections 88 and 89 only on the Central Authority's complaint.

caseLaws.name: Indian Medical Association v
caseLaws.facts: V.P. Shantha (1995) Facts. Conflicting rulings on whether a doctor's or hospital's work is service under the 1986 Act. Principle. Medical work for a fee is service. The patient can seek civil relief before the consumer forum. Significance. Civil liability of professionals under the Act. Spring Meadows Hospital v. Harjot Ahluwalia (1998) Facts. A nurse injected a minor patient without a sensitivity test, leaving him in a vegetative state. Principle. Both the child and the parents are consumers who can each be compensated on their own head of loss. Significance. Compensation as civil liability.

selfTest.a: Section 72. 2. Who can start a prosecution under sections 88 and 89? The Central Authority or an officer it authorises (section 92). 3. What is the minimum punishment if adulterated goods cause death? Imprisonment of at least seven years and fine of at least Rs 10 lakh (section 90(1)(d)).

law-of-torts-u5-t20.subtitle: What counts as a misleading advertisement, and the penalties the Central Authority and the courts can impose

en.inOneMinute: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 deals with misleading advertisements on two levels. The Central Consumer Protection Authority can order the advertisement to stop and can impose a money penalty on the maker and the endorser. A court can also punish the manufacturer or service provider with imprisonment and fine. In exams, this topic is asked as a short note on misleading advertisements and their penalties. The usual trap is to mix the Authority's penalty under section 21 with the court's punishment under section 89.
legalProvision: Section 2(28): a misleading advertisement is one that falsely describes a product or service or gives a false guarantee. It is also one that is likely to mislead consumers about nature, substance, quantity or quality, or that conveys a representation that would be an unfair trade practice. An advertisement that deliberately conceals important information is misleading too. Section 2(18): an endorsement is a message, statement, demonstration, or depiction of a name, likeness or seal that makes the consumer believe it reflects the opinion, finding or experience of the person endorsing. Section 21: the Central Authority may direct discontinuance or modification of the advertisement, impose a penalty, and bar an endorser. Section 89: a manufacturer or service provider who causes a false or misleading advertisement prejudicial to consumers is punishable with imprisonment up to two years and fine up to Rs 10 lakh. For each later offence, imprisonment up to five years and fine up to Rs 50 lakh. Section 92: a court takes cognizance of an offence under section 88 or section 89 only on a complaint by the Central Authority or an officer it authorises. Section 88: failing to comply with a direction of the Central Authority under section 20 or 21 is punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs 20 lakh, or both. Section 24: a person aggrieved by an order of the Central Authority under section 20 or 21 may appeal to the National Commission within 30 days of receiving the order. Section 39(1)(l) and (n): a Commission deciding a complaint may order a corrective advertisement, at the cost of the opposite party, to neutralise a misleading advertisement. It may also order the party to stop issuing misleading advertisements. Section 93: an officer who searches or seizes under section 22 knowing there are no reasonable grounds is punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to Rs 10,000, or both.
en.meaning: A misleading advertisement is not limited to a plain lie. It includes an advertisement that is likely to mislead, one that makes a promise that would be an unfair trade practice, and one that hides important information on purpose. An endorser is the person whose name, face, message or seal is used to lend credit to the advertisement.
keyPoints: Misleading advertisement is defined in section 2(28). Authority penalty: up to Rs 10 lakh; later up to Rs 50 lakh (section 21). Endorser bar: up to one year; later up to three years. Endorser's defence: due diligence (section 21(5)). Court punishment: up to two years and Rs 10 lakh; later up to five years and Rs 50 lakh (section 89).

caseLaws.name: This topic rests on the text of the Act
caseLaws.facts: No judgment in this collection is relied on for it.

selfTest.q: 1. How long can an endorser be barred for a first contravention?
selfTest.a: Up to one year (section 21(3)). 2. What defence does an endorser have? He exercised due diligence to verify the claims (section 21(5)). 3. Who can complain for an offence under section 89? The Central Authority or an officer it authorises (section 92).

legalProvision: సెక్షన్ 2(28): ఉత్పత్తిని లేదా సేవను తప్పుగా వర్ణించే, తప్పుడు హామీ ఇచ్చే, స్వభావం, సారం, పరిమాణం లేదా నాణ్యత గురించి వినియోగదారులను తప్పుదారి పట్టించే అవకాశం ఉన్న, అన్యాయ వాణిజ్య పద్ధతి అయ్యే ప్రాతినిధ్యం తెలిపే, లేదా ముఖ్యమైన సమాచారాన్ని ఉద్దేశపూర్వకంగా దాచే ప్రకటన తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటన. సెక్షన్ 2(18): Endorsement అంటే ఆమోదించే వ్యక్తి అభిప్రాయం, కనుగొన్నది లేదా అనుభవాన్ని ప్రతిబింబిస్తుందని వినియోగదారు నమ్మేలా చేసే సందేశం, ప్రకటన, ప్రదర్శన, లేదా పేరు, రూపం, ముద్ర చిత్రణ. సెక్షన్ 21: ప్రకటనను ఆపమని లేదా మార్చమని Central Authority ఆదేశించవచ్చు, జరిమానా విధించవచ్చు, endorser పై నిషేధం విధించవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 89: వినియోగదారుల ప్రయోజనానికి హానికరమైన తప్పుడు లేదా తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటన చేయించిన తయారీదారు లేదా సేవా ప్రదాతకు రెండేళ్ల వరకు జైలు శిక్ష, రూ. 10 లక్షల వరకు జరిమానా. ప్రతి తదుపరి నేరానికి ఐదేళ్ల వరకు జైలు శిక్ష, రూ. 50 లక్షల వరకు జరిమానా. సెక్షన్ 92: సెక్షన్ 88 లేదా సెక్షన్ 89 నేరంపై Central Authority లేదా అది అధికారమిచ్చిన అధికారి ఫిర్యాదు చేస్తేనే కోర్టు cognizance తీసుకుంటుంది. సెక్షన్ 88: సెక్షన్ 20 లేదా 21 కింద Central Authority ఆదేశాన్ని పాటించకపోతే ఆరు నెలల వరకు జైలు శిక్ష, లేదా రూ. 20 లక్షల వరకు జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ. సెక్షన్ 24: సెక్షన్ 20 లేదా 21 కింద Central Authority ఇచ్చిన ఉత్తర్వుతో బాధపడిన వ్యక్తి, ఉత్తర్వు అందిన 30 రోజుల్లో National Commission కు అప్పీలు చేయవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 39(1)(l), (n): ఫిర్యాదును నిర్ణయించే Commission, తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటన ప్రభావాన్ని తొలగించడానికి ప్రత్యర్థి ఖర్చుతో corrective advertisement ఇవ్వమని ఆదేశించవచ్చు. తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటనలు ఆపమని కూడా ఆదేశించవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 93: సెక్షన్ 22 కింద సోదా లేదా స్వాధీనం చేసిన అధికారికి సరైన కారణాలు లేవని తెలిసి అలా చేస్తే, ఒక సంవత్సరం వరకు జైలు, లేదా రూ. 10,000 వరకు జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ విధించవచ్చు.
te.meaning: తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటన అంటే కేవలం స్పష్టమైన అబద్ధం మాత్రమే కాదు. తప్పుదారి పట్టించే అవకాశం ఉన్న ప్రకటన, అన్యాయ వాణిజ్య పద్ధతి అయ్యే వాగ్దానం చేసే ప్రకటన, ముఖ్యమైన సమాచారాన్ని ఉద్దేశపూర్వకంగా దాచే ప్రకటన కూడా ఇందులో ఉంటాయి. Endorser అంటే ప్రకటనకు విశ్వసనీయత ఇవ్వడానికి తన పేరు, ముఖం, సందేశం లేదా ముద్ర వాడబడిన వ్యక్తి.

selfTest.q: 1. మొదటి ఉల్లంఘనకు endorser ను ఎంతకాలం నిషేధించవచ్చు?
selfTest.a: ఒక సంవత్సరం వరకు (సెక్షన్ 21(3)). 2. Endorser కు ఏ రక్షణ ఉంటుంది? వాదనలను ధృవీకరించడంలో due diligence చూపడం (సెక్షన్ 21(5)). 3. సెక్షన్ 89 నేరంపై ఎవరు ఫిర్యాదు చేయవచ్చు? Central Authority లేదా అది అధికారమిచ్చిన అధికారి (సెక్షన్ 92).

en.meaning:
Before any consumer-specific statute existed, which tort was the primary remedy available to a consumer injured by a defective product or careless service?

Explanation. Before consumer-specific legislation, an injured consumer's only real remedy was the tort of negligence — proving a duty of care, breach, and resulting damage.

What barrier did the doctrine of privity of contract traditionally create for an injured consumer?

Explanation. Privity of contract meant a buyer generally had no claim against a manufacturer or other party they had no direct contract with, even if that party's carelessness caused the harm.

In Donoghue v. Stevenson, what did the House of Lords hold about a manufacturer's duty of care?

Explanation. The House of Lords held that a manufacturer's duty of care to the ultimate consumer exists independently of contract, removing privity as a bar to a negligence claim.

In Cassidy v. Ministry of Health, the Ministry relied on an older, narrower view of hospital liability. Which test did the Court of Appeal move away from?

en.meaning:
Under section 34(1) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the District Commission hears complaints where the consideration paid does not exceed:

Explanation. Section 34(1) fixes the limit at Rs 1 crore and lets the Central Government prescribe another value. The 2021 Rules prescribed Rs 50 lakh. Section 107 repealed the Consumer Protection Act, 1986.

What is the single most significant structural innovation of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?

Explanation. The CCPA is a dedicated regulatory body that can investigate and act on its own initiative, without waiting for an individual consumer complaint — something the 1986 Act had no equivalent of.

How does the 2019 Act treat product liability differently from the position under the 1986 Act?

Explanation. The 2019 Act, for the first time, gives product liability its own dedicated statutory chapter with defined standards, instead of requiring reliance purely on common-law negligence.

law-of-torts-u5-t21.subtitle: Chapter V of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019: the mediation cell, the panel of mediators, their duties and how a settlement becomes an order

en.inOneMinute: Chapter V of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (sections 74 to 81) sets up mediation inside the consumer forums. Each Commission has a consumer mediation cell with a panel of mediators valid for five years. A mediator must disclose any interest, and the Commission records the settlement within seven days. In exams, this topic is asked as a long answer on the empanelment, appointment and duties of mediators and the settlement of disputes. The usual trap is to confuse empanelment, which creates the panel, with nomination, which picks one mediator for one dispute.
legalProvision: Section 37: reference to mediation by the District Commission, with written consent of the parties within five days. Section 74: establishment of the consumer mediation cell. Section 75: empanelment of mediators. Section 76: nomination of mediators from the panel. Section 77: duty of the mediator to disclose certain facts. Section 78: replacement of a mediator. Section 79: procedure for mediation. Section 80: settlement through mediation. Section 81: recording of the settlement and passing of the order. Consumer Protection (Mediation) Rules, 2020: made by the Central Government (G.S.R. 450(E), 15 July 2020, in force from 20 July 2020). They cover the cell, the selection committee, excluded matters, refund of fee and the effect of a settlement. Consumer Protection (Mediation) Regulations, 2020: made by the National Commission (24 July 2020). They cover empanelment, fee, training, code of conduct, procedure, confidentiality and reports.
en.meaning: Mediation is a way of settling a dispute in which a neutral mediator helps the parties reach an agreement. Empanelment means putting a person on the approved panel of mediators. Nomination means choosing a mediator from that panel for a particular dispute.
keyPoints: A mediation cell is attached to every Commission (section 74). The panel is valid for five years, on the recommendation of a selection committee (section 75). The mediator must disclose any interest or doubt about independence (section 77). The mediator is guided by natural justice (section 79). The Commission records the settlement within seven days (section 81). Mediation ends in three months from the first appearance unless extended (Regulation 11(2)). The mediator cannot impose a settlement, and the proceedings are confidential (Regulations 12 and 13). The complainant gets the full application fee back if a settlement is reached (Rule 5).

caseLaws.name: This topic rests on the text of the Act
caseLaws.facts: No judgment in this collection is relied on for it.

selfTest.q: 1. For how long is the panel of mediators valid?
selfTest.a: Five years, with re-empanelment possible (section 75(3)). 2. Who recommends the panel of mediators? A selection committee of the President and a member of the Commission (section 75(1)). 3. What does a mediator send to the Commission after a settlement? The signed agreement with a settlement report (section 80(2)). 4. Within what time must mediation be completed? Three months from the first appearance before the mediator, unless the Commission extends it (Regulation 11(2)). 5. Which matters are not referred to mediation? Those listed in Rule 4, such as medical negligence causing grievous injury or death, and cases of serious fraud or forgery.

legalProvision: సెక్షన్ 37: ఐదు రోజుల్లో పక్షాల రాతపూర్వక సమ్మతితో District Commission mediation కు పంపడం. సెక్షన్ 74: Consumer mediation cell ఏర్పాటు. సెక్షన్ 75: మధ్యవర్తుల empanelment. సెక్షన్ 76: ప్యానెల్ నుండి మధ్యవర్తుల nomination. సెక్షన్ 77: కొన్ని వాస్తవాలను వెల్లడించే మధ్యవర్తి విధి. సెక్షన్ 78: మధ్యవర్తి మార్పు. సెక్షన్ 79: Mediation విధానం. సెక్షన్ 80: Mediation ద్వారా పరిష్కారం. సెక్షన్ 81: పరిష్కారం నమోదు, ఉత్తర్వు జారీ. Consumer Protection (Mediation) Rules, 2020: కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వం చేసిన నియమాలు (G.S.R. 450(E), 15 జూలై 2020; 20 జూలై 2020 నుండి అమలు). Cell, selection committee, మినహాయించిన అంశాలు, ఫీజు వాపసు, పరిష్కారం ప్రభావాన్ని ఇవి చెబుతాయి. Consumer Protection (Mediation) Regulations, 2020: National Commission చేసిన నిబంధనలు (24 జూలై 2020). Empanelment, ఫీజు, శిక్షణ, ప్రవర్తనా నియమావళి, విధానం, గోప్యత, నివేదికలను ఇవి చెబుతాయి.
te.meaning: Mediation అంటే తటస్థ మధ్యవర్తి పక్షాలు ఒప్పందానికి చేరడానికి సహాయం చేసే వివాద పరిష్కార పద్ధతి. Empanelment అంటే ఒక వ్యక్తిని ఆమోదించిన మధ్యవర్తుల ప్యానెల్‌లో చేర్చడం. Nomination అంటే ఆ ప్యానెల్ నుండి ఒక నిర్దిష్ట వివాదానికి మధ్యవర్తిని ఎంచుకోవడం.

selfTest.q: 1. మధ్యవర్తుల ప్యానెల్ ఎంతకాలం చెల్లుబాటు అవుతుంది?
selfTest.a: ఐదేళ్లు, re-empanelment సాధ్యం (సెక్షన్ 75(3)). 2. మధ్యవర్తుల ప్యానెల్‌ను ఎవరు సిఫారసు చేస్తారు? Commission President, ఒక సభ్యునితో కూడిన selection committee (సెక్షన్ 75(1)). 3. పరిష్కారం తర్వాత మధ్యవర్తి Commission కు ఏం పంపుతాడు? సంతకం చేసిన ఒప్పందాన్ని settlement report తో (సెక్షన్ 80(2)). 4. Mediation ఎంత సమయంలో పూర్తి కావాలి? మధ్యవర్తి ముందు మొదటి హాజరు నుండి మూడు నెలలు, Commission పొడిగిస్తే తప్ప (Regulation 11(2)). 5. ఏ అంశాలను mediation కు పంపరు? Rule 4 లో ఉన్నవి: తీవ్రమైన గాయం లేదా మరణానికి దారితీసిన వైద్య నిర్లక్ష్యం, తీవ్రమైన మోసం లేదా ఫోర్జరీ కేసులు వంటివి.

en.meaning:
What best describes 'consumerism'?

Explanation. Consumerism is a collective, organised movement — through associations, advocacy, and legislative lobbying — not merely individual shopping caution.

Why couldn't ordinary tort remedies alone correct market-wide consumer harms such as adulteration or false advertising?

Explanation. Tort remedies compensate one injured consumer at a time, long after harm occurs, and only if that consumer can afford to litigate — inadequate for correcting market-wide problems.

The doctrine of caveat emptor means

Explanation. Caveat emptor, 'let the buyer beware', historically placed the responsibility of examining goods before purchase on the buyer, with limited seller disclosure duties.

Consumerism pushed the law towards a philosophy closer to which principle?

en.meaning:
Under Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a 'consumer' is a person who buys goods or avails a service for consideration, but excludes a person acting for a

Explanation. A person who buys goods or avails a service for a 'commercial purpose' is excluded from the definition of 'consumer' under Section 2(7).

Which of the following buyers is NOT excluded from being a 'consumer', despite the commercial-purpose exclusion?

Explanation. The Act expressly carves out goods bought and used exclusively for earning one's livelihood through self-employment from the commercial-purpose exclusion.

Besides the person who actually pays for goods or a service, who else does the definition of 'consumer' include?

Explanation. The definition extends to a user of goods with the buyer's approval and a beneficiary of a service with the hirer's approval, even if they did not personally pay.

How many consumer rights does the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 expressly recognise?

en.meaning:
Under Section 2(10) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, 'defect' applies to

Explanation. 'Defect' under Section 2(10) is defined specifically in relation to goods or products.

A trader advertises a claim about a product's performance that the product does not actually meet, even though no separate law or contract required that specific standard. Can this still amount to a 'defect'?

Explanation. 'Defect' under Section 2(10) expressly includes a shortfall against a standard 'claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever' about the goods.

Under Section 2(11), 'deficiency' in a service expressly includes

Explanation. Section 2(11) expressly writes negligence and deliberate withholding of relevant information into the definition of 'deficiency'.

How does proof of a defect in goods usually differ from proof of a deficiency in a service?

en.meaning:
How many tiers of Consumer Protection Councils does the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 establish?

Explanation. The Act establishes a three-tier structure of Consumer Protection Councils — Central, State, and District.

Who chairs the Central Consumer Protection Council?

Explanation. The Central Consumer Protection Council is chaired by the Union Minister in charge of Consumer Affairs.

Who chairs the District Consumer Protection Council?

Explanation. The District Consumer Protection Council is chaired by the District Collector or an equivalent officer.

What is the core object of every Consumer Protection Council, regardless of level?

en.meaning:
Under which section of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 is the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) established?

Explanation. Section 10 empowers the Central Government to establish the CCPA by notification.

What is the key difference between the CCPA and the District/State/National Commissions?

Explanation. The CCPA's mandate is regulatory/preventive protection of consumers as a class, distinct from the Commissions' role of adjudicating individual complaints.

On what basis can the CCPA initiate an inquiry or investigation?

Explanation. The CCPA can act suo motu (on its own initiative), on a complaint, or on the direction of the Central Government.

Who heads the CCPA's Investigation Wing?

'Unfair trade practice' under Section 2(47) primarily targets

Explanation. Unfair trade practice targets deceptive or unfair methods used to promote sale/use/supply, such as false representations and false guarantees.

Which of the following is expressly listed as an unfair trade practice under the 2019 Act?

'Restrictive trade practice' under Section 2(41) primarily targets

Explanation. Restrictive trade practice centres on distorting the market's ordinary functioning (price, delivery, supply), harming consumers collectively.

What is a 'tie-in arrangement'?

Which chapter of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 introduces the formal mediation mechanism?

Explanation. Chapter V, Sections 74 to 81, introduces the formal statutory mediation mechanism under the 2019 Act.

Under Section 74, where are consumer mediation cells attached?

Explanation. Section 74 requires mediation cells attached to District Commissions, State Commissions, the National Commission, and its regional Benches.

How are mediators selected under Sections 75-76?

Explanation. Mediators are empanelled by the Commission, and for each dispute referred to mediation, one is nominated from that empanelled panel.

What must a mediator disclose under Section 77?

en.meaning:
What is the fundamental character of civil liability under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?

Explanation. Civil liability under the Act is compensatory — refund, replacement, compensation, and discontinuation orders — not punitive.

Can civil liability and criminal liability under the Act arise from the same underlying conduct?

Explanation. Civil liability (before a Commission) and criminal liability (before a criminal court) can both arise from the same conduct, serving different purposes through different processes.

Under Section 89, the punishment for a first offence of causing a false or misleading advertisement prejudicial to consumers is

Explanation. Section 89 prescribes imprisonment up to two years and a fine up to ten lakh rupees for a first offence.

Under Section 89, what is the punishment for a subsequent (repeat) offence?

Which chapter of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 deals with product liability?

Explanation. Chapter VI (Sections 82 to 87) deals with product liability.

Which section lays down the grounds of liability of a product manufacturer?

Explanation. Section 84 lists the grounds on which a product manufacturer is liable.

Which is NOT a ground of manufacturer liability under Section 84?

Explanation. Section 84 covers manufacturing defect, design defect, deviation from specifications, non-conformity with express warranty and inadequate instructions or warnings.

environmental-law-u1-t1.subtitle: Section 2(a) of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986: water, air, land and their links with living beings and property

en.inOneMinute: Environment means everything that surrounds a living being and affects its life. The law gives it a fixed meaning in section 2(a) of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. That meaning covers water, air and land, and the links between them and all living beings and property. Every pollution case starts from this definition, so exams often begin with it.
legalProvision: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is a Central Act. The text below is checked against the Bare Act page on this site.

Section 2(a): "environment" includes water, air and land and the inter-relationship which exists among and between water, air and land, and human beings, other living creatures, plants, micro-organism and property. Section 2(b): an "environmental pollutant" is any solid, liquid or gaseous substance present in such concentration as may be, or tend to be, injurious to environment. Section 2(c): "environmental pollution" is the presence in the environment of any environmental pollutant. Section 3(1): the Central Government can take all measures it thinks necessary to protect and improve the quality of the environment and to prevent, control and abate pollution.
en.meaning:
In everyday speech, environment means the surroundings of a person or a living being. The word comes from the French environner , which means to encircle . It includes living things such as plants and animals, and non-living things such as air, water and soil.

The law needs a firmer meaning, so section 2(a) of the Act supplies one. The key feature is that the definition names the inter-relationship and not only the physical parts. Water, air and land are one connected system with people, other living creatures, plants, micro-organisms and property.

What "environment" includes under section 2(a) How to read this: start at the top box and follow the lines down. The lower boxes are the things the Act names, and the links between them are part of the definition. Environment (section 2(a)) Water, air and land The physical parts, and the links among them. Living beings Human beings, other living creatures, plants and micro-organism. Property Buildings, monuments and other things people own.
keyPoints: Source: section 2(a), Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. Parts: water, air, land, their inter-relationship, living beings, property. The Act's word is "micro-organism". The definition begins with "includes", so it is not a closed list. Environmental pollution is the presence of an environmental pollutant in the environment (section 2(c)). Ecology and ecosystem are not defined in the Act.

caseLaws.name: M
caseLaws.facts: C. Mehta v. Union of India (Taj Trapezium Case) (1997) Facts. Industrial emissions in the Taj Trapezium Zone were damaging the Taj Mahal. Principle. The Supreme Court ordered the coke- and coal-using industries to switch to natural gas or relocate. Significance. The definition lists property. This case shows air pollution harming a monument handled as an environmental matter. Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar (1991) Facts. A petitioner under Article 32 complained that waste from washeries polluted the Bokaro river water. Principle. The right to life under Article 21 includes the right to enjoy pollution-free water and air. A petition for this must come from a person genuinely interested in the public good, not from personal enmity. Significance. It is the source of the right to a healthy environment under Article 21.

selfTest.q: 1. Which section defines environment in the 1986 Act?
selfTest.a: Section 2(a). 2. Does the definition cover property? Yes. Property is listed with human beings, other living creatures, plants and micro-organism. 3. Why does the word "inter-relationship" matter? It treats water, air, land and living beings as one connected whole, so harm to one part is harm to the environment.

te.meaning:
రోజువారీ భాషలో పర్యావరణం అంటే ఒక వ్యక్తి లేదా జీవి చుట్టూ ఉన్నవి. ఈ పదం ఫ్రెంచ్ environner నుండి వచ్చింది, దాని అర్థం అన్ని వైపుల నుంచి చుట్టుముట్టడం. ఇందులో మొక్కలు, జంతువుల వంటి జీవులు, గాలి, నీరు, నేల వంటి నిర్జీవ పదార్థాలు ఉంటాయి.

చట్టానికి దృఢమైన అర్థం కావాలి, అందుకే చట్టంలోని సెక్షన్ 2(a) ఒక అర్థం ఇచ్చింది. ఇందులో ముఖ్యమైన అంశం ఏమిటంటే, భౌతిక భాగాలనే కాక పరస్పర సంబంధాన్ని కూడా నిర్వచనం పేర్కొంది. నీరు, గాలి, భూమి మానవులు, ఇతర జీవులు, మొక్కలు, సూక్ష్మజీవులు, ఆస్తితో కలిసి ఒకే అనుసంధాన వ్యవస్థ.

సెక్షన్ 2(a) ప్రకారం "పర్యావరణం"లో ఉండేవి ఇలా చదవండి: పై పెట్టె నుండి మొదలుపెట్టి గీతల వెంట కిందికి వెళ్లండి. కింది పెట్టెల్లో చట్టం పేర్కొన్నవి ఉన్నాయి, వాటి మధ్య సంబంధాలు కూడా నిర్వచనంలో భాగమే. పర్యావరణం (సెక్షన్ 2(a)) నీరు, గాలి, భూమి భౌతిక భాగాలు, వాటి మధ్య సంబంధాలు. జీవులు మానవులు, ఇతర జీవులు, మొక్కలు, సూక్ష్మజీవి. ఆస్తి భవనాలు, స్మారక చిహ్నాలు, ప్రజలకు చెందిన ఇతర వస్తువులు.

environmental-law-u1-t2.subtitle: The science of how living things relate to their surroundings, and why environmental law depends on it

en.inOneMinute: Ecology is the scientific study of how living things relate to each other and to their surroundings. It is a science, not a statute. Environmental law uses ecological facts to decide whether an activity will cause harm. Exams ask for the meaning of ecology, its parts and how it differs from environment.
legalProvision: No Indian statute defines ecology. The idea enters the law in two ways.

Section 2(a), Environment (Protection) Act, 1986: environment includes the "inter-relationship" among water, air, land and living beings. This is the relationship ecology studies. Environmental impact assessment: a study of how a project will affect its surroundings, which relies on ecological data.
en.meaning:
Ecology is the scientific study of the relationships between living organisms and their physical surroundings. It looks at how organisms depend on each other and how energy and materials move among them.

The German biologist Ernst Haeckel coined the term in 1866. It joins two Greek words: oikos , meaning house or habitat , and logos , meaning study. The first part of the word shows the idea: living things share one house.

Levels at which ecology studies life How to read this: read from the smallest level to the largest, left to right on a wide screen or top to bottom on a phone. Each level contains the one before it. Level 1 Organism: one living being. Level 2 Population: organisms of one species in an area. Level 3 Community: all populations of different species in an area. Level 4 Ecosystem: a community together with its non-living surroundings. Level 5 Biosphere: all ecosystems of the Earth.
keyPoints: Ecology: scientific study of organisms and their surroundings. Coined by Ernst Haeckel in 1866 from oikos and logos . Biotic factors are living; abiotic factors are non-living. Levels: organism, population, community, ecosystem, biosphere. No Indian Act defines ecology; section 2(a) of the 1986 Act covers the inter-relationship.

caseLaws.name: No Indian case turns on the meaning of ecology
caseLaws.facts: Courts use ecological facts in cases on pollution, forests and wildlife, which are covered in the notes on those topics.

selfTest.q: 1. Who coined the word ecology, and in which year?
selfTest.a: Ernst Haeckel, in 1866. 2. Name two abiotic factors. Any two of sunlight, water, air, soil and temperature. 3. Is ecology defined in the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986? No. The Act defines environment in section 2(a) but does not define ecology.

legalProvision: ఏ భారత చట్టమూ ఎకాలజీని నిర్వచించలేదు. ఈ భావన చట్టంలోకి రెండు విధాలుగా వస్తుంది.

పర్యావరణ (రక్షణ) చట్టం, 1986 సెక్షన్ 2(a): environment లో నీరు, గాలి, భూమి, జీవుల మధ్య "పరస్పర సంబంధం" ఉంటుంది. ఎకాలజీ అధ్యయనం చేసేది ఈ సంబంధాన్నే. పర్యావరణ ప్రభావ మదింపు: ఒక ప్రాజెక్టు తన పరిసరాలను ఎలా ప్రభావితం చేస్తుందో చేసే అధ్యయనం. ఇది ఎకాలజీ డేటాపై ఆధారపడుతుంది.
te.meaning:
ఎకాలజీ అంటే జీవులకు, వాటి భౌతిక పరిసరాలకు మధ్య ఉన్న సంబంధాలను శాస్త్రీయంగా అధ్యయనం చేయడం. జీవులు ఒకదానిపై ఒకటి ఎలా ఆధారపడతాయో, శక్తి, పదార్థాలు వాటి మధ్య ఎలా కదులుతాయో ఇది పరిశీలిస్తుంది.

ఈ పదాన్ని జర్మన్ జీవశాస్త్రవేత్త ఎర్నెస్ట్ హేకల్ 1866లో రూపొందించారు. ఇది రెండు గ్రీకు పదాల కలయిక: oikos అంటే ఇల్లు లేదా ఆవాసం, logos అంటే అధ్యయనం. పదంలోని మొదటి భాగమే భావనను చూపుతుంది: జీవులన్నీ ఒకే ఇంటిని పంచుకుంటాయి.

ఎకాలజీ జీవాన్ని అధ్యయనం చేసే స్థాయిలు ఇలా చదవండి: చిన్న స్థాయి నుండి పెద్ద స్థాయి వరకు చదవండి; వెడల్పు తెరపై ఎడమ నుండి కుడికి, ఫోన్‌లో పై నుండి కిందికి. ప్రతి స్థాయిలో ముందు స్థాయి ఉంటుంది. స్థాయి 1 Organism: ఒక జీవి. స్థాయి 2 Population: ఒక ప్రాంతంలో ఒకే జాతి జీవులు. స్థాయి 3 Community: ఒక ప్రాంతంలోని వివిధ జాతుల జనాభాలన్నీ. స్థాయి 4 Ecosystem: ఒక కమ్యూనిటీ, దాని నిర్జీవ పరిసరాలతో కలిపి. స్థాయి 5 Biosphere: భూమిపై ఉన్న అన్ని ఎకోసిస్టమ్‌లు.

selfTest.q: 1. ఎకాలజీ అనే పదాన్ని ఎవరు, ఏ సంవత్సరంలో రూపొందించారు?
selfTest.a: ఎర్నెస్ట్ హేకల్, 1866లో. 2. రెండు నిర్జీవ కారకాలను చెప్పండి. సూర్యరశ్మి, నీరు, గాలి, నేల, ఉష్ణోగ్రతలలో ఏ రెండైనా. 3. పర్యావరణ (రక్షణ) చట్టం, 1986లో ఎకాలజీని నిర్వచించారా? లేదు. చట్టం సెక్షన్ 2(a)లో పర్యావరణాన్ని నిర్వచిస్తుంది కానీ ఎకాలజీని నిర్వచించదు.

environmental-law-u1-t3.subtitle: Producers, consumers and decomposers, one-way energy flow and recycled nutrients

en.inOneMinute: An ecosystem is a community of living things together with the non-living surroundings they interact with, working as one unit. A pond, a forest patch and a farm are all ecosystems. Energy flows through it in one direction, while nutrients are used again and again. Exams ask for its parts, how energy moves and why pollution upsets its balance.
legalProvision: No Indian Act defines an ecosystem. Two provisions still use the idea.

Section 2(b), Biological Diversity Act, 2002: biological diversity means the variability among living organisms from all sources and the ecological complexes of which they are part, including diversity "of eco-systems". Section 2(a), Environment (Protection) Act, 1986: environment includes the inter-relationship among water, air, land and living beings, which is what an ecosystem is made of.
en.meaning:
An ecosystem is a community of interacting organisms together with their physical surroundings, functioning as a unit. The British ecologist A.G. Tansley introduced the word in 1935.

Ecosystems come in three broad kinds. Terrestrial ones are on land, such as forests and grasslands. Aquatic ones are in water, such as lakes, rivers and oceans. Artificial ones are made by people, such as farms, reservoirs and city parks.

Parts of an ecosystem How to read this: start at the top box and follow the lines down. The left branch is the living part with its three roles. The right branch is the non-living part. Ecosystem Biotic (living) part Producers make food. Consumers eat others. Decomposers break down dead matter. Abiotic (non-living) part Sunlight, water, air, soil and temperature.
keyPoints: Ecosystem: living community plus non-living surroundings as one unit. Roles: producers, consumers, decomposers. Energy flow is one-way; nutrient cycling is circular. A food web joins many food chains. Homeostasis: the ecosystem's tendency to stay balanced. Section 2(b) of the 2002 Act includes diversity of ecosystems.

caseLaws.name: No Indian case turns on the meaning of ecosystem
caseLaws.facts: Courts apply the idea in cases on forests, wetlands and rivers, covered in the notes on those topics.

selfTest.q: 1. Name the three living roles in an ecosystem. Producers, consumers and decomposers. 2. Which moves in a circle, energy or nutrients?
selfTest.a: Nutrients. Energy flows one way and is lost as heat. 3. How is a food web different from a food chain? A chain is one line of feeding. A web joins many chains.

legalProvision: ఏ భారత చట్టమూ ఎకోసిస్టమ్‌ను నిర్వచించలేదు. అయినా రెండు నిబంధనలు ఈ భావనను వాడతాయి.

జీవ వైవిధ్య చట్టం, 2002 సెక్షన్ 2(b): జీవ వైవిధ్యం అంటే అన్ని మూలాల జీవుల మధ్య వైవిధ్యం, అవి భాగమైన పర్యావరణ సముదాయాలు, "eco-systems" వైవిధ్యంతో సహా. పర్యావరణ (రక్షణ) చట్టం, 1986 సెక్షన్ 2(a): పర్యావరణంలో నీరు, గాలి, భూమి, జీవుల మధ్య పరస్పర సంబంధం ఉంటుంది; ఎకోసిస్టమ్ అనేది దీనితోనే ఏర్పడుతుంది.
te.meaning:
ecosystem అంటే పరస్పరం సంబంధం ఉన్న జీవుల సముదాయం, వాటి భౌతిక పరిసరాలతో కలిసి ఒక యూనిట్‌గా పనిచేయడం. ఈ పదాన్ని బ్రిటిష్ ఎకాలజిస్ట్ ఎ.జి. టాన్స్లీ 1935లో ప్రవేశపెట్టారు.

ఎకోసిస్టమ్‌లు మూడు రకాలు. భూమిపై ఉండేవి అడవులు, గడ్డి మైదానాల వంటివి. నీటిలో ఉండేవి సరస్సులు, నదులు, సముద్రాల వంటివి. మనుషులు తయారుచేసినవి పొలాలు, జలాశయాలు, నగర ఉద్యానవనాల వంటివి.

ఎకోసిస్టమ్ భాగాలు ఇలా చదవండి: పై పెట్టె నుండి గీతల వెంట కిందికి వెళ్లండి. ఎడమ శాఖ మూడు పాత్రలతో జీవ భాగం. కుడి శాఖ నిర్జీవ భాగం. ఎకోసిస్టమ్ జీవ (biotic) భాగం ఉత్పత్తిదారులు ఆహారం తయారు చేస్తాయి. వినియోగదారులు ఇతరులను తింటాయి. విచ్ఛిన్నకారులు చనిపోయిన పదార్థాన్ని విడగొడతాయి. నిర్జీవ (abiotic) భాగం సూర్యరశ్మి, నీరు, గాలి, నేల, ఉష్ణోగ్రత.

selfTest.q: 1. ఎకోసిస్టమ్‌లోని మూడు జీవ పాత్రలను చెప్పండి. ఉత్పత్తిదారులు, వినియోగదారులు, విచ్ఛిన్నకారులు. 2. శక్తి, పోషకాల్లో ఏది వృత్తంలో తిరుగుతుంది?
selfTest.a: పోషకాలు. శక్తి ఒకే దిశలో ప్రవహించి వేడిగా పోతుంది. 3. ఆహార వల ఆహార గొలుసుకు ఎలా భిన్నం? గొలుసు ఒకే తినే వరుస. వల అనేక గొలుసులను కలుపుతుంది.

visuals.caption: ఎకోసిస్టమ్ భాగాలు ఇలా చదవండి: పై పెట్టె నుండి గీతల వెంట కిందికి వెళ్లండి. ఎడమ శాఖ మూడు పాత్రలతో జీవ భాగం. కుడి శాఖ నిర్జీవ భాగం.

environmental-law-u1-t5.subtitle: Large climate regions of the Earth, land and water, and the threats they share

en.inOneMinute: A biome is a large region of the Earth with a distinct climate and the plants and animals suited to it. Examples are a desert, a tropical rainforest and a tundra. Biomes are either on land or in water. Exams ask for the kinds of biome, one example of each, and the threats they face.
legalProvision: No Indian Act defines a biome. The concept matters because many protections are designed around regions of distinct life.

Section 2(b), Biological Diversity Act, 2002: biological diversity includes diversity "of eco-systems", which covers the variety found across biomes. Conservation tools: sanctuaries, national parks and biosphere reserves are used to protect samples of different biomes.
en.meaning:
A biome is a large geographical region marked by a distinct climate and by the plant and animal communities adapted to it. An ecosystem can be as small as a pond. A biome spreads across a continent.

Kinds of biome How to read this: start at the top box and follow the lines down. The two middle boxes split biomes into land and water. The lower text lists the types in each. Biomes Terrestrial (land) Tropical rainforest, savanna, desert, temperate grassland, temperate forest, taiga, tundra. Aquatic (water) Freshwater, marine, estuaries.
keyPoints: Biome: large region defined by climate and its adapted life. Terrestrial: rainforest, savanna, desert, grassland, temperate forest, taiga, tundra. Aquatic: freshwater, marine, estuary. Threats: deforestation, climate change, pollution, overuse, habitat loss. Biomes are larger than ecosystems and smaller than the biosphere.

caseLaws.name: No Indian case turns on the meaning of biome
caseLaws.facts: Protection of particular biomes appears in cases on forests, coasts and wetlands, covered in the notes on those topics.

selfTest.q: 1. Name the two broad groups of biome. Terrestrial (land) and aquatic (water). 2. Is the Thar Desert a biome or an ecosystem?
selfTest.a: A biome. A single oasis within it would be an ecosystem. 3. Name two threats common to most biomes. Any two of deforestation, climate change, pollution, overuse and habitat loss.

legalProvision: ఏ భారత చట్టమూ బయోమ్‌ను నిర్వచించలేదు. విలక్షణ జీవం ఉన్న ప్రాంతాల చుట్టూ అనేక రక్షణలు రూపొందించడం వల్ల ఈ భావన ముఖ్యం.

జీవ వైవిధ్య చట్టం, 2002 సెక్షన్ 2(b): జీవ వైవిధ్యంలో "eco-systems" వైవిధ్యం ఉంటుంది; ఇది బయోమ్‌ల అంతటా ఉన్న వైవిధ్యాన్ని కలుపుకుంటుంది. పరిరక్షణ సాధనాలు: వివిధ బయోమ్‌ల నమూనాలను కాపాడడానికి అభయారణ్యాలు, జాతీయ ఉద్యానవనాలు, బయోస్ఫియర్ రిజర్వ్‌లను వాడతారు.
te.meaning:
biome అంటే విలక్షణ వాతావరణం, దానికి అలవాటు పడిన మొక్కలు, జంతువుల సముదాయాలతో గుర్తించే పెద్ద భౌగోళిక ప్రాంతం. ఎకోసిస్టమ్ చెరువంత చిన్నదిగా ఉండవచ్చు. బయోమ్ ఒక ఖండమంత విస్తరిస్తుంది.

బయోమ్ రకాలు ఇలా చదవండి: పై పెట్టె నుండి గీతల వెంట కిందికి వెళ్లండి. మధ్యలోని రెండు పెట్టెలు బయోమ్‌లను భూమి, నీరుగా విభజిస్తాయి. కింది వచనం ప్రతిదానిలోని రకాలను చెబుతుంది. బయోమ్స్ భూమి (terrestrial) ఉష్ణమండల వర్షారణ్యం, సవన్నా, ఎడారి, సమశీతోష్ణ గడ్డి మైదానం, సమశీతోష్ణ అడవి, టైగా, టండ్రా. నీరు (aquatic) మంచినీరు, సముద్రం, నదీ ముఖద్వారాలు.

selfTest.q: 1. బయోమ్‌ల రెండు విస్తృత సమూహాలను చెప్పండి. భూమి (terrestrial), నీరు (aquatic). 2. థార్ ఎడారి బయోమా లేక ఎకోసిస్టమా?
selfTest.a: బయోమ్. అందులోని ఒక ఒయాసిస్ ఎకోసిస్టమ్ అవుతుంది. 3. చాలా బయోమ్‌లకు ఉమ్మడిగా ఉన్న రెండు ముప్పులను చెప్పండి. అడవుల నరికివేత, వాతావరణ మార్పు, కాలుష్యం, అతి వినియోగం, ఆవాస నష్టాల్లో ఏ రెండైనా.

environmental-law-u1-t4.subtitle: The thin zone of the Earth where life exists, and why protecting it crosses borders

en.inOneMinute: The biosphere is the whole zone of the Earth where life exists. It is the sum of all ecosystems, found where land, water and air meet. Pollution in one place moves through it and harms places far away. That is why many environmental treaties talk about the biosphere. Exams ask for its meaning and how it differs from an ecosystem and a biome.
legalProvision: No Indian Act defines the biosphere. The idea appears in policy and in international law.

Section 2(a), Environment (Protection) Act, 1986: environment covers water, air and land and the inter-relationship among them and with human beings, other living creatures, plants, micro-organisms and property. This is related to the biosphere idea. Biosphere reserves: India uses biosphere reserves as a conservation tool to protect whole-ecosystem function. They are a policy designation, not a statutory category.
en.meaning:
The biosphere is the global sum of all ecosystems, the thin zone of the planet in which life exists. It forms where the lithosphere (land), the hydrosphere (water) and the atmosphere (air) overlap .

Where the biosphere sits How to read this: the outer box is the largest. Each inner box lies inside the one around it. Biosphere the whole zone of life Biomes large climate regions Ecosystems: a pond, a forest patch, a farm
keyPoints: Biosphere: the global sum of all ecosystems. It is where lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere overlap. Pollution moves through it, so harm crosses borders. A biosphere reserve protects whole-ecosystem function. Biosphere is one; biomes are its large regions.

caseLaws.name: No Indian case turns on the meaning of biosphere
caseLaws.facts: The idea appears in the treaties covered in the notes on international environmental law.

selfTest.q: 1. What three layers overlap in the biosphere?
selfTest.a: The lithosphere (land), the hydrosphere (water) and the atmosphere (air). 2. Why do treaties speak of the biosphere? Pollution moves through the connected biosphere and harms places far from its source. 3. What does a biosphere reserve protect? The health of a whole ecosystem, not only one species.

legalProvision: ఏ భారత చట్టమూ బయోస్ఫియర్‌ను నిర్వచించలేదు. ఈ భావన విధానంలో, అంతర్జాతీయ చట్టంలో కనిపిస్తుంది.

పర్యావరణ (రక్షణ) చట్టం, 1986 సెక్షన్ 2(a): పర్యావరణం నీరు, గాలి, భూమిని, వాటి మధ్య, అలాగే మానవులు, ఇతర జీవులు, మొక్కలు, సూక్ష్మజీవులు, ఆస్తితో ఉన్న పరస్పర సంబంధాన్ని కలుపుకుంటుంది. ఇది బయోస్ఫియర్ భావనకు సంబంధించినది. బయోస్ఫియర్ రిజర్వ్‌లు: మొత్తం ఎకోసిస్టమ్ పనితీరును కాపాడడానికి భారతదేశం బయోస్ఫియర్ రిజర్వ్‌లను పరిరక్షణ సాధనంగా వాడుతుంది. ఇది విధాన పరమైన హోదా; చట్టబద్ధమైన వర్గం కాదు.
te.meaning:
biosphere అంటే అన్ని ఎకోసిస్టమ్‌ల భూగోళ మొత్తం, జీవం ఉండే గ్రహం యొక్క పలుచని మండలం. ఇది లిథోస్ఫియర్ (భూమి), హైడ్రోస్ఫియర్ (నీరు), అట్మాస్ఫియర్ (గాలి) కలిసే చోట ఏర్పడుతుంది.

బయోస్ఫియర్ ఎక్కడ ఉంటుంది ఇలా చదవండి: బయటి పెట్టె అతి పెద్దది. ప్రతి లోపలి పెట్టె తన చుట్టూ ఉన్న పెట్టెలో ఉంటుంది. బయోస్ఫియర్ జీవం ఉన్న మొత్తం మండలం బయోమ్స్ పెద్ద వాతావరణ ప్రాంతాలు ఎకోసిస్టమ్‌లు: చెరువు, అడవి భాగం, పొలం

selfTest.q: 1. బయోస్ఫియర్‌లో ఏ మూడు పొరలు కలుస్తాయి?
selfTest.a: లిథోస్ఫియర్ (భూమి), హైడ్రోస్ఫియర్ (నీరు), అట్మాస్ఫియర్ (గాలి). 2. ఒప్పందాలు బయోస్ఫియర్ గురించి ఎందుకు మాట్లాడతాయి? కాలుష్యం అనుసంధానమైన బయోస్ఫియర్ గుండా కదిలి, మూలం నుండి దూరంగా ఉన్న చోట్ల హాని చేస్తుంది. 3. బయోస్ఫియర్ రిజర్వ్ దేన్ని కాపాడుతుంది? ఒక్క జాతిని కాదు, మొత్తం ఎకోసిస్టమ్ ఆరోగ్యాన్ని.

environmental-law-u1-t7.subtitle: The rise in the Earth's average surface temperature caused by greenhouse gases

en.inOneMinute: Global warming is the long-term rise in the Earth's average surface temperature. Gases such as carbon dioxide and methane trap heat in the air, and human activity has added a great deal of them. It is the main driver of climate change. Exams ask for causes, effects and the treaty response.
legalProvision: India has no single Act on global warming. The law reaches it through these sources.

Section 2(a), Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981: an "air pollutant" is any solid, liquid or gaseous substance (including noise) present in the atmosphere in such concentration as may be or tend to be injurious to human beings, other living creatures, plants, property or environment. Section 3(1), Environment (Protection) Act, 1986: the Central Government can take all measures it thinks necessary to protect the environment and control pollution. UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, 1992, Kyoto Protocol, 1997 and Paris Agreement: the treaties that set the global response. Article 2, Paris Agreement: the goal of holding the rise in global average temperature well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Efforts continue to limit it to 1.5 degrees.
en.meaning:
Global warming is the long-term rise in the Earth's average surface temperature, caused by the build-up of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. A greenhouse gas is a gas that traps heat. The Earth needs some of them to stay warm enough for life. The problem is the extra amount.

How extra greenhouse gases warm the Earth How to read this: follow the boxes from top to bottom. Each step causes the next. The last box is the result. 1. Sunlight reaches the Earth and warms the surface. 2. The surface sends heat back towards space. 3. Greenhouse gases in the air trap part of that heat. 4. Human activity adds more gases, so more heat is trapped. 5. Result The average temperature of the surface rises.
keyPoints: Global warming: long-term rise in average surface temperature. Gases: carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, CFCs, water vapour. Causes: fossil fuels, deforestation, industry, farming, cities. Paris Agreement, Article 2: well below 2 degrees, efforts towards 1.5 degrees. No separate Indian Act. The Air Act and the 1986 Act apply to harmful gases. Kyoto Annex A: six gases (carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, HFCs, PFCs, sulphur hexafluoride). Paris Art 4(1): peaking, then balance in the second half of the century.

caseLaws.name: No case in the syllabus list turns only on global warming
caseLaws.facts: Indian courts have treated climate harm as part of the right to a healthy environment, as covered in the note on climate justice.

selfTest.q: 1. Name three greenhouse gases. Any three of carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, CFCs and water vapour. 2. What temperature goal does Article 2 of the Paris Agreement state?
selfTest.a: Holding the rise well below 2 degrees Celsius and pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5 degrees. 3. Is the greenhouse effect itself harmful? No. It is natural and keeps the Earth warm. The harm comes from the extra gases.

legalProvision: భూతాపంపై భారతదేశంలో ఒకే చట్టం లేదు. చట్టం దీన్ని ఈ మూలాల ద్వారా చేరుతుంది.

గాలి (కాలుష్య నివారణ, నియంత్రణ) చట్టం, 1981 సెక్షన్ 2(a): "air pollutant" అంటే వాతావరణంలో మానవులకు, ఇతర జీవులకు, మొక్కలకు, ఆస్తికి లేదా పర్యావరణానికి హానికరంగా ఉండే లేదా ఉండే అవకాశమున్న సాంద్రతలో ఉన్న ఏదైనా ఘన, ద్రవ లేదా వాయు పదార్థం (శబ్దంతో సహా). పర్యావరణ (రక్షణ) చట్టం, 1986 సెక్షన్ 3(1): పర్యావరణాన్ని కాపాడటానికి, కాలుష్యాన్ని నియంత్రించడానికి అవసరమని భావించే అన్ని చర్యలను కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వం తీసుకోవచ్చు. ఐక్యరాజ్యసమితి వాతావరణ మార్పు ఫ్రేమ్‌వర్క్ కన్వెన్షన్, 1992, క్యోటో ప్రోటోకాల్, 1997, పారిస్ ఒప్పందం: ప్రపంచ స్పందనను నిర్ణయించే ఒప్పందాలు. పారిస్ ఒప్పందం ఆర్టికల్ 2: ప్రపంచ సగటు ఉష్ణోగ్రత పెరుగుదలను పారిశ్రామికీకరణకు ముందు స్థాయిల కంటే 2 డిగ్రీల సెల్సియస్ కంటే చాలా తక్కువగా ఉంచడం, దాన్ని 1.5 డిగ్రీలకు పరిమితం చేసే ప్రయత్నాలు కొనసాగించడం లక్ష్యం.
te.meaning:
Global warming అంటే వాతావరణంలో గ్రీన్‌హౌస్ వాయువులు పేరుకుపోవడం వల్ల భూమి సగటు ఉపరితల ఉష్ణోగ్రత దీర్ఘకాలంగా పెరగడం. గ్రీన్‌హౌస్ వాయువు అంటే వేడిని బంధించే వాయువు. జీవానికి సరిపడా వెచ్చదనం కోసం భూమికి వీటిలో కొంత అవసరం. సమస్య అదనపు పరిమాణమే.

అదనపు గ్రీన్‌హౌస్ వాయువులు భూమిని ఎలా వేడెక్కిస్తాయి ఇలా చదవండి: పై నుండి కిందికి పెట్టెలను అనుసరించండి. ప్రతి దశ తర్వాతి దశకు కారణం. చివరి పెట్టె ఫలితం. 1. సూర్యకాంతి భూమిని చేరి ఉపరితలాన్ని వేడెక్కిస్తుంది. 2. ఉపరితలం వేడిని తిరిగి అంతరిక్షం వైపు పంపుతుంది. 3. గాలిలోని గ్రీన్‌హౌస్ వాయువులు ఆ వేడిలో కొంత భాగాన్ని బంధిస్తాయి. 4. మానవ కార్యకలాపాలు ఎక్కువ వాయువులను చేర్చడంతో ఎక్కువ వేడి బంధించబడుతుంది. 5. ఫలితం ఉపరితల సగటు ఉష్ణోగ్రత పెరుగుతుంది.

selfTest.q: 1. మూడు గ్రీన్‌హౌస్ వాయువుల పేర్లు చెప్పండి. కార్బన్ డయాక్సైడ్, మీథేన్, నైట్రస్ ఆక్సైడ్, CFCలు, నీటి ఆవిరిలో ఏ మూడైనా. 2. పారిస్ ఒప్పందం ఆర్టికల్ 2 ఏ ఉష్ణోగ్రత లక్ష్యం చెబుతుంది?
selfTest.a: పెరుగుదలను 2 డిగ్రీల సెల్సియస్ కంటే చాలా తక్కువగా ఉంచడం, 1.5 డిగ్రీలకు పరిమితం చేసే ప్రయత్నాలు కొనసాగించడం. 3. గ్రీన్‌హౌస్ ప్రభావం స్వయంగా హానికరమా? కాదు. ఇది సహజమైనది, భూమిని వెచ్చగా ఉంచుతుంది. హాని అదనపు వాయువుల వల్ల వస్తుంది.

environmental-law-u1-t6.subtitle: Thinning of the stratospheric ozone layer, its causes, effects and the legal response

en.inOneMinute: The ozone layer is a thin shield of gas high in the atmosphere that blocks most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet rays. Ozone depletion is the thinning of that shield. It is caused mainly by man-made chemicals such as CFCs and halons. The world answered with the Montreal Protocol. Exams ask for causes, effects and this legal response.
legalProvision: Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer: adopted on 22 March 1985. The UN Treaty Collection gives its entry into force as 22 September 1988, under article 17(1). Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer: concluded on 16 September 1987, in force from 1 January 1989 (article 16(1), as the UN Treaty Collection records). London Amendment to the Montreal Protocol: adopted on 29 June 1990 at the Second Meeting of the Parties. It entered into force on 10 August 1992, under article 2(1) of the Amendment (UN Treaty Collection). Ozone Depleting Substances (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000: made under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 (Gazette notification S.O. 670(E) of 19 July 2000), to regulate and phase out such substances in India. Annex A to the Protocol: the list of controlled substances (CFCs and halons) with their ozone depleting potentials. Section 3(1), Environment (Protection) Act, 1986: the source of the Central Government's power to take measures to prevent and control pollution.
en.meaning:
Ozone depletion is the thinning of the ozone layer in the stratosphere, caused by the breakdown of ozone (O₃) molecules. The layer lies roughly 10 to 50 kilometres above the Earth's surface. It absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

How a CFC destroys ozone How to read this: follow the boxes from top to bottom. Each step leads to the next. The last box is the result for people and wildlife. 1. A CFC leaks from an old refrigerator or air conditioner. 2. The gas drifts up to the stratosphere. 3. Ultraviolet rays break the CFC and free chlorine atoms. 4. One chlorine atom destroys many ozone molecules. 5. Result The layer thins and more ultraviolet rays reach the ground.
keyPoints: Ozone layer: stratosphere, about 10 to 50 km above the surface. Causes: CFCs, halons, carbon tetrachloride, methyl chloroform, methyl bromide. Vienna Convention: 1985. Montreal Protocol: 1987, in force 1989. India: Ozone Depleting Substances (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000. Vienna Convention: framework, 21 articles and 2 annexes, no limits. Montreal Protocol: 20 articles and Annex A, with limits. Group I freeze at the 1986 level, then 80 per cent from 1 July 1993 and 50 per cent from 1 July 1998. Developing countries (under 0.3 kg per capita) may delay by ten years. Original Protocol: no Multilateral Fund; Article 13 charges costs to the Parties' contributions. The London Amendment (1990, in force 10 August 1992) created the Multilateral Fund under Article 10 and added Articles 2C to 2E, Annexes B and C, and Article 10A. Later amendments: Copenhagen 1992 (HCFCs, HBFCs, methyl bromide), Montreal 1997 (Article 4A, licensing under Article 4B), Beijing 1999 (bromochloromethane, HCFC production), Kigali 2016 (HFC phase-down, Annex F, Article 2J). Many such substances are also heat-trapping gases, but ozone depletion is not global warming.

caseLaws.name: No case on the cases list of the syllabus turns on ozone depletion
caseLaws.facts: The law here rests on the treaties and the 2000 Rules.

selfTest.q: 1. In which layer is the ozone layer?
selfTest.a: The stratosphere. 2. Name the treaty of 1987 on ozone-depleting substances. The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer. 3. What does the original Protocol require of Group I substances by 1 July 1998? Consumption and production at no more than fifty per cent of the 1986 level, unless the Parties decide otherwise (Art 2(4)). 4. What does Article 5 give developing countries? A ten-year delay, if consumption is under 0.3 kilograms per capita, with help to get alternatives. 5. Under which Act were India's Rules of 2000 made? The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

ProvisionWhat it says
PreambleThe Parties are aware of the harmful impact of ozone-layer modification on human health and the environment. They recall the Stockholm Declaration principle on the sovereign right to use resources and the duty not to damage other States. They note the special needs of developing countries, the need for research, and the need for international co-operation based on scientific and technical considerations.
Article 1Definitions. The "ozone layer" is the layer of atmospheric ozone above the planetary boundary layer. "Adverse effects" are changes in the physical environment or biota, including climate, that have significant harmful effects on human health, on natural and managed ecosystems, or on materials useful to mankind. The Article also defines alternative technologies or equipment, alternative substances, Parties, a regional economic integration organization, and protocols.
Article 2General obligations. Parties must take appropriate measures to protect human health and the environment against adverse effects of human activities that modify the ozone layer (Art 2(1)). They must co-operate through systematic observation, research and information exchange, adopt legislative or administrative measures, co-operate in agreed measures, procedures and standards, and work with competent international bodies (Art 2(2)). A Party may take additional domestic measures that are consistent with the Convention (Art 2(3)). Application of the Article rests on relevant scientific and technical considerations (Art 2(4)).
Article 3Research and systematic observations. Parties undertake to co-operate in research and assessment on the physical and chemical processes affecting the ozone layer, health and biological effects including UV-B radiation, climatic effects, effects on materials, substances and activities that may affect the layer, alternative substances and technologies, and socio-economic matters (Art 3(1)). They promote joint programmes for systematic observation, as set out in Annex I (Art 3(2)). They co-operate in collecting, validating and passing on data through world data centres (Art 3(3)).
Article 4Co-operation in the legal, scientific and technical fields. Parties facilitate the exchange of scientific, technical, socio-economic, commercial and legal information, as set out in Annex II. Confidential information supplied by a Party must not be disclosed (Art 4(1)). They co-operate in developing and transferring technology and knowledge, with special regard to developing countries. This covers help in acquiring alternative technologies, information and manuals, equipment for research and observation, and training of personnel (Art 4(2)).
Article 5Transmission of information. Parties send, through the secretariat, information on the measures they have adopted to the Conference of the Parties, in the form and at the intervals the meetings decide.
Article 6Conference of the Parties. The Conference is established. Its first meeting is convened within one year after entry into force. Extraordinary meetings can be held when the Conference thinks necessary, or when a Party asks in writing and one third of the Parties support the request within six months (Art 6(1)-(2)). It adopts its rules of procedure and financial rules by consensus (Art 6(3)). It keeps the Convention under continuous review, reviews the scientific information, promotes harmonised policies, adopts research programmes, considers amendments, annexes and protocols, and creates subsidiary bodies (Art 6(4)). The United Nations, its specialised agencies, the International Atomic Energy Agency and States not party may attend as observers (Art 6(5)).
Article 7Secretariat. Its functions are to arrange and service meetings, prepare and send reports, perform functions assigned by any protocol, report on its own activities, co-ordinate with other international bodies, and do whatever else the Conference decides (Art 7(1)). The United Nations Environment Programme acts as interim secretariat until the Conference designates one at its first ordinary meeting (Art 7(2)).
Article 8Adoption of protocols. The Conference of the Parties may adopt protocols at a meeting. The text of a proposed protocol must reach the Parties at least six months before that meeting.
Article 9Amendment of the Convention or protocols. Any Party may propose amendments, taking account of scientific and technical considerations (Art 9(1)). An amendment to the Convention is adopted at a meeting of the Conference. An amendment to a protocol is adopted at a meeting of the Parties to that protocol. The text goes to the Parties at least six months before the meeting (Art 9(2)). The Parties first try for consensus. As a last resort, an amendment to the Convention is adopted by a three-fourths majority of the Parties present and voting (Art 9(3)). For a protocol, a two-thirds majority of its Parties present and voting is enough (Art 9(4)). An adopted amendment enters into force on the ninetieth day after the Depositary receives acceptance from at least three-fourths of the Parties to the Convention, or at least two-thirds of the Parties to the protocol (Art 9(5)).
Article 10Annexes. Annexes form an integral part of the Convention or protocol and are limited to scientific, technical and administrative matters (Art 10(1)). An additional annex to the Convention follows the Article 9 procedure for adoption by consensus or a three-fourths majority. A Party that cannot approve it notifies the Depositary within six months. Otherwise it becomes effective for all Parties six months after the Depositary circulates it (Art 10(2)). An annex that needs an amendment to the Convention or protocol does not enter into force until that amendment does (Art 10(4)).
Article 11Settlement of disputes. Parties first seek a solution by negotiation, then may jointly seek good offices or mediation (Art 11(1)-(2)). A State may declare in writing that it accepts arbitration, or submission to the International Court of Justice, or both, as compulsory (Art 11(3)). If no such procedure is accepted, the dispute goes to conciliation unless the parties agree otherwise (Art 11(4)). The conciliation commission has an equal number of members from each party and a chairman chosen jointly. It gives a final and recommendatory award, which the parties consider in good faith (Art 11(5)).
Articles 12-14Signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession. The Convention was open for signature in Vienna from 22 March 1985 to 21 September 1985, and at United Nations Headquarters in New York from 22 September 1985 to 21 March 1986 (Art 12). States and regional economic integration organizations ratify, accept or approve it and deposit the instruments with the Depositary (Art 13). It is open for accession after it closes for signature (Art 14).
Article 15Right to vote. Each Party has one vote. A regional economic integration organization votes, in matters within its competence, with as many votes as its member States that are Parties, and does not vote if its member States do.
Article 16Relationship between the Convention and its protocols. A State may not become a party to a protocol unless it is, or at the same time becomes, a Party to the Convention. Decisions on a protocol are taken only by the Parties to that protocol.
Article 17Entry into force. The Convention enters into force on the ninetieth day after the deposit of the twentieth instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession (Art 17(1)). A protocol enters into force on the ninetieth day after the eleventh instrument, unless it says otherwise (Art 17(2)). An instrument deposited by a regional economic integration organization is not counted in addition to those of its member States (Art 17(5)).
Article 18Reservations. No reservations may be made to the Convention.
Article 19Withdrawal. A Party may withdraw by written notice at any time after four years from the date the Convention entered into force for it. Withdrawal takes effect one year after the Depositary receives the notice, or later if the notice says so. A Party that withdraws from the Convention is treated as having withdrawn from every protocol it is party to.
Articles 20-21The Secretary-General of the United Nations is the Depositary and informs the Parties of signatures, deposits, entry into force, withdrawals, amendments, annexes, declarations and notifications (Art 20). The Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish texts are equally authentic (Art 21). The Convention was done at Vienna on 22 March 1985.
Annex IResearch and systematic observations. It names two major scientific issues: change in the UV-B radiation reaching the Earth, and change in the vertical distribution of ozone, which could alter the temperature structure of the atmosphere. It lists research on atmospheric physics and chemistry, health, biological and photodegradation effects, and climate, and systematic observation of the ozone layer.
Annex IIInformation exchange. It covers scientific, technical, socio-economic and commercial, and legal information.

ProvisionWhat it says
Article 1Definitions. "Controlled substance" means a substance listed in Annex A, alone or in a mixture, but not one that is inside a manufactured product other than a container used to transport or store it. "Production" is the amount produced minus the amount destroyed by technologies the Parties approve. "Consumption" is production plus imports minus exports of controlled substances. "Industrial rationalization" is the transfer of all or part of one Party's calculated production level to another, to gain economic efficiency or meet expected supply shortfalls from plant closures.
Article 2Control measures. It freezes and then cuts production and consumption of the controlled substances in stages (see the timetable below). A group of Parties that belong to a regional economic integration organization may fulfil the consumption obligations jointly (Art 2(8)). The Parties may later adjust the ozone depleting potentials and the reductions. Consensus is tried first, and the last resort is a two-thirds majority of Parties present and voting that also represents at least fifty per cent of total consumption of the controlled substances. These decisions bind all Parties (Art 2(9)). The Parties may add or remove substances in an annex by a two-thirds majority (Art 2(10)). Parties may take more stringent measures than the Article requires (Art 2(11)).
Article 3Calculation of control levels. A Party multiplies the annual production of each controlled substance by its ozone depleting potential in Annex A and adds the results for each Group. Imports and exports are worked out the same way. Consumption is calculated production plus calculated imports minus calculated exports. From 1 January 1993, exports to non-Parties are not subtracted.
Article 4Control of trade with non-Parties. Within one year of entry into force each Party bans the import of controlled substances from any State not party (Art 4(1)). From 1 January 1993 a Party operating under Article 5(1) may not export them to a non-Party (Art 4(2)). Lists of products containing controlled substances, and of products made with them, are to be drawn up for import bans or restrictions (Art 4(3)-(4)). Parties discourage export of the technology for producing and using controlled substances and refrain from new subsidies, aid, credits, guarantees or insurance for exports that would help production (Art 4(5)-(6)). These last two rules do not apply to technology that improves containment, recovery, recycling or destruction, or promotes alternatives (Art 4(7)). Imports from a non-Party may be allowed if a meeting of the Parties finds it in full compliance and it has reported data (Art 4(8)).
Article 5Special situation of developing countries. A developing country whose annual calculated consumption is under 0.3 kilograms per capita may delay compliance with Article 2(1)-(4) by ten years, to meet its basic domestic needs. It must not exceed 0.3 kilograms per capita. Its compliance basis is the lower of its average annual consumption for 1995 to 1997 and 0.3 kilograms per capita (Art 5(1)). The Parties undertake to help such countries get safe alternative substances and technology (Art 5(2)). They undertake to facilitate subsidies, aid, credits, guarantees or insurance for alternative technology and substitutes (Art 5(3)).
Article 6Assessment and review of control measures. Beginning in 1990, and at least every four years after that, the Parties assess the control measures on the basis of scientific, environmental, technical and economic information. Expert panels are convened at least one year before each assessment and report within one year.
Article 7Reporting of data. Each Party gives the secretariat data on its production, imports and exports of each controlled substance for 1986, within three months of becoming a Party (Art 7(1)). It then sends annual data on production (with amounts destroyed shown separately), imports and exports to Parties and non-Parties, no later than nine months after the end of the year (Art 7(2)).
Article 8Non-compliance. At their first meeting the Parties consider and approve procedures and institutional mechanisms for deciding non-compliance and for treating Parties found in non-compliance. The Article itself does not set out those procedures.
Article 9Research, development, public awareness and exchange of information. Parties co-operate on the best technologies for containment, recovery, recycling or destruction, on alternatives, and on costs and benefits of control strategies (Art 9(1)). They promote public awareness of the environmental effects of emissions (Art 9(2)). Within two years of entry into force and every two years after, each Party submits a summary of its activities (Art 9(3)).
Article 10Technical assistance. Parties co-operate in promoting technical assistance, with special regard to developing countries. Any Party or Signatory may ask the secretariat for assistance (Art 10(1)-(2)). At their first meeting the Parties begin deliberations on means of fulfilling Article 9 and this Article, including workplans that pay special attention to developing countries (Art 10(3)).
Article 11Meetings of the Parties. The first meeting is convened within one year after entry into force. Later ordinary meetings are held with meetings of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention, unless the Parties decide otherwise (Art 11(1)-(2)). At the first meeting the Parties adopt rules of procedure and financial rules by consensus, set up the Article 6 panels, approve the non-compliance procedures and begin the workplans (Art 11(3)). Their functions include reviewing implementation, deciding adjustments and reductions, adding or removing substances, reviewing technical assistance requests, adopting amendments and the budget (Art 11(4)).
Article 12Secretariat. It arranges meetings, receives and makes available the data under Article 7, prepares and distributes reports, notifies requests for technical assistance, encourages non-Parties to attend as observers, and performs other functions the Parties assign.
Article 13Financial provisions. The funds needed to run the Protocol, including its secretariat, are charged exclusively against contributions from the Parties (Art 13(1)). The Parties adopt financial rules by consensus at their first meeting (Art 13(2)).
Article 14Relationship to the Convention. Unless the Protocol says otherwise, the Convention's provisions on its protocols apply to this Protocol.
Articles 15-17Signature was open in Montreal on 16 September 1987, in Ottawa from 17 September 1987 to 16 January 1988, and in New York from 17 January 1988 to 15 September 1988 (Art 15). The Protocol enters into force on 1 January 1989 if at least eleven instruments are deposited by States or organizations representing at least two thirds of estimated 1986 global consumption, and the Convention's article 17(1) is fulfilled. If not, it enters into force on the ninetieth day after those conditions are met (Art 16(1)). A later Party becomes bound on the ninetieth day after depositing its instrument (Art 16(3)). A Party that joins later must at once fulfil the obligations under Articles 2 and 4 that apply at that date, subject to Article 5 (Art 17).
Article 18Reservations. No reservations may be made to the Protocol.
Article 19Withdrawal. The Convention's withdrawal rule applies. A developing country Party under Article 5(1) may withdraw by written notice at any time after four years of assuming the obligations in Article 2(1)-(4). Withdrawal takes effect one year after receipt, or later if the notice says so.
Article 20Authentic texts. The Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish texts are equally authentic. The Protocol was done at Montreal on 16 September 1987.
